Commentary on Surat al-Tawbah [[in K: "Bara'ah"]]

Medinan [[addition from K.]]

* *

This noble surah is among the last of what was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as al-Bukhari said.

Abu al-Walid narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara' say: "The last verse revealed was: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning al-Kalalah﴾ [al-Nisa': 176], and the last surah revealed was Bara'ah." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4645.] [[the "Abu" is an addition from D, K, and al-Bukhari.]]

The reason it does not begin with the basmalah (the phrase "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful") is that the Companions did not write the basmalah at its beginning in the Imam Mushaf (the master copy of the Qur'an). Following them in this was the Commander of the Faithful, 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him and content him, as al-Tirmidhi said:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Yahya ibn Sa'd, Muhammad ibn Ja'far [[in D, K: "Muhammad ibn Abi Ja'far"]] and Ibn Abi 'Adi, and Sahl ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: 'Awf ibn Abi Jamilah [[in T: "Hamlah"]] narrated to us, saying: Yazid al-Fari informed me, saying: Ibn 'Abbas informed me, saying: I said to 'Uthman ibn 'Affan: "What led you to take al-Anfal, which is among the mathani (the oft-repeated surahs, those of medium length), and Bara'ah, which is among the mi'in (surahs of about a hundred verses), and join them together, and not write between them the line ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾, and place them among the al-sab' al-tiwal (the seven long surahs)? What led you to do that?" 'Uthman said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would often be in a time when surahs with many verses were revealed to him. Whenever something was revealed to him, he would call some of those who wrote for him and say: 'Place these verses in the surah in which such-and-such is mentioned.' When a verse was revealed to him, he would say: 'Place this verse [[in K, A: "this verse"]] in the surah in which such-and-such is mentioned.' Al-Anfal was among the first things revealed at Medina, and Bara'ah was among the last of the Qur'an. Its story resembled the story of [[in T: "some of it"]] it, and I thought it was part of it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died and did not make clear to us that it was part of it. For this reason I joined them together, and I did not write between them the line ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾, and I placed them in the seven long surahs."" [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3086.]

It was also related by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, through other chains, from 'Awf al-A'rabi, with the same wording. [Al-Musnad (1/57), Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 786, al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 8007, and al-Mustadrak (2/330).] Al-Hakim said: "Its isnad is sahih, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not narrate it."

The beginning of this noble surah was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he returned from the Battle of Tabuk and intended to perform Hajj. It was then mentioned that the polytheists would attend that season that year as was their custom, and that they would circumambulate the House naked. He disliked mixing with them, so he sent Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, as amir (leader) over the Hajj that year, to lead the people in their rites, and to inform the polytheists that they must not perform Hajj after that year, and to proclaim Bara'ah among the people. When [Abu Bakr] had departed, he sent 'Ali ibn Abi Talib after him, so that he would convey [the message] on behalf of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because he was his close kinsman ('asabah), as its explanation will come later.

So His saying: ﴿A declaration of immunity from Allah and His Messenger﴾ means: this is a declaration of immunity, that is, a disavowal from Allah and His Messenger ﴿to those with whom you made covenants among the polytheists. So travel freely in the land for four months﴾.

The commentators differed greatly here. Some said: this verse concerns those with open-ended covenants, not bound by a fixed term, or those whose covenant was less than four months, so it is completed to four months for them. As for one who had a covenant with a fixed term, his term extends to its term, whatever it may be, based on His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So fulfill their covenant to them until their term. Indeed, Allah loves those who fear Him﴾ [al-Tawbah: 4], and based on what will come in the hadith: "Whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his covenant lasts until its term." This is the best and strongest of the opinions. Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, chose it, and it was narrated from al-Kalbi, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and others.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿A declaration of immunity from Allah and His Messenger to those with whom you made covenants among the polytheists. So travel freely in the land for four months﴾, he said: "Allah set a limit of four months for those who had covenants with His Messenger, to travel in the land wherever they wished. He set the term for one who had no covenant as the end of the sacred months, from the Day of Sacrifice to the end of Muharram, which is fifty nights. When the sacred months had passed, He commanded him to lay down the sword against those who had no covenant."

It was also narrated in this way by al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

Al-Dahhak said, after his saying "which is fifty nights": "Allah commanded His Prophet that when Muharram had passed, he should lay down the sword against those with whom he had no covenant, to kill them until they enter Islam. And He commanded that for those who had a covenant, when four months had passed from the Day of Sacrifice to ten nights of Rabi' al-Akhir had elapsed, he should lay down the sword against them [[in T: "the sword too"]] until they enter Islam."

Abu Ma'shar al-Madani said: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and others narrated to us, saying: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Abu Bakr as amir over the season in the year nine, and sent 'Ali ibn Abi Talib with thirty or forty verses of 'Bara'ah', and he recited them to the people, granting the polytheists a period of four months to travel in the land. He recited them to them on the Day of 'Arafah. He gave the polytheists a term from the twentieth of Dhu al-Hijjah, and Muharram, and Safar, and the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, and ten days of Rabi' al-Akhir. He recited them to them in their dwellings and said: 'No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year of ours, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked.'"

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid: ﴿A declaration of immunity from Allah and His Messenger﴾ [is addressed] to the people of covenant: Khuza'ah, Mudlij, and whoever had a covenant or others. "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came back from Tabuk when he had finished, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended to perform Hajj. Then he said: 'The polytheists only attend and circumambulate naked, so I do not like to perform Hajj until that no longer happens.' So he sent Abu Bakr and 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with both of them, and they went among the people at Dhu al-Majaz and at their places where they used to trade in all the seasons. They informed the people of covenant that they would be secure for four months, which are the consecutive months: from the twentieth of Dhu al-Hijjah to ten nights of Rabi' al-Akhir had passed. After that they would have no covenant. And they announced to all the people that they would fight, except those who sought security."

It was narrated in the same way from al-Suddi and Qatadah.

Al-Zuhri said: "The start of the term was from Shawwal, and its end was the end of Muharram."

This opinion is strange, for how could they be held accountable for a period whose ruling had not reached them? Its matter only became manifest to them on the Day of Sacrifice, when the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proclaimed it. For this reason Exalted Allah said:

[In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And in Him I seek help, and He is sufficient for me, and how excellent a Guardian He is.] [[addition from K.]]

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger" and a declaration (taqaddum) and a warning to the people, "on the Day of the Greatest Hajj," which is the Day of Sacrifice (yawm al-nahr), the best and most prominent of the days of the rites (manasik) and the day on which the greatest number gather. [In another manuscript: "and the greatest of them in its entirety."] "That Allah is free from obligation to the polytheists, and so is His Messenger" — that is, He is free of them as well.

Then He called them to repent to Him, saying: "So if you repent" — that is, from the polytheism and misguidance you are in — "it is better for you. But if you turn away" — that is, you persist in what you are upon — "then know that you cannot escape Allah" — rather, He is capable, and you are in His grip, under His subjugation and His will. "And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment" — that is, in this world with disgrace and retribution, and in the Hereafter with iron maces and shackles.

Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, Uqayl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, sent me in that Hajj among the criers (al-mu'adhdhinin), whom he sent on the Day of Sacrifice to proclaim at Mina: "No polytheist may perform Hajj after this year, and no one may circumambulate the House naked." Humayd said: Then the Prophet ﷺ sent after him Ali ibn Abi Talib and commanded him to proclaim Bara'ah. Abu Hurayrah said: So Ali proclaimed with us among the people of Mina on the Day of Sacrifice the (verses of) Bara'ah, and that no polytheist may perform Hajj after this year, and no one may circumambulate the House naked. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4655.]

Al-Bukhari also narrated: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: Abu Bakr sent me among those who proclaimed on the Day of Sacrifice at Mina: "No polytheist may perform Hajj after this year, and no one may circumambulate the House naked. The Day of the Greatest Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice." It was said "the Greatest" only because of the people's saying "the Lesser Hajj." So Abu Bakr dispatched (a notice) to the people in that year, and no polytheist performed Hajj in the year of the Farewell Hajj in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed Hajj.

This is the wording of al-Bukhari in the Book of Jihad. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3177.]

Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning His words: "A declaration from Allah and His Messenger," he said: When the Prophet ﷺ was at (the time of) Hunayn, he performed Umrah from al-Ji'ranah, then he commanded Abu Bakr over that Hajj. Ma'mar said: al-Zuhri said: Abu Hurayrah used to narrate that Abu Bakr commanded Abu Hurayrah to proclaim Bara'ah during the Hajj of Abu Bakr [in another manuscript: "during the Hajj of Abu Bakr in Makkah"]. Abu Hurayrah said: Then the Prophet ﷺ sent Ali after us and commanded him to proclaim Bara'ah, while Abu Bakr remained in charge of the season as he was, or he said: in his condition. [What is in Abd al-Razzaq's tafsir is what came in the Sahih; perhaps he narrated it in his Musannaf.]

This narration has an oddity, in that the one in charge of the Hajj in the year of the Umrah from al-Ji'ranah was only Attab ibn Usayd, whereas Abu Bakr was in charge only in the year nine (AH).

Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, from Muharrir ibn Abi Hurayrah, from his father, who said: I was with Ali ibn Abi Talib when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him to the people of Makkah with "Bara'ah." He said: "What were you calling out?" He said: "We were calling: No one enters Paradise except a believer, no one circumambulates the House naked, and whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his term extends to four months. When the four months have passed, Allah is free of the polytheists, and so is His Messenger. No polytheist may perform Hajj to this House after this year." He said: "So I kept calling until my voice became hoarse." [Musnad (2/299).] al-Sha'bi also said: Muharrir ibn Abi Hurayrah narrated to me, from his father, who said: I was with Ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him to proclaim; whenever he became hoarse, I would call out. I asked: "With what were you proclaiming?" He said: "With four things: No one circumambulates the Ka'bah naked; whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his covenant runs to its term; no one enters Paradise except a believing soul; and no polytheist performs Hajj after our year."

Ibn Jarir narrated it through more than one chain from al-Sha'bi. Shu'bah narrated it from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, with the same, except that he said: "Whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his covenant is to four months," and he mentioned the rest of the hadith. [Tafsir al-Tabari (14/103–105).]

Ibn Jarir said: I fear that it is a mistake of some of its transmitters, because the reports are consistent regarding the term, contrary to this.

Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Simak, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent "Bara'ah" with Abu Bakr; when he reached Dhu al-Hulayfah he said: "None shall convey it except I or a man from my household." So he sent it with Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him. [Musnad (3/283).]

al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Tafsir, from Bundar, from Affan and Abd al-Samad, both from Hammad ibn Salamah with it. Then he said: "Hasan gharib, from the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him."

Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Muhammad ibn Sulayman (Luwayn) narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Jabir narrated to us, from Simak, from Hanash, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When ten verses of "Bara'ah" were revealed to the Prophet ﷺ, the Prophet ﷺ called Abu Bakr and sent him with them to recite them to the people of Makkah. Then he called me and said: "Catch up with Abu Bakr; wherever you overtake him, take the writing from him, and go to the people of Makkah and recite it to them." So I caught up with him at al-Juhfah, took the writing from him, and Abu Bakr returned to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, has something been revealed concerning me?" He said: "No, but Jibril came to me and said: None shall convey it on your behalf except you or a man from you." [Zawa'id al-Musnad (1/151).]

This chain contains weakness.

The intended meaning is not that Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, returned immediately; rather, after completing the rites which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had appointed him to lead, as is clarified in the other narration.

Abd Allah also said: Abu Bakr narrated to me, Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, from Asbat ibn Nasr, from Simak, from Hanash, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him with "Bara'ah," he said: "O Prophet of Allah, I am not eloquent nor a skilled speaker." He said: "There is no way but that I go with it or you go with it." He said: "If it must be so, then I will go." He said: "Set out, for Allah will make your tongue firm and guide your heart." He said: Then he placed his hand on his mouth. [Zawa'id al-Musnad (1/150); in its chain are Asbat ibn Nasr and Hanash ibn al-Mu'tamir, both of whom are spoken of (criticised).]

Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd ibn Yuthay' (a man of Hamdan): We asked Ali: "With what were you sent?" — meaning: on the day the Prophet ﷺ sent him with Abu Bakr for the Hajj. He said: "I was sent with four: No one enters Paradise except a believing soul; no one circumambulates the House naked; whoever has a covenant with the Prophet ﷺ, his covenant is to its term; and polytheists and Muslims shall not perform Hajj after this their year."

al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Qilabah, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, with it, and said: "Hasan sahih." [Musnad (1/79); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3092.]

Thus he said. Shu'bah narrated it from Abu Ishaq and said: "from Zayd ibn Yuthay'" — he erred in it. al-Thawri narrated it from Abu Ishaq, from one of his companions, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Waki' narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd ibn Yuthay', from Ali who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me when "Bara'ah" was revealed with four: that no one circumambulates the House naked; that no polytheist approaches the Sacred Mosque after this their year; whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, it is to its term; and no one enters Paradise except a believing soul. [Tafsir al-Tabari (14/106).]

Then Ibn Jarir narrated from Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Thawr, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from Ali who said: I was commanded with four, and he mentioned it.

Isra'il said, from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd ibn Yuthay' who said: "Bara'ah" was revealed, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Abu Bakr, then sent Ali and took it from him. When Abu Bakr returned he said: "Has something been revealed concerning me?" He said: "No, but I was commanded that it be conveyed by me or by a man from my household." So he set out to the people of Makkah and stood among them with four: No polytheist may enter Makkah after this year; no one circumambulates the House naked; no one enters Paradise except a Muslim soul; and whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his covenant is to its term. [Al-Tabari narrated it in his tafsir (14/107) through the chain of Isra'il.]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Hakim ibn Hakim ibn Abbad ibn Hunayf, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali who said: When "Bara'ah" was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he had sent Abu Bakr to establish the Hajj for the people. It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, would that you sent (someone) to Abu Bakr." He said: "None shall convey on my behalf except a man from my household." Then he called Ali and said: "Go out with this account from the beginning of Bara'ah, and proclaim to the people on the Day of Sacrifice when they gather at Mina: that no disbeliever enters Paradise, no polytheist performs Hajj after this year, no one circumambulates the House naked, and whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his covenant is to its term."

So Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, went out on the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ she-camel al-Adba', until he overtook Abu Bakr on the road. When Abu Bakr saw him he said: "Are you a commander or one commanded?" He said: "Rather, one commanded." Then both proceeded. Abu Bakr led the people in Hajj, and the Arabs at that time in that year were in their places of Hajj which they had followed in the Jahiliyyah. Then when the Day of Sacrifice came, Ali ibn Abi Talib stood and proclaimed among the people what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had commanded him, saying: "O people, indeed no disbeliever enters Paradise, no one performs Hajj after this year, no one circumambulates the House naked, and whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, it is to its term." So no polytheist performed Hajj after that year, and no one circumambulated the House naked. Then both returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. This was from "Bara'ah" concerning those among the polytheists who had a general covenant, and those with a term until the appointed time.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to us, Abu Zur'a Wahb Allah ibn Rashid informed us, Haywa ibn Shurayh informed us: Abu [[In A: "Ibn".]] Sakhr informed us, that he heard Abu Mu'awiya al-Bajali, from the people of Kufa, say: I heard Abu al-Sahba' al-Bakri say: I asked 'Ali ibn Abi Talib [[In D: "I asked Ali".]] about "the Day of the Greater Hajj," and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafa to lead the people in the Hajj, and sent me with him with forty verses of "Bara'a" (Surat al-Tawba). When he reached 'Arafa, he addressed the people on the Day of 'Arafa. When he had finished his sermon, he turned to me and said: "Stand up, O 'Ali, and deliver the message of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." So I stood and recited to them the forty verses of "Bara'a." Then we departed and came to Mina. I threw the pebbles at the Jamra, sacrificed the camel, then shaved my head. I knew that the people of the gathering had not all attended Abu Bakr's sermon on the Day of 'Arafa, so I went around searching for them among the tents, reciting it to them. Hence I suppose that you have assumed it was the Day of Sacrifice [Alā wa huwa yawmu al-nahr] [[Addition from D.]] Alā, it is the Day of 'Arafa [[In K: "Ahuwa".]] [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/113).]]

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ishaq: I asked Abu Juhayfa about the Day of the Greater Hajj. He said: It is the Day of 'Arafa. I said: Is this from you, or from the companions of Muhammad ﷺ? He said: Each of them [says so]. [[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/241).]]

'Abd al-Razzaq also said, from Juraij, from 'Ata', who said: The Day of the Greater Hajj is the Day of 'Arafa.

'Umar ibn al-Walid al-Shanni said: Shihab ibn 'Abbad al-'Asri narrated to us, from his father, who said: I heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab say: This is the Day of 'Arafa, this is the Day of the Greater Hajj, so let no one fast it. He said: I performed Hajj after my father, and came to Madina, and asked about its most virtuous people. They said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. So I went to him and said: I was told that the most virtuous person in Madina is Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. Tell me about fasting the Day of 'Arafa. He said: I will tell you about one who is a hundred times better than me: 'Umar, or Ibn 'Umar, used to forbid fasting it, and he would say: It is the Day of the Greater Hajj.

Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/114).]] Similarly it has been related from Ibn 'Abbas, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, 'Ikrima and Tawus that they said: The Day of 'Arafa is the Day of the Greater Hajj.

There is also a mursal hadith on this, narrated by Ibn Juraij: I was informed, from Muhammad ibn Qays ibn Makhrama, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a sermon on the Day of 'Arafa and said: "This is the Day of the Greater Hajj." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/116).]]

It was also narrated by another route from Ibn Juraij, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from al-Miswar ibn Makhrama, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he addressed them at 'Arafat, praised and extolled Allah, then said: "Amma ba'du, this is the Day of the Greater Hajj."

The second view is that it is the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr).

Hushaym said, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Day of the Greater Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice.

Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i said, from al-Harith al-A'war: I asked 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, about the Day of the Greater Hajj, and he said: [It is] [[Addition from T.]] the Day of Sacrifice.

Shu'ba said, from al-Hakam: I heard Yahya ibn al-Jazzar narrate from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he went out on the Day of Sacrifice upon a white mule, intending the Jabbana (the place of prayer outside the town). A man came and took hold of the bridle of his mount and asked him about the Greater Hajj. He said: It is this day of yours; let go of her.

'Abd al-Razzaq said, from Sufyan, from Shu'ba [[In D: "From Shu'ba".]], from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, that he said: The Day of the Greater Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice.

Shu'ba and others narrated from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr something similar. Likewise Hushaym and others narrated it from al-Shaybani, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa. [[In T, K: "And similarly".]]

Al-A'mash said, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said: al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba addressed us on the Day of Adha, from a camel, and said: This is the Day of Adha, this is the Day of Sacrifice, and this is the Day of the Greater Hajj.

Hammad ibn Salama said, from Simak, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: The Greater Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice.

Likewise it has been related from Abu Juhayfa, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Had, Nafi' ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, al-Sha'bi, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Mujahid, 'Ikrima, Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, al-Zuhri and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, that they said: The Day of the Greater Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice. Ibn Jarir chose this view. The hadith from Abu Hurayra in Sahih al-Bukhari has already been mentioned, that Abu Bakr sent them on the Day of Sacrifice to proclaim the call in Mina. Other hadiths have also been transmitted on this, as the Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Sahl ibn Muhammad al-Sijistani narrated to me, Abu Jabir al-Haramiyy narrated to us, Hisham ibn al-Ghaz al-Jurashi narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood on the Day of Sacrifice at the Jamarat during the Farewell Hajj, and said: "This is the Day of the Greater Hajj." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/124).]]

Similarly, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Abu Jabir, whose name is Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik, with it. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it from the hadith of al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Hisham ibn al-Ghaz, with it. Then he narrated it from the hadith of Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Aziz, from Nafi', with it.

Shu'ba said, from 'Amr ibn Murra, from Murra al-Hamdani, from a man among the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us upon a red she-camel with a split ear, and said: "Do you know which day this day of yours is?" They said: The Day of Sacrifice. He said: "You have spoken truly; it is the Day of the Greater Hajj." [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (14/125).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, Ibn 'Awn narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakra, from his father, who said: When that day came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat upon his camel while the people took hold of its halter, or its reins, and he said: "What day is this?" He said: We remained silent until we thought he would name it by another name. Then he said: "Is this not the Day of the Greater Hajj?" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/123), and its origin is in Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4406) and Sahih Muslim no. (1679).]]

This is a sahih isnad, and its origin is recorded in the Sahih.

Abu al-Ahwas said, from Shabib ibn Gharqada, from Sulayman ibn 'Amr ibn al-Ahwas, from his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the Farewell Hajj say: "What day is this?" They said: "Today is the Greater Hajj." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. (2159), from Hannad, from Abu al-Ahwas with it, at greater length, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."]]

It is also reported from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab that he said: The Day of the Greater Hajj is the second day after the Day of Sacrifice. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Mujahid also said: The Day of the Greater Hajj is all the days of the Hajj.

Abu 'Ubayd likewise said, and Sufyan said: "the Day of the Hajj," "the Day of the Camel," and "the Day of Siffin," meaning all its days.

Sahl al-Sarraj said: al-Hasan al-Basri was asked about the Day of the Greater Hajj, and he said: What have you to do with the Greater Hajj? That was the year in which Abu Bakr performed Hajj, the one whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had appointed as successor, and he led the people in Hajj. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Waki' narrated to us, Abu Usama narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn: I asked Muhammad, meaning Ibn Sirin, about the Day of the Greater Hajj, and he said: It was a day on which the Hajj of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ coincided with the Hajj of the people of the wabar (dwellers of hair tents). [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/121).]]

This is an exception from the rule of the four-month grace period, for one who has an open-ended covenant that is not time-limited. His term is four months, during which he may travel through the land, going wherever he wishes to save himself. But one who has a time-limited covenant, his term extends to the fixed period for which he was bound by treaty. The hadiths have already been mentioned: "Whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his covenant lasts until its term." This holds on condition that the covenanted party does not break his covenant and does not support anyone against the Muslims, i.e., does not collude with others against them. Such a person is kept to his pledge and covenant until its term. For this reason Allah the Exalted urged fulfilment of this, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the righteous﴾, i.e., those who fulfil their covenants.

The mufassirun differed about what is meant here by "the sacred months" (al-Ashhur al-Hurum). Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) held that they are the four mentioned in His saying, ﴿Of them, four are sacred. That is the upright religion, so do not wrong yourselves during them﴾ [At-Tawbah: 36]. This was reported from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir [[Addition from manuscripts T and A.]]. But Ibn Jarir said: "The last of the sacred months, according to them, is Muharram." This view which he adopted was related by Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn Abbas, and al-Dahhak also adopted it. However, it is open to question. What appears from the context is the view of Ibn Abbas in the narration of al-Awfi from him, and it was also held by Mujahid, Amr ibn Shu'ayb, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam: that the intended months are the four months of travel (ashhur al-tasyir) specified in His saying, ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾ [At-Tawbah: 2]. Then He said, ﴿When the sacred months have passed﴾, meaning: when the four months in which We forbade you to fight them, and gave them a respite, have ended, then wherever you find them, kill them. This is because returning a pronoun to something already mentioned is preferable to returning it to something implied. Furthermore, the ruling on the four sacred months will be explained in another verse later in this noble surah.

* *

His saying, ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾, meaning: within the land. This is general, but the well-known view is that it is restricted by the prohibition of fighting in the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram), by His saying, ﴿And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you there; but if they fight you, then kill them﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 191].

* *

His saying, ﴿And capture them﴾, meaning: and take them prisoner, if you wish, by killing, or if you wish, by taking them captive.

* *

His saying, ﴿And besiege them and sit in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾, meaning: do not be content merely with finding them, but target them with a siege in their strongholds and fortresses, and with ambush on their roads and routes, until you constrict the wide space for them and compel them to either be killed or embrace Islam. For this reason He said: ﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then let them go their way. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

For this reason, al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) relied on this noble verse and similar ones when fighting those who withheld zakah, since it prohibits fighting them on condition of these acts, namely entering Islam and carrying out its obligations. He drew attention to the highest of them as an indication of the lowest, for after the testimony of faith, the most honored of the pillars is prayer, which is the right of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. After it is the payment of zakah, which is a benefit extending to the poor and the needy, and it is the most honored of the acts related to created beings. For this reason Allah often links prayer and zakah together. It has been reported in the two Sahihs [[In T and A: "al-Sahih".]] from Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with both of them), from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "I have been commanded to fight people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establish prayer, and give zakah," and the hadith continues.

Abu Ishaq related from Abu Ubaydah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "You were commanded to establish prayer and give zakah, and whoever does not give zakah, there is no prayer for him."

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Allah refused to accept prayer except with zakah." And he said: "May Allah have mercy on Abu Bakr; how learned in jurisprudence he was!"

Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Humayd al-Tawil informed us, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been commanded to fight people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. When they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, face our qiblah, eat our slaughtered animals, and pray our prayer, then their blood and their property are forbidden to us except by their due right. They have what the Muslims have, and they bear what the Muslims bear."

Al-Bukhari in his Sahih and the authors of the Sunan (except Ibn Majah) related it from the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, with this chain [[Al-Musnad (3/199); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 392; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 2641; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2608; Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/109).]]

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Abd al-Ala ibn Wasil al-Asadi narrated to us, Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, Abu Ja'far al-Razi informed us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas [from Anas] [[Addition from manuscripts T and A, and al-Tabari.]], who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever departs from this world sincerely devoted to Allah alone, worshipping Him and not associating anything with Him, departs while Allah is pleased with him." He said: Anas said: "That is the religion of Allah with which the messengers came and which they conveyed from their Lord, before the chattering of hadiths and the divergence of desires, and the confirmation of this is in the Book of Allah in the last of what was revealed. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then let them go their way﴾." He said: "Their repentance is the abandonment of idols, the worship of their Lord, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakah." Then He said in another verse: ﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion﴾ [At-Tawbah: 11] [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/135). Ibn Majah related it in al-Sunan, no. 70, through the chain of Ubayd Allah ibn Musa in similar wording. Al-Busayri said in al-Zawa'id (1/56): "This chain is weak; al-Rabi' ibn Anas is weak here."]].

Ibn Mardawayh also related it.

Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi related it in his book "al-Salah" (The Prayer): Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Hakkam ibn Salm informed us, Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, with the same [chain] [[Ta'zim qadr al-salah, no. 1.]].

This noble verse is the verse of the sword, concerning which al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said: "It abrogated (nasakha) every covenant between the Prophet ﷺ and any of the polytheists, and every treaty and every term."

Al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas concerning this verse: "No polytheist retained any covenant or protection since Bara'ah (At-Tawbah) was revealed and the sacred months had passed. The term for those polytheists who had a covenant before it was revealed was four months, from the day Bara'ah was proclaimed until the tenth of the first month of Rabi' al-Akhir."

Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas concerning this verse, he said: "Allah commanded him to put the sword to those who had made a treaty if they did not enter Islam, and to annul what had been agreed upon for them of the pact and covenant, and to remove the first condition."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Musa al-Ansari narrated to us, who said: Sufyan [[In T, K, and A: "Sufyan ibn Uyaynah".]] said: Ali ibn Abi Talib said: "The Prophet ﷺ was sent with four swords: a sword against the polytheists among the Arabs. Allah said: ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them [and take them captive]﴾ [[Addition from manuscript A.]]"

Thus he related it in abridged form, and I think that the second sword is the fighting against the People of the Book in His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful and who do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled﴾ [At-Tawbah: 29]. The third sword is the fighting against the hypocrites in His saying: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them﴾ [At-Tawbah: 73; At-Tahrim: 9] [[Addition from manuscript A.]]. The fourth is the fighting against the rebellious in His saying: ﴿And if two groups of believers fight, then make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of Allah﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 9].

Then the mufassirun differed concerning this verse of the sword. Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: it is abrogated by His saying: ﴿Then either grace afterward or ransom﴾ [Muhammad: 4]. Qatadah said the opposite.

Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him: ﴿And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection﴾, those whom I commanded you to fight, and whose lives and property I made lawful for you to take, ﴿seeks your protection﴾, meaning: asks you for safe conduct, so grant him his request ﴿until he hears the words of Allah﴾, meaning: [the Qur'an] [[Addition from manuscripts ت، د، ك، أ.]], that you recite to him and mention to him some of [the matter] [[Addition from manuscripts ت، د، ك، أ.]] of the religion, by which you establish the proof of Allah against him. ﴿Then escort him to his place of safety﴾, meaning: while he is secure, with his safety continuing until he returns to his land, his home and his refuge. ﴿That is because they are a people who do not know﴾, meaning: We only prescribed safe conduct for such people so that they may learn the religion of Allah, and so that the call of Allah may spread among His servants.

Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid, regarding the interpretation of this verse, that he said: "A person who comes to you to hear what you say and what has been revealed to you is secure until he comes to you and hears the words of Allah, and until he reaches his place of safety, wherever he came from."

From this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to grant safe conduct to whoever came to him seeking guidance or on a mission, just as there came to him at Hudaybiyyah a group of envoys from Quraysh, among them: Urwah ibn Mas'ud, Mikraz ibn Hafs, Suhayl ibn Amr, and others, one after another, going back and forth regarding the matter between him and the polytheists. They saw from the Muslims' veneration of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) what overwhelmed them, and what they had not witnessed beside any king or Caesar. So they returned to their people and informed them of that, and that and similar things were among the greatest causes of the guidance of most of them.

Likewise, when the messenger of Musaylimah the Liar came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said to him: "Do you bear witness that Musaylimah is the Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Were it not that messengers are not killed, I would have struck off your neck." [[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (3/487) and Abu Dawud in al-Sunan, no. (2761), by way of Salamah ibn al-Fadl, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'd ibn Tariq, from Salamah ibn Nu'aym, from his father, who said: "I was with the Prophet (ﷺ) when the envoys of Musaylimah came to him," and he mentioned something similar.]] Allah later decreed the striking of his neck during the governorship of Ibn Mas'ud over Kufa. He was called Ibn al-Nawwahah. It became known during the time of Ibn Mas'ud that he was testifying to Musaylimah's prophethood. Ibn Mas'ud sent for him and said to him: "You are now not on a mission," and he ordered him to be executed, so his neck was struck. May Allah not have mercy on him and may He curse him.

The point is that whoever comes from the abode of war to the abode of Islam on a mission, or for trade, or seeking a truce or a treaty, or to deliver the jizyah, or for something similar among the reasons, and asks the imam or his deputy for safe conduct, is granted safe conduct for as long as he moves about in the abode of Islam, and until he returns to his place of safety and homeland. However, the scholars said: it is not permitted to allow him to reside in the abode of Islam for a year, but it is permitted to allow him to stay for four months. As for what lies between that, beyond four months but less than a year, there are two opinions, reported from Imam al-Shafi'i and other scholars, may Allah have mercy on them.

How can there be a covenant with God and with His Messenger for the polytheists (mushrikun), when they are polytheists, disbelievers in God and in His Messenger? Ibn Kathir says: God, exalted is He, here explains His wisdom in declaring disavowal (bara'a) from the polytheists and giving them four months' respite, and after that the drawn sword wherever they are found. He said, exalted is He: "How can there be a covenant for the polytheists" and a guarantee of safety, and they be left in what they are in, while they are polytheists with God, disbelievers in Him and in His Messenger? "Except those with whom you made a covenant at al-Masjid al-Haram" means on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, as He said: "They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from al-Masjid al-Haram and the sacrifice detained from reaching its place" (al-Fath 25). "So as long as they are upright toward you, be upright toward them": meaning, as long as they adhere to what you contracted with them and covenanted with them of abandoning war between you and them for ten years, "then be upright toward them. Indeed, Allah loves those who fear Him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims did that: the contract and truce with the people of Makkah continued from Dhu al-Qa'dah in the year six, until Quraysh broke the covenant and backed their allies Banu Bakr against Khuza'ah, the allies of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they killed them along with them in the Sacred Precinct as well. At that, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) campaigned against them in Ramadan of the year eight, and Allah granted him the sacred city, and enabled him over their forelocks, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace. He released those of them who embraced Islam after subduing and overpowering them, and they were called the Tulaqa' (the freed ones), and they were nearly two thousand. As for those who persisted in their disbelief and fled from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he sent to them a guarantee of safety and freedom to travel in the land for four months, going wherever they wished. Among them were Safwan ibn Umayyah, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and others. Then Allah guided them afterward to complete Islam, and Allah is the One praised for all that He decrees and does.

Allah the Exalted says, urging the believers to oppose the polytheists and to disassociate themselves from them, and making clear that they do not deserve to have any covenant, because of their polytheism toward Allah and their disbelief in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Even if they were to gain the upper hand over the Muslims and prevail against them, they would not spare them, nor would they refrain from harming them, nor would they observe any kinship or covenant regarding them.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, ʿIkrimah, and al-ʿAwfi related from Ibn ʿAbbas: "al-Ill" means kinship, and "adh-Dhimmah" means covenant. Likewise said ad-Dahhak and as-Suddi, as Tamim ibn Muqbil said:

"Corrupted the people, successors who left behind, / They severed the ill (kinship) and the veins of the womb."

Hassan ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him, also said:

"We found them liars regarding their ill (kinship), / And the one who holds ill and covenant does not lie."

The editor of the Shaʿb edition commented: Ibn Kathir attributes this to Hassan ibn Thabit, but we have not found it in his Diwan. The verse in Tafsir al-Tabari (15/148) is unattributed. The verse of Hassan that al-Tabari cited is "By your life, indeed your ill is from Quraysh... like the ill of the she-camel's young from the ostrich's chicks." This verse is in the Diwan of Hassan, p. 336, and in Lisan al-ʿArab, root "a-l-l."

Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid regarding the verse ﴿They do not observe toward a believer any ill﴾, that he said: "Allah." In another narration: "They do not observe Allah nor anything else."

Ibn Jarir said: Yaʿqub related to me, Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from Sulayman, from Abu Mijlaz regarding His saying, ﴿They do not observe toward a believer any ill nor covenant﴾, like His saying "Jibra'il," "Mika'il," "Israfil," [as if he meant: he adds "Jibr," "Mika," and "Israf" to "Il," meaning "ʿAbd Allah" said: ﴿They do not observe toward a believer any ill﴾] as if he meant: they do not observe Allah.

The first opinion is more well-known and more apparent, and most scholars hold it.

Also from Mujahid: "al-Ill" means covenant. Qatadah said: "al-Ill" means alliance.

Ibn Kathir (may God have mercy on him) said, censuring the polytheists and urging the believers to fight them: ﴿They have sold the signs of God for a small price﴾. This means that they exchanged following the signs of God for the lowly worldly matters that occupied them. ﴿And they have averted [others] from His way﴾, that is, they prevented the believers from following the truth. ﴿Evil is what they have been doing. They do not observe toward a believer any ties of kinship or covenant﴾. Its explanation has already passed, and likewise the verse that follows: ﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah﴾ through to the end of it, has already passed.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Bakr narrated to us, Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, al-Rabi' ibn Anas narrated to us, saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever departs from this world sincere to God in worship, not associating anything with Him, establishes prayer, and gives zakah, departs while God is pleased with him. This is the religion of God which the messengers brought and conveyed from their Lord, before the chaos of hadith and the divergence of desires." [[In manuscripts T and K: "la shareek" (without a partner).]]

The confirmation of this in the Book of God is: ﴿But if they repent﴾, meaning: if they renounce the idols and their worship, ﴿and establish prayer and give zakah, then let them go their way﴾. And in another verse He said: ﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion﴾.

Then al-Bazzar said: In my view, the end of the hadith, and God knows best, is: "departs while He is pleased with him," and the rest of it, in my view, is from the speech of al-Rabi' ibn Anas. Al-Hakim said: "Its chain is sound" (sahih al-isnad), and al-Dhahabi responded: "I say: the beginning of the hadith is marfu' and the rest, as I see it, is mudraj (interpolated)."]]

The Exalted says: "And if they break their oaths after their covenant, and attack your religion" (﴿وَإِنْ نَكَثَ هَؤُلَاءِ الْمُشْرِكُونَ الَّذِينَ عَاهَدْتُمُوهُمْ عَلَى مُدَّةٍ مُعَيَّنَةٍ أَيْمَانَهُمْ وَطَعَنُوا فِي دِينِكُمْ﴾). That is, their oaths means their covenants and pacts. "Attack" means they disparage it and belittle it. From this verse is derived the ruling on killing one who reviles the Messenger (ﷺ), or who attacks the religion of Islam or mentions it with disparagement. For this reason He said: "So fight the leaders of disbelief, for indeed they have no oaths, so that they may desist" (﴿فَقَاتِلُوا أَئِمَّةَ الْكُفْرِ إِنَّهُمْ لَا أَيْمَانَ لَهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَنْتَهُونَ﴾). That is, that they may return from the disbelief, obstinacy and misguidance they are in.

Qatadah and others said: The leaders of disbelief are such as Abu Jahl, Utbah, Shaybah and Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and he enumerated other men.

It is narrated from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas that he said: Sa'd passed by a man from the Khawarij (a dissenting sect), and the Khariji said: "This is one of the leaders of disbelief." Sa'd said: "You lie, rather I am the one who fought the leaders of disbelief." Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh.

Al-A'mash said, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Hudhayfah, that he said: "No one has fought the people of this verse since."

It is also narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, something similar.

The correct view is that the verse is general, and although the occasion of its revelation was the polytheists of Quraysh, it applies to them and to others, and Allah knows best.

Al-Walid ibn Muslim said: Safwan ibn Amr narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr: that during the time of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, when he directed the people toward al-Sham, he said: "You will find a people whose heads are shaved, so strike the knots of Satan among them with swords. By Allah, for me to kill one man of them is dearer to me than to kill seventy of others. That is because Allah says: 'So fight the leaders of disbelief'." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

This is also an incitement, an urging and an exhortation to fight the polytheists who broke their oaths, those who plotted to expel the Messenger from Makkah, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to restrain you, or kill you, or expel you. They plot, and Allah plots. And Allah is the best of plotters.﴾ [al-Anfal: 30].

And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They expel the Messenger and yourselves because you believe in Allah, your Lord. [If you have come out for jihad in My cause and seeking My approval...]﴾ [[Addition from A.]] — the verse [al-Mumtahanah: 1]. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And indeed, they almost succeeded in driving you out of the land to expel you from it; but then they would not remain [there] after you, except for a little.﴾ [al-Isra: 76]. And His saying ﴿while they initiated [hostilities] against you the first time﴾ — it has been said that what is meant by this is the Day of Badr, when they went out to defend their caravan [[In D: "to defend their caravan."]]. When it escaped and they learned of that, they persisted in their course [[In T, K: "their course."]], seeking battle, out of transgression and arrogance, as the explanation of this has already been presented.

It has also been said: what is meant is their breaking of the covenant and their fighting [[In T: "fighting them."]] alongside their allies, the Banu Bakr, against Khuza'ah, the allies of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ marched against them in the year of the Conquest, and what happened, happened. And all praise is due to Allah.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Do you fear them? Allah has more right that you fear Him, if you are believers﴾ [[In K: "Do you fear them" which is an error.]] — Allah the Exalted says: Do not fear them; fear Me. I am worthy that My servants fear My punishment and My retribution. The matter is in My hand; what I will is, and what I do not will does not happen.

Then Allah the Exalted said, as a binding command upon the believers and an explanation of His wisdom in what He prescribed for them of jihad, despite His power to destroy the enemies by a command from Him: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them and heal the breasts of a believing people.﴾ This is general for all the believers.

Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and as-Suddi said regarding this verse, ﴿and heal the breasts of a believing people﴾, that it refers to Khuza'ah.

And the pronoun in His saying ﴿and remove the rage of their hearts﴾ also refers back to them.

Ibn 'Asakir mentioned in the biography of a muezzin of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, may Allah be pleased with him, on the authority of Muslim ibn Yasar, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he became angry, would take hold of her nose and say: "O Uways, say: 'Allahumma, Lord of the Prophet Muhammad, forgive my sin, remove the rage of my heart, and protect me from misleading trials.'"

He related it through the route of Abu Ahmad al-Hakim, from al-Baghandi, from Hisham ibn 'Ammar, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Jawn narrated to us, from him [[Tarikh Dimashq (19/335) "manuscript". It was also related by Ibn as-Sunni in 'Amal al-Yawm wal-Laylah through the route of Abu al-'Umays from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr from 'A'ishah, and through the route of Salamah ibn 'Ali from Hisham ibn 'Urwah from 'A'ishah.]]

He is the Just Judge who never oppresses, and does not waste the weight of an atom's worth of good or evil, but rewards for it in this world and the Hereafter.

Allah the Exalted says: "Or do you think" (O believers) that We would leave you neglected, without testing you through matters in which those of sincere resolve are distinguished from the liars? For this reason He said: "And Allah has not yet known those among you who strive (jahadu) and do not take, other than Allah and His Messenger and the believers, any intimate (waliyjah)," that is: any confidant and inner circle [in one manuscript: "dukhlah"]. Rather, they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger both outwardly and inwardly. So He suffices with one of the two categories over the other, as the poet said:

"And I do not know, when I set out for a land, seeking good, which of the two will befall me..."

And Allah the Exalted said in another verse: "Alif, Lam, Mim. Do people think that they will be left alone because they say, 'We believe,' and they will not be tried? And We had already tried those before them, so Allah will surely make known those who are truthful and will surely make known the liars." [Al-'Ankabut: 1-3] And Allah the Exalted said: "Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet known those among you who strive and known the patient?" [Al 'Imran: 142] And Allah the Exalted said: "Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good. And Allah would not inform you of the unseen." [Al 'Imran: 179]

The summary is that when Allah legislated jihad for His servants, He made clear that there is wisdom in it, namely testing His servants: who obeys Him and who disobeys Him. He is the Exalted, who knows what has been, what will be, and what would have been had it not been, how it would have occurred. He knows a thing before it happens and while it is as it is. There is no god but Him, no lord besides Him, and none can repel what He has decreed and enacted.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Tawbah (9), verses 17–18

Allah the Exalted says: It is not fitting for the polytheists (al-mushrikun), who associate partners with Allah, to maintain the mosques of Allah, which were built for Him alone with no partner.

Whoever reads "masjid Allah" (in the singular) means by it al-Masjid al-Haram (the Sacred Mosque), the most honoured of the mosques on earth, which has been built from the first day for the worship of Allah alone, with no partner. It was founded by Khalil al-Rahman (Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful), ﴿and they bear witness against themselves to disbelief﴾, that is, by their state and their words. As al-Suddi said: If you asked the Christian, "What is your religion?" he would say, "Christian." If you asked the Jew, he would say, "Jew." If you asked the Sabian, he would say, "Sabian." If you asked the polytheist, he would say, "Polytheist."

﴿Those—their deeds have come to nothing﴾, that is, because of their polytheism, ﴿and in the Fire they will abide forever.﴾ As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And what is [wrong] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar [people] from al-Masjid al-Haram, though they are not its guardians? Its guardians are only the God-fearing, but most of them do not know.﴾ [al-Anfal 8:34]

Therefore He said: ﴿Only those who believe in Allah and the Last Day maintain the mosques of Allah.﴾ So Allah the Exalted testified to the faith of those who maintain the mosques. As Imam Ahmad said:

Surayj narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from Amr ibn al-Harith, that Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you see a man frequenting the mosque, then bear witness to his faith." Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Only those who believe in Allah and the Last Day maintain the mosques of Allah.﴾

[al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak also narrated it from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Wahb, with this chain.] [Ahmad, Musnad (3/68); Tirmidhi, no. 3093; al-Mustadrak (2/332). Darraj from Abu al-Haytham is weak.]

Abd ibn Humayd said in his Musnad: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Salih al-Murri narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Maymun ibn Siyah and Ja'far ibn Zayd, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, the maintainers of the mosques are the people of Allah." [In its chain is Salih al-Murri, who is weak, and he was differed with regarding it, as will come in the narration of al-Bazzar.] Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated it from Abd al-Wahid ibn Ghiyath, from Salih ibn Bashir al-Murri, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, the maintainers of the mosques are the people of Allah." Then he said: We do not know anyone who narrated it from Thabit except Salih. [Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 433, Kashf al-Astar. Al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (3/66) narrated it through Hashim ibn al-Qasim from Salih al-Murri with the same wording. Al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id (2/23) said: "In it is Salih al-Murri, who is weak."]

Al-Daraqutni narrated in al-Afrad through the route of Hakkama bint Uthman ibn Dinar, from her father, from her brother Malik ibn Dinar, from Anas, traced to the Prophet: "When Allah intends a calamity for a people, He looks at the people of the mosques and averts it from them." Then he said: Gharib (a single-route narration). [I did not find it in the Atraf of Ibn al-Qaysarani.]

Al-Hafiz al-Baha' narrated in al-Mustaqsa, through his father with his chain to Abu Umayya al-Tarsusi: Mansur ibn Suqayr narrated to us: Salih al-Murri narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, traced to the Prophet: "Allah says: By My might and My majesty, I am about to bring a punishment upon the people of the earth. But when I look at the maintainers of My houses, and at those who love one another for My sake, and at those who seek forgiveness at dawn, I turn it away from them." Then Ibn Asakir said: A gharib hadith. [In it is Mansur ibn Suqayr, of whom Abu Hatim said: "Not strong." Al-Uqayli said: "In his narrations there is some error." Ibn Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (4/61) through Sa'id ibn Ash'ath from Salih al-Murri with similar wording. Al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (no. 9051) narrated it through Abdan from Mu'adh ibn Khalid ibn Shuqayq from Salih al-Murri with similar wording. Salih al-Murri is weak.]

Imam Ahmad said: Rawh narrated to us: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: al-Ala' ibn Ziyad narrated to us, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, Satan is the wolf of man, like the wolf of the sheep, which seizes the straying sheep and the one that goes off to the side. So beware of the mountain paths, and keep to the community (al-jama'ah), the general body of Muslims, and the mosque." [Musnad (5/232). Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Tawbah (9), verses 17–18

Allah the Exalted says: It is not fitting for the polytheists (al-mushrikun), who associate partners with Allah, to maintain the mosques of Allah, which were built for Him alone with no partner.

Whoever reads "masjid Allah" (in the singular) means by it al-Masjid al-Haram (the Sacred Mosque), the most honoured of the mosques on earth, which has been built from the first day for the worship of Allah alone, with no partner. It was founded by Khalil al-Rahman (Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful), ﴿and they bear witness against themselves to disbelief﴾, that is, by their state and their words. As al-Suddi said: If you asked the Christian, "What is your religion?" he would say, "Christian." If you asked the Jew, he would say, "Jew." If you asked the Sabian, he would say, "Sabian." If you asked the polytheist, he would say, "Polytheist."

﴿Those—their deeds have come to nothing﴾, that is, because of their polytheism, ﴿and in the Fire they will abide forever.﴾ As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And what is [wrong] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar [people] from al-Masjid al-Haram, though they are not its guardians? Its guardians are only the God-fearing, but most of them do not know.﴾ [al-Anfal 8:34]

Therefore He said: ﴿Only those who believe in Allah and the Last Day maintain the mosques of Allah.﴾ So Allah the Exalted testified to the faith of those who maintain the mosques. As Imam Ahmad said:

Surayj narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from Amr ibn al-Harith, that Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you see a man frequenting the mosque, then bear witness to his faith." Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Only those who believe in Allah and the Last Day maintain the mosques of Allah.﴾

[al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak also narrated it from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Wahb, with this chain.] [Ahmad, Musnad (3/68); Tirmidhi, no. 3093; al-Mustadrak (2/332). Darraj from Abu al-Haytham is weak.]

Al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id (2/23) said: "In it is Salih al-Murri, who is weak."]

When al-Jarrah persisted, his son Abu 'Ubaydah went for him and killed him, and Allah revealed concerning him this verse: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾ and so on [al-Mujadilah: 22] [[Sunan al-Bayhaqi al-Kubra (9/27), through the chain of al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman from Asad ibn Musa from Dhamrah ibn Rabi'ah from Abdullah ibn Shawdhab. al-Bayhaqi said: "This is munqati' (disconnected)."]]

Then Allah commanded His Messenger to threaten those who prefer their family, relatives and kinsfolk over Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause. He said: (Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your kinsfolk, the wealth you have acquired, the commerce you fear will decline, and the dwellings you are pleased with are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His way) — that is, you have gained and acquired them — (and commerce whose slump you fear, and dwellings you are content with) — that is, you love them for their goodness and beauty; meaning, if these things are (dearer to you than Allah, His Messenger and striving in His way, then wait) — that is, await what will befall you of His punishment and retribution upon you. Therefore He said: (until Allah brings His command. And Allah does not guide the defiant people.)

Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Zuhrah ibn Ma'bad, from his grandfather, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was holding the hand of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. He said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, you are dearer to me than everything except my own self." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "None of you believes until I am dearer to him than his own self." 'Umar said: "Then by Allah, you are now dearer to me than my own self." The Messenger of Allah said: "Now, O 'Umar" [[Musnad (4/336).]]

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it, from Yahya ibn Sulayman, from Ibn Wahb, from Haywah ibn Shurayh, from Abu 'Uqayl Zuhrah ibn Ma'bad, that he heard his grandfather Abdullah ibn Hisham, from the Prophet ﷺ, with this [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6632).]]

It is also established in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, none of you believes until I am dearer to him than his father, his child, and all people" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (14) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud narrated — and the wording is his — from the hadith of Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Khurasani, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "When you engage in 'inah sales, take hold of the tails of cows, are content with agriculture, and abandon jihad, Allah will send down upon you a humiliation which He will not remove until you return to your religion" [[Musnad (2/42) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3462).]]

Imam Ahmad also narrated from Yazid ibn Harun, from Abu Janab, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, that he heard Abdullah ibn 'Amr from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ something similar [[Musnad (2/84).]] This is a supporting witness to the preceding, and Allah knows best.

Allah, exalted is He, commanded disassociation from the disbelievers because of Him, even if they were fathers or sons, and forbade allying with them when they (preferred) — that is, chose disbelief over faith — and He threatened for that, as He said: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their kinsfolk. Those — He has written within their hearts faith and strengthened them with a spirit from Him, and He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 22] and so on.

Al-Hafiz [Abu Bakr] al-Bayhaqi [[Addition from manuscripts T, K, A.]] narrated from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Shawdhab, who said: The father of Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah kept describing the gods to him on the day of Badr, and Abu 'Ubaydah kept turning away from him. Therefore He said: (until Allah brings His command. And Allah does not guide the defiant people.)

Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Zuhrah ibn Ma'bad, from his grandfather, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was holding the hand of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. (3462).]]
