Ibn Juraij said, on the authority of Mujahid: "This was the first verse revealed from [Surat] "Bara'ah" (al-Tawbah)."

He, exalted is He, reminds the believers of His favour upon them and His kindness toward them in His granting them victory in many battlegrounds of their campaigns alongside His Messenger (ﷺ), and that this came from Him, exalted is He, by His support and His decree, not by their number or their strength. He alerted them that victory comes from Him, whether the host is small or large. On the day of Hunayn, their great numbers pleased them, yet this availed them nothing: they turned back in retreat, except for a few of them who remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then Allah sent down His victory and support upon His Messenger and upon the believers who were with him, as we will explain in detail, if Allah wills, so that they might know that victory comes from Him alone, by His aid, even if the host is small. How many a small company has overcome a large company by the permission of Allah! And Allah is with the patient.

Imam Ahmad has said: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, my father narrated to us, I heard Yunus narrate from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best of companions are four, the best of detachments are four hundred, the best of armies are four thousand, and twelve thousand will never be defeated for lack of numbers."

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it in this way. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith. Only Jarir ibn Hazim has transmitted it with a connected chain, and it is related from al-Zuhri from the Prophet (ﷺ) as a mursal report."

Ibn Majah, al-Bayhaqi and others have also narrated it, from Akthum ibn al-Jawn, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in similar wording. And Allah knows best.

The battle of Hunayn took place after the conquest of Makkah, in Shawwal of the eighth year after the Hijrah. This was when he (peace be upon him) had finished with the conquest of Makkah, its affairs had been settled, most of its people had embraced Islam, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had released them. It reached him that Hawazin had gathered to fight him, and that their commander was Malik ibn Awf al-Nasri, with him all of Thaqif, the Banu Jusham, the Banu Sa'd ibn Bakr, scattered groups of the Banu Hilal (who were few), and some people of the Banu Amr ibn Amir and Awf ibn Amir. They had come with them their women, children, sheep and camels, and they came with all of their people. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to them with the army that had come with him for the conquest, which numbered ten thousand from the Muhajirun and the Ansar and the tribes of the Arabs, and with him also those from the people of Makkah who had embraced Islam, the Tulaqa', numbering two thousand as well. He marched with them toward the enemy, and they met in a valley between Makkah and al-Ta'if called "Hunayn." The battle took place at the beginning of the day, in the dimness of dawn. They descended into the valley, though Hawazin had lain in ambush there. When they came face to face, the Muslims were aware of nothing until they were upon them: they rushed at them, shot arrows, drew their swords, and charged as one man, as their king had commanded them. At that moment the Muslims turned back in retreat, as Allah, mighty and majestic, has said. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood firm, riding that day his white mule, driving it toward the heart of the enemy, while his uncle al-Abbas held the right stirrup and Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib held the left stirrup, restraining it so that it would not go too fast. He was calling out his own name, peace be upon him, and calling the Muslims to return, saying: "Where to, O servants of Allah? Come to me, I am the Messenger of Allah!" and he was saying at that moment:

"I am the Prophet, no lie,
I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib."

About a hundred of his companions remained with him, and some said eighty. Among them were Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, al-Abbas and Ali, al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas, Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith, Ayman ibn Umm Ayman, Usamah ibn Zayd, and others, may Allah be pleased with them all. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded his uncle al-Abbas, who had a loud voice, to call out at the top of his voice: "O companions of the tree!" (meaning the tree of the Pledge of Ridwan, under which the Muslims of the Muhajirun and the Ansar had pledged not to flee from him). So he began calling to them: "O companions of the acacia tree!" and at times he would say: "O companions of Surat al-Baqarah!" They began saying: "Labbayk, labbayk!" The people turned back and began returning to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so much so that if a man's camel would not obey him in turning back, he would put on his armour, leap down from it, let it go, and return on foot to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When a company of them gathered, he (peace be upon him) commanded them to charge truthfully. He took a handful of dust after he had supplicated his Lord and sought His help, and said: "O Allah, fulfil for me what You have promised me." Then he threw it at the people, and not one of them remained without some of it reaching his eyes and mouth, occupying him from fighting. Then they were routed, and the Muslims pursued them, killing and taking captives. The remaining people did not return except when the captives were lying bound before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Imam Ahmad has said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Yala ibn Ata informed us, from Abd Allah ibn Yasar Abi Hammam, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Fihri, whose name is Yazid ibn Usayd, and it is said: Yazid ibn Unays, and it is said: Kurz, who said: "I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the battle of Hunayn. We marched on a day of scorching, fierce heat, and we stopped beneath the shade of the trees. When the sun passed its zenith, I put on my armour and mounted my horse, and I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was in his tent. I said: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, and the mercy of Allah. Is it time for the ride?' He said: 'Yes.' Then he said: 'O Bilal!' and Bilal leapt from beneath an acacia tree, his shadow like the shadow of a bird, and said: 'Labbayka wa sa'daayka, and I am your ransom.' He said: 'Saddle my horse for me.' So he brought a saddle whose two sides were of palm fibre, with neither ostentation nor arrogance in them."

He said: "So he saddled it, and he mounted, and we mounted. We lined up against them that evening and through the night, and the two hosts clashed, and the Muslims turned back in retreat, as Allah, mighty and majestic, has said: (Then you turned back in retreat). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O servants of Allah, I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger!' Then he said: 'O assembly of the Muhajirun, I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger!' He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) leapt down from his horse, took a handful of dust, and the one who was nearest to him told me that he struck their faces with it and said: 'May the faces be disfigured!' And Allah, mighty and majestic, routed them. Yala ibn Ata said: their sons narrated to me from their fathers that they said: 'None of us remained without his eyes and mouth being filled with dust, and we heard a clanging between heaven and earth, like the dragging of iron across a new basin.'"

Al-Hafiz al-Bayhaqi narrated it in this way in "Dala'il al-Nubuwwah," from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah narrated to me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jabir, from his father Jabir, from Abd Allah, who said: Malik ibn Awf set out with those who were with him toward Hunayn, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived there before him. They prepared and readied themselves in the narrow passes of the valley and its sides. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions advanced until the valley brought them down in the dimness of dawn. When the people descended, the horses rushed upon them from the front and pressed hard upon them, and the people were routed and turned back, none turning to another. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) withdrew to the right, saying: "O people, come to me! I am the Messenger of Allah, I am the Messenger of Allah, I am Muhammad ibn Abd Allah!" But nothing came of it, and the camels crowded upon one another. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw the state of the people, he said: "O Abbas, cry out: O assembly of the Ansar, O companions of the acacia tree!" They answered him: "Labbayk, labbayk!" A man would try to turn his camel and could not, so he would throw his armour over his neck, take his sword and bow, and then head toward the voice, until a hundred of them had gathered to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The people then clashed and fought. The call had first been made to the Ansar, then it was raised to the Khazraj, and they were steadfast in battle. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rose up on his mount, looked at the body of the fighting men, and said: "Now the furnace has become hot!" He said: By Allah, the people did not return except when the captives were lying before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Allah slew whoever He slew of them, and whoever fled of them fled, and Allah gave His Messenger their wealth and their children as spoils.

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a man said to him: "O Abu Umarah, did you flee from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Hunayn?" He said: "But the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not flee. Hawazin were a people skilled in archery. When we met them and charged upon them, they were routed, and the people turned to the spoils, and they met us with arrows, so the people fled. I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith was holding the bridle of the Messenger of Allah's white mule, while he was saying:

"I am the Prophet, no lie,
I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib."

I say: This is at the very height of perfect courage: in such a day, in the thick of battle, when his army had been scattered from around him, he was still on a mule, which was not swift in running and was not suited to attack, retreat or flight, and yet he was driving it toward them and calling out his own name so that whoever did not know him would know him, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him always until the Day of Judgement. All of this was only trust in Allah, reliance upon Him, and knowledge on his part that He would grant him victory, complete what He sent him with, and make His religion prevail over all other religions. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, said: (Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger), that is, His reassurance and steadfastness upon His Messenger, (and upon the believers), that is, those who were with him, (and sent down hosts you did not see), and they are the angels, as Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir has said:

[Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying] [Addition from manuscripts T, A, and al-Tabari.] Al-Hasan ibn Arafa narrated to me, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to me, from Awf (he is Ibn Abi Jamila al-A'rabi), who said: I heard 'Abd al-Rahman, the client (mawla) of Ibn Burthun, say: a man who had been with the polytheists on the Day of Hunayn narrated to me, saying: When we met the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Day of Hunayn, they did not stand against us for the duration of a sheep's milking. He said: When we routed them, we began driving them before us in pursuit, until we reached the rider of the white mule, and behold, it was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: There, men with fair faces and handsome features met us and said to us: "May your faces be disgraced! Turn back!" He said: So we were routed, and they mounted upon our shoulders, and it was as they had described.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz informed us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Balawayh narrated to me, Ishaq ibn al-Hasan al-Harbi [in manuscript K: "al-Jurmi"] narrated to us, 'Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, al-Harith ibn Hasira narrated to us, al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from his father, who said: Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Day of Hunayn, when the people turned away from him, and I remained with him, along with eighty men from the Muhajirun and the Ansar. We advanced and did not turn our backs to them, and they were those upon whom Allah sent down tranquility. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on his mule, proceeding forward, when his mule swerved and he fell from the saddle. I said: "Rise up, may Allah raise you." He said: "Hand me a handful of dust." So I handed it to him, and he struck it into their faces, and their eyes were filled with dust. He said: "Where are the Muhajirun and the Ansar?" I said: "They are over there." He said: "Call out to them." So I called out to them, and they came with their swords in their right hands, as if they were shooting stars, and the polytheists turned their backs in flight.

Imam Ahmad also narrated it in his Musnad from 'Affan, with similar wording.

Al-Walid ibn Muslim said: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from Ikrima, the client of Ibn 'Abbas, from Shayba ibn 'Uthman, who said: When I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Day of Hunayn, he had been exposed, and I recalled my father and my uncle, and the killing of 'Ali and Hamza by them. I said: "Today I will take my revenge upon him." He said: So I went to approach him from his right, and behold, al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib was standing there, wearing a white coat of mail that looked like silver, its brightness shining through the dust. I said: "He is his uncle, and he will not abandon him." He said: Then I came to him from his left, and behold, Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib was there. I said: "He is his cousin, and he will not abandon him." So I came to him from behind, and I was about to lunge at him with the sword, when a flame of fire rose up between me and him, like lightning, and I feared that it would burn me. So I placed my hand over my eyes and walked backwards. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned and said: "O Shayba, O Shayba, come near to me. O Allah, remove Satan from him." He said: So I raised my eyes to him, and he was dearer to me than my hearing and my sight. Then he said: "O Shayba, fight the disbelievers."

Al-Bayhaqi narrated it from the hadith of al-Walid, and he mentioned it. Then he narrated from the hadith of Ayyub ibn Jabir, from Sadaqa ibn Sa'id, from Mus'ab ibn Shayba, from his father, who said: I went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Day of Hunayn. By Allah, Islam and knowledge of it did not bring me out, but I refused that Hawazin should prevail over Quraysh. I said, while standing with him: "O Messenger of Allah, I see white horses." He said: "O Shayba, none sees them except a disbeliever." Then he struck his hand upon my chest and said: "O Allah, guide Shayba." Then he struck it a second time and said: "O Allah, guide Shayba." Then he struck it a third time and said: "O Allah, guide Shayba." He said: By Allah, he did not lift his hand from my chest in the third strike until there was no one among Allah's creation more beloved to me than him. He mentioned the rest of the hadith, concerning the meeting of the people, the rout of the Muslims, the call of al-'Abbas, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seeking help, until Allah defeated the polytheists.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: My father Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated to me, from one who narrated to him, from Jubayr ibn Mut'im, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Day of Hunayn, and the people were fighting, I looked and saw something like a black cloth descending from the sky, until it fell between us and the enemy, and behold, it was scattered ants that had filled the valley. There was nothing but the defeat of the enemy, and we did not doubt that they were the angels.

Sa'id ibn al-Sa'ib ibn Yasar said, from his father, who said: I heard Yazid ibn 'Amir al-Suwa'i, who had witnessed Hunayn with the polytheists and then later embraced Islam (and we used to ask him about the terror that Allah cast into the hearts of the polytheists on the Day of Hunayn), and he would take a pebble and throw it into a basin, and it would ring, and he would say: "We used to find in our insides something like this."

A witness to this has already been mentioned from the hadith of Yazid ibn Abi Usayd, and Allah knows best.

In Sahih Muslim, from Muhammad ibn Rafi', from 'Abd al-Razzaq, who informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam, who said: This is what Abu Hurayra narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been given victory through terror, and I have been given concise and comprehensive speech." [Sahih Muslim, no. 523.]

And for this reason, He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down soldiers you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved. That is the recompense of the disbelievers.﴾ [In manuscripts K and A: "fa-anzal", which is an error.]

Ibn Juraij said, on the authority of Mujahid: "This was the first verse revealed from [Surat] "Bara'ah" (al-Tawbah)."

He alerted them that victory comes from Him, whether the host is small or large. On the day of Hunayn, their great numbers pleased them, yet this availed them nothing: they turned back in retreat, except for a few of them who remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then Allah sent down His victory and support upon His Messenger and upon the believers who were with him, as we will explain in detail, if Allah wills, so that they might know that victory comes from Him alone, by His aid, even if the host is small. How many a small company has overcome a large company by the permission of Allah! And Allah is with the patient.

Come to me, I am the Messenger of Allah!" and he was saying at that moment:

"I am the Prophet, no lie,
I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib."

About a hundred of his companions remained with him, and some said eighty. Among them were Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, al-Abbas and Ali, al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas, Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith, Ayman ibn Umm Ayman, Usamah ibn Zayd, and others, may Allah be pleased with them all. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded his uncle al-Abbas, who had a loud voice, to call out at the top of his voice: "O companions of the tree!" (meaning the tree of the Pledge of Ridwan, under which the Muslims of the Muhajirun and the Ansar had pledged not to flee from him). So he began calling to them: "O companions of the acacia tree!" and at times he would say: "O companions of Surat al-Baqarah!" They began saying: "Labbayk, labbayk!" The people turned back and began returning to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so much so that if a man's camel would not obey him in turning back, he would put on his armour, leap down from it, let it go, and return on foot to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When a company of them gathered, he (peace be upon him) commanded them to charge truthfully. He took a handful of dust after he had supplicated his Lord and sought His help, and said: "O Allah, fulfil for me what You have promised me." Then he threw it at the people, and not one of them remained without some of it reaching his eyes and mouth, occupying him from fighting. Then they were routed, and the Muslims pursued them, killing and taking captives. The remaining people did not return except when the captives were lying bound before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Imam Ahmad has said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Yala ibn Ata informed us, from Abd Allah ibn Yasar Abi Hammam, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Fihri, whose name is Yazid ibn Usayd, and it is said: Yazid ibn Unays, and it is said: Kurz, who said: "I was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the battle of Hunayn. We marched on a day of scorching, fierce heat, and we stopped beneath the shade of the trees. When the sun passed its zenith, I put on my armour and mounted my horse, and I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was in his tent. I said: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, and the mercy of Allah. Is it time for the ride?' He said: 'Yes.' Then he said: 'O Bilal!' and Bilal leapt from beneath an acacia tree, his shadow like the shadow of a bird, and said: 'Labbayka wa sa'daayka, and I am your ransom.' He said: 'Saddle my horse for me.' So he brought a saddle whose two sides were of palm fibre, with neither ostentation nor arrogance in them."

He said: "So he saddled it, and he mounted, and we mounted. We lined up against them that evening and through the night, and the two hosts clashed, and the Muslims turned back in retreat, as Allah, mighty and majestic, has said: (Then you turned back in retreat). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O servants of Allah, I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger!' Then he said: 'O assembly of the Muhajirun, I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger!' He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) leapt down from his horse, took a handful of dust, and the one who was nearest to him told me that he struck their faces with it and said: 'May the faces be disfigured!' And Allah, mighty and majestic, routed them. Yala ibn Ata said: their sons narrated to me from their fathers that they said: 'None of us remained without his eyes and mouth being filled with dust, and we heard a clanging between heaven and earth, like the dragging of iron across a new basin.'"

Al-Hafiz al-Bayhaqi narrated it in this way in "Dala'il al-Nubuwwah," from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah narrated to me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jabir, from his father Jabir, from Abd Allah, who said: Malik ibn Awf set out with those who were with him toward Hunayn, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived there before him. They prepared and readied themselves in the narrow passes of the valley and its sides. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions advanced until the valley brought them down in the dimness of dawn. When the people descended, the horses rushed upon them from the front and pressed hard upon them, and the people were routed and turned back, none turning to another. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) withdrew to the right, saying: "O people, come to me! I am the Messenger of Allah, I am the Messenger of Allah, I am Muhammad ibn Abd Allah!" But nothing came of it, and the camels crowded upon one another. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw the state of the people, he said: "O Abbas, cry out: O assembly of the Ansar, O companions of the acacia tree!" They answered him: "Labbayk, labbayk!" A man would try to turn his camel and could not, so he would throw his armour over his neck, take his sword and bow, and then head toward the voice, until a hundred of them had gathered to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The people then clashed and fought. The call had first been made to the Ansar, then it was raised to the Khazraj, and they were steadfast in battle. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rose up on his mount, looked at the body of the fighting men, and said: "Now the furnace has become hot!" He said: By Allah, the people did not return except when the captives were lying before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Allah slew whoever He slew of them, and whoever fled of them fled, and Allah gave His Messenger their wealth and their children as spoils.

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a man said to him: "O Abu Umarah, did you flee from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Hunayn?" He said: "But the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not flee. Hawazin were a people skilled in archery. When we met them and charged upon them, they were routed, and the people turned to the spoils, and they met us with arrows, so the people fled. I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith was holding the bridle of the Messenger of Allah's white mule, while he was saying:

"I am the Prophet, no lie,
I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib."

I say: This is at the very height of perfect courage: in such a day, in the thick of battle, when his army had been scattered from around him, he was still on a mule, which was not swift in running and was not suited to attack, retreat or flight, and yet he was driving it toward them and calling out his own name so that whoever did not know him would know him, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him always until the Day of Judgement. All of this was only trust in Allah, reliance upon Him, and knowledge on his part that He would grant him victory, complete what He sent him with, and make His religion prevail over all other religions. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, said: (Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger), that is, His reassurance and steadfastness upon His Messenger, (and upon the believers), that is, those who were with him, (and sent down hosts you did not see), and they are the angels, as Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir has said:

[Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying] [Addition from manuscripts T, A, and al-Tabari.] Al-Hasan ibn Arafa narrated to me, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to me, from Awf (he is Ibn Abi Jamila al-A'rabi), who said: I heard 'Abd al-Rahman, the client (mawla) of Ibn Burthun, say: a man who had been with the polytheists on the Day of Hunayn narrated to me, saying: When we met the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Day of Hunayn, they did not stand against us for the duration of a sheep's milking. He said: When we routed them, we began driving them before us in pursuit, until we reached the rider of the white mule, and behold, it was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: There, men with fair faces and handsome features met us and said to us: "May your faces be disgraced! Turn back!" He said: So we were routed, and they mounted upon our shoulders, and it was as they had described.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz informed us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Balawayh narrated to me, Ishaq ibn al-Hasan al-Harbi [in manuscript K: "al-Jurmi"] narrated to us, 'Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, al-Harith ibn Hasira narrated to us, al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from his father, who said: Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Day of Hunayn, when the people turned away from him, and I remained with him, along with eighty men from the Muhajirun and the Ansar. We advanced and did not turn our backs to them, and they were those upon whom Allah sent down tranquility. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on his mule, proceeding forward, when his mule swerved and he fell from the saddle. I said: "Rise up, may Allah raise you." He said: "Hand me a handful of dust." So I handed it to him, and he struck it into their faces, and their eyes were filled with dust. He said: "Where are the Muhajirun and the Ansar?" I said: "They are over there." He said: "Call out to them." So I called out to them, and they came with their swords in their right hands, as if they were shooting stars, and the polytheists turned their backs in flight.

Imam Ahmad also narrated it in his Musnad from 'Affan, with similar wording.

Al-Walid ibn Muslim said: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from Ikrima, the client of Ibn 'Abbas, from Shayba ibn 'Uthman, who said: When I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Day of Hunayn, he had been exposed, and I recalled my father and my uncle, and the killing of 'Ali and Hamza by them. I said: "Today I will take my revenge upon him." He said: So I went to approach him from his right, and behold, al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib was standing there, wearing a white coat of mail that looked like silver, its brightness shining through the dust. I said: "He is his uncle, and he will not abandon him." He said: Then I came to him from his left, and behold, Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib was there. I said: "He is his cousin, and he will not abandon him." So I came to him from behind, and I was about to lunge at him with the sword, when a flame of fire rose up between me and him, like lightning, and I feared that it would burn me. So I placed my hand over my eyes and walked backwards. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned and said: "O Shayba, O Shayba, come near to me. O Allah, remove Satan from him." He said: So I raised my eyes to him, and he was dearer to me than my hearing and my sight. Then he said: "O Shayba, fight the disbelievers."

Al-Bayhaqi narrated it from the hadith of al-Walid, and he mentioned it. Then he narrated from the hadith of Ayyub ibn Jabir, from Sadaqa ibn Sa'id, from Mus'ab ibn Shayba, from his father, who said: I went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Day of Hunayn. By Allah, Islam and knowledge of it did not bring me out, but I refused that Hawazin should prevail over Quraysh. I said, while standing with him: "O Messenger of Allah, I see white horses." He said: "O Shayba, none sees them except a disbeliever." Then he struck his hand upon my chest and said: "O Allah, guide Shayba." Then he struck it a second time and said: "O Allah, guide Shayba." Then he struck it a third time and said: "O Allah, guide Shayba." He said: By Allah, he did not lift his hand from my chest in the third strike until there was no one among Allah's creation more beloved to me than him. He mentioned the rest of the hadith, concerning the meeting of the people, the rout of the Muslims, the call of al-'Abbas, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seeking help, until Allah defeated the polytheists.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: My father Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated to me, from one who narrated to him, from Jubayr ibn Mut'im, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the Day of Hunayn, and the people were fighting, I looked and saw something like a black cloth descending from the sky, until it fell between us and the enemy, and behold, it was scattered ants that had filled the valley. There was nothing but the defeat of the enemy, and we did not doubt that they were the angels.

Sa'id ibn al-Sa'ib ibn Yasar said, from his father, who said: I heard Yazid ibn 'Amir al-Suwa'i, who had witnessed Hunayn with the polytheists and then later embraced Islam (and we used to ask him about the terror that Allah cast into the hearts of the polytheists on the Day of Hunayn), and he would take a pebble and throw it into a basin, and it would ring, and he would say: "We used to find in our insides something like this."

A witness to this has already been mentioned from the hadith of Yazid ibn Abi Usayd, and Allah knows best.

In Sahih Muslim, from Muhammad ibn Rafi', from 'Abd al-Razzaq, who informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam, who said: This is what Abu Hurayra narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been given victory through terror, and I have been given concise and comprehensive speech." [Sahih Muslim, no. 523.]

And for this reason, He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down soldiers you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved. That is the recompense of the disbelievers.﴾ [In manuscripts K and A: "fa-anzal", which is an error.]

Ibn Juraij said, from Mujahid: "This is the first verse to be revealed from [Surah] Bara'ah (At-Tawbah)."

He, exalted is He, reminds the believers of His favour upon them and His kindness towards them in granting them victory in many battlefields of their campaigns alongside His Messenger, and that this comes from Him, exalted is He, by His support and His decree, not by their number nor by their strength. He alerts them that victory is from Him, whether the host is small or large. On the Day of Hunayn, their great number pleased them, yet it availed them nothing, and they turned back in retreat, except for a few of them who stayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then Allah sent down His victory and His support upon His Messenger and upon the believers who were with him, as we will explain in detail, Allah willing, so that they would know that victory is from Him alone, by His aid, even if the host is small. How many a small company has overcome a large company by Allah's leave! And Allah is with the patient.

Imam Ahmad said: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, my father narrated to us, I heard Yunus narrate from al-Zuhri, from Ubaydullah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The best of companions are four, the best of detachments are four hundred, the best of armies are four thousand, and twelve thousand will never be defeated through lack of numbers."

Thus it was also narrated by Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi, and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith. None transmits it with a chain except Jarir ibn Hazim, and it is only narrated from al-Zuhri, from the Prophet ﷺ, as a mursal (report)."

Ibn Majah, al-Bayhaqi and others also narrated it, from Aktham ibn al-Jawn, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in similar wording. And Allah knows best.

The Battle of Hunayn took place after the Conquest of Makkah, in Shawwal of the eighth year after the Hijrah. This was when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished with the conquest of Makkah, its affairs had been settled, most of its people had embraced Islam, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had released them. Then news reached him that Hawazin had gathered to fight him, and that their commander was Malik ibn Awf al-Nasri, with him the whole of Thaqif, Banu Jusham, Banu Sa'd ibn Bakr, groups from Banu Hilal (and they were few), and some people from Banu Amr ibn Amir and Awf ibn Amir. They had come with their women, children, sheep and camels, having arrived in full force, all of them together. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to them with the army that had come with him for the Conquest, which numbered ten thousand from the Muhajirun, the Ansar and the Arab tribes, along with those from the people of Makkah who had embraced Islam, the Tulaqa', who were also two thousand. He led them towards the enemy, and they met at a valley between Makkah and al-Ta'if called "Hunayn." The battle took place at the beginning of the day, in the dimness of dawn. They descended into the valley while Hawazin had lain in ambush in it. When they came face to face, the Muslims had no warning except that they were upon them: they attacked them, shot arrows, drew swords, and charged like one man, as their king had ordered. At that, the Muslims turned back in retreat, as Allah, exalted is He, said. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained firm; he was riding his white mule that day, driving it towards the enemy's front, while his uncle al-Abbas held the right stirrup and Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib held the left stirrup, restraining it so that it would not hasten. He ﷺ was calling out his name, and calling the Muslims to return, saying: "Where are you, O servants of Allah? Come to me! I am the Messenger of Allah." And he would say at that moment:

I am the Prophet, no lie,
I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib.

Nearly a hundred of his companions remained with him, and some said eighty. Among them were Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, al-Abbas and Ali, al-Fadl ibn Abbas, Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith, Ayman ibn Umm Ayman, Usamah ibn Zayd, and others, may Allah be pleased with them all. Then the Prophet ﷺ commanded his uncle al-Abbas, who had a loud voice, to call out at the top of his voice: "O companions of the tree!" — meaning the tree of the Pledge of Ridwan, under which the Muslims, Muhajirun and Ansar, had pledged allegiance to him not to flee from him. He began calling to them: "O companions of the acacia tree!" and at times saying: "O companions of Surat al-Baqarah!" They began to say: "Here we are, here we are!" and the people turned back and returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to the extent that if a man could not get his camel to turn around, he would put on his armour, dismount from it, release it, and return on foot to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When a group of them had gathered, the Prophet ﷺ ordered them to make a true charge. He took a handful of dust after supplicating to his Lord and seeking His help, and said: "O Allah, fulfil for me what You have promised me." Then he threw it at the people, and not a single person among them remained without being struck in his eyes and mouth by it, which occupied him from fighting. Then they were routed, and the Muslims pursued their backs, killing and taking captives, and the rest of the people did not regroup until the captives were bound before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Yala ibn Ata informed us, from Abdullah ibn Yasar Abu Hammam, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Fihri, whose name is Yazid ibn Usayd, and it is said: Yazid ibn Unays, and it is said: Kurz. He said: "I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the campaign of Hunayn. We marched on a day scorching and intensely hot, so we halted under the shade of the trees. When the sun had passed its zenith, I put on my armour and mounted my horse, and I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in his tent. I said: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah, and the mercy of Allah. Is it time for the departure?' He said: 'Yes.' Then he said: 'O Bilal!' So Bilal sprang from beneath an acacia tree, as if his shadow were the shadow of a bird, and said: 'At your service, I answer you, and I am your ransom.' He said: 'Saddle my horse for me.' So he brought a saddle whose two sides were of palm fibre, having neither ostentation nor insolence in them."

He said: So he saddled it, and the Prophet mounted, and we mounted. We lined up against them that evening and through the night, and the two cavalries clashed, and the Muslims turned back in retreat, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then you turned back in retreat﴾. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O servants of Allah, I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger." Then he said: "O company of the Muhajirun, I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger." He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ leapt down from his horse, took a handful of dust, and the one who was nearest to him told me that he struck their faces with it and said: "May the faces be disfigured." So Allah, exalted is He, routed them. Yala ibn Ata said: their sons narrated to me from their fathers that they said: "None of us remained without his eyes and mouth being filled with dust, and we heard a clanging between the sky and the earth, like the scraping of iron on a new basin."

Thus it was also narrated by the hafiz al-Bayhaqi in "Dala'il al-Nubuwwah," from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah narrated to me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jabir, from his father Jabir, from Abdullah, who said: Malik ibn Awf went out with those who were with him to Hunayn, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached it before him. They prepared and readied themselves in the narrow passes of the valley and its bends. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions advanced until the valley brought them down in the haze of dawn. When the people had descended, the horses charged into their faces, pressing hard upon them, and the people fell back in rout, none turning back for another. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ moved to the right, saying: "O people, come to me! I am the Messenger of Allah, I am the Messenger of Allah, I am Muhammad ibn Abdullah." But nothing happened, and the camels crowded against one another. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw the people's state, he said: "O Abbas, call out: O company of the Ansar, O companions of the acacia tree!" They answered: "Here we are, here we are!" A man would try to turn his camel but could not, so he would throw his armour around his neck, take his sword and bow, and then head towards the voice, until a hundred of them had gathered to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The people then encountered one another and fought. The call had first been directed at the Ansar, then was later directed at the Khazraj, and they were steadfast in war. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose up on his mounts and looked at the mass of the people, and said: "Now the furnace has heated up." He said: By Allah, the people did not return except while the captives were gathered before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Allah killed those among them who were killed, some of them fled, and Allah granted His Messenger their wealth and their sons as booty.

In the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, may Allah be pleased with both of them, that a man said to him: "O Abu Umarah, did you flee from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Hunayn?" He said: "But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not flee. Hawazin were a people skilled in archery. When we met them and charged upon them, they were routed. The people turned to the spoils, and they received us with arrows, so the people fled. I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith was holding the bridle of the Messenger of Allah's white mule, while he was saying:

I am the Prophet, no lie,
I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib."

I say: This is in the utmost degree of complete courage: that in such a day, in the thick of battle, when his army had been scattered from him, he was nonetheless on a mule that was not swift in running, and not suited to charging, to flight, or to escape. Yet even so, he drove it towards their faces and called out his name so that whoever did not know him would know him, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him always until the Day of Recompense. All of this was only out of trust in Allah, reliance upon Him, and knowledge that He would help him, complete what He had sent him with, and make His religion prevail over all other religions. For this reason, Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger﴾, i.e., His calm and steadfastness upon His Messenger, ﴿and upon the believers﴾, i.e., those who were with him, ﴿and sent down hosts you did not see﴾, and they were the angels, as Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said:

[He said:] Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Arafa narrated to me, saying: Al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to me, from Awf — that is Ibn Abi Jamila al-A'rabi — who said: I heard Abd al-Rahman, the client of Ibn Burthun, say: a man who had been with the polytheists on the day of Hunayn narrated to me, saying: When we met, we and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Hunayn, [the polytheists] did not stand against us for the time it takes to milk a goat. He said: When we routed them, we began driving them before us, until we reached the one on the white mule, and behold, it was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: Men with white faces and fine features met us there, and they said to us: "May the faces be disfigured! Turn back!" He said: So we were routed, and they rode upon our shoulders, and it was as they had said.

And al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abd Allah al-Hafiz informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Balawayh narrated to me, saying: Ishaq ibn al-Hasan al-Harbi narrated to us, saying: Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: al-Harith ibn Hasira narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from his father, who said: Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Hunayn, when the people turned away from him, and I remained with him along with eighty men from the Muhajirun and the Ansar. We advanced and did not turn our backs to them, and they were the ones upon whom Allah sent down tranquility. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was on his mule, moving forward, when his mule swerved and he leaned away from the saddle. I said: "Rise up, may Allah raise you." He said: "Pass me a handful of dust." So I passed it to him, and he struck it against their faces, and their eyes were filled with dust. He said: "Where are the Muhajirun and the Ansar?" I said: "They are over there." He said: "Call out to them." So I called out to them, and they came with their swords in their right hands, as if they were shooting stars, and the polytheists turned their backs in flight.

Imam Ahmad also narrated it in his Musnad from Affan, with similar wording.

And al-Walid ibn Muslim said: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to me, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from Ikrima, client of Ibn Abbas, from Shayba ibn Uthman, who said: When I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Hunayn, he had been struck with dust. I remembered my father and my uncle, and the killing of Ali and Hamza by them, and I said: "Today I will avenge my vengeance upon him." He said: So I went to approach him from his right, and behold, al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib was standing there, wearing a white coat of mail that looked like silver, from which the dust was being brushed. I said: "He is his paternal uncle, and he will not abandon him." He said: So I came to him from his left, and behold, Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib was there. I said: "He is his cousin, and he will not abandon him." So I came to him from behind, and I was about to lunge at him with the sword, when a flame of fire rose up between me and him, like lightning, and I feared it would burn me. So I put my hand over my eyes and walked backwards. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned and said: "O Shayba, O Shayba, come near to me. O Allah, remove Satan from him." He said: So I raised my eyes to him, and he was dearer to me than my hearing and my sight. Then he said: "O Shayba, fight the disbelievers."

Al-Bayhaqi narrated it from the hadith of al-Walid, and then he related from the hadith of Ayyub ibn Jabir, from Sadaqa ibn Sa'id, from Mus'ab ibn Shayba, from his father, who said: I went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Hunayn. By Allah, Islam had not driven me out, nor any knowledge of it, but I refused that Hawazin should prevail over Quraysh. I said while standing with him: "O Messenger of Allah, I see white horses." He said: "O Shayba, none sees them except a disbeliever." Then he struck his hand against my chest and said: "O Allah, guide Shayba." Then he struck it a second time, and said: "O Allah, guide Shayba," then he struck it a third time, and said: "O Allah, guide Shayba." He said: By Allah, he did not lift his hand from my chest at the third time until there was no one among Allah's creation more beloved to me than him. He mentioned the rest of the hadith, concerning the meeting of the people, the rout of the Muslims, the call of al-Abbas, and the seeking of help by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, until Allah defeated the polytheists.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: My father Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated to me, from one who narrated to him, from Jubayr ibn Mut'im, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We were truly with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Hunayn, and the people were fighting, when I looked and saw something like a black cloth falling from the sky, until it landed between us and the enemy, and behold, it was a scattering of ants that filled the valley. There was nothing but the rout of the enemy, and we did not doubt that they were the angels.

Sa'id ibn al-Sa'ib ibn Yasar said, from his father: I heard Yazid ibn Amir al-Suwa'i — and he had witnessed Hunayn with the polytheists and then embraced Islam afterward — and we used to ask him about the terror that Allah cast into the hearts of the polytheists on the day of Hunayn. He would take a pebble and throw it into a basin, and it would ring, and then he would say: "We used to find in our insides something like this."

A supporting report has already preceded from the hadith of Yazid ibn Abi Usayd, and Allah knows best.

In Sahih Muslim, from Muhammad ibn Rafi, from Abd al-Razzaq, who informed us, from Ma'mar, from Hammam, who said: This is what Abu Hurayra narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been aided with terror, and I have been given concise and comprehensive speech." [Sahih Muslim, no. 523.]

For this reason, He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down soldiers you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved. That is the recompense of the disbelievers.﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then Allah will relent after that to whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: Allah relented toward the remnant of Hawazin, and they embraced Islam and came to him as Muslims, and they joined him when he had approached Mecca at al-Ji'ranah, about twenty days after the battle. At that point he gave them the choice between their captives and their wealth, and they chose their captives, who numbered six thousand, between children and women. So he returned them to them, and divided their wealth among the warriors. He also gave bounties to some of the Tulaqa' in order to win their hearts to Islam, giving them one hundred camels each. Among those who were given one hundred was Malik ibn Awf al-Nasri, and he was put in charge of his people as before. He praised him in his poem, in which he says:

Never have I seen or heard of one like him among all the people, like Muhammad.
He fulfilled and gave generously when he was asked, and if you wish, he will tell you of what is to come.
And when the battalion bares its fangs with spears and every sharp blade,
He is like a lion over his cubs, resting in ambush in the thicket.

Almighty Allah commanded His believing servants, who are pure in religion and in their persons, to expel the polytheists, who are impure in religion, from the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram), and not to approach it after the revelation of this verse. This verse was revealed in the ninth year (of the Hijrah). For this reason, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent 'Ali, together with Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with them both) that year, and instructed him to proclaim among the polytheists: "No polytheist may perform Hajj after this year, and no one may circumambulate the House naked." Allah then completed this, and decreed it both legally and by destiny.

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah say concerning the words of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are impure, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this year of theirs﴾, "except for a slave, or one of the people of protection (ahl al-dhimmah)."

It has also been related as a marfu' report (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) through another route. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn narrated to us, Shurayk narrated to us, from al-Ash'ath (i.e., Ibn Sawwar), from al-Hasan, from Jabir, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "No polytheist shall enter our mosque after this year of ours, except the people of the covenant and their servants." Ahmad alone related it as marfu', and the mawquf (stopping at the companion) version is sounder in its chain. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/10): "In it is Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, who is weak but has been deemed trustworthy."

Imam Abu Amr al-Awza'i said: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote: "Prevent the Jews and Christians from entering the mosques of the Muslims," and he followed his prohibition with the words of Allah: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are impure﴾.

Ata' said: The entire Haram is a mosque, based on the words of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿So let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this year of theirs﴾.

This noble verse indicates the impurity of the polytheist, just as it indicates the purity of the believer. And in the authentic hadith it is reported: "The believer does not become impure" (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 283, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, with the wording: "Indeed the Muslim does not become impure"). As for the bodily impurity of the People of the Book, the majority hold that they are not physically or essentially impure, because Allah made lawful the food of the People of the Book. Some of the Zahiris (adherents of the literalist school, al-Zahiriyyah) held that their bodies are impure.

Ash'ath related from al-Hasan: "Whoever shakes hands with them should perform wudu'." Ibn Jarir narrated it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills﴾. Ibn Ishaq said: This is because the people said: "The markets will be cut off from us, trade will perish, and the profits we used to gain from them will be lost." So the verse was revealed from another angle: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills﴾, up to His words: ﴿while they are humbled﴾. That is: this is the compensation for what you feared of the cutting off of those markets; Allah compensated them for what He cut off from them of the matter of polytheism by what He gave them of the necks of the People of the Book, in the form of the jizyah.

This is likewise narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and others.

﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing﴾, that is, of what benefits you; ﴿All-Wise﴾, that is, in what He commands and prohibits, because He is perfect in His actions and words, just in His creation and command, blessed and exalted is He. For this reason He compensated them for those gains with the wealth of the jizyah which they take from the people of protection. He said: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day, and do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture, until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled﴾. In reality, when they disbelieved in Muhammad ﷺ, they no longer had sound faith in any of the Messengers or in what they brought. They only follow their opinions, their desires and their fathers in what they are upon, not because it is the Law of Allah and His religion. For if they had truly believed in what is in their hands with sound faith, that would have led them to faith in Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, because all the Prophets gave glad tidings of him and commanded following him. When he came and they disbelieved in him, though he is the most noble of the Messengers, it became known that they are not adhering to the law of the earlier Prophets as being from Allah, but rather for their own shares and desires. For this reason their faith in the rest of the Prophets does not benefit them, since they have disbelieved in their master, the best of them, their seal and most perfect. For this reason He said: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day, and do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture﴾. This noble verse was revealed at the beginning of the command to fight the People of the Book, after the affairs of the polytheists had been settled and people had entered the religion of Allah in multitudes. When the Arabian Peninsula was firmly established, Allah and His Messenger commanded fighting the two groups of the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, and this was in the ninth year. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prepared for battle against the Romans, called the people to it, made it known to them, and sent to the Arab tribes around Madinah, summoning them, and they came out with him fully. About thirty thousand fighters gathered, and some of the people of Madinah and those around it, hypocrites and others, stayed behind. That was in a year of drought and in a time of intense summer heat. He, peace be upon him, set out intending al-Sham to fight the Romans, and reached Tabuk. He stopped there and remained near its water for about twenty days, then sought Allah's guidance (istikharah) about returning, and he returned that same year because of the hardship of the situation and the weakness of the people, as its explanation will come later, if Allah wills.

Those who hold that the jizyah is taken only from the People of the Book, or from their likes such as the Magians (al-Majus), have used this noble verse as evidence, since an authentic hadith states that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took it from the Magians of Hajar. This is the position of al-Shafi'i and of Ahmad according to the well-known report from him. Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Rather, it is taken from all non-Arabs, whether they are People of the Book or polytheists, and it is not taken from Arabs except from the People of the Book.

Imam Malik said: Rather, it is permissible to impose the jizyah on all disbelievers, whether People of the Book, Magians, idolaters, or others. The place for discussing the foundations of these positions and their evidences is elsewhere than this, and Allah knows best.

* *

As for His words: ﴿until they give the jizyah﴾, that is, if they do not embrace Islam; ﴿willingly﴾ (ʿan yadin), that is, under compulsion and subjugation; ﴿while they are humbled﴾, that is, debased, belittled, and disgraced. For this reason it is not permissible to honor the people of protection or to elevate them over the Muslims; rather, they are to be humbled, diminished, and wretched, as came in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Do not initiate greeting the Jews and Christians with salam, and when you meet one of them on a road, force him to its narrowest part."

For this reason the Commander of the Faithful Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, imposed upon them those well-known conditions for their humiliation, diminishment, and belittling. This was related by the great memorizers of hadith from the narration of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm al-Ash'ari, who said: I wrote for Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, when he made peace with the Christians of al-Sham:

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. This is a letter to the servant of Allah, Umar, Commander of the Faithful, from the Christians of such-and-such city. When you came to us, we asked you for security for ourselves, our offspring, our wealth, and the people of our religion, and we stipulated for you against ourselves that we will not build in our city or in what surrounds it a monastery, church, hermitage, or monk's cell, nor will we repair what has fallen into ruin from them, nor revive any of them that lie within the lands of the Muslims. We will not prevent our churches from being used by any Muslim, by night or by day, and we will widen their doors for passersby and travelers, and whoever of the Muslims passes by us may stay in them for three days, and we will feed them. We will not shelter in our churches or our homes a spy, nor conceal any deceit against the Muslims, nor teach our children the Qur'an, nor openly display polytheism, nor invite anyone to it. We will not prevent any of our relatives from entering Islam if they wish it. We will show respect to the Muslims, and we will rise for them from our gatherings if they wish to sit. We will not imitate them in any of their clothing: in a qalansuwah, a turban, sandals, or the parting of hair. We will not speak in their manner, nor take their kunyas. We will not ride saddles, nor gird on swords, nor take or carry any weapons. We will not engrave our seals in Arabic. We will not sell wine. We will trim the fronts of our heads, and we will keep to our distinctive dress wherever we are, and we will tie the zunnar (girdle) around our waists. We will not display the cross on our churches, nor display our crosses or our books in any of the roads or markets of the Muslims. We will not strike our nawaqis (bells) in our churches except softly. We will not raise our voices in recitation in our churches in the presence of Muslims. We will not carry out the Shaʿanin or the Baʿuth processions, nor raise our voices with our dead, nor display fires with them in any of the roads or markets of the Muslims, nor bring our dead close to them. We will not acquire any slaves over whom the arrows of the Muslims have passed, and we will guide the Muslims, and we will not spy on them in their homes.

He said: When I brought the letter to Umar, he added: "And we will not strike any Muslim. We have stipulated this for you against ourselves and the people of our religion, and in return we have accepted security. If we oppose you in anything of what we have stipulated for you and have imposed upon ourselves, then we have no protection (dhimmah), and it becomes lawful for you to treat us as one treats the people of hostility and defiance."

This is an incitement from God Most High to the believers to fight the disbelieving polytheists among the Jews and Christians, because of their repugnant statement and their slander against God Most High. As for the Jews, they said concerning 'Uzayr (Ezra), "He is the son of God." Exalted is God far above that, to a great degree.

Al-Suddi and others mentioned that the confusion which arose for them in this matter was that when the Amalekites prevailed over the Children of Israel, killing their scholars and taking their nobles captive, 'Uzayr remained weeping for the Children of Israel and for the disappearance of knowledge from among them, until the lids of his eyes fell off. Then one day he passed by a graveyard, and there was a woman weeping at a grave, saying: "O my feeder! O my clother!" He said to her: "Woe to you! Who used to feed you before this?" She said: "God." He said: "Indeed God is living and does not die!" She said: "O 'Uzayr, then who used to teach the scholars before the Children of Israel?" He said: "God." She said: "Then why do you weep over them?" He realized that he had been admonished by something. Then it was said to him: "Go to such-and-such river, bathe in it, and pray two rak'ahs there, for you will meet there an old man. Whatever he feeds you, eat it." He went and did what he was commanded. There was an old man, and he said to him: "Open your mouth." He opened his mouth, and the old man cast into it something like a great burning ember, three times. 'Uzayr returned, and he was among the most knowledgeable of people in the Torah. He said: "O Children of Israel, I have come to you with the Torah." They said: "O 'Uzayr, you were not a liar." So he took a pen, tied it to one of his fingers, and wrote the Torah with all his finger. When the people returned from their enemy and the scholars came back, and they were informed about the matter of 'Uzayr, they brought out the copies which they had deposited in the mountains, and compared them with it, and found that what he had brought was correct. Then some of their ignorant ones said: "He only did this because he is the son of God."

As for the misguidance of the Christians concerning the Messiah, it is evident. For this reason God, glorified is He, refuted both groups, saying: ﴿That is their saying with their mouths﴾, meaning they have no basis for what they claim except their fabrication and invention. ﴿They imitate﴾, meaning they resemble ﴿the saying of those who disbelieved before them﴾, meaning the nations before them, who went astray as these have gone astray. ﴿May God destroy them﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: May God curse them. ﴿How are they deluded?﴾ meaning: how do they stray from the truth, which is evident, and turn toward falsehood?

﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God, and the Messiah, son of Mary﴾. Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir related through several chains, from 'Adi ibn Hatim, may God be pleased with him, that when the call of the Messenger of God ﷺ reached him, he fled to Syria, and he had become a Christian in the Jahiliyyah. His sister and a group of his people were taken captive, then the Messenger of God ﷺ showed favour to his sister and gave her gifts, so she returned to her brother and encouraged him to embrace Islam and to come to the Messenger of God ﷺ. 'Adi came to Medina, and he was a chief among his people, Tayy, and his father was Hatim al-Ta'i, famous for generosity. People talked about his arrival, so he entered upon the Messenger of God ﷺ while there was a silver cross around 'Adi's neck. The Messenger of God ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾. He said: I said: "They did not worship them." He said: "Yes, indeed, they forbade them the lawful and made lawful for them the unlawful, and they followed them; that is their worship of them." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "O 'Adi, what do you say? Does it please you that it be said, 'God is greatest'? Do you know of anything greater than God? What is it that troubles you? Does it please you that it be said, 'There is no god but God'? Do you know of any god besides God?" Then he invited him to Islam, and he embraced it and bore witness to the truth. He said: "I saw his face light up with joy," and then he said: "Indeed the Jews are those who have earned anger, and the Christians are those who have gone astray." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3095) and Tafsir al-Tabari (14/209-211) through the chain of 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb from Ghutayf ibn A'yan from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd from 'Adi ibn Hatim, may God be pleased with him. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the hadith of 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb, and Ghutayf ibn A'yan is not well known in hadith."]

Al-Suddi said: they sought counsel from men and cast the Book of God behind their backs.

This is an incitement from God Most High to the believers to fight the disbelieving polytheists among the Jews and Christians, because of their repugnant statement and their slander against God Most High. As for the Jews, they said concerning 'Uzayr (Ezra), "He is the son of God." Exalted is God far above that, to a great degree.

Al-Suddi and others mentioned that the confusion which arose for them in this matter was that when the Amalekites prevailed over the Children of Israel, killing their scholars and taking their nobles captive, 'Uzayr remained weeping for the Children of Israel and for the disappearance of knowledge from among them, until the lids of his eyes fell off. Then one day he passed by a graveyard, and there was a woman weeping at a grave, saying: "O my feeder! O my clother!" He said to her: "Woe to you! Who used to feed you before this?" She said: "God." He said: "Indeed God is living and does not die!" She said: "O 'Uzayr, then who used to teach the scholars before the Children of Israel?" He said: "God." She said: "Then why do you weep over them?" He realized that he had been admonished by something. Then it was said to him: "Go to such-and-such river, bathe in it, and pray two rak'ahs there, for you will meet there an old man. Whatever he feeds you, eat it." He went and did what he was commanded. There was an old man, and he said to him: "Open your mouth." He opened his mouth, and the old man cast into it something like a great burning ember, three times. 'Uzayr returned, and he was among the most knowledgeable of people in the Torah. He said: "O Children of Israel, I have come to you with the Torah." They said: "O 'Uzayr, you were not a liar." So he took a pen, tied it to one of his fingers, and wrote the Torah with all his finger. When the people returned from their enemy and the scholars came back, and they were informed about the matter of 'Uzayr, they brought out the copies which they had deposited in the mountains, and compared them with it, and found that what he had brought was correct. Then some of their ignorant ones said: "He only did this because he is the son of God."

As for the misguidance of the Christians concerning the Messiah, it is evident. For this reason God, glorified is He, refuted both groups, saying: ﴿That is their saying with their mouths﴾, meaning they have no basis for what they claim except their fabrication and invention. ﴿They imitate﴾, meaning they resemble ﴿the saying of those who disbelieved before them﴾, meaning the nations before them, who went astray as these have gone astray. ﴿May God destroy them﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: May God curse them. ﴿How are they deluded?﴾ meaning: how do they stray from the truth, which is evident, and turn toward falsehood?

﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God, and the Messiah, son of Mary﴾. Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir related through several chains, from 'Adi ibn Hatim, may God be pleased with him, that when the call of the Messenger of God ﷺ reached him, he fled to Syria, and he had become a Christian in the Jahiliyyah. His sister and a group of his people were taken captive, then the Messenger of God ﷺ showed favour to his sister and gave her gifts, so she returned to her brother and encouraged him to embrace Islam and to come to the Messenger of God ﷺ. 'Adi came to Medina, and he was a chief among his people, Tayy, and his father was Hatim al-Ta'i, famous for generosity. People talked about his arrival, so he entered upon the Messenger of God ﷺ while there was a silver cross around 'Adi's neck. The Messenger of God ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾. He said: I said: "They did not worship them." He said: "Yes, indeed, they forbade them the lawful and made lawful for them the unlawful, and they followed them; that is their worship of them." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "O 'Adi, what do you say? Does it please you that it be said, 'God is greatest'? Do you know of anything greater than God? What is it that troubles you? Does it please you that it be said, 'There is no god but God'? Do you know of any god besides God?" Then he invited him to Islam, and he embraced it and bore witness to the truth. He said: "I saw his face light up with joy," and then he said: "Indeed the Jews are those who have earned anger, and the Christians are those who have gone astray." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3095) and Tafsir al-Tabari (14/209-211) through the chain of 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb from Ghutayf ibn A'yan from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd from 'Adi ibn Hatim, may God be pleased with him. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except from the hadith of 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb, and Ghutayf ibn A'yan is not well known in hadith."]

Allah, the Exalted, says: These disbelievers, from among the polytheists and the People of the Book, want ﴿to extinguish the light of Allah﴾ [[In T and A: "liyutfi'u" (with the lam), which is an error.]], that is, what Allah sent His Messenger with of guidance and the religion of truth, merely by their disputation and their fabrication. Their example in this is like the example of one who wants to extinguish the rays of the sun, or the light of the moon, by blowing on it. This is impossible. Likewise, what Allah sent His Messenger with must certainly be completed and must prevail. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, says in response to them, regarding what they attempted and intended: ﴿But Allah refuses except to complete His light, although the disbelievers dislike it﴾.

Al-kafir (the disbeliever) is one who covers a thing and conceals it. From this, the night is called "kafir", because it covers things. And the farmer is called "kafir", because he covers the seed in the earth, as He said: ﴿It pleases the farmers [al-kuffar] with its growth﴾ [al-Hadid: 20] [[In all copies: "yu'jib" (pleases), and the correct reading is what we have recorded.]].

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth﴾. So guidance is what he brought of true reports, correct faith, and beneficial knowledge. And the religion of truth is the correct, beneficial righteous deeds in this world and the Hereafter.

﴿That He may make it prevail over all religion﴾, that is, over all other religions, as is established in the Sahih, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed Allah folded up the earth for me, so that I saw its easts and its wests, and the dominion of my Ummah will reach what was folded up for me of it." [Sahih Muslim, no. (2889), from the hadith of Thawban, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Ya'qub: I heard Shaqiq ibn Hayyan narrating from Mas'ud ibn Qabisah, or Qabisah ibn Mas'ud, saying: This clan of Muharib prayed the dawn prayer, and when they had prayed, a young man among them said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed, the easts and wests of the earth will be opened for you, and its governors are in the Fire, except for one who fears Allah and fulfills the trust." [Al-Musnad (5/366).]

He said: I had not finished saying it when I humbled myself before it. He said: "As for me, I know what prevents you from Islam: you say, 'Only the weak among the people follow him, and those who have no strength, and the Arabs have thrown them off.' He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, Allah will certainly complete this affair until a woman riding in a litter will leave al-Hirah and circumambulate the House without being under the protection of anyone, and you will surely open the treasures of Kisra ibn Hurmuz." I said: "Kisra ibn Hurmuz?" He said: "Yes, Kisra ibn Hurmuz, and wealth will be spent until no one accepts it."
