Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 9, verses 34–35 (part 1 of 2):

As-Suddi said: "The rabbis (al-ahbar) are from among the Jews, and the monks (ar-ruhban) are from among the Christians."

This is as he said. The ahbar are the scholars of the Jews, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them from uttering sin and consuming the unlawful?﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 63]. The ruhban are the worshippers of the Christians, and the qissisun (qissisin) are their scholars, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 82].

The purpose here is a warning against corrupt scholars and misguided worshippers. Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: "Whoever among our scholars becomes corrupt has in him a resemblance to the Jews, and whoever among our worshippers becomes corrupt has in him a resemblance to the Christians." And in the authentic hadith: "You will certainly follow the ways of those before you, step by step, exactly like the feather of an arrow matching its fellow." They said: "The Jews and the Christians?" He said: "Who else?" In another narration: "Persia and Byzantium?" He said: "And who are the people other than these?" (Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 3456, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2669, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him.)

The summary is a warning against imitating them in their conduct and their sayings. Therefore Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, they consume the wealth of people unjustly﴾, because they consume worldly gain through religion, and through their positions and their leadership among the people, they consume their wealth by this. Just as the rabbis of the Jews had honour among the people of the Jahiliyyah, and they received from them tribute, gifts and taxes that came to them. When Allah sent His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, they persisted in their misguidance, disbelief and obstinacy, hoping that those leaderships would remain for them. So Allah extinguished them with the light of prophethood, stripped them of them, and replaced them with humiliation and poverty, and they incurred wrath from Allah.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they bar from the way of Allah﴾, meaning: while they consume the unlawful, they also bar people from following the truth, and they confuse truth with falsehood, and they show to those among the ignorant who follow them that they call to good, while they are not as they claim, but rather they are callers to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah — give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾. These are the third category of the leaders of the people, for people are dependent upon the scholars, the worshippers and the owners of wealth. When their conditions are corrupted, the conditions of the people are corrupted, as one of them (Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, may Allah have mercy on him) said:

"Has anything corrupted the religion except the kings, and the evil rabbis and their monks?"

As for hoarding (kanz), Malik narrated from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Umar, that he said: "It is the wealth from which zakah is not paid."

Ath-Thawri and others narrated from Ubayd Allah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "Whatever zakah has been paid on is not hoarding, even if it is beneath seven earths, and whatever is apparent and its zakah is not paid is hoarding." This has also been related from Ibn 'Abbas, Jabir and Abu Hurayrah, both as a statement of the companion and as a marfu' report, and from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, similarly, may Allah be pleased with them: "Any wealth whose zakah you have paid is not hoarding, even if it is buried in the earth, and any wealth whose zakah you have not paid is hoarding, by which its owner will be branded, even if it is upon the surface of the earth."

Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadith of az-Zuhri, from Khalid ibn Aslam, who said: "We went out with Abdullah ibn 'Umar, and he said: 'This was before the zakah was revealed. When it was revealed, Allah made it a purification for wealth.'" (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1404.)

Similarly, 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz and 'Iraq ibn Malik said: it was abrogated by His saying: ﴿Take from their wealth﴾ [At-Tawbah: 103].

Sa'id ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated from Abu Umamah that he said: "The ornaments of swords are from hoarding. I only tell you what I have heard."

Ath-Thawri said, from Abu Husayn, from Abu ad-Duha, from Ja'dah ibn Hubayrah, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Four thousand and less than it is spending (nafaqah); whatever is more than that is hoarding."

This is a strange report. Numerous hadiths have come in praise of minimizing gold and silver and in condemnation of accumulating them, and we will cite here a portion that indicates the rest. 'Abd ar-Razzaq said: Ath-Thawri informed us, Abu Husayn informed me, from Abu ad-Duha, from Ibn Ja'dah ibn Hubayrah, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah﴾: the Prophet ﷺ said: "Woe to gold, woe to silver," saying it three times. He said: This was difficult for the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they said: "Then what wealth should we acquire?" 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I will find out for you about that." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, your Companions have found it difficult," and they said: "Then what wealth should we acquire?" He said: "A remembering tongue, a grateful heart, and a wife who helps one of you in his religion." (Mentioned by az-Zayla'i in Takhrij al-Kashshaf (2/71) and attributed it to 'Abd ar-Razzaq in his Tafsir after mentioning it from the hadith of Thawban and 'Umar, then said: "The conclusion is that it is a weak hadith because of its confusion (idtirab).")

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, Salim narrated to me, Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl narrated to me, a companion of mine narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Woe to gold and silver." He said: My companion narrated to me that he went out with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and he said: "O Messenger of Allah, your saying 'Woe to gold and silver' — what should we store up?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A remembering tongue, a grateful heart, and a wife who helps you in the matter of the Hereafter."

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn Murrah narrated to us, from his father, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Thawban, who said: "When what was revealed concerning gold and silver was revealed, they said: 'Then what wealth should we acquire?' 'Umar said: 'I will find that out for you.' He mounted a camel and caught up with him, and I was following him. He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what wealth should we acquire?' He said: 'Let each one of you acquire a grateful heart, a remembering tongue, and a wife who helps one of you in the matter of the Hereafter.'"

At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it through more than one route from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd. At-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan." It is related from al-Bukhari that Salim did not hear it from Thawban.

I say: For this reason, some of them narrated it from him as mursal, and Allah knows best.

Another hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Humayd ibn Malik narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ya'la al-Muharibi narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Ghaylan ibn Jami' al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Uthman Abu al-Yaqzan, from Ja'far ibn Iyas, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "When this verse was revealed: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾ to the end of the verse, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims, and they said: 'None of us can leave to his child what will not remain after him.' 'Umar said: 'I will relieve you of this.' 'Umar set off, and Thawban followed him, and he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'O Prophet of Allah, this verse has weighed heavily upon your Companions.' The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: 'Allah did not prescribe zakah except to purify with it what remains of your wealth, and He prescribed inheritance from wealth that remains after you.' He said: 'So 'Umar exclaimed Allahu akbar.' Then the Prophet ﷺ said to him: 'Shall I inform you of the best thing a man can hoard? A righteous woman, who, when he looks at her, pleases him, when he commands her she obeys him, and when he is absent from her she guards him.'"

Abu Dawud, al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it from the hadith of Yahya ibn Ya'la, with the same chain. Al-Hakim said: "Sahih according to their condition, though they did not record it." (Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1664; al-Mustadrak (2/333). adh-Dhahabi said: "I do not know Uthman, and the report is strange.")

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Rawh narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, from Hassan ibn 'Atiyyah who said: Shaddad ibn Aws, may Allah be pleased with him, was on a journey, and he stopped at a station and said to his servant: "Bring us the razor, we will play with it." I objected to him, and he said: "I have not spoken a word since I embraced Islam except that I restrain it and bridle it, except for this word of mine, so do not hold it against me, and remember what I say to you: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'When people hoard gold and silver, then hoard these words: O Allah, I ask You for steadfastness in the matter, and resolve upon right guidance, and I ask You for the gratitude of Your blessing, and I ask You for good worship of You, and I ask You for a sound heart, and I ask You for a truthful tongue, and I ask You for the best of what You know, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of what You know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what You know, indeed You are the Knower of the unseen.'" (Musnad (4/123).)

And His saying: ﴿On the Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell and their foreheads, their sides and their backs will be branded with it: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard."﴾ That is, these words will be said to them as rebuke, reproach and mockery, as in His saying: ﴿Then pour over his head some of the torment of boiling water. Taste it! Indeed, you were the mighty, the noble﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 48–49], meaning: this is in exchange for that, and this is what you used to hoard for yourselves. Therefore it is said: whoever loves something and prefers it over obedience to Allah, will be punished by it. Since the gathering of this wealth was dearer to them than the pleasure of Allah with them, they were punished by it, just as Abu Lahab, may Allah curse him, was striving in enmity against the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and his wife was helping him in that; she will be a helper in his punishment on the Day of Resurrection as well: ﴿Around her neck is a rope of fibre﴾ [Al-Masad: 5], that is, she gathers firewood in the Fire and throws it upon him, so that it will be more severe in his punishment from one who was most compassionate toward him in the world. Just as these wealths, since they were the most precious things to their owners, will be the most harmful things to them in the Hereafter: it will be heated in the fire of Hell, and how intense its heat is, and their foreheads, sides and backs will be branded with it.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 9, verses 34–35 (part 2 of 2):

Sufyan said, from al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "By Allah, other than whom there is no god, a servant is not branded with a hoard so that one dinar touches another dinar, nor one dirham another dirham. Rather, his skin is widened, and each dinar and dirham is placed on its own [[In A: "his skin."]] [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/233) through Sufyan with this chain.]]"

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from Abu Hurayrah in a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) form, but its attribution to the Prophet is not sound. Allah knows best.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, who said: "It has reached me that on the Day of Resurrection the hoard will turn into a male serpent (shuja') that follows its owner while he flees from it, and it says: 'I am your hoard!' He cannot escape it, and it seizes whatever part of him it reaches."

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Bishr narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah, from Thawban, that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "Whoever leaves behind him a hoard, on the Day of Resurrection it will be made into a bald male serpent with two black spots over its eyes. It will follow him, saying: 'Woe to you! What are you?' He will say: 'I am your hoard that you left behind after you!' It will keep following him until it puts its hand in his mouth, and it will bite it off, and then it will follow the rest of his body."

Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Yazid, from Sa'id with this chain [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/232), and Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. (803) in the Mawarid edition. Ibn Khuzaymah also narrated it in his Sahih, no. (2255), through Bishr ibn Mu'adh with this chain.]]. The origin of this hadith is in the two Sahihs, through the narration of Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4659). I did not find it in Sahih Muslim through this chain.]]. In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No man who does not pay the zakat on his wealth will have, on the Day of Resurrection, sheets of fire made for him, with which his side, forehead and back will be branded, on a day whose length is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people, then he will see his path, either to Paradise or to the Fire." And he mentioned the rest of the hadith [[Sahih Muslim, no. (987).]].

Al-Bukhari said in his commentary on this verse: Qutaybah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Husayn, from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: "I passed by Abu Dharr at al-Rabadhah and said: 'What brought you to this land?' He said: 'We were in Syria, and I recited: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of Allah — give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ Mu'awiyah said: "This is not about us; it is only about the People of the Book." I said: "It is about us and about them."' [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4660).]]"

Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of 'Abthar ibn al-Qasim, from Husayn, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), and mentioned it, adding: "Then the dispute between me and him escalated, so he wrote to Uthman complaining about me. Uthman wrote to me asking me to come to him. So I came, and when I arrived in Medina, people gathered around me as if they had not seen me before that day. I complained of this to Uthman, and he said to me: 'Withdraw a little distance.' I said: 'By Allah, I will not abandon what I used to say [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/227).]]'."

I say: It was part of Abu Dharr's position (may Allah be pleased with him) to forbid storing what exceeds the needs of one's dependents. He used to issue rulings to that effect, urging people toward it, commanding them, and being harsh toward those who opposed it. Mu'awiyah forbade him, but he did not desist. Mu'awiyah feared that this would harm the people in this matter, so he wrote complaining about him to the Commander of the Faithful Uthman and asking that Abu Dharr be taken to him. Uthman summoned him to Medina, then settled him alone at al-Rabadhah, where he died during Uthman's caliphate (may Allah be pleased with him). Mu'awiyah (may Allah be pleased with him) had also tested him while he was with him, to see whether his practice matched his words. He sent him a thousand dinars, and Abu Dharr distributed them the same day. Then Mu'awiyah sent the man who had brought them to him, saying: "Mu'awiyah only sent me to someone other than you, and I made a mistake. So give me back the gold!" Abu Dharr said: "Woe to you! It has already gone out. But when my wealth comes, we will settle accounts with you over it [[In T and A: "we will settle accounts with him."]]."

Similarly, Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that it is general in meaning.

Al-Suddi said: it concerns the People of the Qiblah (i.e., Muslims).

Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays said: "I came to Medina, and while I was in a circle with a group of Quraysh, a man came, roughly dressed, rough of body and rough of face. He stood over them and said: 'Give the hoarders tidings of heated stones heated in the fire of Hell, which will be placed on the nipple of one of them until it exits from the blade of his shoulder, and placed on the blade of his shoulder until it exits from the nipple of his breast, trembling.' He said: The people lowered their heads, and I did not see any of them answer him with anything. He said: Then he turned away, and I followed him until he sat down beside a pillar. I said: 'I did not see these people but that they disliked what you said to them.' He said: 'These people do not know anything.'"

It is in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Dharr: "It would not please me to have gold equal to Mount Uhud with me, and that three nights pass over me while there is anything of it left with me, except a dinar which I set aside for a debt" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6444).]].

This, Allah knows best, is what moved Abu Dharr to hold this view.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn al-Samit (may Allah be pleased with him), that he was with Abu Dharr when his stipend was paid out, and with him was a slave-girl of his who began to carry out his needs. Seven [dirhams] remained over with her, so he ordered her to buy small coins with them. He said: "If you had saved it for a need that might befall you, or for a guest who might come to you!" He said: "My close friend (khalil) instructed me that whatever gold or silver is tied up (awka), it becomes a burning coal for its owner until he spends it in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic [[Al-Musnad (5/156).]]."

He also narrated it from Yazid, from Hammam, with this chain, and added: "spending it (ifraghan) [[Al-Musnad (5/175). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/240): "its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]]."

Al-Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir, with his chain to Abu Bakr al-Shibli, in his biography, from Muhammad ibn Mahdi: 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, from Sadaqah ibn 'Abdullah, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Farwah al-Ruhawi, from 'Ata', from Abu Sa'id (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Meet Allah poor, and do not meet Him rich." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can I do that?" He said: "Do not refuse what you are asked for, and do not hide what you are provided with." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can I do that?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "That is it; otherwise, the Fire [[See: Mukhtasar Tarikh Dimashq by Ibn Manzur (28/168). Al-Khatib narrated it in Tarikh Baghdad (14/390) in the biography of al-Shibli through Muhammad ibn Mahdi al-Misri with this chain.]]." Its chain is weak.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us, 'Utaybah narrated to us, from Buraydah ibn Asram, who said: "I heard Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) say: A man from the People of the Suffah (Ahl al-Suffah, the poor companions who lived in the mosque) died and left two dinars, or two dirhams. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Two brands (kayyatan). Pray over your companion [[Al-Musnad (1/101).]].'" This has been narrated through other routes [[Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (1/137, 138) through Qatan ibn Nusayr, Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd and Hibban ibn Hilal, all from Ja'far ibn Sulayman with similar wording. It also came from a hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/412); from a hadith of Salamah ibn al-Akwa', narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (4/47), a lengthy hadith; and from a hadith of Abu Hurayrah, narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/429).]].

Qatadah said, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Umamah Sudayy ibn 'Ajlan, who said: "A man from the People of the Suffah died, and a dinar was found in his loincloth. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'One brand.' Then another man died, and two dinars were found in his loincloth. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Two brands [[Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/253) and al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/222) through Qatadah with this chain.]].'"

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Nadr Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Faradisi narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Yahya al-Atrabulusi narrated to us, Artah narrated to me, Abu 'Amir al-Hawzani narrated to me: "I heard Thawban, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), say: 'No man dies while he has gold or silver (ahmar aw abyad), but that Allah makes for every qirat (a unit of weight) a sheet of fire with which he is branded from his foot to his chin.'"

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Muhammad ibn Khidash narrated to us, Sayf ibn Muhammad al-Thawri narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A dinar is not placed on a dinar, nor a dirham on a dirham, but his skin is widened and they are branded with them on their foreheads, their sides and their backs: 'This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard [[Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, as in al-Durr al-Manthur by al-Suyuti (4/179).]].'" Sayf is a liar (kadhdhab) and abandoned (matruk) in narration.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 9, verses 34–35 (part 1 of 2):

As-Suddi said: "The rabbis (al-ahbar) are from among the Jews, and the monks (ar-ruhban) are from among the Christians."

This is as he said. The ahbar are the scholars of the Jews, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them from uttering sin and consuming the unlawful?﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 63]. The ruhban are the worshippers of the Christians, and the qissisun (qissisin) are their scholars, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 82].

The purpose here is a warning against corrupt scholars and misguided worshippers. Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: "Whoever among our scholars becomes corrupt has in him a resemblance to the Jews, and whoever among our worshippers becomes corrupt has in him a resemblance to the Christians." And in the authentic hadith: "You will certainly follow the ways of those before you, step by step, exactly like the feather of an arrow matching its fellow." They said: "The Jews and the Christians?" He said: "Who else?" In another narration: "Persia and Byzantium?" He said: "And who are the people other than these?" (Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 3456, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2669, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him.)

The summary is a warning against imitating them in their conduct and their sayings. Therefore Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, they consume the wealth of people unjustly﴾, because they consume worldly gain through religion, and through their positions and their leadership among the people, they consume their wealth by this. Just as the rabbis of the Jews had honour among the people of the Jahiliyyah, and they received from them tribute, gifts and taxes that came to them. When Allah sent His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, they persisted in their misguidance, disbelief and obstinacy, hoping that those leaderships would remain for them. So Allah extinguished them with the light of prophethood, stripped them of them, and replaced them with humiliation and poverty, and they incurred wrath from Allah.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they bar from the way of Allah﴾, meaning: while they consume the unlawful, they also bar people from following the truth, and they confuse truth with falsehood, and they show to those among the ignorant who follow them that they call to good, while they are not as they claim, but rather they are callers to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah — give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾. These are the third category of the leaders of the people, for people are dependent upon the scholars, the worshippers and the owners of wealth. When their conditions are corrupted, the conditions of the people are corrupted, as one of them (Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, may Allah have mercy on him) said:

"Has anything corrupted the religion except the kings, and the evil rabbis and their monks?"

As for hoarding (kanz), Malik narrated from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Umar, that he said: "It is the wealth from which zakah is not paid."

Ath-Thawri and others narrated from Ubayd Allah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "Whatever zakah has been paid on is not hoarding, even if it is beneath seven earths, and whatever is apparent and its zakah is not paid is hoarding." This has also been related from Ibn 'Abbas, Jabir and Abu Hurayrah, both as a statement of the companion and as a marfu' report, and from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, similarly, may Allah be pleased with them: "Any wealth whose zakah you have paid is not hoarding, even if it is buried in the earth, and any wealth whose zakah you have not paid is hoarding, by which its owner will be branded, even if it is upon the surface of the earth."

Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadith of az-Zuhri, from Khalid ibn Aslam, who said: "We went out with Abdullah ibn 'Umar, and he said: 'This was before the zakah was revealed. When it was revealed, Allah made it a purification for wealth.'" (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1404.)

Similarly, 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz and 'Iraq ibn Malik said: it was abrogated by His saying: ﴿Take from their wealth﴾ [At-Tawbah: 103].

Sa'id ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated from Abu Umamah that he said: "The ornaments of swords are from hoarding. I only tell you what I have heard."

Ath-Thawri said, from Abu Husayn, from Abu ad-Duha, from Ja'dah ibn Hubayrah, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Four thousand and less than it is spending (nafaqah); whatever is more than that is hoarding."

This is a strange report. Numerous hadiths have come in praise of minimizing gold and silver and in condemnation of accumulating them, and we will cite here a portion that indicates the rest. 'Abd ar-Razzaq said: Ath-Thawri informed us, Abu Husayn informed me, from Abu ad-Duha, from Ibn Ja'dah ibn Hubayrah, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the saying of Allah: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah﴾: the Prophet ﷺ said: "Woe to gold, woe to silver," saying it three times. He said: This was difficult for the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they said: "Then what wealth should we acquire?" 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I will find out for you about that." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, your Companions have found it difficult," and they said: "Then what wealth should we acquire?" He said: "A remembering tongue, a grateful heart, and a wife who helps one of you in his religion." (Mentioned by az-Zayla'i in Takhrij al-Kashshaf (2/71) and attributed it to 'Abd ar-Razzaq in his Tafsir after mentioning it from the hadith of Thawban and 'Umar, then said: "The conclusion is that it is a weak hadith because of its confusion (idtirab).")

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, Salim narrated to me, Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl narrated to me, a companion of mine narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Woe to gold and silver." He said: My companion narrated to me that he went out with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and he said: "O Messenger of Allah, your saying 'Woe to gold and silver' — what should we store up?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A remembering tongue, a grateful heart, and a wife who helps you in the matter of the Hereafter."

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn Murrah narrated to us, from his father, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Thawban, who said: "When what was revealed concerning gold and silver was revealed, they said: 'Then what wealth should we acquire?' 'Umar said: 'I will find that out for you.' He mounted a camel and caught up with him, and I was following him. He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what wealth should we acquire?' He said: 'Let each one of you acquire a grateful heart, a remembering tongue, and a wife who helps one of you in the matter of the Hereafter.'"

At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it through more than one route from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd. At-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan." It is related from al-Bukhari that Salim did not hear it from Thawban.

I say: For this reason, some of them narrated it from him as mursal, and Allah knows best.

Another hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Humayd ibn Malik narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ya'la al-Muharibi narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Ghaylan ibn Jami' al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Uthman Abu al-Yaqzan, from Ja'far ibn Iyas, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "When this verse was revealed: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver﴾ to the end of the verse, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims, and they said: 'None of us can leave to his child what will not remain after him.' 'Umar said: 'I will relieve you of this.' 'Umar set off, and Thawban followed him, and he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'O Prophet of Allah, this verse has weighed heavily upon your Companions.' The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: 'Allah did not prescribe zakah except to purify with it what remains of your wealth, and He prescribed inheritance from wealth that remains after you.' He said: 'So 'Umar exclaimed Allahu akbar.' Then the Prophet ﷺ said to him: 'Shall I inform you of the best thing a man can hoard? A righteous woman, who, when he looks at her, pleases him, when he commands her she obeys him, and when he is absent from her she guards him.'"

Abu Dawud, al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it from the hadith of Yahya ibn Ya'la, with the same chain. Al-Hakim said: "Sahih according to their condition, though they did not record it." (Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1664; al-Mustadrak (2/333). adh-Dhahabi said: "I do not know Uthman, and the report is strange.")

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Rawh narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, from Hassan ibn 'Atiyyah who said: Shaddad ibn Aws, may Allah be pleased with him, was on a journey, and he stopped at a station and said to his servant: "Bring us the razor, we will play with it." I objected to him, and he said: "I have not spoken a word since I embraced Islam except that I restrain it and bridle it, except for this word of mine, so do not hold it against me, and remember what I say to you: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'When people hoard gold and silver, then hoard these words: O Allah, I ask You for steadfastness in the matter, and resolve upon right guidance, and I ask You for the gratitude of Your blessing, and I ask You for good worship of You, and I ask You for a sound heart, and I ask You for a truthful tongue, and I ask You for the best of what You know, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of what You know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what You know, indeed You are the Knower of the unseen.'" (Musnad (4/123).)

And His saying: ﴿On the Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell and their foreheads, their sides and their backs will be branded with it: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard."﴾ That is, these words will be said to them as rebuke, reproach and mockery, as in His saying: ﴿Then pour over his head some of the torment of boiling water. Taste it! Indeed, you were the mighty, the noble﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 48–49], meaning: this is in exchange for that, and this is what you used to hoard for yourselves. Therefore it is said: whoever loves something and prefers it over obedience to Allah, will be punished by it. Since the gathering of this wealth was dearer to them than the pleasure of Allah with them, they were punished by it, just as Abu Lahab, may Allah curse him, was striving in enmity against the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and his wife was helping him in that; she will be a helper in his punishment on the Day of Resurrection as well: ﴿Around her neck is a rope of fibre﴾ [Al-Masad: 5], that is, she gathers firewood in the Fire and throws it upon him, so that it will be more severe in his punishment from one who was most compassionate toward him in the world. Just as these wealths, since they were the most precious things to their owners, will be the most harmful things to them in the Hereafter: it will be heated in the fire of Hell, and how intense its heat is, and their foreheads, sides and backs will be branded with it.

Sufyan said, from al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "By Allah, other than whom there is no god, a servant is not branded with a hoard so that one dinar touches another dinar, nor one dirham another dirham. Ibn Khuzaymah also narrated it in his Sahih, no. (2255), through Bishr ibn Mu'adh with this chain.]]. The origin of this hadith is in the two Sahihs, through the narration of Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4659). I did not find it in Sahih Muslim through this chain.]]. In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No man who does not pay the zakat on his wealth will have, on the Day of Resurrection, sheets of fire made for him, with which his side, forehead and back will be branded, on a day whose length is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people, then he will see his path, either to Paradise or to the Fire." And he mentioned the rest of the hadith [[Sahih Muslim, no. (987).]].

Al-Bukhari said in his commentary on this verse: Qutaybah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Husayn, from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: "I passed by Abu Dharr at al-Rabadhah and said: 'What brought you to this land?' He said: 'We were in Syria, and I recited: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend them in the way of Allah — give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ Mu'awiyah said: "This is not about us; it is only about the People of the Book." I said: "It is about us and about them."' [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4660).]]"

Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of 'Abthar ibn al-Qasim, from Husayn, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), and mentioned it, adding: "Then the dispute between me and him escalated, so he wrote to Uthman complaining about me. Uthman wrote to me asking me to come to him. So I came, and when I arrived in Medina, people gathered around me as if they had not seen me before that day. I complained of this to Uthman, and he said to me: 'Withdraw a little distance.' I said: 'By Allah, I will not abandon what I used to say [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/227).]]'."

I say: It was part of Abu Dharr's position (may Allah be pleased with him) to forbid storing what exceeds the needs of one's dependents. He used to issue rulings to that effect, urging people toward it, commanding them, and being harsh toward those who opposed it. Mu'awiyah forbade him, but he did not desist. Mu'awiyah feared that this would harm the people in this matter, so he wrote complaining about him to the Commander of the Faithful Uthman and asking that Abu Dharr be taken to him. Uthman summoned him to Medina, then settled him alone at al-Rabadhah, where he died during Uthman's caliphate (may Allah be pleased with him). Mu'awiyah (may Allah be pleased with him) had also tested him while he was with him, to see whether his practice matched his words. He sent him a thousand dinars, and Abu Dharr distributed them the same day. Then Mu'awiyah sent the man who had brought them to him, saying: "Mu'awiyah only sent me to someone other than you, and I made a mistake. So give me back the gold!" Abu Dharr said: "Woe to you! It has already gone out. But when my wealth comes, we will settle accounts with you over it [[In T and A: "we will settle accounts with him."]]."

Similarly, Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that it is general in meaning.

Al-Suddi said: it concerns the People of the Qiblah (i.e., Muslims).

Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays said: "I came to Medina, and while I was in a circle with a group of Quraysh, a man came, roughly dressed, rough of body and rough of face. He stood over them and said: 'Give the hoarders tidings of heated stones heated in the fire of Hell, which will be placed on the nipple of one of them until it exits from the blade of his shoulder, and placed on the blade of his shoulder until it exits from the nipple of his breast, trembling.' He said: The people lowered their heads, and I did not see any of them answer him with anything. He said: Then he turned away, and I followed him until he sat down beside a pillar. I said: 'I did not see these people but that they disliked what you said to them.' He said: 'These people do not know anything.'"

It is in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Dharr: "It would not please me to have gold equal to Mount Uhud with me, and that three nights pass over me while there is anything of it left with me, except a dinar which I set aside for a debt" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6444).]].

This, Allah knows best, is what moved Abu Dharr to hold this view.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn al-Samit (may Allah be pleased with him), that he was with Abu Dharr when his stipend was paid out, and with him was a slave-girl of his who began to carry out his needs. Seven [dirhams] remained over with her, so he ordered her to buy small coins with them. He said: "If you had saved it for a need that might befall you, or for a guest who might come to you!" He said: "My close friend (khalil) instructed me that whatever gold or silver is tied up (awka), it becomes a burning coal for its owner until he spends it in the way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic [[Al-Musnad (5/156).]]."

He also narrated it from Yazid, from Hammam, with this chain, and added: "spending it (ifraghan) [[Al-Musnad (5/175). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/240): "its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]]."

Al-Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir, with his chain to Abu Bakr al-Shibli, in his biography, from Muhammad ibn Mahdi: 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, from Sadaqah ibn 'Abdullah, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Farwah al-Ruhawi, from 'Ata', from Abu Sa'id (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Meet Allah poor, and do not meet Him rich." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can I do that?" He said: "Do not refuse what you are asked for, and do not hide what you are provided with." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can I do that?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "That is it; otherwise, the Fire [[See: Mukhtasar Tarikh Dimashq by Ibn Manzur (28/168). Al-Khatib narrated it in Tarikh Baghdad (14/390) in the biography of al-Shibli through Muhammad ibn Mahdi al-Misri with this chain.]]." Its chain is weak.

Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us, 'Utaybah narrated to us, from Buraydah ibn Asram, who said: "I heard Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) say: A man from the People of the Suffah (Ahl al-Suffah, the poor companions who lived in the mosque) died and left two dinars, or two dirhams. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Two brands (kayyatan). Pray over your companion [[Al-Musnad (1/101).]].'" This has been narrated through other routes [[Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (1/137, 138) through Qatan ibn Nusayr, Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd and Hibban ibn Hilal, all from Ja'far ibn Sulayman with similar wording. It also came from a hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/412); from a hadith of Salamah ibn al-Akwa', narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (4/47), a lengthy hadith; and from a hadith of Abu Hurayrah, narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/429).]].

Qatadah said, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Umamah Sudayy ibn 'Ajlan, who said: "A man from the People of the Suffah died, and a dinar was found in his loincloth. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'One brand.' Then another man died, and two dinars were found in his loincloth. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Two brands [[Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/253) and al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/222) through Qatadah with this chain.]].'"

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Nadr Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Faradisi narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Yahya al-Atrabulusi narrated to us, Artah narrated to me, Abu 'Amir al-Hawzani narrated to me: "I heard Thawban, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), say: 'No man dies while he has gold or silver (ahmar aw abyad), but that Allah makes for every qirat (a unit of weight) a sheet of fire with which he is branded from his foot to his chin.'"

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Muhammad ibn Khidash narrated to us, Sayf ibn Muhammad al-Thawri narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A dinar is not placed on a dinar, nor a dirham on a dirham, but his skin is widened and they are branded with them on their foreheads, their sides and their backs: 'This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard [[Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, as in al-Durr al-Manthur by al-Suyuti (4/179).]].'" Sayf is a liar (kadhdhab) and abandoned (matruk) in narration.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 9, verse 36 (part 1 of 2):

Imam Ahmad said: Ismail narrated to us, Ayyub informed us, Muhammad ibn Sirin informed us, from Abu Bakrah, that the Prophet ﷺ delivered a sermon during his Hajj, and he said: "Behold, time has returned to its original form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, of which four are sacred (ḥurum), three of them consecutive: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and al-Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar, which lies between Jumada and Sha'ban." Then he said: "What day is this?" We said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He remained silent until we thought he would name it by another name. He said: "Is it not the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm an-Nahr)?" We said: "Yes." Then he said: "What month is this?" We said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He remained silent until we thought he would name it by another name. He said: "Is it not Dhu al-Hijjah?" We said: "Yes." Then he said: "What land is this?" We said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He remained silent until we thought he would name it by another name. He said: "Is it not the land (al-Baldah)?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Indeed your blood and your properties—he said: and I think he said: and your honour—are forbidden to you, as the sanctity of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this land of yours. You will meet your Lord, and He will question you about your deeds. Beware, do not revert to misguidance after me, striking one another's necks. Behold, have I conveyed? Let the one present convey it to the one absent, for perhaps the one to whom it is conveyed may understand it better than some who hear it."

It is also narrated by al-Bukhari in at-Tafsir and elsewhere, and by Muslim, from the hadith of Ayyub, from Muhammad—that is Ibn Sirin—from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, from his father, with the same wording.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to us, Rawh narrated to us, Ashath narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed time has returned to its original form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth, and indeed the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah on the day He created the heavens and the earth, of which four are sacred: three consecutive, and Rajab of Mudar between Jumada and Sha'ban."

Al-Bazzar narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ma'mar with the same wording [in T and A: "Mu'awiyah"]. Then he said: This is not narrated from Abu Hurayrah except through this route, and it was narrated by Ibn 'Awn and Qurrah from Ibn Sirin, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, from his father, with the same wording.

Ibn Jarir also said: Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, Musa ibn Ubaydah al-Rabadhi narrated to us, Sadaqah ibn Yasar narrated to me, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a sermon during the Farewell Pilgrimage at Mina, in the middle of the days of Tashriq, and said: "O people, indeed time has returned, so it is today in its original form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth. The number of months with Allah is twelve months, of which four are sacred: first of them Rajab of Mudar between Jumada and Sha'ban, then Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and al-Muharram."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Musa ibn Ubaydah, from Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn Amr, something similar to it or close to it.

Hammad ibn Salamah said: Ali ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Abu Harrah [in K and A: "Hamzah"], al-Raqashi narrated to me, from his paternal uncle—and he had companionship with the Prophet—who said: I was holding the rein of the camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the middle of the days of Tashriq, keeping people away from him, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Behold, time has returned to its original form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth, and indeed the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah on the day He created the heavens and the earth, of which four are sacred, so do not wrong yourselves in them."

Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿of them four are sacred﴾, he said: Muharram, Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah.

* *

His saying ﷺ in the hadith: "Indeed time has returned to its original form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth" is an affirmation from him, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and a confirmation of the matter as Allah ordained it at the beginning, without advancement or delay, without addition or reduction, and without intercalation (nasi') or alteration, just as he said regarding the sanctity of Makkah: "Indeed this land was made sacred by Allah on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by the sanctity of Allah until the Day of Resurrection." Likewise, he said here: "Indeed time has returned to its original form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth," meaning: the matter today is in legislation as Allah began it in His Book on the day He created the heavens and the earth.

Some of the exegetes and scholars who spoke on this hadith said: The meaning of his saying "has returned to its original form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth" is that it coincided that the Hajj of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in that year fell in Dhu al-Hijjah, whereas the Arabs had practised intercalation (nasi'), performing Hajj in many years, indeed most of them, in other than Dhu al-Hijjah. They claimed that the Hajj of Abu Bakr in the ninth year was in Dhu al-Qa'dah. Yet this requires examination, as we will explain when we discuss nasi'.

Stranger than this is what al-Tabarani narrated from one of the early generations, within a longer hadith, that the Hajj of the Muslims, the Jews, and the Christians coincided on one day, which is the Day of Sacrifice, in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage. And Allah knows best.

[Appended section] [Addition from K, A.]

Shaykh 'Alam al-Din al-Sakhawi mentioned, in a booklet he compiled titled "al-Mashhur fi Asma' al-Ayyam wa al-Shuhur," that al-Muharram was so named because it is a forbidden month. In my view, it was named thus to emphasise its sanctity, because the Arabs would shift it, making it lawful one year and forbidden another year. He said: It is pluralised as muharramat, mahaarim, and mahareem.

Safar: it was named so because their houses were empty of them when they went out for fighting and travel. It is said: "safira al-makan" when it became empty. Its plural is asfar, like jamal and ajmal.

Rabi' al-Awwal: it was named so because of their settling (irtibau) in it. Irtibau means dwelling in the cultivation of the pasture. Its plural is arba' like naseeb and ansiba', and arba'ah like raghif and arghifah.

Rabi' al-Akhir: like the first.

Jumada: it was named so for the freezing (jumud) of water in it. He said: The months in their reckoning did not revolve. In this there is room for examination, since their months were tied to the crescents, and they must revolve. Perhaps they named it thus when it was first named, at the freezing of water in the cold, as the poet said:

And a night of Jumada, full of dew,
In whose darkness the servant cannot see the tent-ropes.
No dog barks in it except once,
Until it wraps its tail around its snout.

Its plural is jumadiyat, like hubara and hubariyat. It may be masculine or feminine, so one says Jumada al-Ula and al-Awwal, and Jumada al-Akhir and al-Akhirah.

Rajab: from tarjib, which is glorification (ta'zim). Its plurals are arjab, rijab, and rajabat.

Sha'ban: from the dispersal (tashaʻʻub) and scattering of the tribes for raiding. Its plurals are sha'abin and sha'banat [in K: "sha'abat"].

Ramadan: from the intensity of the heat (ramda'), which is the scorching heat. It is said: "ramidat al-fisal" when the young camels became thirsty. Its plurals are ramadanat, ramadin, and armidah. He said: The saying of whoever says "it is a name of Allah" is an error not to be regarded or heeded.

I say: a hadith has been reported concerning it, but it is weak, and I clarified this at the beginning of the Book of Fasting.

Shawwal: from "shalat al-ibil bi adhnabiha lil-tirad" (the camels raised their tails for chasing). He said: Its plurals are shawawil, shawawil, and shawwalat.

Dhu al-Qa'dah: with the letter qaf vowelled with fatha (I say: and kasra), because of their sitting in it from fighting and travelling. Its plural is dhawat al-qa'dah.

Dhu al-Hijjah: with the letter ha' vowelled with kasra (I say: and fatha), named so because they performed Hajj in it. Its plural is dhawat al-hijjah.

Names of the days: the first is al-Ahad, pluralised as ahad, uhad, and wuhud. Then Yawm al-Ithnayn, pluralised as athanin. Al-Thulathaa: it is lengthened, may be masculine or feminine, and pluralised as thalathawat and athalith. Then al-Arba'a, lengthened, pluralised as arba'awat and arabi'. Al-Khamis: pluralised as akhmisah and akhamis. Then al-Jumu'ah, with damma on the mim, with sukun, and with fatha as well, pluralised as juma' and jumu'at.

Al-Sabt: derived from al-sabt, which is cutting, because the counting ends with it. The Arabs used to name the days: awwal, then ahwan, then jubar, then dubar, then mu'nis, then al-'arubah, then shiyar. A poet of the early Arab stock said:

I hope to live, and that my day
Is awwal, or ahwan, or jubar,
Or the one following, dubar; if I miss it,
Then mu'nis, or 'arubah, or shiyar.

* *

His saying Most High: ﴿Of them four are sacred﴾. This is among what the Arabs also held sacred in the Jahiliyyah, and it is what the majority of them followed, except for a group among them called al-Basl, who would declare eight months of the year sacred, out of excessive strictness and severity.

As for his saying: "Three consecutive: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and al-Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar, which lies between Jumada and Sha'ban," he attributed it to Mudar in order to clarify the correctness of their statement regarding Rajab, that it is the month between Jumada and Sha'ban, not as Rabi'ah supposed, that Rajab al-Muharram is the month between Sha'ban and Shawwal, which is today Ramadan. So he, upon him be prayer and peace, clarified that it is Rajab of Mudar, not Rajab of Rabi'ah. The sacred months were four: three in succession and one standing alone, for the sake of performing the rites of Hajj and 'Umrah. So one month before the month of Hajj was made sacred, namely Dhu al-Qa'dah, because they sit in it, refraining from fighting. Dhu al-Hijjah was made sacred because they perform Hajj in it and occupy themselves with the rites. After it another month was made sacred, namely al-Muharram, so that they might return in it to the farthest parts of their lands in safety. Rajab was made sacred in the middle of the year, for the sake of visiting the House and performing 'Umrah there, for whoever comes to it from the farthest end of the Arabian Peninsula, so that he may visit it and then return to his homeland in safety.

* *

His saying Most High: ﴿That is the upright religion﴾. That is, this is the straight law, by complying with the command of Allah regarding the sacred months that He appointed, and by adhering to them as was prescribed in the earlier Book of Allah.

And He Most High said: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾. That is, in these sacred months, for sin in them is more emphatic and more grave than in others, just as sins in the Sacred City are multiplied, due to His saying Most High: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation with injustice—We will make him taste a painful punishment﴾ [al-Hajj: 25]. Likewise the sacred month is one in which sins are made more severe; therefore blood-money is made heavier in it according to the school of al-Shafi'i and a great many scholars, and likewise regarding one who kills within the Sanctuary or kills a close relative (dhu mahram).

Hammad ibn Salamah said, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿so do not wrong yourselves therein﴾, he said: In all the months.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months﴾ [in the Book of Allah] on the day He created the heavens and the earth, ... ﴿so do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ — meaning in all of them. Then He singled out from among them four months and made them sacred, magnified their sanctity, made sin therein greater, and made righteous deeds and reward greater.

Qatadah said regarding His saying: ﴿so do not wrong yourselves therein﴾: Indeed, wrongdoing in the sacred months is greater in sin and burden than wrongdoing in other than them, although wrongdoing is great in every circumstance. But Allah magnifies of His command what He wills. He said: Indeed, Allah chose from His creation chosen ones: from the angels He chose messengers, and from mankind He chose messengers; from speech He chose His remembrance; from the earth He chose the mosques; from the months He chose Ramadan and the sacred months; from the days He chose the day of Friday; and from the nights He chose the Night of Decree. So magnify what Allah has magnified, for matters are magnified by what Allah has magnified them with, in the sight of people of understanding and people of intellect.

Al-Thawri narrated from Qays ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah: [it means] that you should not make them sacred in the same way as their sanctity [is not to be treated].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ﴿so do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ means: do not make their sacred [months] lawful, nor their lawful [months] sacred, as the polytheists did. The *nasi'* (postponement of sacred months) which they practised was only an increase in disbelief: ﴿by which those who disbelieve are led astray﴾ [at-Tawbah: 37].

This view is the one chosen by Ibn Jarir.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And fight against the polytheists all together﴾ — meaning all of you — ﴿as they fight against you all together﴾ — meaning all of them — ﴿And know that Allah is with the righteous.﴾

The scholars differed concerning the prohibition of initiating fighting in the sacred month: is it abrogated (*mansukh*) or still in force (*muhkam*)? There are two opinions:

The first, which is the more well-known, is that it has been abrogated, because He, exalted is He, said here: ﴿so do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ and commanded fighting against the polytheists. The apparent context indicates that this command was general. Had fighting in the sacred month been forbidden, He would have likely restricted it by the end of those months. Also, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ besieged the people of al-Ta'if in a sacred month, which is Dhu al-Qa'dah, as is established in the two Sahihs: he went out against Hawazin in Shawwal, and when he defeated them, collected their wealth, and their remnants retreated and took refuge in al-Ta'if, he went to al-Ta'if and besieged it for forty days, then withdrew without conquering it. Thus it is established that he besieged during a sacred month.

The other opinion is that initiating fighting in the sacred month is forbidden, and that the prohibition has not been abrogated, based on His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not violate the sanctity of Allah's rites or of the sacred month﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 2], and His saying: ﴿The sacred month for the sacred month, and violations are subject to retribution. So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 194], and His saying: ﴿And when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists﴾ [at-Tawbah: 5].

It has already been mentioned that these are the four months established each year, not the months of postponement (*tasyir*) according to one of the two opinions.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And fight against the polytheists all together as they fight against you all together﴾, it may be that it is disconnected from what precedes it and is a new ruling, and it is of the category of inciting and urging: that is, just as they gather to fight you when they fight you, so gather you also against them when you fight them, and fight them with the like of what they do. It may also be that He permitted the believers to fight the polytheists in the sacred month when the initiative comes from them, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿The sacred month for the sacred month, and violations are subject to retribution﴾ [al-Baqarah: 194], and He said, exalted is He: ﴿And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque until they fight you therein; but if they fight you, then kill them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 191]. The same answer applies to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ besieging the people of al-Ta'if and continuing the siege until the sacred month entered, for it was part of the continuation of the fighting with Hawazin and their allies from Thaqif, since they were the ones who initiated the fighting, gathered the men, and called to war and combat. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ marched against them as mentioned, and they fortified themselves in al-Ta'if, he went to them to bring them down from their fortresses, and they struck the Muslims and killed a group of them. The siege continued with catapults and other means for nearly forty days. Its beginning was in a permissible month, and the sacred month entered while it was ongoing, so he continued in it for some days, then withdrew from them, because what is overlooked in continuation is not overlooked in initiation. This is a established principle, and it has many parallels. And Allah knows best.

We shall mention the ahadith related to this matter. [[The editor notes: the text here is missing in some manuscripts.]] We have verified this in the *Sirah*, and Allah knows best.

This is one of the things for which Allah the Exalted condemned the polytheists: they arbitrarily altered the law of Allah by their corrupt opinions, changed the rulings of Allah according to their baseless whims, made lawful what Allah had made unlawful, and made unlawful what Allah had made lawful. They had such fierce, arrogant, and zealous temperaments that they overstepped the bounds during the three months of the sacred period, which prevented them from attaining their aims of fighting their enemies. Some time before Islam, they had introduced the practice of making the sacred month lawful and postponing its sanctity to Safar. Thus they would make the sacred month lawful and declare the lawful month sacred, in order to match the number of the four months, as their poet said. He was Umayr ibn Qays, known as Jidhl al-Ta'an (the trunk of spear-thrusting):

"Ma'add has indeed known that my people
are the most noble of people, and that they have nobility.

Are we not the postponers (al-nasi'in) on Ma'add,
making the months of permission sacred?

Which people has not been struck by our vengeance?
And which people have we not bridled?"

[See: al-Sira al-Nabawiyya by Ibn Hisham (1/45).]

Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, the postponement is an increase in disbelief﴾. He said: The postponement (al-nasi') was that Junada ibn Awf ibn Umayya al-Kinani, who would attend the season every year, and whose kunya was "Abu Thumama," would call out: "Behold, Abu Thumama cannot be opposed or blamed. Behold, Safar of this year is lawful." So he would make it lawful for the people, and they would make Safar sacred one year and make Muharram sacred another year. That is the meaning of Allah's words: ﴿Indeed, the postponement is an increase in disbelief﴾ [up to His words: ﴿the disbelievers﴾]. And His words ﴿Indeed, the postponement is an increase in disbelief﴾ [[Addition from T, K, A, and al-Tabari.]] mean: they leave Muharram one year and make it sacred another year.

Al-Awfi also narrated similarly from Ibn Abbas.

Layth ibn Abi Sulaym said, from Mujahid: A man from Banu Kinana would come to the season every year on his donkey and say: "O people, I am not to be blamed nor opposed, and there is no rejection of what I say. We have made Muharram sacred and postponed Safar." Then the following year he would come and say the same statement, saying: "We have made Safar sacred and postponed Muharram." This is His words: ﴿so that they may match the number of what Allah has made sacred﴾, meaning the four, ﴿and so they make lawful what Allah has made unlawful﴾, by postponing this sacred month.

Similar was narrated from Abu Wa'il, al-Dahhak, and Qatada.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, the postponement is an increase in disbelief﴾ up to the end of the verse: This was a man from Banu Kinana called "al-Qalammas." In the Jahiliyya, they did not raid one another during the sacred month; a man would meet the killer of his father and would not extend his hand to him. When it was his turn, he said: "Let us set out." They said to him: "This is Muharram!" He said: "We will postpone it this year; these are two Safars. When next year comes, we will make them both sacred." He did that, and when the following year came, he said: "Do not raid during Safar; make it sacred along with Muharram; they are two sacred months."

This is a strange description of the postponement, and it is open to question, because in one year they would make only three months sacred according to this, while in the following year they would make five months sacred. How does this agree with His words: ﴿They make it lawful one year and make it sacred another year, so that they may match the number of what Allah has made sacred﴾?

A second strange description was also narrated from Mujahid. Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, the postponement is an increase in disbelief﴾ up to the end of the verse. He said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made Hajj obligatory in Dhu al-Hijja. He said: The polytheists used to name the months: Dhu al-Hijja, Muharram, Safar, Rabi', Rabi', Jumada, Jumada, Rajab, Sha'ban, Ramadan, Shawwal [[In A: "Shawwal."]], and Dhu al-Qa'da. They performed Hajj in Dhu al-Hijja once more, then they would remain silent about Muharram and not mention it. Then they would return and call Safar "Safar," then they would call Rajab "Jumada al-Akhira," then they would call Sha'ban "Ramadan," then they would call Shawwal "Ramadan," then they would call Dhu al-Qa'da "Shawwal," then they would call Dhu al-Hijja "Dhu al-Qa'da," then they would call Muharram "Dhu al-Hijja," and perform Hajj in it, and its name for them was Dhu al-Hijja. Then they returned to the same story, so they would perform Hajj in every month once every two years, until the Hajj of Abu Bakr coincided with Dhu al-Qa'da in the second of the two years [[In K, A: "Dhu al-Qa'da."]]. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) performed the Hajj he performed, and it coincided with Dhu al-Hijja. That is when the Prophet (ﷺ) said in his sermon: "Indeed, time has returned to its form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth."

What Mujahid said here is also open to question. How could the Hajj of Abu Bakr be valid if it occurred in Dhu al-Qa'da? And how could this be? Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And an announcement from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater Hajj that Allah is free of the polytheists, and so is His Messenger﴾ [al-Tawba: 3]. This announcement was made during the Hajj of Abu Bakr. If it had not been in Dhu al-Hijja, He would not have said ﴿the day of the greater Hajj﴾. Moreover, the postponement they practised does not necessarily require what he mentioned, namely the year turning around for them and their performing Hajj in every month once every two years, for the postponement occurs without this. When they made Muharram lawful one year, they made Safar sacred in its place; after it came Rabi' and Rabi', until the end of the year. The year remained in its state, with its order, its count, and its month names. Then in the following year they made Muharram sacred and left it sacred, followed by Safar, Rabi', and Rabi', until the end. So they made it lawful one year and made it sacred another year, so that they might match the number of what Allah had made sacred, thereby making lawful what Allah had made unlawful, that is, regarding the sanctity of four months of the year. However, sometimes they would advance the sanctity of the third of the three consecutive months, which is Muharram, and sometimes they would postpone it to Safar, that is, they would delay it.

We have already discussed His words (ﷺ): "Indeed, time has returned to its form on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, of which four are sacred: three consecutive ones, Dhu al-Qa'da, Dhu al-Hijja, and Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar." That is, the matter concerns the number of the months and the sanctity of those that are sacred among them, according to what preceded in the Book of Allah regarding the count and the succession, not as the ignorant Arabs relied upon, by distinguishing the sanctity of some of them through postponement of one over another. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Salih ibn Bishr ibn Salama al-Tabarani narrated to us, Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Musa ibn Ubayda narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn Umar, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood at al-Aqaba, and whomever Allah willed of the Muslims gathered to him. He praised Allah and extolled Him with what is worthy of Him. Then he said: "Indeed, the postponement is from Satan, an increase in disbelief, by which those who disbelieve are led astray. They make it lawful one year and make it sacred another year." So they would make Muharram sacred one year, and make Safar lawful and make Muharram lawful, and this is the postponement. [[In T, K, A: "Safar of it."]] [[Also narrated by Abu al-Shaykh al-Asbahani, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/188).]]

Imam Muhammad ibn Ishaq has spoken on this in his book "al-Sira" with good, useful, and excellent words. He said: The first to postpone the months among the Arabs, making lawful what Allah had made unlawful and making unlawful what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, had made lawful, was "al-Qalammas," who was Hudhayfa ibn Abd Mudrika Fuqaym [[In T, K, A: "Abd ibn Fuqaym."]] ibn Adi ibn Amir ibn Tha'laba ibn al-Harith ibn Malik ibn Kinana ibn Khuzayma ibn Mudrika ibn Ilyas ibn Mudar ibn Nizar ibn Ma'add ibn Adnan. After him, his son Abbad continued this practice, then after Abbad his son Qal' ibn Abbad, then his son Umayya ibn Qal', then his son Awf ibn Umayya, then his son Abu Thumama Junada ibn Awf, who was the last of them, and upon this Islam came. Whenever the Arabs finished their Hajj, they gathered around him, and he stood among them as a preacher. He made Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'da, and Dhu al-Hijja sacred, and he made Muharram lawful one year and put Safar in its place, and he made it sacred another year, so as to match the number of what Allah had made sacred, thereby making lawful what Allah had made unlawful. That is: and making unlawful what Allah had made lawful.

This is the beginning of a rebuke of those who stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the expedition of Tabuk, when the fruits had ripened and there was shade in the intense heat and the blazing of the summer heat. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿O you who believe, what is [the matter] with you that when it is said to you, "Go forth in the way of Allah," you adhere heavily to the earth?﴾ That is: when you are called to jihad in the way of Allah, ﴿you adhere heavily to the earth﴾, meaning you grew lazy and inclined to remain in ease, comfort, and the pleasant fruits. ﴿Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter?﴾ That is: what has come over you, that you have done this, being content with this world in place of the Hereafter?

Then the Blessed and Exalted One denounced the world and encouraged [desire for] the Hereafter, saying: ﴿Yet the enjoyment of the life of this world, compared to the Hereafter, is but little.﴾ As Imam Ahmad said:

Waki' and Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, both saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from Qays, from al-Mustawrid, brother of the Banu Fihr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The likeness of this world compared to the Hereafter is only like one of you dipping this finger of his into the sea, so let him see with what it returns," and he pointed with the index finger.

Muslim alone recorded it. [Al-Musnad (4/228) and Sahih Muslim, no. (2858).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Bishr ibn Muslim ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Himsi narrated to us, al-Rabi' ibn Rawh narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Wahbi narrated to us, Ziyad—meaning al-Jassas—narrated to us, from Abu Uthman, who said: I said, "O Abu Hurayrah, I heard from my brothers in Basra that you say: I heard the Prophet of Allah say, 'Indeed Allah rewards a good deed with a thousand thousand good deeds.'" Abu Hurayrah said: "Rather, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, 'Indeed Allah rewards a good deed with two thousand thousand good deeds.'" Then he recited this verse: ﴿Yet the enjoyment of the life of this world, compared to the Hereafter, is but little.﴾ [Also narrated by Abdullah ibn Ahmad in Zawa'id al-Zuhd, and Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/193).]

So the world, what has passed of it and what remains of it, is little in the sight of Allah.

Al-Thawri narrated from al-A'mash regarding the verse: ﴿Yet the enjoyment of the life of this world, compared to the Hereafter, is but little.﴾ He said: "Like the provision of a traveller."

And Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Hazim narrated from his father, who said: When death came to Abd al-Aziz ibn Marwan, he said: "Bring me my shroud in which I will be shrouded, that I may look at it." When it was placed before him, he looked at it and said: "Is there not for me, from the great [wealth] of the world, anything I can leave behind except this?" Then he turned his back and wept, saying: "Alas for you, O abode! If your abundance is indeed little, and if your little is indeed brief, then we are indeed in delusion from you."

Then Allah threatened those who abandon jihad, saying: ﴿If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called upon a tribe of the Arabs to go forth, but they hesitated, so Allah withheld the rain from them, and that was their punishment.

﴿And He will replace you with another people﴾, that is, to support His Prophet and establish His religion, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿If you turn away, He will replace you with another people, then they will not be like you﴾ [Muhammad: 38].

﴿And you will not harm Him at all﴾, that is, you will not harm Allah at all by your turning away from jihad, your reluctance, and your heaviness toward it. ﴿And Allah is over all things Competent﴾, that is, Able to grant victory over the enemies without you.

It has been said that this verse, and His saying: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ and His saying: ﴿It was not for the people of Medina and those around them of the Bedouins to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah﴾ [At-Tawbah: 120], are abrogated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And it is not [fitting] for the believers to go forth all together. Why should not a group from every division among them go forth?﴾ [At-Tawbah: 122]. This was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, al-Hasan, and Zayd ibn Aslam. Ibn Jarir rejected this and said: "This applies only to those whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called to jihad, so it became obligatory upon them, and if they abandoned it they would be punished for it."

This view has its merit, and Allah, glory be to Him, the Exalted, knows best the correct position.
