Ibn Jarir rejected this and said: "This applies only to those whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called to jihad, so it became obligatory upon them, and if they abandoned it they would be punished for it."

This view has its merit, and Allah, glory be to Him, the Exalted, knows best the correct position.

Almighty Allah says: "If you do not help him" — that is, if you do not help His Messenger — then indeed Allah is his Helper, his Supporter, his Sufficiency and his Protector, just as He took charge of his victory when "those who disbelieved expelled him, the second of two [when they were both in the cave]." [The bracketed words are an addition from manuscript K.] That was in the year of the Hijrah, when the polytheists resolved to kill him, or imprison him, or banish him. So he went out from them fleeing, in the company of his close friend and companion Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah, and they took refuge in the Cave of Thawr for three days, so that the pursuers who had set out on their trail would turn back, and then they would travel toward Madinah. Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, grew anxious that someone might discover them and reach the Messenger with harm. The Prophet ﷺ kept calming him and steadying him, saying: "O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two whose third is Allah?" As Imam Ahmad said:

Ahmad related to us: Affan related to us, Hammam related to us, Thabit informed us, from Anas, that Abu Bakr related to him, saying: I said to the Prophet ﷺ while we were in the cave: "If one of them were to look down at his feet, he would see us beneath his feet." He said: He (the Prophet) said: "O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two whose third is Allah?"

Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in the Two Sahihs. [Musnad 1/4; Sahih al-Bukhari no. 3653; Sahih Muslim no. 2381.]

Therefore He said: "Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon him" — that is, His support and His aid upon him. That is, upon the Messenger, according to the more well-known of the two opinions. It was also said: upon Abu Bakr, and this is related from Ibn Abbas and others, who said: because the Messenger always had tranquillity with him. This does not preclude a renewed, specific tranquillity in that situation. For this reason He said: "and strengthened him with hosts you did not see" — that is, the angels — "and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah is the highest."

Ibn Abbas said: "the word of those who disbelieved" means shirk, and "the word of Allah" is: there is no god but Allah.

In the Two Sahihs, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about a man who fights out of bravery, fights out of zealotry, and fights for show: which of these is in the way of Allah? He said: "Whoever fights so that the word of Allah is the highest, he is in the way of Allah." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2810; Sahih Muslim no. 1904.]

* *

His saying "And Allah is Almighty" — that is, in His retribution and His victory, unassailable in His dominion; none is wronged who seeks refuge at His door and takes shelter in holding fast to His address. "All-Wise" — in His sayings and His deeds.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 9, verse 41:

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from his father, from Abu al-Duha Muslim ibn Subaih: "This verse: ﴿Go forth, whether light or heavy﴾ was the first thing revealed of Surat Bara'ah."

Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman said, from his father, who said: A Hadrami claimed that it was mentioned to him that some people, one of whom might be sick or old, would say: "I am not sinning [by staying back]," so Allah revealed: ﴿Go forth, whether light or heavy﴾, the verse.

Allah the Exalted commanded general mobilization (nafir 'amm) along with the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, in the year of the Battle of Tabuk, to fight the enemies of Allah from among the disbelieving Romans of the People of the Book. He made it obligatory upon the believers to set out with him in every condition, in ease and hardship, whether eager or reluctant, saying: ﴿Go forth, whether light or heavy﴾.

'Ali ibn Zayd said, from Anas, from Abu Talhah: "Elderly and young. I do not hear that Allah has excused anyone." Then he went out to Syria and fought until he was killed.

In another narration: Abu Talhah recited Surat Bara'ah, and when he came to this verse: ﴿Go forth, whether light or heavy, and strive with your wealth and your lives in the way of Allah﴾, he said: "I see that our Lord is calling us to mobilize, the old and the young. Equip me, my sons." His sons said: "May Allah have mercy on you, you fought with the Messenger of Allah until he died, and with Abu Bakr until he died, and with 'Umar until he died, so we will fight on your behalf." He refused, so he boarded the sea and died. They could not find an island to bury him in until after nine days, and he had not changed, so they buried him there.

It is similarly narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Abu Salih, al-Hasan al-Basri, Shamr ibn 'Atiyyah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Sha'bi and Zayd ibn Aslam that they said in explaining this verse: ﴿Go forth, whether light or heavy﴾: "Elderly and young." Likewise 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, Muqatil ibn Hayyan and others said so.

Mujahid said: "Young and old, and rich and poor." Abu Salih and others said likewise.

al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah said: "Those who are busy and those who are not busy."

al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Go forth, whether light or heavy﴾: "He means: go forth whether energetic or not energetic." Qatadah said likewise.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid: ﴿Go forth, whether light or heavy﴾: "They said: 'Indeed among us are the heavy, those with needs, those with responsibilities, those occupied, and those for whom the matter is easy.' So Allah revealed, and refused to excuse them unless they go forth, light or heavy, and regardless of their condition."

al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri also said: "In hardship and in ease." All of this is among the implications of the generality of the verse, and this is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir.

Imam Abu 'Amr al-Awza'i said: "If the mobilization is toward the frontiers of the Romans, the people go forth to them light and mounted; and if the mobilization is toward these coasts, they go forth to them light and heavy, mounted and on foot." This is a detailed treatment of the matter.

It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, 'Ata' al-Khurasani and others that this verse is abrogated by His saying: ﴿Why should not a group from every section of them go forth﴾. The discussion of this will come, Allah willing.

al-Suddi said regarding His saying: ﴿Go forth, whether light or heavy﴾: "Wealthy and poor, strong and weak." On that day a man came to him, whom they claimed was al-Miqdad, and he was large and heavy, and he complained to him and asked him to permit him, but he refused, and so this verse was revealed that day: ﴿Go forth, whether light or heavy﴾. When this verse was revealed, its matter weighed heavily upon the people, so Allah abrogated it, saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who do not find anything to spend, when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger﴾ [At-Tawbah: 91].

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub related to me, Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, Ayyub related to us, from Muhammad, who said: Abu Ayyub witnessed Badr with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and then he did not lag behind from any expedition of the Muslims except that he was among the others, except for one year. He said: Abu Ayyub used to say: "Allah said: ﴿Go forth, whether light or heavy﴾, so I do not find myself except light or heavy."

Ibn Jarir said: Sa'id ibn 'Umar al-Sakuni related to me, Baqiyyah related to us, Hariz related to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Maysarah related to me, Abu Rashid al-Hubrani related to me, who said: I met al-Miqdam ibn al-Aswad, the rider of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, sitting on a coffin from the coffins of the money-changers in Homs, and his size had overflowed beyond it, and he intended to go on expedition. I said to him: "Allah has indeed excused you." He said: "The Surah of the Dispatches came upon us: ﴿Go forth, whether light or heavy﴾."

Ibn Jarir also said, saying: Hayyan ibn Zayd al-Shar'abi related to me, who said: We went forth with Safwan ibn 'Amr, who was governor of Homs before al-Afsus, to al-Jarajimah. I met an elderly man, very frail, whose eyebrows had fallen over his eyes, from the people of Damascus, on his mount, among those who raided. I approached him and said: "O uncle, Allah has indeed excused you." He said: He raised his eyebrows and said: "O nephew, Allah has called us to go forth, light and heavy. Indeed, whomever Allah loves, He tests; then Allah restores him and keeps him alive, and Allah only tests from among His servants those who give thanks, endure, remember, and worship none but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." Then the Exalted encouraged spending in His way and giving up souls for His pleasure and the pleasure of His Messenger, saying: ﴿And strive with your wealth and your lives in the way of Allah. That is better for you, if you only knew﴾, meaning: this is better for you in this world and the Hereafter, and because you will pay a little in expenditure, Allah will enrich you with the wealth of your enemy in this world, along with the honour stored up for you in the Hereafter, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah guarantees for the one who fights in His way, if He takes him, that He will admit him to Paradise, or return him to his home with what he has gained of reward or booty."

For this reason the Exalted said: ﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you, and it is hateful to you. But it may be that you hate a thing and it is good for you; and it may be that you love a thing and it is bad for you. And Allah knows, while you know not﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 216].

Of this kind is what Imam Ahmad narrated:

Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, from Humayd, from Anas, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said to a man: "Embrace Islam." He said: "I find myself averse." He said: "Embrace Islam even if you are averse."

Allah the Exalted says, rebuking those who stayed behind from the Prophet [In manuscript A: "the Messenger of Allah"] (ﷺ) during the expedition of Tabuk, and who remained behind from the Prophet (ﷺ) after asking his permission in that matter, showing that they were people with excuses when they were not. So He said: ﴿Had it been a near gain and a moderate journey, they would have followed you.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: a near spoil (ghanimah). ﴿And a moderate journey﴾ means near as well. ﴿They would have followed you﴾ means they would have come with you for that. ﴿But the distance seemed long to them﴾ means the distance to al-Sham. ﴿And they will swear by Allah﴾ means to you, when you return to them: ﴿If we had been able, we would have gone out with you.﴾ means if we had had no excuses, we would have gone out with you. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They destroy themselves, and Allah knows that they are liars.﴾

"Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abi narrated to us, Abu Husayn ibn [Yahya ibn] Sulayman al-Razi narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna narrated to us, from Mis'ar, from 'Awn, who said: Have you heard of a rebuke more gentle than this? He began with pardon before the rebuke, saying: ﴿May Allah pardon you. Why did you grant them permission?﴾ Muwarriq al-'Ijli and others also said the same.

Qatada said: He rebuked him as you hear, then He revealed the verse in Surah an-Nur, granting him leave to permit them if he wished: ﴿So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs, give permission to whom you will among them﴾ [an-Nur: 62]. The same was also related from 'Ata' al-Khurasani.

Mujahid said: This verse was revealed concerning people who said: "Ask the Messenger of Allah for permission; if he grants you leave, sit at home, and if he does not grant you leave, sit at home."

And for this reason He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Until it becomes clear to you who are truthful⦋﴾ meaning: in presenting their excuses, ﴿and you know the liars﴾. He, the Exalted, says: Why did you not leave them alone when they asked your permission, so that you would not grant permission to any of them to remain behind, in order that you might know the truthful among them in displaying obedience to you from the liar? For they had been insisting on remaining behind from the expedition [even if you did not grant them permission to do so]. For this reason, He, the Exalted, informed that no one who believes in Allah and His Messenger asks your permission to remain behind from the expedition. So He said: ﴿Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask your permission [to be excused] from striving with their wealth and their lives﴾, because those people regard jihad as an act of nearness to Allah, and when He urged them to it, they hastened and complied. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the righteous.⦋﴾ ﴿It is only those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day who ask your permission﴾ meaning: to remain behind, from among those who have no excuse, ﴿and whose hearts are in doubt﴾ meaning: they doubted the soundness of what you brought them, ﴿so they are hesitating in their doubt﴾ meaning: they are bewildered, advancing one foot and withdrawing the other, having no firm footing in anything. They are a bewildered, perishing people, belonging neither to these nor to those. ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, you will not find for him a way.⦋﴾

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And if they had intended to go forth﴾, that is, with you to the battle, ﴿they would have prepared for it some preparation﴾, that is, they would have made ready for it. ﴿But Allah disliked their being sent forth﴾, that is, He hated that they should go out with you by decree, ﴿so He held them back﴾, that is, He delayed them, ﴿and it was said, "Sit with those who sit"﴾, that is, by decree.

Then Allah explained the reason for His dislike of their going out with the believers. He said: ﴿Had they gone forth among you, they would not have increased you except in corruption﴾, that is, because they are cowardly and forsaken, ﴿and they would have hastened between you, seeking to cause dissension among you﴾, that is, they would have hurried about among you with tale-bearing, enmity and sedition. ﴿And among you are those who listen to them﴾, that is, those who obey them and approve of their speech and talk, taking their advice, even though they do not know their true condition. This leads to the occurrence of evil among the believers and great corruption.

Mujahid, Zayd ibn Aslam and Ibn Jarir said: ﴿And among you are those who listen to them﴾ means spies who listen to news for them and convey it to them.

This meaning is not confined to their going out with them; rather, it is general in all circumstances. The first meaning is more apparent given the context, and this is the view of Qatadah and other exegetes.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "It has reached me that among those who sought permission from the nobles among them were Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and al-Jadd ibn Qays, who were nobles among their people. Allah held them back, knowing about them, from going out with him, lest they corrupt his army. In his army were people who loved them and obeyed them in what they called them to, because of their nobility among them. So He said: ﴿And among you are those who listen to them﴾."

Then Allah informed of the completeness of His knowledge, saying: ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾. He thus informed that He knows what has occurred, what will occur, and what has not occurred, and how it would have occurred had it occurred. Therefore He said: ﴿Had they gone forth among you, they would not have increased you except in corruption﴾, informing of their condition as it would have been had they gone forth, though in fact they did not go forth. As He said: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾ [Al-An'am: 28]. And He said: ﴿And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were refusing﴾ [Al-Anfal: 23]. And He said: ﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," few of them would have done it. But if they had done what they were admonished to do, it would have been better for them and stronger in firmness. And then We would have given them from Us a great reward and guided them to a straight path﴾ [An-Nisa: 66-68]. The verses on this are many.

Allah says, urging His Prophet (peace be upon him) against the hypocrites: ﴿Indeed, they had sought discord before, and they had upended affairs for you.﴾ That is: they truly applied their thinking and turned their opinions over in plotting against you, against your companions, and against the forsaking and extinguishing of your religion, for a long period. This was from the first arrival of the Prophet (ﷺ) in Madinah, when the Arabs shot at him with one bow, and the Jews of Madinah and its hypocrites waged war against him. Then, when Allah gave him victory on the day of Badr and raised high His word, ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions said: "This matter has indeed gained ascendancy." So they entered Islam outwardly, but whenever Allah strengthened Islam and its people, that enraged them and displeased them. For this reason Allah says: ﴿Until the truth came and the command of Allah prevailed, while they were averse.﴾

Allah the Exalted says: "And among the hypocrites is one who says to you, O Muhammad: ﴿Grant me leave﴾ to stay behind, ﴿and do not put me to trial﴾ by going out with you, because of the slave-girls from the women of the Romans." Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Surely they have fallen into trial already﴾, meaning: they have already fallen into trial by this statement of theirs.

As Muhammad ibn Ishaq related from al-Zuhri, Yazid ibn Ruman, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah and others, they said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said one day, while he was preparing for the expedition, to al-Jadd ibn Qays, brother of Banu Salamah: "Would you join us this year in fighting the Banu al-Asfar (the Byzantines)?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you grant me leave and not put me to trial? By Allah, my people know that no man is more prone to being captivated by women than I am, and I fear that if I see the women of the Banu al-Asfar I will not be able to restrain myself from them." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned away from him and said: "I have granted you leave." Concerning al-Jadd ibn Qays this was revealed: ﴿And among them is one who says, "Grant me leave and do not put me to trial"﴾, the verse, meaning: even if he fears only the women of the Banu al-Asfar, and that is not the real reason, then the trial he has already fallen into by staying behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and by preferring his own self over his self is greater.

Likewise it was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others that it was revealed concerning al-Jadd ibn Qays. Al-Jadd ibn Qays was one of the nobles of Banu Salamah. In the Sahih it is reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Who is your chief, O Banu Salamah?" They said: "Al-Jadd ibn Qays, but we consider him stingy (nubakhkhiluh)." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And what disease is more severe than stinginess? Rather, your chief is the fair-complexioned, curly-haired young man, Bishr ibn al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And indeed, Hell encompasses the disbelievers﴾, meaning: there is no escape for them from it, no evasion, and no refuge.

Allah, blessed and exalted is He, informs His Prophet of these people's enmity towards him, because whatever good befalls him, meaning victory, triumph and success over the enemies, which pleases him and his companions, displeases them. ﴿And if a misfortune befalls you, they say: "We had already taken our precaution before this,"﴾ meaning: we had already guarded ourselves against following him before this. ﴿And they turn away while they are rejoicing.﴾ So Allah the Exalted guided His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, to how to answer them regarding this complete enmity of theirs, and He said: ﴿Say﴾, meaning to them: ﴿"Nothing will befall us except what Allah has decreed for us."﴾ Meaning: we are under the will and decree of Allah. ﴿He is our Protector﴾, meaning: our Master and our Refuge. ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾ Meaning: we too rely upon Him, and He is sufficient for us and the best Disposer of affairs.

Allah, blessed and exalted is He, informs His Prophet of these people's enmity towards him, because whatever good befalls him, meaning victory, triumph and success over the enemies, which pleases him and his companions, displeases them. ﴿And if a misfortune befalls you, they say: "We had already taken our precaution before this,"﴾ meaning: we had already guarded ourselves against following him before this. ﴿And they turn away while they are rejoicing.﴾ So Allah the Exalted guided His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, to how to answer them regarding this complete enmity of theirs, and He said: ﴿Say﴾, meaning to them: ﴿"Nothing will befall us except what Allah has decreed for us."﴾ Meaning: we are under the will and decree of Allah. ﴿He is our Protector﴾, meaning: our Master and our Refuge. ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾ Meaning: we too rely upon Him, and He is sufficient for us and the best Disposer of affairs.

Allah the Exalted says: Say (O Muhammad) to them: "Do you await for us anything but one of the two best outcomes?" That is, do you wait for us anything except one of the two good things: martyrdom or victory over you. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and others. "And we await for you that Allah will afflict you with a punishment from Himself or at our hands." That is, we wait for one of two things concerning you: either Allah will strike you with a calamity from Himself, or it will be at our hands, by taking you captive or by killing you. "So wait; indeed we are waiting along with you."

* *

As for His saying: "Say: Spend willingly or unwillingly; it will never be accepted from you. Indeed, you have been a defiantly disobedient people." That is, whatever you spend, whether willingly or unwillingly, it will not be accepted from you, "for you have been a defiantly disobedient people."

Then Allah informed of the reason for this, which is that their spending is not accepted: "Nothing prevents their contributions from being accepted except that they have disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger." That is, [they have disbelieved] (an addition from manuscript A), and deeds are only valid with faith. "And they do not come to prayer except while lazy, and they do not spend except while unwilling." That is, they have no sound intention, and no determination in action.

The truthful one, whose truthfulness is affirmed, has informed us that Allah does not tire until you tire, and that He is Good and accepts only what is good. Therefore Allah does not accept from these people any spending or any deed, because He only accepts from the God-fearing (al-muttaqun).

Allah says to His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him: ﴿So let not their wealth nor their children impress you.﴾ As Allah said elsewhere: ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward that with which We have provided [some] categories of them, the splendor of the worldly life, by which We may test them. But the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting.﴾ [Ta-Ha: 131] And He said: ﴿Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children is [because] We hasten for them good things? Rather, they do not perceive.﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 55-56]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Allah only wants to punish them thereby in the worldly life﴾, al-Hasan al-Basri said: "By their zakat, and by spending from them in the way of Allah."

Qatadah said: "This is of the inversion (al-muqaddam wa al-mu'akhkhar, transposition of word order), its meaning being: ﴿So let not their wealth nor their children impress you﴾ [in the worldly life], ﴿Allah only wants to punish them thereby﴾ [in the Hereafter]."

Ibn Jarir chose the saying of al-Hasan, and it is the strong, good opinion.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and that their souls depart while they are disbelievers﴾, meaning: He wants them to die upon disbelief when they die, so that this will be more painful for them and more severe for their punishment, we seek refuge in Allah from that. This is from the category of gradual leading (istidraj) for them in what they are in.

Allah informs His Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, about their anxiety, their terror, their fear and their panic: that they ﴿swear by Allah that they are surely of you﴾, with a strongly emphatic oath, ﴿but they are not of you﴾, i.e., in reality. ﴿Rather, they are a people who are fearful﴾, i.e., it is this fear that moved them to swear. ﴿If they could find a refuge﴾, i.e., a fortress in which to take shelter and a stronghold in which to guard themselves, ﴿or caves﴾, which are those in the mountains, ﴿or a place of entry﴾, which is a tunnel or passage into the earth. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said this regarding the three: ﴿they would turn towards it while rushing headlong﴾, i.e., they would hasten off to depart from you, because they only mix with you out of hatred, not love, and they wish that they did not mix with you. But necessity has its rulings. For this reason they are constantly in distress, sorrow and grief, because Islam and its people are always in might, victory and exaltation. Therefore, whenever the believers rejoice, that troubles them, so they wish not to mix with the believers. For this reason He said: ﴿If they could find a refuge, or caves, or a place of entry, they would turn towards it while rushing headlong.﴾

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, regarding the words of Allah Most High: "And among them are some who find fault with you concerning the distribution of the charities (ṣadaqāt)."

Allah Most High says: "And among them" (wa-minhum), i.e., among the hypocrites, "are those who find fault with you" (yalmizuka), i.e., criticize you, "concerning" the distribution (qasm) of "the charities" when you distribute them, and accuse you in that matter. They are the accused, the ones who are discredited (al-ma'bunūn). Despite this, they do not deny the religion; they only object out of concern for their own share. Therefore, "if they are given from them, they are pleased, but if they are not given from them, behold, they become angry" (yaskhaṭūn), i.e., they become angry on their own behalf.

Ibn Jurayj said: Dawud ibn Abi 'Asim informed me, saying: A charity was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he distributed it here and there until it was gone. He said: Behind him was a man from the Ansar who said, "Is this distribution just?" So this verse was revealed.

Qatadah said concerning His words, "And among them are those who find fault with you concerning the charities": he means, "And among them are those who slander you concerning the charities." It has been mentioned to us that a man from the people of the desert, recently come from a Bedouin background, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was distributing gold and silver, and said: "O Muhammad, by Allah, if Allah has commanded you to be just, then you have not been just!" The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "Woe to you! Who will be just if I am not?" Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "Beware of this one and his like, for among my nation there will be those like him, who recite the Qur'an but it does not pass beyond their throats. When they go out, kill them; then when they go out, kill them; then when they go out, kill them." It has also been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to say: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, I do not give you anything, nor do I withhold it from you; I am only a treasurer."

What Qatadah mentioned resembles what the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Sa'id, concerning the story of Dhu al-Khuwaysirah, whose name was Hurqus, when he objected to the Prophet ﷺ at the time he distributed the spoils of Hunayn. He said to him: "Be just, for you have not been just." He replied: "Indeed I would be a loser and a failure if I were not just." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, seeing him turn away: "There will come forth from the offspring of this man a people, whose prayer you will consider insignificant compared to their prayer, and whose fasting you will consider insignificant compared to their fasting. They will pass through the religion as an arrow passes through its target. Wherever you meet them, kill them, for they are the worst of creatures slain beneath the sky." And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3610), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1064).]

Then Allah Most High said, admonishing them toward what is better for them than that, saying: "And if only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and said, 'Sufficient for us is Allah; Allah will give us of His bounty, and [so will] His Messenger. Indeed, we are toward Allah inclined.'" This noble verse contains great etiquette and a noble secret, as it makes contentment with what Allah and His Messenger give, and reliance upon Allah alone, the matter of His saying: "and said, 'Sufficient for us is Allah.'" Likewise, turning in desire to Allah alone for success in obeying the Messenger, complying with his commands, abstaining from his prohibitions, affirming his reports, and following his example.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, regarding the words of Allah Most High: "And among them are some who find fault with you concerning the distribution of the charities (ṣadaqāt)."

Allah Most High says: "And among them" (wa-minhum), i.e., among the hypocrites, "are those who find fault with you" (yalmizuka), i.e., criticize you, "concerning" the distribution (qasm) of "the charities" when you distribute them, and accuse you in that matter. They are the accused, the ones who are discredited (al-ma'bunūn). Despite this, they do not deny the religion; they only object out of concern for their own share. Therefore, "if they are given from them, they are pleased, but if they are not given from them, behold, they become angry" (yaskhaṭūn), i.e., they become angry on their own behalf.

Ibn Jurayj said: Dawud ibn Abi 'Asim informed me, saying: A charity was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he distributed it here and there until it was gone. He said: Behind him was a man from the Ansar who said, "Is this distribution just?" So this verse was revealed.

Qatadah said concerning His words, "And among them are those who find fault with you concerning the charities": he means, "And among them are those who slander you concerning the charities." It has been mentioned to us that a man from the people of the desert, recently come from a Bedouin background, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was distributing gold and silver, and said: "O Muhammad, by Allah, if Allah has commanded you to be just, then you have not been just!" The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "Woe to you! Who will be just if I am not?" Then the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "Beware of this one and his like, for among my nation there will be those like him, who recite the Qur'an but it does not pass beyond their throats. When they go out, kill them; then when they go out, kill them; then when they go out, kill them." It has also been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to say: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, I do not give you anything, nor do I withhold it from you; I am only a treasurer."

He said to him: "Be just, for you have not been just." He replied: "Indeed I would be a loser and a failure if I were not just." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, seeing him turn away: "There will come forth from the offspring of this man a people, whose prayer you will consider insignificant compared to their prayer, and whose fasting you will consider insignificant compared to their fasting. They will pass through the religion as an arrow passes through its target. Wherever you meet them, kill them, for they are the worst of creatures slain beneath the sky." And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3610), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1064).]
