Indeed, we are toward Allah inclined.'" This noble verse contains great etiquette and a noble secret, as it makes contentment with what Allah and His Messenger give, and reliance upon Allah alone, the matter of His saying: "and said, 'Sufficient for us is Allah.'" Likewise, turning in desire to Allah alone for success in obeying the Messenger, complying with his commands, abstaining from his prohibitions, affirming his reports, and following his example.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 9, verse 60 (part 1 of 2):

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the objection of the ignorant hypocrites against the Prophet ﷺ and their finding fault with him concerning the distribution of the charities (sadaqat), He explained that it is He Who distributed them and stated their ruling, and He took charge of their affair Himself, and did not leave their distribution to anyone other than Himself. So He divided them among those mentioned, as Imam Abu Dawud related in his Sunan from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad ibn An'am (and in it there is weakness), from Ziyad ibn Nu'aym, from Ziyad ibn al-Harith al-Sudai, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ and pledged allegiance to him. A man came and said: "Give me something from the charity." He said to him: "Allah has not been pleased with the judgment of a prophet or of anyone else concerning the charities until He Himself judged regarding them. So He divided them into eight categories. If you are among those categories, I will give you." [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1630)]

The scholars differed regarding these eight categories: is it obligatory to distribute to all of them, or to as many of them as possible? There are two opinions:

The first: that it is obligatory, and this is the view of al-Shafi'i and a group.

The second: that it is not obligatory to cover all of them; rather it is permissible to give to one of them, and to give the entire charity even while the others are present. This is the view of Malik and a group of the early and later scholars, among them: Umar, Hudhayfah, Ibn Abbas, Abu al-Aliyah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Maymun ibn Mihran.

Ibn Jarir said: "This is the view of the general body of scholars." Accordingly, I have mentioned the categories here only to explain the recipients, not to make covering all of them obligatory in giving.

The arguments and evidences for these positions have a different place, and Allah knows best.

The fuqara' (the poor) were mentioned first here because, according to the well-known view, they are in greater need than the rest, due to the severity of their destitution and need. According to Abu Hanifah, the miskin (the needy) is in a worse condition than the faqir, and this is as he said. Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub related to me, Ibn Ulayyah related to us, Ibn Awn informed us, from Muhammad, who said: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The faqir is not the one who has no property, but the faqir is the one whose earning has been cut off (al-akhlaq al-kasb)." Ibn Ulayyah said: "al-akhlaq" means al-mahraf (one deprived) in our understanding. [Tafsir al-Tabari (14/308)]

However, the majority hold the opposite. It is related from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan al-Basri, and Ibn Zayd. Ibn Jarir and others chose that the faqir is the one who is abstinent and does not ask people for anything, and the miskin is the one who asks, goes around, and follows people.

Qatadah said: The faqir is one who has a disability (zamanah), and the miskin is one who is physically healthy.

Al-Thawri related from Mansur, from Ibrahim: "They are the poor of the Muhajirun." Sufyan al-Thawri said: meaning: and the Bedouins are not given anything from it.

Similarly it is related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza.

Ikrimah said: "Do not call the poor among the Muslims miskin; the miskin are the miskin of the People of the Book."

Let us mention hadiths relating to each of the eight categories.

As for "the poor" (al-fuqara'): from Ibn Amr [in T, K, A: "Ibn Umar"] who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Charity is not lawful for a rich person, nor for one with sound strength." Related by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi. [Musnad (2/164), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1634), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (652)]

Also Ahmad, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah from Abu Hurayrah, the same. [Musnad (2/377), Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/99), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1839)]

And from Ubayd Allah ibn Adi ibn al-Khiyar: that two men informed him that they came to the Prophet ﷺ asking him for charity, so he looked at them and saw that they were strong, and said: "If you wish, I will give you, but there is no share in it for the rich or for the strong earner."
Related by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa'i with a good, strong chain. [Musnad (4/224), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1633), Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/99)]

Ibn Abi Hatim said in Kitab al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil: Abu Bakr al-Absi said: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, recited: ﴿Charities are only for the poor﴾ and said: "They are the People of the Book." [addition from T, K, A] Umar ibn Nafi' related from him, saying: I heard my father say that. [al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil (9/341), and there is a gap there.]

I say: This is a very strange view, assuming the chain is sound, for this Abu Bakr, although Abu Hatim did not explicitly state his unknown status, is in the position of an unknown narrator.

As for al-Masakin (the needy): from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The miskin is not this wanderer who goes around the people, and a morsel or two turns him away, or a date or two." They said: "Then who is the miskin, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The one who does not find sufficient wealth to suffice him, and whose condition is not known so that charity is given to him, and who does not ask people for anything."
Related by the two Shaykhs, al-Bukhari and Muslim. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1479), Sahih Muslim no. (1039)]

As for those employed to collect it (al-'amilina 'alayha): they are the tax collectors and agents, who deserve a portion of it for that work. It is not permissible for them to be from the relatives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, those for whom charity is forbidden, due to what is established in Sahih Muslim from Abd al-Muttalib ibn Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith: that he and al-Fadl ibn Abbas went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him to appoint them over the charity, and he said: "Charity is not lawful for Muhammad or the family of Muhammad; it is only the filth of the people." [Sahih Muslim no. (1072)]

As for those whose hearts are to be reconciled (al-mu'allafah qulubuhum): there are categories. Among them are those given so that they may embrace Islam, as the Prophet ﷺ gave Safwan ibn Umayyah from the booty of Hunayn, though he had witnessed it as a polytheist. He said: "He kept giving me until he became the dearest of people to me, after he had been the most hateful of people to me," as Imam Ahmad said:

Zakariya ibn Adi related to us, Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Yunus, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Safwan ibn Umayyah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me on the day of Hunayn, and he was the most hateful of people to me, and he kept giving me until he became the dearest of people to me.

Muslim and al-Tirmidhi also related it from the hadith of Yunus, from al-Zuhri, with the same wording. [Musnad (6/465), Sahih Muslim no. (2313), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (666)]

Among them are those given so that their Islam may become good and their hearts may be firm, as he also gave on the day of Hunayn a group of the notables and chiefs of the Tulaqa': a hundred camels each, and he said: "Indeed I give to a man while another is more beloved to me than him, out of fear that Allah will throw him on his face into the Fire of Hell." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1478), from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him.]

In the two Sahihs from Abu Sa'id: that Ali sent to the Prophet ﷺ a piece of gold ore from its earth from Yemen, and he divided it among four men: al-Aqra' ibn Habis, Uyaynah ibn Badr, Alqamah ibn Ulathah, and Zayd al-Khayr, and he said: "I am reconciling their hearts." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3344), Sahih Muslim no. (1064)]

Among them are those given in hope of the Islam of their peers. Among them are those given to collect charities from those near them, or to repel harm from the borders of the Muslim lands from the outskirts of the lands. The detailed treatment of this belongs in the books of furu' (jurisprudence), and Allah knows best.

Is it permissible to give to the mu'allafah for Islam after the Prophet ﷺ? There is disagreement about this. It is related from Umar, Amir al-Sha'bi, and a group that they are not to be given after him, because Allah has honoured Islam and its people, established them in the lands, and subdued the necks of the servants to them.

Others said: rather they are to be given, because peace and blessings be upon him gave to them after the conquest of Makkah and the defeat of Hawazin, and this is a matter that may be needed, so it is directed to them.

As for al-Riqab (captives/slaves): it is related from al-Hasan al-Basri, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Nakha'i, al-Zuhri, and Ibn Zayd that they are the mukatabun (slaves under contract for manumission). It is also related from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari something similar, and this is the view of al-Shafi'i and al-Layth.

Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan said: "There is no harm in freeing a slave (riqabah) from zakat." This is the position of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Malik, and Ishaq; that is, the riqab is more general than giving to a mukatab, or buying a slave and freeing him independently. Numerous hadiths have come concerning the reward for manumission and releasing a slave, and that Allah frees, for each limb of the slave, a limb of the one who freed him, even the private part for the private part; and this is only because the recompense is of the same kind as the deed: ﴿And you are only recompensed for what you used to do﴾ [al-Saffat: 39].

From Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Three are a right upon Allah to help: the one who fights in the way of Allah, the mukatab who wishes to pay, and the one who marries wishing chastity."
Related by Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan except Abu Dawud. [Musnad (2/251), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1655), Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/61), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2518); al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith."]

In the Musnad, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, who said: A man came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, guide me to a deed that brings me near to Paradise and keeps me far from the Fire." He said: "Free the soul (nasamah) and release the captive (raqabah)." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, are they not one and the same?" He said: "No. Freeing the soul is that you alone free it, and releasing the captive is that you help with its price." [Musnad (4/299)]

As for al-Gharimun (those in debt): they are of several kinds. Among them are those who take on a debt (hamalah) or guarantee a debt and are obligated to it so that it consumes their wealth, or who incur expenses in paying their debt, or in disobedience and then repent; these are given from it. The basis of this chapter is the hadith of Qabisah ibn Mukhariq al-Hilali, who said: I took on a debt (hamalah), so I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him about it, and he said: "Remain until charity comes to us, and we will order it for you." Then he said: "O Qabisah, begging is not lawful except for one of three: a man who took on a debt, so begging became lawful for him until he obtains it, then he refrains; and a man whom a calamity struck and destroyed his wealth, so begging became lawful for him until he obtains sustenance (qiwam) from his livelihood, or he said: sufficiency (sidad) from his livelihood; and a man whom poverty struck until three wise men from his people testify that poverty has struck so-and-so, so begging became lawful for him until he obtains sustenance or sufficiency from his livelihood. Other than these, begging is unlawful (suht), and its taker consumes it unlawfully." Related by Muslim. [Sahih Muslim no. (1044)]

And from Abu Sa'id, who said: A man was afflicted in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with losses in fruit that he had bought, and his debt grew large, so the Prophet ﷺ said: "Give charity to him." People gave charity, but it did not reach the amount to pay off his debt, so the Prophet ﷺ said to his creditors: "Take what you find, and you have no right to more than that." Related by Muslim. [Sahih Muslim no. (1556)]

Imam Ahmad said: Abdus-Samad narrated to us, Sadaqah ibn Musa informed us, from Abu Imran al-Jawni, from Qays ibn Zayd, from the judge of the two cities [[In A: "al-Misriyyin".]], from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the Day of Resurrection Allah will summon the debtor, and he will be made to stand before Him. He will say: 'O son of Adam, why did you take this debt? And why did you squander people's rights?' He will say: 'O Lord, You know that I took it and did not eat or drink with it, and I did not squander it, but it came into my hands either by burning, theft, or loss.' Allah will say: 'My servant has spoken the truth. I am most worthy to settle on your behalf today.' Then Allah will bring something and place it in one pan of his scale, and his good deeds will outweigh his bad deeds, and he will enter Paradise by the grace of Allah and His mercy." [[Al-Musnad (1/197, 198).]]

As for "in the way of Allah" (fi sabil Allah): among them are the warriors (al-ghuzat) who have no share in the register (al-diwan). According to Imam Ahmad, al-Hasan, and Ishaq, the Hajj is also part of the way of Allah, based on a hadith.

Likewise, ibn al-sabil (the wayfarer): he is the traveller passing through a land who has nothing with which to meet the cost of his journey, so he is given from the zakat what suffices him to reach his homeland, even if he has wealth [at home]. The same ruling applies to one who wishes to begin a journey from his own land and has nothing with him; he is given from the zakat funds what suffices him for his going and returning. The evidence for this is the verse, and what Imam Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated through Ma'mar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Charity is not lawful for a rich person except for five: one who works to collect it, or a man who buys it with his own wealth, or one burdened with debt, or one who fights in the way of Allah, or a poor person to whom something of it is given as a gift and who then gives it to a rich person." [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1635), and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (1841).]]

The two Sufyans also narrated it from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata', as a mursal report. And Abu Dawud has, from Atiyyah al-Awfi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Charity is not lawful for a rich person except in the way of Allah, and for the wayfarer, or a poor neighbour who gives you a gift or invites you." [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1637). Atiyyah al-Awfi is weak.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿a obligation from Allah﴾ means a ruling determined by Allah's decree, His obligation and His apportionment. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ means: All-Knowing of the outward and inward aspects of matters and of the interests of His servants; ﴿All-Wise﴾ in what He does, says, legislates and judges. There is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him.

Allah the Exalted says: "And among the hypocrites are those who harm the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with their speech about him, and they say: ﴿He is an ear﴾," meaning: whoever tells him something, he believes it, and whoever relates to him about us, he believes it. "When we come to him and swear to him, he believes us." This meaning has been related from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: "An ear of good for you"﴾, meaning: he is an ear of good, who distinguishes the truthful from the liar. ﴿He believes in Allah and believes the believers﴾, meaning: he gives credence to the believers. ﴿And a mercy to those of you who believe﴾, meaning: and he is a proof against the disbelievers. For this reason Allah said: ﴿And those who harm the Messenger of Allah will have a painful punishment.﴾

Qatadah, regarding His statement, the Exalted: ﴿They swear by Allah to you in order to please you﴾ and the rest of the verse, said: It was mentioned to us that a man among the hypocrites said: "By Allah, these people (the Muslims) are indeed our best and our nobles, and even if what Muhammad says is true, they are worse than donkeys." He said: A man among the Muslims heard it and said: "By Allah, what Muhammad says is indeed true, and you are worse than a donkey." He said: The man went and reported it to the Prophet ﷺ, informing him. So the Prophet ﷺ sent for the man and summoned him, and said: "What prompted you to say what you said?" The man began to swear by Allah that he had not said that, and to take oaths of cursing (invoking a curse upon himself). Meanwhile the Muslim man kept saying: "O Allah, make the truthful one truthful and the liar a liar." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿They swear by Allah to you in order to please you, but Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him, if they are believers﴾.

* *

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, for him is the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein?﴾ That is: Do they not verify and know that whoever opposes (ḥādda, i.e., defies, confronts, wars against and contravenes) Allah, meaning he opposes Him, wars against Him and contravenes Him, and is in a limit (ḥadd, i.e., a side or boundary) opposed to Allah and His Messenger, ﴿for him is the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein﴾, meaning: humiliated and punished. ﴿That is the great disgrace﴾, meaning: this is the great humiliation and the great wretchedness.

Qatadah, regarding His statement, the Exalted: ﴿They swear by Allah to you in order to please you﴾ and the rest of the verse, said: It was mentioned to us that a man among the hypocrites said: "By Allah, these people (the Muslims) are indeed our best and our nobles, and even if what Muhammad says is true, they are worse than donkeys." He said: A man among the Muslims heard it and said: "By Allah, what Muhammad says is indeed true, and you are worse than a donkey." He said: The man went and reported it to the Prophet ﷺ, informing him. So the Prophet ﷺ sent for the man and summoned him, and said: "What prompted you to say what you said?" The man began to swear by Allah that he had not said that, and to take oaths of cursing (invoking a curse upon himself). Meanwhile the Muslim man kept saying: "O Allah, make the truthful one truthful and the liar a liar." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿They swear by Allah to you in order to please you, but Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him, if they are believers﴾.

* *

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, for him is the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein?﴾ That is: Do they not verify and know that whoever opposes (ḥādda, i.e., defies, confronts, wars against and contravenes) Allah, meaning he opposes Him, wars against Him and contravenes Him, and is in a limit (ḥadd, i.e., a side or boundary) opposed to Allah and His Messenger, ﴿for him is the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein﴾, meaning: humiliated and punished. ﴿That is the great disgrace﴾, meaning: this is the great humiliation and the great wretchedness.

Mujahid said: "They speak the words among themselves, then they say: 'Perhaps Allah will not expose our secret.'"

This verse is similar to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you, and they say to themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?" Sufficient for them is Hell; they will burn therein, and wretched is the destination.﴾ [al-Mujadila: 8] And He said in this verse: ﴿Say, "Mock on. Indeed, Allah will bring out what you fear."﴾ That is: indeed, Allah will send down to His Messenger that which will disgrace you, and will make clear to him your affair [[In A: "for you."]], as He said: ﴿Or do those in whose hearts is a disease think that Allah will not bring out their resentments? ... And We would surely make them known to you by their distinctive manner of speech. And Allah knows your deeds.﴾ [Muhammad: 29, 30] [[In A: "their secret," which is an error.]]; and for this reason Qatadah said: "This surah used to be called 'al-Fadihah' (the Disgracer), for it disgraced the hypocrites."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 9, verse 65–66:

Abu Ma'shar al-Madini (in one manuscript: "al-Ma'dini") related from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and others, who said: A man among the hypocrites said: "I see these reciters of ours to be none other than the greediest of stomachs, the most lying of tongues, and the most cowardly at the time of encounter." This was reported to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the man came to the Messenger of Allah as he had set off and mounted his she-camel, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we were only conversing and playing." He said: ﴿Was it at Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking?﴾ up to His words: ﴿criminals﴾. Indeed his two feet were scraping the stones, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not turn to him, and he was clinging to the strap of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ saddle.

Abdullah ibn Wahb said: Hisham ibn Sa'd informed me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: A man said during the Battle of Tabuk, in a gathering: "I have never seen the like of these reciters of ours: the greediest of stomachs, the most lying of tongues, and the most cowardly at the time of encounter." A man in the mosque said: "You lie, but you are a hypocrite. I will certainly inform the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." This reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Qur'an was revealed. Abdullah ibn Umar said: "I saw him clinging to the thong of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ she-camel, with the stones striking him, and he was saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, we were only conversing and playing,' while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was saying: ﴿Was it at Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief﴾."

Ibn Lahi'a narrated it from Hisham ibn Sa'd in similar terms (al-Tabari, Tafsir, 14/333–334).

Ibn Ishaq said: A group of the hypocrites, among them Wadi'ah ibn Thabit, brother of Bani Umayyah ibn Zayd, from Bani Amr ibn Awf, and a man from Ashja' allied to Bani Salamah called Mukhashshin (in one manuscript: "Mukhashshi") ibn Humayr, were pointing toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as he set out for Tabuk. Some of them said to others: "Do you suppose that fighting the sons of al-Asfar (the Byzantines) is like the fighting of the Arabs against one another? By Allah, it is as if we see you tomorrow bound together in ropes," spreading rumours and intimidating the believers. Mukhashshin ibn Humayr said: "By Allah, I would love to be punished with a hundred lashes each, on condition that nothing be revealed about us because of your words." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, as has reached me, to Ammar ibn Yasir: "Catch up with the people, for they have ignited (in their talk); ask them what they said, and if they deny it, say: 'Yes, you said such and such.'" Ammar went to them and said this to them, and they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ making excuses to him. Wadi'ah ibn Thabit said, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing on his mount, and he was holding its thong: "O Messenger of Allah, we were only conversing and playing." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And if you asked them, they would surely say, "We were only conversing and playing."﴾ [added from manuscripts T, A and Ibn Hisham's Sirah]. Mukhashshin ibn Humayr said: "O Messenger of Allah, my name and my father's name have kept me back." So the one pardoned in this verse was Mukhashshin ibn Humayr, who named himself Abd al-Rahman and asked Allah to be killed as a martyr whose place is not known. He was killed on the Day of Yamamah, and no trace of him was found (Ibn Hisham, al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah, 2/524).

Qatadah said concerning ﴿And if you asked them, they would surely say, "We were only conversing and playing"﴾: While the Prophet ﷺ was on the expedition to Tabuk, a group of hypocrites were riding ahead of him, and they said: "This man thinks he will conquer the palaces and fortresses of Rome. Far-fetched, far-fetched!" Allah informed His Prophet ﷺ of what they had said, and he said: "Bring these men to me." He summoned them and said: "You said such and such." They swore: "We were only conversing and playing."

Ikrimah said concerning this verse: There was a man among those whom Allah, if He wills, pardons, who would say: "O Allah, I hear a verse that concerns me, which makes the skins shudder and the hearts respond. O Allah, make my death a killing in Your way, so that no one can say: 'I was washed, I was shrouded, I was buried.'" He was struck down on the Day of Yamamah, and not a single Muslim was found except that he had been found [with wounds] (in one manuscript: "a lesson").

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief﴾, i.e., by this statement with which you mocked. ﴿If We pardon a group among you, We will punish another group﴾, i.e., not all of you will be pardoned, and some of you must be punished, ﴿because they were criminals﴾, i.e., criminals by this wicked and sinful utterance.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 9, verse 65–66:

Abu Ma'shar al-Madini (in one manuscript: "al-Ma'dini") related from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and others, who said: A man among the hypocrites said: "I see these reciters of ours to be none other than the greediest of stomachs, the most lying of tongues, and the most cowardly at the time of encounter." This was reported to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the man came to the Messenger of Allah as he had set off and mounted his she-camel, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we were only conversing and playing." He said: ﴿Was it at Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking?﴾ up to His words: ﴿criminals﴾. Indeed his two feet were scraping the stones, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not turn to him, and he was clinging to the strap of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ saddle.

Abdullah ibn Wahb said: Hisham ibn Sa'd informed me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: A man said during the Battle of Tabuk, in a gathering: "I have never seen the like of these reciters of ours: the greediest of stomachs, the most lying of tongues, and the most cowardly at the time of encounter." A man in the mosque said: "You lie, but you are a hypocrite. I will certainly inform the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." This reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Qur'an was revealed. Abdullah ibn Umar said: "I saw him clinging to the thong of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ she-camel, with the stones striking him, and he was saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, we were only conversing and playing,' while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was saying: ﴿Was it at Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief﴾."

Ibn Lahi'a narrated it from Hisham ibn Sa'd in similar terms (al-Tabari, Tafsir, 14/333–334).

Ibn Ishaq said: A group of the hypocrites, among them Wadi'ah ibn Thabit, brother of Bani Umayyah ibn Zayd, from Bani Amr ibn Awf, and a man from Ashja' allied to Bani Salamah called Mukhashshin (in one manuscript: "Mukhashshi") ibn Humayr, were pointing toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as he set out for Tabuk. Some of them said to others: "Do you suppose that fighting the sons of al-Asfar (the Byzantines) is like the fighting of the Arabs against one another? By Allah, it is as if we see you tomorrow bound together in ropes," spreading rumours and intimidating the believers. Mukhashshin ibn Humayr said: "By Allah, I would love to be punished with a hundred lashes each, on condition that nothing be revealed about us because of your words." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, as has reached me, to Ammar ibn Yasir: "Catch up with the people, for they have ignited (in their talk); ask them what they said, and if they deny it, say: 'Yes, you said such and such.'" Ammar went to them and said this to them, and they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ making excuses to him. Wadi'ah ibn Thabit said, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing on his mount, and he was holding its thong: "O Messenger of Allah, we were only conversing and playing." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And if you asked them, they would surely say, "We were only conversing and playing."﴾ [added from manuscripts T, A and Ibn Hisham's Sirah]. Mukhashshin ibn Humayr said: "O Messenger of Allah, my name and my father's name have kept me back." So the one pardoned in this verse was Mukhashshin ibn Humayr, who named himself Abd al-Rahman and asked Allah to be killed as a martyr whose place is not known. He was killed on the Day of Yamamah, and no trace of him was found (Ibn Hisham, al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah, 2/524).

Qatadah said concerning ﴿And if you asked them, they would surely say, "We were only conversing and playing"﴾: While the Prophet ﷺ was on the expedition to Tabuk, a group of hypocrites were riding ahead of him, and they said: "This man thinks he will conquer the palaces and fortresses of Rome. Far-fetched, far-fetched!" Allah informed His Prophet ﷺ of what they had said, and he said: "Bring these men to me." He summoned them and said: "You said such and such." They swore: "We were only conversing and playing."

Ikrimah said concerning this verse: There was a man among those whom Allah, if He wills, pardons, who would say: "O Allah, I hear a verse that concerns me, which makes the skins shudder and the hearts respond. O Allah, make my death a killing in Your way, so that no one can say: 'I was washed, I was shrouded, I was buried.'" He was struck down on the Day of Yamamah, and not a single Muslim was found except that he had been found [with wounds] (in one manuscript: "a lesson").

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief﴾, i.e., by this statement with which you mocked. ﴿If We pardon a group among you, We will punish another group﴾, i.e., not all of you will be pardoned, and some of you must be punished, ﴿because they were criminals﴾, i.e., criminals by this wicked and sinful utterance.

He, exalted is He, says, rebuking the hypocrites who have the opposite of the qualities of the believers. Since the believers [[In MS K: "al-mu'minin", which is an error.]] enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, these people are the ones who ﴿enjoin what is wrong and forbid what is right, and withhold their hands﴾, meaning from spending in the way of Allah. ﴿They forgot Allah﴾, meaning they forgot the remembrance of Allah, ﴿so He forgot them﴾, meaning He treated them as one who has forgotten them, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it will be said, "This Day We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your Day"﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 34] [[In MSS T, K, and A: "fa-al-yawm", which is an error.]]. ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning those who have departed from the path of truth and entered the path of misguidance.

* *

His saying: ﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell﴾, meaning for this conduct that has been mentioned of them, ﴿wherein they will abide eternally﴾, meaning they will remain in it forever, ﴿it is sufficient for them﴾, meaning it is their full recompense in punishment, ﴿and Allah has cursed them﴾, meaning He has expelled them and removed them far away, ﴿and for them is an enduring punishment﴾.

He, exalted is He, says, rebuking the hypocrites who have the opposite of the qualities of the believers. Since the believers [[In MS K: "al-mu'minin", which is an error.]] enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, these people are the ones who ﴿enjoin what is wrong and forbid what is right, and withhold their hands﴾, meaning from spending in the way of Allah. ﴿They forgot Allah﴾, meaning they forgot the remembrance of Allah, ﴿so He forgot them﴾, meaning He treated them as one who has forgotten them, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it will be said, "This Day We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your Day"﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 34] [[In MSS T, K, and A: "fa-al-yawm", which is an error.]]. ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning those who have departed from the path of truth and entered the path of misguidance.

* *

His saying: ﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell﴾, meaning for this conduct that has been mentioned of them, ﴿wherein they will abide eternally﴾, meaning they will remain in it forever, ﴿it is sufficient for them﴾, meaning it is their full recompense in punishment, ﴿and Allah has cursed them﴾, meaning He has expelled them and removed them far away, ﴿and for them is an enduring punishment﴾.

Allah says: Those (who came before) were afflicted with the punishment of Allah in this world and the Hereafter, just as those before them were afflicted. They were stronger than them and had more wealth and children. ﴿So they enjoyed their share (khalaq) [of worldly pleasures]⟩ Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Their share" means their religion. ﴿Just as those before you enjoyed their share, and you indulged in vain talk as they indulged﴾, i.e., in falsehood and vanity. ﴿Those, their deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and those are the losers﴾, i.e., their efforts have been nullified, so there is no reward for them for these deeds, because they were corrupt. ﴿...and those are the losers﴾, because they gained no reward from them.

Ibn Juraij reported from Umar ibn Ata, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Like those before you﴾ (the verse). Ibn Abbas said: "How similar is the night to the previous night." ﴿Like those before you﴾ refers to the Children of Israel; we are compared to them. I do not know except that he said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will surely follow them, until if one of them entered a lizard's hole, you would enter it too."

Ibn Juraij said: Ziyad ibn Sa'd informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad ibn Muhajir, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will surely follow the ways of those before you, span by span, cubit by cubit, and fathom by fathom, until even if they entered a lizard's burrow, you would enter it." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are they? The People of the Book?" He said: "Then who else?" [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/342).]

Abu Ma'shar narrated the same from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), mentioning it, and he added: Abu Hurairah said: "Recite, if you wish, the Qur'an: ﴿Like those before you, who were stronger than you in power and had more wealth and children; so they enjoyed their share, and you enjoyed your share as those before you enjoyed their share﴾." Abu Hurairah said: "Khalaq" means religion. ﴿And you indulged as they indulged﴾. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, like what Persia and Rome did?" He said: "And who else are the people but they?" [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/341).] This hadith has a corroborating report in Sahih (al-Bukhari), no. (7319), through Muhammad ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.

Allah the Exalted says, admonishing these hypocrites who denied the Messengers: ﴿Has there not come to them the news of those before them?﴾ That is: Have you not been told the report of those nations before you who denied the Messengers: ﴿the people of Noah﴾, and what befell them of the general drowning that covered all the inhabitants of the earth, except those who believed in His servant and messenger Noah, peace be upon him; ﴿and ʿAad﴾, how they were destroyed by the furious wind when they denied Hud, peace be upon him; ﴿and Thamud﴾, how the Blast seized them when they denied Salih, peace be upon him, and they hamstrung the she-camel; ﴿and the people of Abraham﴾, how Allah helped him against them, supported him with clear miracles against them, and destroyed their king, Nimrod son of Canaan son of Kush the Canaanite, may Allah curse him; ﴿and the companions of Madyan﴾, who were the people of Shuʿayb, peace be upon him, and how the Quake and the Blast and the punishment of the Day of the Canopy befell them; ﴿and the overturned cities﴾, the people of Lot, who used to dwell in cities. And in another verse He said: ﴿And the overturned cities He hurled down﴾ [An-Najm 53:53], that is, the overturned community. It was also said: the mother of their townships, which is "Sodom." The point is that Allah the Exalted destroyed them to the last one because they denied His prophet Lot, peace be upon him, and committed the vile act that no one among the worlds had preceded them in.

﴿Their Messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾, that is, with decisive arguments and evidences. ﴿So Allah would not have wronged them﴾, that is, by destroying them, because He had established the proof against them by sending the Messengers and removing excuses. ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾, that is, by denying the Messengers and opposing the truth, so they came to the punishment and ruin they met.

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the blameworthy attributes of the hypocrites, He followed it with mention of the praiseworthy attributes of the believers, saying: ﴿The believing men and believing women are allies of one another﴾, meaning they support and aid one another. As is related in the Sahih: "The believer to the believer is like the bricks of a building, each part strengthening the other," and he interlaced his fingers [(Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 481, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2585) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him]. Also in the Sahih: "The likeness of the believers in their mutual love, mercy and compassion is that of one body: when one of its limbs complains, the whole body responds to it with wakefulness and fever" [(Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6011, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2586) from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, may Allah be pleased with him].

His saying: ﴿they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And let there be [arising] from you a nation calling to the good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. And those are the successful﴾ [Al 'Imran: 104].

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and they establish prayer and give zakah﴾, meaning they obey Allah and are good to His creation. ﴿And they obey Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning in what He commands and in abandoning what He forbids. ﴿Those – Allah will have mercy upon them﴾, meaning Allah will surely have mercy upon whoever is characterized by these attributes. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise﴾, meaning He is Mighty; whoever obeys Him, He honours. For honour belongs to Allah, to His Messenger and to the believers. ﴿Wise﴾ in His apportioning these attributes to these people, and His singling out the hypocrites with their aforementioned attributes, for He has wisdom in all that He does, blessed and exalted is He.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah informs of what He has prepared for the believing men and believing women of good things and lasting bliss: ﴿Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever﴾, meaning, remaining in them eternally, ﴿and pleasant dwellings﴾, meaning, well-built, pleasant in their abode. As came in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from the hadith of Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Musa 'Abd Allah ibn Qays al-Ash'ari, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Two gardens of gold, their vessels and all that is in them, and two gardens of silver, their vessels and all that is in them. Nothing stands between the people and looking upon their Lord except the cloak of greatness over His face, in the Garden of Eden." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4878) and Sahih Muslim no. (180).]

And with this chain: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, for the believer in Paradise there is a tent of a single hollow pearl, its length sixty miles in the sky, and the believer has families there, whom he goes around to visit, and they do not see one another." Related by both (al-Bukhari and Muslim). [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4879) and Sahih Muslim no. (2838).]

Also in the two Sahihs, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever believes in Allah and His Messenger, establishes the prayer and fasts Ramadan, it is a right upon Allah to admit him into Paradise, whether he migrates in the way of Allah or remains seated in the land where he was born." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not inform the people?" He said: "Indeed, in Paradise there are one hundred levels, which Allah has prepared for those who strive in His way; between each two levels is as the distance between the heaven and the earth. So when you ask Allah, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the highest and the middle of Paradise, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (7423), from the route of Fulayh, from Hilal, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

And in al-Tabarani, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from the narration of Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say... and he mentioned the like of it. [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (20/158), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2530), and in Ibn Majah the second part of it no. (4331). The Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) pointed to the disagreement over 'Ata' ibn Yasar.]

And in al-Tirmidhi, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, the like of it. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2531).] And from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, the people of Paradise will look at the chambers in Paradise as you look at the star in the sky." Related by both in the two Sahihs. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6555) and Sahih Muslim no. (2830).]

Then let it be known that the highest station in Paradise is a place called "al-Wasilah," because of its nearness to the Throne, and it is the dwelling of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Paradise, as Imam Ahmad [ibn Hanbal] said.

'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Sufyan informed us, from Layth, from Ka'b, from Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you send blessings upon me, ask Allah for al-Wasilah for me." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-Wasilah?" He said: "The highest level in Paradise, which none will attain except one man, and I hope that I will be that one." [al-Musnad (2/256).]

And in Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Ka'b ibn 'Alqamah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "When you hear the muezzin, say the like of what he says, then send blessings upon me, for whoever sends one blessing upon me, Allah sends ten upon him. Then ask Allah for al-Wasilah for me, for it is a station in Paradise that is not fitting except for one of the servants of Allah, and I hope that I will be that one. Whoever asks Allah for al-Wasilah for me, intercession will be due to him on the Day of Resurrection." [Sahih Muslim no. (1384).]

[And in Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever says when he hears the call: O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and established prayer, grant Muhammad al-Wasilah and al-Fadilah, and raise him to the praiseworthy station which You have promised him, will have intercession made for him on the Day of Resurrection."] [Addition from the manuscripts. It is in Sahih al-Bukhari no. (614).]

And al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Abbar narrated to us, al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-Harrani narrated to us, Musa ibn A'yan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Ask Allah for al-Wasilah for me, for no servant asks it for me in this world except that I will be a witness for him, or an intercessor, on the Day of Resurrection." [al-Mu'jam al-Awsat no. (639), "Majma' al-Bahrayn."]

And in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from the hadith of Sa'd Abu Mujahid al-Ta'i, from Abu al-Mudilla, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell us about Paradise, what is its construction?" He said: "A brick of gold and a brick of silver, its mortar is musk, its pebbles are pearls and rubies, and its soil is saffron. Whoever enters it will be blessed and will not be miserable, and will abide and not die; his garments will not wear out and his youth will not fade." [al-Musnad (2/304).]

And it is narrated from Ibn 'Umar, marfu'an, similar to it. [Narrated by Abu Nu'aym in Sifat al-Jannah no. (96), through 'Umar ibn Rabi'ah, from al-Hasan al-Basri, from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, marfu'an, similar to the hadith of Abu Hurairah.] And in al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from al-Nu'man ibn Sa'd, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, in Paradise there are chambers whose outside can be seen from their inside, and whose inside can be seen from their outside." A Bedouin stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, for whom are they?" He said: "For those who speak kindly, feed the food, persist in fasting, and pray at night while people are asleep." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2527).]

Then he said: It is a gharib hadith.

Al-Tabarani related it from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr and Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, each of them from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to it. [As for the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, Imam Ahmad also related it in his Musnad (2/173) through Huyayy ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both. As for the hadith of Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, it is in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/301) and will come at the commentary of verse 20 of Surah al-Zumar.] Both chains are good and sound. And according to him (al-Tabarani), the questioner was "Abu Malik." Allah knows best.

And from Usamah ibn Zayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Does anyone strive for Paradise? For indeed Paradise has no equal. It is, by the Lord of the Ka'bah, a shining light, a swaying fragrant plant, a lofty palace, a flowing river, a ripe fruit, a beautiful and graceful wife, many garments, and a lasting abode in a safe house, with fruits, greenery, joy and blessing, in a high and radiant dwelling." They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah, we are the ones who strive for it." He said: "Say: if Allah wills." So the people said: "If Allah wills." Related by Ibn Majah. [Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4332), through al-Dahhak al-Ma'afiri, from Sulayman ibn Musa, from Kurayb, from Usamah ibn Zayd. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/325): "This chain contains some criticism."]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the good pleasure from Allah is greater﴾, meaning, Allah's pleasure with them is greater, more majestic and more magnificent than the bliss they are in. As Imam Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to the people of Paradise: O people of Paradise! They will say: Here we are, our Lord, at Your service and good pleasure, and all good is in Your hand. He will say: Are you pleased? They will say: And why would we not be pleased, O Lord, when You have given us what You have not given any of Your creation? He will say: Shall I not give you something better than that? They will say: O Lord, and what is better than that? He will say: I will bestow upon you My pleasure, and I will never be displeased with you after it, ever." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) related it through the narration of Malik. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6549) and Sahih Muslim no. (2829).]

And Abu 'Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn Isma'il al-Mahamili said: al-Fadl al-Rukhami narrated to us, al-Firyabi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: Do you desire anything that I may increase for you? They will say: O our Lord, what is better than what You have given us? He will say: My pleasure is greater."

Al-Bazzar related it in his Musnad, from the hadith of al-Thawri. [Abu Nu'aym in Sifat al-Jannah no. (238) and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (1/82) related it through Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firyabi similarly, and al-Hakim said: "Sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it."] The Hafiz Diya' al-Maqdisi said in his book "Sifat al-Jannah": "This, in my view, meets the conditions of the Sahih. And Allah knows best."

God Most High commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and to be harsh with them, just as He commanded him to lower his wing to the believers who followed him. He also informed him that the destination of the disbelievers and the hypocrites is the Fire in the Hereafter.

It has already been related from the Commander of the Faithful, ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent with four swords: a sword against the polytheists, ﴿Then when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists﴾ [At-Tawbah 9:5]; a sword against the disbelievers among the People of the Book, ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day, and who do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and who do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture, until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled﴾ [At-Tawbah 9:29]; a sword against the hypocrites, ﴿Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ [At-Tawbah 9:73; At-Tahrim 66:9]; and a sword against the rebellious, ﴿Fight the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of Allah﴾ [Al-Hujurat 49:9]."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Allah Most High commanded him to strive against the disbelievers with the sword and against the hypocrites with the tongue, and to remove gentleness from dealing with them."

Ad-Dahhak said: "Strive against the disbelievers with the sword, and be harsh with the hypocrites with words; this is their struggle." The same was related from Muqatil and ar-Rabiʿ.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "Their struggle is the establishment of the prescribed punishments (hudud) upon them."

It may be said that there is no contradiction between these statements, for he sometimes takes them to account in this way and sometimes in that way, according to the circumstances. And Allah knows best.

As for His words, ﴿They swear by Allah that they said nothing, but they had indeed uttered the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam﴾, Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy. The reason was that two men fought, one a Juhani and the other an Ansari. The Juhani overcame the Ansari, so ʿAbdullah said to the Ansar: "Will you not support your brother? By Allah, our example and the example of Muhammad is only like the saying of the one who said: 'Fatten your dog and it will devour you.'" And he said: ﴿If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel the more humble from it﴾ [Al-Munafiqun 63:8]. A man from the Muslims reported this to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he sent for him and questioned him, and he began swearing by Allah that he had not said it. So Allah revealed this verse concerning him. [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/364).]

Ismaʿil ibn Ibrahim ibn ʿUqbah related from his paternal uncle Musa ibn ʿUqbah, who said: ʿAbdullah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us that he heard Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) say: "I was grieved over those of my people who were killed at al-Harrah. Zayd ibn Arqam wrote to me, having learned of the intensity of my grief, mentioning that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'O Allah, forgive the Ansar and the sons of the Ansar'" — Ibn al-Fadl was uncertain whether he said "the sons of the sons of the Ansar." Ibn al-Fadl said: Someone present asked Anas about Zayd ibn Arqam, and he said: "He is the one to whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Allah has fulfilled for him with his ear.'" This was when he heard a man among the hypocrites saying, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was delivering a sermon: "If what this man says is true, then we are worse than donkeys." Zayd ibn Arqam said: "By Allah, he is truthful, and you are worse than a donkey." Then this was reported to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the speaker denied it, so Allah revealed this verse confirming Zayd, meaning His words: ﴿They swear by Allah that they said nothing﴾, to the end of the verse.

This was related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, from Ismaʿil ibn Abi Uways, from Ismaʿil ibn Ibrahim ibn ʿUqbah, up to his words: "This is the one to whom Allah fulfilled with his ear." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4906.] It is likely that what follows is from the words of Musa ibn ʿUqbah. Muhammad ibn Fulayh related it from Musa ibn ʿUqbah with its chain, then said: "Ibn Shihab said," and then mentioned what follows from Musa, from Ibn Shihab.

The well-known account of this incident is that it took place during the expedition against Banu al-Mustaliq. Perhaps the narrator made a mistake in mentioning the verse, intending to mention something else, and so he mentioned it. And Allah knows best.

[Margin note]

He mentioned the lengthy hadith, until he said: Among the hypocrites who stayed behind, and about whom the Qur'an was revealed, from those who were with the Prophet (ﷺ), was al-Jullas ibn Suwayd ibn al-Samit, who was under the guardianship of Umayr ibn Saʿd, and Umayr was in his care. When the Qur'an was revealed and Allah mentioned them with what He mentioned about the hypocrites, al-Jullas said: "By Allah, if this man is truthful in what he says about us, then we are worse than donkeys." Umayr ibn Saʿd heard it and said: "By Allah, O Jullas, you are the dearest of people to me, the best of them in my estimation, and the one I would least like to see harmed by anything he dislikes. You have said a statement which, if I mention it, will expose you, and if I conceal it, will destroy me; yet one of the two is easier for me than the other." So he went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned to him what al-Jullas had said. [See: Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/519).] Thus this came as mudraj (interpolated) in the hadith, connected to it; and it appears, and Allah knows best, that it is from the words of Ibn Ishaq himself, not from the words of Kaʿb ibn Malik.

Al-Jullas said: "If what Muhammad brought is true, then we are worse than these donkeys we are riding." Mus'ab said: "As for me, by Allah, O enemy of Allah, I will surely inform the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of what you said." So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ), but I feared that the Qur'an would be revealed concerning me, or that a calamity would strike me, or that I would be implicated in his sin. So I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I and al-Jullas came from Quba', and he said such and such." And had it not been for my fear of being implicated in a sin, or of a calamity striking me, I would not have told you. He said: So he summoned al-Jullas and said: "O Jullas, did you say what Mus'ab said?" He swore, and Allah revealed: ﴿They swear by Allah that they said nothing, but they had indeed uttered the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam﴾, the verse.

Not long after, a blue-eyed man appeared, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called him and said: "Why do you and your companions revile me?" The man went off and brought his companions, and they swore by Allah that they had not said it, until he overlooked them. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿They swear by Allah that they said nothing﴾, the verse. [Tafsir al-Tabari (14/363).]

This is clarified in what al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi related in his book Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from [Abu] al-Bakhtari, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "I was holding the halter of the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), leading her, while ʿAmmar was driving the camel — or I was driving it and ʿAmmar was leading it — until when we were at the 'Aqabah, there were twelve riders who had blocked his way there. He said: I alerted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to them, and he shouted at them, and they turned back fleeing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to us: 'Did you recognize the people?' We said: 'No, O Messenger of Allah, they were masked, but we recognized the mounts.' He said: 'These are the hypocrites until the Day of Resurrection. Do you know what they intended?' We said: 'No.' He said: 'They intended to crowd the Messenger of Allah at the 'Aqabah, so as to throw him down from it.' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, shall we not send to their clans so that every people sends you the head of its companion?' He said: 'I do not wish that the Arabs should speak among themselves that Muhammad fought with a people, and when Allah gave him victory over them, he turned upon them to kill them.' Then he said: 'O Allah, strike them with the Dubaylah.' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the Dubaylah?' He said: 'A flame of fire that falls upon the heart-strings of one of them, and he perishes.'" [Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (5/260).]

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Yazid narrated to us; al-Walid ibn ʿAbdullah ibn Jumayʿ informed us, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from the expedition of Tabuk, he ordered a caller who announced: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has taken the 'Aqabah, so let no one take it." While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was being led by Hudhayfah and driven by ʿAmmar, twelve masked men on mounts came up, covering ʿAmmar, who was driving the Messenger of Allah. ʿAmmar (may Allah be pleased with him) approached, striking the faces of the mounts. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Hudhayfah: "Slow, slow." Until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) descended, and when he descended, ʿAmmar came back. He said: "O ʿAmmar, did you recognize the people?" He said: "I recognized most of the mounts, and the people were masked." He said: "Do you know what they intended?" He said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "They intended to startle the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and throw him down." Then ʿAmmar whispered to a man from the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I beseech you by Allah, how many do you know were the companions of the 'Aqabah?" He said: "Fourteen." He said: "If you were among them, then they were fifteen." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) excluded three of them, who said: "By Allah, we did not hear the caller of the Messenger of Allah, and we did not know what the people intended." ʿAmmar said: "I bear witness that the remaining twelve are at war with Allah and His Messenger in the life of this world, and on the Day when the witnesses stand." [Musnad Ahmad (5/453). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (6/195): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

Ibn Lahi'ah narrated similarly from Abu al-Aswad, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the people to walk in the bottom of the valley, while he himself and Hudhayfah and 'Ammar ascended the 'Aqabah. These wretched men followed them, masking their faces, and they intended to take the 'Aqabah. Allah informed His Messenger ﷺ of their intention, so he ordered Hudhayfah to return to them, and he struck the faces of their mounts. They were terrified and returned in disgrace. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed Hudhayfah and 'Ammar of their names and of what they had intended to do to him, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and he commanded them both to keep this concealed.[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (5/256).]]

Similarly, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated from Ibn Ishaq, except that he named a group of them. Allah knows best.[[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (5/257).]]

It is also related in the Mu'jam of al-Tabarani, as al-Bayhaqi said. The authenticity of this story is supported by what Muslim narrated:

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Abu Ahmad al-Kufi narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Jumay' narrated to us: Abu al-Tufayl said: There was some dispute between a man from the People of the 'Aqabah and Hudhayfah, so he said: "I adjure you by Allah, how many were the Companions of the 'Aqabah?" He said: The people said to him: "Tell him, since he has asked you." He said: "We used to be informed that they were fourteen. If you are one of them, then the people were fifteen. And I testify by Allah that twelve of them are at war with Allah and His Messenger in this worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses stand. And three excused themselves, saying: 'We did not hear the caller of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor did we know what the people intended.'" And he had been in a stony tract and walked, and said: "Indeed the water is scarce, so let no one reach it before me." He found some people who had already reached it, so he cursed them that day.[[Sahih Muslim, no. (2779).]]

And also what Muslim narrated, from the hadith of Qatadah, from Abu Nadrah, from Qays ibn 'Abbad, from 'Ammar ibn Yasir, who said: Hudhayfah informed me, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Among my Companions are twelve hypocrites who will not enter Paradise, nor will they smell its fragrance, until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. Eight of them are sufficed by the Dubaylah: a lamp of fire that appears between their shoulders until it emerges from their chests."[[Sahih Muslim, no. (2779).]]

For this reason Hudhayfah was called "the confidant of the secret, which no one else knows," meaning concerning the identification of a group of the hypocrites, and these were they; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed him of them to the exclusion of others. Allah knows best. Al-Tabarani, in the Musnad of Hudhayfah, titled a chapter naming the Companions of the 'Aqabah, then narrated from 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, from al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar, that he said: They were Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, Wadi'ah ibn Thabit, Jadd ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Nabtal ibn al-Harith from Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, al-Harith ibn Yazid al-Ta'i, Aws ibn Qayzi, al-Harith ibn Suwayd, Sa'd ibn Zurarah, Qays ibn Fahd, Suwayd and Da'is from Banu al-Hublay, Qays ibn 'Amr ibn Sahl, Zayd ibn al-Lasit, and Sulalah ibn al-Himam, and both of them were from Banu Qaynuqa', who had outwardly embraced Islam.[[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/165-167).]]

His saying: ﴿And they did not resent except that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them of His bounty﴾ means: there was no fault in the Messenger in their eyes, except that Allah had enriched them through his blessing and the auspiciousness of his mission. Had felicity been fully decreed for them, Allah would have guided them to what he brought, just as he (peace be upon him) said to the Ansar: "Did I not find you astray, and Allah guided you through me? And you were divided, and Allah united you through me? And you were poor, and Allah enriched you through me?" Whenever he said something, they replied: "Allah and His Messenger are the most gracious."

This expression is used where there is no fault, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Buruj: 8]. And as he (peace be upon him) said: "Ibn Jamil resents only that he was poor, and Allah enriched him."

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, called them to repentance, saying: ﴿So if they repent, it will be better for them; but if they turn away, Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter﴾. That is: if they persist in their path. ﴿Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world﴾: that is, by killing, distress and grief. ﴿And the Hereafter﴾: that is, by torment, retribution, humiliation and abasement. ﴿And they will have on earth no protector or helper﴾: that is, there is no one who will assist them or come to their aid, nor will anyone bring them any good, nor will anyone repel any evil from them.
