This is clarified in what al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi related in his book Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from [Abu] al-Bakhtari, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "I was holding the halter of the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), leading her, while ʿAmmar was driving the camel — or I was driving it and ʿAmmar was leading it — until when we were at the 'Aqabah, there were twelve riders who had blocked his way there. He said: I alerted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to them, and he shouted at them, and they turned back fleeing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to us: 'Did you recognize the people?' We said: 'No, O Messenger of Allah, they were masked, but we recognized the mounts.' He said: 'These are the hypocrites until the Day of Resurrection. Do you know what they intended?' We said: 'No.' He said: 'They intended to crowd the Messenger of Allah at the 'Aqabah, so as to throw him down from it.' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, shall we not send to their clans so that every people sends you the head of its companion?' He said: 'I do not wish that the Arabs should speak among themselves that Muhammad fought with a people, and when Allah gave him victory over them, he turned upon them to kill them.' Then he said: 'O Allah, strike them with the Dubaylah.' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the Dubaylah?' He said: 'A flame of fire that falls upon the heart-strings of one of them, and he perishes.'" [Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (5/260).]

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Yazid narrated to us; al-Walid ibn ʿAbdullah ibn Jumayʿ informed us, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from the expedition of Tabuk, he ordered a caller who announced: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has taken the 'Aqabah, so let no one take it." While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was being led by Hudhayfah and driven by ʿAmmar, twelve masked men on mounts came up, covering ʿAmmar, who was driving the Messenger of Allah. ʿAmmar (may Allah be pleased with him) approached, striking the faces of the mounts. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Hudhayfah: "Slow, slow." Until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) descended, and when he descended, ʿAmmar came back. He said: "O ʿAmmar, did you recognize the people?" He said: "I recognized most of the mounts, and the people were masked." He said: "Do you know what they intended?" He said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "They intended to startle the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and throw him down." Then ʿAmmar whispered to a man from the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I beseech you by Allah, how many do you know were the companions of the 'Aqabah?" He said: "Fourteen." He said: "If you were among them, then they were fifteen." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) excluded three of them, who said: "By Allah, we did not hear the caller of the Messenger of Allah, and we did not know what the people intended." ʿAmmar said: "I bear witness that the remaining twelve are at war with Allah and His Messenger in the life of this world, and on the Day when the witnesses stand." [Musnad Ahmad (5/453). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (6/195): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

Ibn Lahi'ah narrated similarly from Abu al-Aswad, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered the people to walk in the bottom of the valley, while he himself and Hudhayfah and 'Ammar ascended the 'Aqabah. These wretched men followed them, masking their faces, and they intended to take the 'Aqabah. Allah informed His Messenger ﷺ of their intention, so he ordered Hudhayfah to return to them, and he struck the faces of their mounts. They were terrified and returned in disgrace. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed Hudhayfah and 'Ammar of their names and of what they had intended to do to him, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and he commanded them both to keep this concealed.[[Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (5/256).]]

Similarly, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated from Ibn Ishaq, except that he named a group of them. Allah knows best.[[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (5/257).]]

It is also related in the Mu'jam of al-Tabarani, as al-Bayhaqi said. The authenticity of this story is supported by what Muslim narrated:

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Abu Ahmad al-Kufi narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Jumay' narrated to us: Abu al-Tufayl said: There was some dispute between a man from the People of the 'Aqabah and Hudhayfah, so he said: "I adjure you by Allah, how many were the Companions of the 'Aqabah?" He said: The people said to him: "Tell him, since he has asked you." He said: "We used to be informed that they were fourteen. If you are one of them, then the people were fifteen. And I testify by Allah that twelve of them are at war with Allah and His Messenger in this worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses stand. And three excused themselves, saying: 'We did not hear the caller of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor did we know what the people intended.'" And he had been in a stony tract and walked, and said: "Indeed the water is scarce, so let no one reach it before me." He found some people who had already reached it, so he cursed them that day.[[Sahih Muslim, no. (2779).]]

And also what Muslim narrated, from the hadith of Qatadah, from Abu Nadrah, from Qays ibn 'Abbad, from 'Ammar ibn Yasir, who said: Hudhayfah informed me, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Among my Companions are twelve hypocrites who will not enter Paradise, nor will they smell its fragrance, until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. Eight of them are sufficed by the Dubaylah: a lamp of fire that appears between their shoulders until it emerges from their chests."[[Sahih Muslim, no. (2779).]]

For this reason Hudhayfah was called "the confidant of the secret, which no one else knows," meaning concerning the identification of a group of the hypocrites, and these were they; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed him of them to the exclusion of others. Allah knows best. Al-Tabarani, in the Musnad of Hudhayfah, titled a chapter naming the Companions of the 'Aqabah, then narrated from 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, from al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar, that he said: They were Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, Wadi'ah ibn Thabit, Jadd ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Nabtal ibn al-Harith from Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, al-Harith ibn Yazid al-Ta'i, Aws ibn Qayzi, al-Harith ibn Suwayd, Sa'd ibn Zurarah, Qays ibn Fahd, Suwayd and Da'is from Banu al-Hublay, Qays ibn 'Amr ibn Sahl, Zayd ibn al-Lasit, and Sulalah ibn al-Himam, and both of them were from Banu Qaynuqa', who had outwardly embraced Islam.[[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/165-167).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And they did not resent except that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them of His bounty﴾ means: there was no fault in the Messenger in their eyes, except that Allah had enriched them through his blessing and the auspiciousness of his mission. Had felicity been fully decreed for them, Allah would have guided them to what he brought, just as he (peace be upon him) said to the Ansar: "Did I not find you astray, and Allah guided you through me? And you were divided, and Allah united you through me? And you were poor, and Allah enriched you through me?" Whenever he said something, they replied: "Allah and His Messenger are the most gracious."

This expression is used where there is no fault, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Buruj: 8]. And as he (peace be upon him) said: "Ibn Jamil resents only that he was poor, and Allah enriched him."

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, called them to repentance, saying: ﴿So if they repent, it will be better for them; but if they turn away, Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter﴾. That is: if they persist in their path. ﴿Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world﴾: that is, by killing, distress and grief. ﴿And the Hereafter﴾: that is, by torment, retribution, humiliation and abasement. ﴿And they will have on earth no protector or helper﴾: that is, there is no one who will assist them or come to their aid, nor will anyone bring them any good, nor will anyone repel any evil from them.

Allah, exalted is He, says: Among the hypocrites are those who made a covenant with Allah, saying: "If He grants us of His bounty, we will surely give charity (ṣadaqah) from our wealth, and we will surely be among the righteous." But when He granted them of His bounty, they were stingy with it and turned away, while they were averse. So He caused hypocrisy to follow in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they broke what they promised Allah and because they used to lie. Did they not know that Allah knows their secret and their private talk, and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?

Many of the exegetes, among them Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, mentioned that the occasion of revelation of this noble verse concerned Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib al-Anṣārī.

A ḥadīth has been narrated about him, related by Ibn Jarīr here and by Ibn Abī Ḥātim, through Muʿān ibn Rifāʿah, from ʿAlī ibn Yazīd, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the freedman of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah, from Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī, from Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib al-Anṣārī, that he said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Pray to Allah that He grants me wealth." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Woe to you, O Thaʿlabah! A little that you can render thanks for is better than a lot that you cannot bear." He said: Then he asked again, and he said: "Are you not content to be like the Prophet of Allah? By Him in whose hand my soul is, if I wished that mountains would walk with me as gold and silver, they would walk." He said: "By He who sent you with the truth, if you pray to Allah and He grants me wealth, I will surely give every owner of a right his right." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Allah, provide Thaʿlabah with wealth." He said: So he acquired sheep, and they multiplied as worms multiply, and the city became too narrow for him, so he withdrew from it and settled in one of its valleys, until he began to pray Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr in congregation and to leave aside what was other than them. Then they multiplied and increased, so he withdrew further until he abandoned the prayers except Friday, and they kept multiplying as worms multiply, until he abandoned Friday too. He then began to meet the riders on Friday, asking them for news. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What has Thaʿlabah done?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, he acquired sheep, and the city became too narrow for him." They informed him of his matter, and he said: "Woe to Thaʿlabah! Woe to Thaʿlabah! Woe to Thaʿlabah!" And Allah, may His praise be exalted, revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cleanse them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 103]. He said: The obligatory rules of charity (farāʾiḍ al-ṣadaqah) were revealed concerning him, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent two men to collect the charity: a man from Juhaynah and a man from Sulaym, and he wrote to them how they should take charity from the Muslims. He said to them: "Go to Thaʿlabah, and to so-and-so, a man from Banū Sulaym, and take their charities." So the two went out until they came to Thaʿlabah, and they asked him for the charity and read to him the letter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: "This is nothing but a jizyah (poll tax). This is nothing but a sister of the jizyah. I do not know what this is. Go until you are finished, then come back to me." So the two went off, and the Sulamī heard of them, so he looked at the best of his camels, set them aside for charity, and then met them with them. When they saw them, they said: "This is not obligatory upon you, and we do not want to take this from you." He said: "Yes, take them, for my soul is content with that, and they are for Him." So they took them from him. When the two had finished with their charities, they returned and passed by Thaʿlabah, and he said: "Show me your letter." He looked into it and said: "This is nothing but a sister of the jizyah. Go until I see my opinion." So they went until they came to the Prophet ﷺ, and when he saw them he said, before speaking to them: "Woe to Thaʿlabah," and he invoked blessing upon the Sulamī. They informed him of what Thaʿlabah had done and what the Sulamī had done. Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity"﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and because they used to lie﴾. He said: With the Messenger of Allah ﷺ there was a man from Thaʿlabah's relatives, who heard that, so he went out until he came to him and said: "Woe to you, O Thaʿlabah! Allah has revealed concerning you such and such." So Thaʿlabah went out until he came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him to accept his charity. He said: "Allah has forbidden me to accept your charity from you." So he began throwing dust upon his head. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "This [is] your deed; I commanded you, but you did not obey me." When he refused, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not accept it, and he returned to his home. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died and did not accept anything from him. Then he came to Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, when he was appointed caliph, and said: "You know my position with the Messenger of Allah and my standing among the Anṣār, so accept my charity." Abū Bakr said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not accept it from you, and he refused to accept it." So Abū Bakr died without accepting it. When ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, became ruler, he came to him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, accept my charity." He said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not accept it, nor did Abū Bakr, and I will accept it from you!" So he died without accepting it. Then ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, became ruler, and he came to him and asked him to accept his charity. He said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not accept it, nor Abū Bakr, nor ʿUmar, and I will accept it from you!" So he did not accept it from him, and Thaʿlabah died during the caliphate of ʿUthmān.

[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (14/370). The scholars have rejected this story and declared it false. Among those who said so is the Imām Ibn Ḥazm. He said in al-Muḥallā (11/207, 208): "We have also narrated a report that is not authentic, that it was revealed concerning Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib, and this is false, because Thaʿlabah was a known Badrī (one who fought at Badr). Then he related the ḥadīth with its chain through the route of Muʿān ibn Rifāʿah, from ʿAlī ibn Yazīd, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Umāmah, and said: 'This is undoubtedly false, because Allah commanded the collection of the zakāt of the wealth of the Muslims, and the Prophet ﷺ commanded at his death that no two religions should remain in the Arabian Peninsula. Thaʿlabah must either be a Muslim, in which case it was obligatory upon Abū Bakr and ʿUmar to collect his zakāt without any leeway, or he was a disbeliever, in which case it was obligatory that he not remain in the Arabian Peninsula. Thus this report is undoubtedly baseless. Among its narrators are Muʿān ibn Rifāʿah, al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and ʿAlī ibn Yazīd (he is Ibn ʿAbd al-Malik), and all of them are weak.' The distinguished scholar ʿAdnān al-Ḥimash wrote a treatise criticizing this story, in which he gathered the statements of the scholars about it, entitled Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib al-Ṣaḥābī al-Muftarā ʿalayh (Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib, the Companion who was slandered).]

A ḥadīth has been narrated about him, related by Ibn Jarīr here and by Ibn Abī Ḥātim, through Muʿān ibn Rifāʿah, from ʿAlī ibn Yazīd, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the freedman of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiyah, from Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī, from Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib al-Anṣārī, that he said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Pray to Allah that He grants me wealth." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Woe to you, O Thaʿlabah! A little that you can render thanks for is better than a lot that you cannot bear." He said: Then he asked again, and he said: "Are you not content to be like the Prophet of Allah? By Him in whose hand my soul is, if I wished that mountains would walk with me as gold and silver, they would walk." He said: "By He who sent you with the truth, if you pray to Allah and He grants me wealth, I will surely give every owner of a right his right." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Allah, provide Thaʿlabah with wealth." He said: So he acquired sheep, and they multiplied as worms multiply, and the city became too narrow for him, so he withdrew from it and settled in one of its valleys, until he began to pray Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr in congregation and to leave aside what was other than them. Then they multiplied and increased, so he withdrew further until he abandoned the prayers except Friday, and they kept multiplying as worms multiply, until he abandoned Friday too. He then began to meet the riders on Friday, asking them for news. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What has Thaʿlabah done?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, he acquired sheep, and the city became too narrow for him." They informed him of his matter, and he said: "Woe to Thaʿlabah! Woe to Thaʿlabah! Woe to Thaʿlabah!" And Allah, may His praise be exalted, revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cleanse them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 103]. He said: The obligatory rules of charity (farāʾiḍ al-ṣadaqah) were revealed concerning him, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent two men to collect the charity: a man from Juhaynah and a man from Sulaym, and he wrote to them how they should take charity from the Muslims. He said to them: "Go to Thaʿlabah, and to so-and-so, a man from Banū Sulaym, and take their charities." So the two went out until they came to Thaʿlabah, and they asked him for the charity and read to him the letter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: "This is nothing but a jizyah (poll tax). This is nothing but a sister of the jizyah. I do not know what this is. Go until you are finished, then come back to me." So the two went off, and the Sulamī heard of them, so he looked at the best of his camels, set them aside for charity, and then met them with them. When they saw them, they said: "This is not obligatory upon you, and we do not want to take this from you." He said: "Yes, take them, for my soul is content with that, and they are for Him." So they took them from him. When the two had finished with their charities, they returned and passed by Thaʿlabah, and he said: "Show me your letter." He looked into it and said: "This is nothing but a sister of the jizyah. Go until I see my opinion." So they went until they came to the Prophet ﷺ, and when he saw them he said, before speaking to them: "Woe to Thaʿlabah," and he invoked blessing upon the Sulamī. They informed him of what Thaʿlabah had done and what the Sulamī had done. Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity"﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and because they used to lie﴾. He said: With the Messenger of Allah ﷺ there was a man from Thaʿlabah's relatives, who heard that, so he went out until he came to him and said: "Woe to you, O Thaʿlabah! Allah has revealed concerning you such and such." So Thaʿlabah went out until he came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him to accept his charity. He said: "Allah has forbidden me to accept your charity from you." So he began throwing dust upon his head. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "This [is] your deed; I commanded you, but you did not obey me." When he refused, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not accept it, and he returned to his home. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died and did not accept anything from him. Then he came to Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, when he was appointed caliph, and said: "You know my position with the Messenger of Allah and my standing among the Anṣār, so accept my charity." Abū Bakr said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not accept it from you, and he refused to accept it." So Abū Bakr died without accepting it. When ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, became ruler, he came to him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, accept my charity." He said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not accept it, nor did Abū Bakr, and I will accept it from you!" So he died without accepting it. Then ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, became ruler, and he came to him and asked him to accept his charity. He said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not accept it, nor Abū Bakr, nor ʿUmar, and I will accept it from you!" So he did not accept it from him, and Thaʿlabah died during the caliphate of ʿUthmān.

[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (14/370). The scholars have rejected this story and declared it false. Among those who said so is the Imām Ibn Ḥazm. He said in al-Muḥallā (11/207, 208): "We have also narrated a report that is not authentic, that it was revealed concerning Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib, and this is false, because Thaʿlabah was a known Badrī (one who fought at Badr). Then he related the ḥadīth with its chain through the route of Muʿān ibn Rifāʿah, from ʿAlī ibn Yazīd, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Umāmah, and said: 'This is undoubtedly false, because Allah commanded the collection of the zakāt of the wealth of the Muslims, and the Prophet ﷺ commanded at his death that no two religions should remain in the Arabian Peninsula. Thaʿlabah must either be a Muslim, in which case it was obligatory upon Abū Bakr and ʿUmar to collect his zakāt without any leeway, or he was a disbeliever, in which case it was obligatory that he not remain in the Arabian Peninsula. Thus this report is undoubtedly baseless. Among its narrators are Muʿān ibn Rifāʿah, al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and ʿAlī ibn Yazīd (he is Ibn ʿAbd al-Malik), and all of them are weak.' The distinguished scholar ʿAdnān al-Ḥimash wrote a treatise criticizing this story, in which he gathered the statements of the scholars about it, entitled Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib al-Ṣaḥābī al-Muftarā ʿalayh (Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib, the Companion who was slandered).]

His saying: ﴿Did they not know that Allah knows their secret and their private talk, and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?﴾ Allah, exalted is He, informs them that He knows the secret and what is more hidden, and that He is most knowing of their inner thoughts, even if they show that if wealth comes to them they will give charity from it and be thankful for it. He knows them better than they know themselves, because He, exalted is He, is ʿAllām al-Ghuyūb (the Knower of the unseen), meaning He knows every unseen and every witnessed thing, every secret and private talk, and He knows what is apparent and what is hidden.

This is also one of the characteristics of the hypocrites: none of the believers is safe from their faultfinding and mockery in any circumstance. Even those who give charity are not spared from them. If one of them brought a large amount of wealth, they would say, "This is for show." And if he brought something small, they would say, "Allah is not in need of this man's charity." As al-Bukhari said:

Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Abu al-Nu'man al-Basri narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sulayman, from Abu Wa'il, from Abu Mas'ud, who said: "When the verse about charity was revealed, we used to carry loads on our backs [to earn money for charity]. A man came and gave a large amount in charity, and they said, 'He is showing off.' Another man came and gave one sa' (a measure), and they said, 'Allah is not in need of this man's charity.' Then the following was revealed: ﴿Those who find fault with the believers who give charity voluntarily, and with those who find nothing to give except their effort﴾ until the end of the verse."

Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Shu'bah with the same chain. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1415), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1018).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us: al-Jurayri narrated to us, from Abu al-Salil, who said: A man stood before us in our gathering at al-Baqi' and said: "My father, or my paternal uncle, told me that he saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at al-Baqi', and he was saying: 'Who will give charity, for which I will bear witness on his behalf on the Day of Resurrection?'" He said: "I untied from my turban one or two pieces of cloth, intending to give them in charity, but then what afflicts the son of Adam overtook me, so I tied my turban again. Then a man came whom I had never seen at al-Baqi', darker in complexion than anyone, and smaller than anyone, and with a camel he was driving, and I had never seen at al-Baqi' a she-camel better than it. He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, is this a charity?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Take this she-camel.' Then a man found fault with him and said: 'This man is giving this in charity! By Allah, it is better than him.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard him and said: 'You have lied; rather, he is better than you and better than it,' three times. Then he said: 'Woe to the owners of hundreds of camels,' three times. They said: 'Except for whom, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Except for whoever gives wealth like this and like this,' and he joined his two palms, to his right and to his left. Then he said: 'Successful is the one who abstains and strives,' three times: the one who abstains from comfortable living, the one who strives in worship."

[[Al-Musnad (5/34).]]

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, and said: "Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with forty uqiyyah of gold, and a man from the Ansar came with a sa' of food. Some of the hypocrites said: 'By Allah, Abd al-Rahman has not brought what he brought except for show.' And they said: 'If Allah and His Messenger were in need of this sa', [they would not accept it].'" [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/382).]]

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to the people one day and called out among them: "Gather your charities." The people gathered their charities. Then a man from the last of them came with a sa' of dates and said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is a sa' of dates. I spent my night drawing water with a rope until I earned two sa's of dates. I kept one of them, and I have brought you the other." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered him to scatter it among the charities. Some men mocked him and said: "Allah and His Messenger are in need of neither this nor anything of your sa'." Then Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Has anyone from among the recipients of charity remained?" He said: "No." Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said to him: "I have a hundred uqiyyah of gold for charity." Then Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said to him: "Are you insane?" He said: "I am not insane." He said: "Did you do what you did?" He said: "Yes. I have eight thousand. As for four thousand, I lend it to my Lord, and as for four thousand, it is for me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "May Allah bless you in what you kept and in what you gave." The hypocrites also found fault with him and said: "By Allah, Abd al-Rahman gave his gift only for show." And they were liars; he had only given voluntarily. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed his excuse and the excuse of his companion, the poor man who brought the sa' of dates. Allah, the Exalted, said in His Book: ﴿Those who find fault with the believers who give charity voluntarily﴾ until the end of the verse.

Similarly it was narrated from Mujahid and others.

Ibn Ishaq said: Those among the believers who gave charity voluntarily were: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, who gave four thousand dirhams; and Asim ibn Adi, brother of the Banu al-Ajlan. That was because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) encouraged charity and urged it. So Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf stood up and gave four thousand, and Asim stood up and gave one hundred wasq of dates. They found fault with both of them and said: "This is nothing but show." And the one who gave according to his effort was Abu Aqil, brother of the Banu Unayf al-Irashi, an ally of the Banu Amr ibn Awf, who brought a sa' of dates and poured it into the charity. They ridiculed him and said: "Allah is not in need of the sa' of Abu Aqil."

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Talut ibn Abbad narrated to us: Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Umar ibn Abi Salamah, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give charity, for I intend to send out an expedition." He said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have four thousand: two thousand I lend to my Lord, and two thousand for my dependants." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah bless you in what you gave and bless you in what you kept." A man from the Ansar spent the night and got two sa's of dates, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I got two sa's of dates: one sa' I lend to my Lord, and one sa' for my dependants." He said: The hypocrites found fault with him and said: "The one who gave is no different from Ibn Awf; he gave only for show!" And they said: "Were Allah and His Messenger not in need of this sa'?" So Allah revealed: ﴿Those who find fault with the believers who give charity voluntarily, and with those who find nothing to give except their effort, and they mock them, [Allah mocks them]﴾ until the end of the verse. [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (2216), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7/32): "In its chain is Amr ibn Abi Salamah, whom al-Ijli declared reliable, and Abu Khaythamah and Ibn Hibban; Shu'bah and others declared him weak, and the rest of its narrators are reliable."]]

Then he narrated it from Abu Kamil, from Abu Awanah, from Umar ibn Abi Salamah, from his father, as a mursal (a narration whose chain omits the Companion). [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (2216), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari (8/332), after quoting this mursal narration: "Abd ibn Humayd also narrated it from Yunus ibn Muhammad from Abu Awanah, and Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabari and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through other chains from Abu Awanah as a mursal."]] He said: No one transmitted it with a full chain except Talut.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakic narrated to us: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ubaydah, who narrated to me Khalid ibn Yasar, from Ibn Abi Aqil, from his father, who said: "I spent the night dragging a rope over my back for two sa's of dates. I went home with one of them for my family to live on, and I brought the other to draw near to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him, and he said: 'Scatter it among the charities.' He said: The people mocked and said: 'Allah was certainly not in need of the charity of this poor man.' So Allah revealed: ﴿Those who find fault with the believers who give charity voluntarily﴾, the two verses." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/388).]] Al-Tabarani also narrated it similarly from the hadith of Zayd ibn al-Hubab, from him. And he said: The name of Abu Aqil is Hubab. It is also said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Tha'labah. [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (4/45). In one report it reads "from Zayd ibn al-Hubab, from Khalid ibn Yasar," omitting Musa ibn Ubaydah; therefore al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7/33): "Its narrators are reliable, but I have not found anyone who declared Khalid ibn Yasar reliable or weak." However, al-Zayla'i in Takhrij al-Kashshaf (2/88) attributed it to al-Tabarani in his Mu'jam through the chain of Musa ibn Ubaydah from Khalid ibn Yasar, so perhaps it was dropped from the copies of al-Tabarani or al-Zayla'i made an error. Note: this is how it occurs here and in al-Tabarani: "The name of Abu Aqil is Hubab." Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Isabah (1/389): "So it occurs in al-Tabarani, but the correct form is Hibhab."]]

* *

His saying: ﴿They mock them; Allah mocks them﴾. This is by way of reciprocation for their evil conduct and their ridicule of the believers, since the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. He treated them as one who mocks others, as a vindication of the believers in this world, and He has prepared for the hypocrites in the Hereafter a painful punishment.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 9, verse 80:

Allah, the Exalted, informs His Prophet ﷺ that these hypocrites are not deserving of forgiveness, and that even if he seeks forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them.

It has been said that the number seventy was mentioned only to cut off the matter of seeking forgiveness for them, because the Arabs, in their modes of speech, mention seventy for emphasis and do not intend a precise limit by it, nor that whatever exceeds it would be contrary to it.

It has also been said: rather, it has a specific meaning (mafhum), as al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said when this verse was revealed: "I heard my Lord has permitted me regarding them. By Allah, I will seek forgiveness for them more than seventy times, perhaps Allah will forgive them!" So Allah said, out of His intense anger toward them: ﴿It is the same for them whether you seek forgiveness for them or do not seek forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 6].

Al-Sha'bi said: When 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy became gravely ill, his son went to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "My father is at the point of death, and I would love for you to attend him and pray over him." The Prophet ﷺ said: "What is your name?" He said: "al-Hubab ibn 'Abdullah." He said: "Rather, you are 'Abdullah ibn 'Abdullah, for al-Hubab is the name of a devil." He said: So he went with him until he attended him, and he put his shirt on him while he was in a state of sweat, and he prayed over him. He was asked: "Do you pray over him while he is a hypocrite [and he is a hypocrite]?" [Added from manuscripts T and A.] He said: "Allah said: ﴿Whether you seek forgiveness for them seventy times﴾, and I will seek forgiveness for him seventy, seventy, and seventy times."

Similarly, this was narrated from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid ibn Jabr, and Qatadah ibn Di'amah. Ibn Jarir narrated it with his chains of transmission.

Allah the Exalted says, censuring the hypocrites who stayed behind from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Battle of Tabuk, "and they rejoiced in their sitting [behind] after the Messenger's departure, and disliked to strive with their wealth and their lives in the way of Allah." And "they said" (i.e., some of them said to others), "Do not go forth in the heat." The going forth to the Battle of Tabuk was in the intense heat, at the time when the shade and the fruits were pleasant, and so they said, "Do not go forth in the heat." Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger, "Say" to them, "the Fire of Hell," to which you will return because of your opposition, "is more intense in heat" than what you fled from of heat; indeed, it is far more intense in heat than the fire, as the Imam Malik said, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The fire of the children of Adam, with which they kindle, is one part of seventy parts of the Fire of Hell." They said, "O Messenger of Allah, indeed it would have been sufficient." He said, "It has been made superior to it by sixty-nine parts." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) related it in their Sahihs from the hadith of Malik, with it.

And the Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan related to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Indeed, this fire of yours is one part of seventy parts of the Fire of Hell, and it was struck in the sea twice, and were it not for that, Allah would not have placed benefit in it for anyone." And its chain is also sound.

Al-Imam Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah related, from Abbas al-Duri, from Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr, from Sharik, from Asim, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Fire was kindled for a thousand years until it became red, then it was kindled for a thousand years until it became white, then it was kindled for a thousand years until it became black, so it is black like the dark night." Then al-Tirmidhi said: I do not know anyone who raised it except Yahya. Thus he said.

Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh related it from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Mukram, from Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'd, from his paternal uncle, from Sharik, who is Ibn Abd Allah al-Nakha'i, with it. Ibn Mardawayh also related, through the narration of Mubarak ibn Fadalah, from Thabit, from Anas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: "a fire whose fuel is people and stones" (al-Tahrim: 6), and said: "It was kindled over it for a thousand years until it became white, and a thousand years until it became red, and a thousand years until it became black, so it is black like the night, its flame does not shine."

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani related from the hadith of Tammam ibn Najih (whose status has been disputed), from al-Hasan, from Anas, raised (to the Prophet ﷺ): "If a spark of the fire of Hell were in the east, the one in the west would feel its heat."

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la related from Ishaq ibn Abi Isra'il, from Abu Ubaydah al-Haddad, from Hisham ibn Hassan (in all the copies: "Husam", and the correction is from Abu Ya'la), from Muhammad ibn Shabib, from Ja'far ibn Abi Wahshiyyah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If this mosque were a hundred thousand or more, and among them was a man from the people of the Fire who breathed, his breath would reach them, and the mosque and whoever is in it would burn." It is gharib.

Al-A'mash related from Abu Ishaq, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the least punished of the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection is the one who has two sandals and two thongs of fire, his brain boiling from them like a cauldron boils. He sees no one among the people of the Fire who is punished more severely than him, and indeed he is the least punished of them." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) related it in their Sahihs from the hadith of al-A'mash.

Muslim also said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah related to us, Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr related to us, Zuhayr ibn Muhammad related to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from al-Nu'man ibn Abi Ayyash, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the least punished of the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection is the one who wears two sandals of fire, his brain boiling from the heat of his sandals."

The Imam Ahmad said: Yahya related to us, from Ibn Ajlan, I heard my father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Indeed, the least punished of the people of the Fire is a man for whom two sandals will be made, from which his brain boils."

This is a good, strong chain; its narrators are on the condition of Muslim, and Allah knows best.

The hadiths and narrations from the Prophet on this are numerous. Allah the Exalted said in His Mighty Book: "No! Indeed it is the Blaze, stripping away the scalp" (al-Ma'arij: 15-16). And Allah the Exalted said: "Boiling water will be poured over their heads, by which what is in their bellies and the skins will be melted. And for them are maces of iron. Every time they wish to get out of it from distress, they will be returned into it, and [it will be said], 'Taste the punishment of the burning'" (al-Hajj: 19-22). And Allah the Exalted said: "Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our verses, We will drive them into a Fire. Every time their skins are roasted through, We will substitute for them other skins that they may taste the punishment" (al-Nisa: 56).

And Allah the Exalted said in this noble verse [the other one]: "Say, 'The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if they only understood.'" That is: if they had understanding and comprehension, they would have gone forth with the Messenger in the way of Allah in the heat, to protect themselves thereby from the heat of Hell, which is many times greater than this. But they are, as the other poet said:

"Like one seeking refuge from the scorching sand in the fire."

And another said:

"You have spent your life in protecting yourself from the heat and the cold...
And it would have been more fitting for you to guard against sins out of fear of the Fire..."

Then Allah, the Exalted in majesty, said, threatening these hypocrites for this their deed: "So let them laugh little, and let them weep much, as recompense for what they used to earn."

Ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas: "The worldly life is little; so let them laugh in it as much as they wish. When the worldly life ends and they arrive at Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, they will begin a weeping that never ends." Likewise said Abu Razin, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, Awn al-Uqayli, and Zayd ibn Aslam.

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Samad ibn Abi Khidash related to us, Muhammad ibn Humayd related to us (in all the copies: "Muhammad ibn Jubayr", and the correction is from Abu Ya'la), from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Imran ibn Zayd, Yazid al-Raqashi related to us, from Anas ibn Malik who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "O people, weep; and if you do not weep, then feign weeping, for the people of the Fire weep until their tears flow down their faces like streams, until the tears run out, then blood flows, and the eyes become ulcerated. Even if ships were sent sailing in them, they would sail."

Ibn Majah related it from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Yazid al-Raqashi, with it.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas related to us, Hammad al-Jazari related to us, from Zayd ibn Rufay', raising it, who said: "When the people of the Fire enter the Fire, they weep tears for a time, then they weep pus for a time." He said: "The guardians will say to them: 'O assembly of the wretched, you abandoned weeping in the abode in which its people were shown mercy in the world. Do you find today anyone you can seek help from?'" He said: "They will raise their voices: 'O people of Paradise, O assembly of fathers, mothers and children, we came out of the graves thirsty, and we were thirsty throughout the standing place, and we are thirsty today, so pour upon us some water or what Allah has provided you.' They will call for forty years and will not be answered; then He will answer them: 'Indeed you will remain' (al-Zukhruf: 77), and they will despair of every good."

Allah the Exalted says, commanding His Messenger (ﷺ) — [[In manuscript A: "ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam".]] "If Allah brings you back," that is, returns you from this expedition of yours, "to a group of them" — Qatadah said: "It was related to us that they were twelve men" — "and they ask your permission to go out," that is, to go with you on another expedition, "then say: 'You will never go out with me, and you will never fight an enemy with me.'" That is, as a rebuke and a punishment for them. Then He gave the reason for this in His words: "Indeed, you were content with sitting back the first time." This is like His saying, "And We turn their hearts and their sights away, as they did not believe in it the first time" (Al-An'am: 110). Indeed, among the recompense for an evil deed is another evil deed after it, just as among the reward for a good deed is another good deed after it. Similarly, He said regarding the Hudaybiyah expedition: "Those who were left behind will say, when you set out to take spoils, 'Leave us to follow you.' They want to change the words of Allah. Say: 'You will never follow us; thus has Allah said beforehand'" (Al-Fath: 15).

* *

As for His saying, "So sit with those who remain behind" (fa-uq'udu ma'a al-khalifin): Ibn ʿAbbas said: "That is, the men who stayed behind from the raiders." Qatadah said: "'So sit with those who remain behind' — that is, with the women."

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: "This does not hold, because the plural of the women (al-nisa') is not formed with the (ya' and nun) ending; and if the women were intended, it would have said: fa-uq'udu ma'a al-khawalif, or al-khalifat (the feminine plurals)." He preferred the view of Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/405).]]

God Almighty commanded His Messenger ﷺ to disassociate himself from the hypocrites, and forbade him to pray over any of them when they died, or to stand at their graves to seek forgiveness for them or to supplicate for them, because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and died in that state. This is a general ruling concerning everyone whose hypocrisy is known, although the occasion of the revelation of the verse concerned ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the leader of the hypocrites, as al-Bukhari stated:

Ubayd ibn Ismaʿil narrated to us, from Abu Usama, from Ubaydullah, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn Umar, who said: When ʿAbdullah (that is, Ibn Ubayy) died, his son ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbdullah came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him to give him his shirt in which to shroud his father. He gave it to him. Then he asked him to pray over him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up to pray over him. ʿUmar stood up, took hold of the garment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you pray over him when your Lord has forbidden you to pray over him?!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah only gave me a choice when He said: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them. Even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them﴾, and I will increase it beyond the seventy." He said: "He is a hypocrite!" So he prayed over him [the Messenger of Allah ﷺ]. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the verse: ﴿And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave﴾.

Muslim narrated it similarly, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba, from Abu Usama Hammad ibn Usama, with the same chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4670) and Sahih Muslim no. (2774).]

Then al-Bukhari narrated it from Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir, from Anas ibn Iyad, from Ubaydullah, who is Ibn Umar al-ʿUmari, with the same chain, and he said: "So he prayed over him, and we prayed with him, and Allah revealed: ﴿And never pray over any of them who dies﴾", to the end of the verse.

Similarly Imam Ahmad narrated it from Yahya ibn Saʿid al-Qattan, from Ubaydullah, with the same chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4672) and al-Musnad (2/18).]

It has also been narrated from the hadith of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab himself, in a similar manner. Imam Ahmad said:

Yaʿqub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, Al-Zuhri narrated to me, from Ubaydullah ibn ʿAbdullah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, say: "When ʿAbdullah ibn [Ubayy died, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was called to pray over him. He went to him, and when he stood over him intending to pray, I moved until I stood in front of his chest, and I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, over the enemy of Allah, ʿAbdullah ibn] Ubayy, who on such-and-such a day said such-and-such?" — enumerating his days. He said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was smiling, until when I had said too much, he said: 'Step back from me, O ʿUmar. I was given a choice and I chose. It has been said to me: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them. Even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 80]. If I knew that if I increased beyond the seventy he would be forgiven, I would increase.'" He said: Then he prayed over him, walked with him, and stood at his grave until the burial was finished. ʿUmar said: "I am astonished at myself and my boldness towards the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah and His Messenger know best!" He said: "By Allah, it was not long before these two verses were revealed: ﴿And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave. Indeed, they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and died while they were defiantly disobedient﴾."

So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never prayed over any hypocrite after him, nor stood at his grave, until Allah took him, Mighty and Majestic.

Similarly al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his "al-Tafsir", from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, with the same chain, and said: "Hasan sahih." Al-Bukhari narrated it from Yahya ibn Bukayr, from al-Layth, from ʿUqayl, from al-Zuhri, with the same chain, mentioning the like of it and saying: "Step back from me, O ʿUmar." When I had said too much to him, he said: "I was given a choice and I chose. And if I knew that if I increased beyond the seventy he would be forgiven [in K: 'would be forgiven'], I would increase beyond them." He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over him, then left. He did not remain long before the two verses of Bara'ah were revealed: ﴿And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave﴾, to the end of the verse. So I was astonished afterwards at my boldness towards the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ knows best. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4671).]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi ʿUbayd narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: When ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy died, his son came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you do not go to him, we will continue to be disgraced by this." So the Prophet ﷺ came to him, and found that he had been placed in his grave. He said: "Why not before you placed him in it!" So he was taken out of his grave, and he spat on him from his head to his feet, and clothed him in his shirt.

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from Abu Dawud al-Harrani, from Yaʿla ibn ʿUbayd, from ʿAbd al-Malik, who is Ibn Abi Sulayman, with the same chain. [Al-Musnad (3/371) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (9665).]

Al-Bukhari said: ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUthman narrated to us, Ibn ʿUyayna informed us, from ʿAmr, who heard Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah say: The Prophet ﷺ came to ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy after he had been placed in his grave, so he ordered that he be brought out, and he was placed on his knees, and he spat on him with his saliva, and clothed him in his shirt. And Allah knows best. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5795).]

He also narrated it in more than one place together with Muslim and al-Nasa'i, through different routes, from Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna, with the same chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (1270, 1350, 3008), Sahih Muslim no. (2773) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (4/37, 38).]

Imam Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Khaliq al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: ʿAmr ibn ʿAli narrated to us, Yahya narrated to us, Mujalid narrated to us, ʿAmir narrated to us, Jabir narrated to us (ḥ). And Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Maghraʾ al-Dawsi narrated to us, Mujalid narrated to us, from al-Shaʿbi, from Jabir, who said: When the head of the hypocrites died — Yahya ibn Saʿid said: "in Medina" — he had bequeathed that the Prophet ﷺ should pray over him. His son came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: "My father bequeathed that he be shrouded in your shirt." This statement is in the narration of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Maghraʾ. Yahya said in his narration: "So he prayed over him and clothed him in his shirt, and Allah, Most High, revealed: ﴿And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave﴾." ʿAbd al-Rahman added: "The Prophet ﷺ took off his shirt and gave it to him, and walked and prayed over him and stood at his grave. Jibril, peace be upon him, came to him when he turned away and said: ﴿And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave﴾." [Ibn Majah also narrated it in al-Sunan no. (1524) by way of Yahya ibn Saʿid from Mujalid, with similar wording.] This is an isnad with no fault in it, and what precedes it corroborates it.

Imam Abu Jaʿfar al-Tabari said: [Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, (Abu Ahmad narrated to us,)] Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wanted to pray over ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy, and Jibril took hold of his garment and said: ﴿And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave﴾.

Al-Hafiz Abu Yaʿla narrated it in his Musnad, from the hadith of Yazid al-Raqashi, and it is weak. [Tafsir al-Tabari (14/407) and Musnad Abi Yaʿla (7/145).]

Qatadah said: ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy sent to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was ill. When he entered upon him, the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Has the love of the Jews destroyed you?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I only sent for you so that you would ask forgiveness for me, and I did not send for you so that you would rebuke me!" Then ʿAbdullah asked him to give him his shirt to shroud his father in, so he gave it to him, prayed over him, and stood at his grave. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave﴾.

Some of the early scholars mentioned that he clothed him in his shirt only because when al-Abbas was brought [as a captive], a shirt was sought for him, but no garment fitting his size was found except the shirt of ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy, since he was large and tall. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did this for him as a reward for him. Allah knows best.

For this reason, after the revelation of this noble verse, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not pray over any of the hypocrites, nor stand at their graves, as Imam Ahmad said:

Yaʿqub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from his father, ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Qatadah narrated to me, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he was called to a funeral, would ask about the deceased. If good was said about him, he would stand and pray over him, and if anything other than that was said about him, he would say to his family: "Deal with him as you see fit," and he would not pray over him. [Al-Musnad (5/299).]

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab would not pray over the funeral of anyone whose condition was unknown until Huzayfah ibn al-Yaman prayed over it, because he knew the identities of the hypocrites whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had informed him of. For this reason he was called "the keeper of the secret," which no one else among the Companions knew.

Abu ʿUbayd said in the book "al-Gharib" regarding the hadith of ʿUmar that he wanted to pray over the funeral of a man, so Huzayfah pushed him (fa-marzahu), as if he wanted to stop him from praying over it. Then it was reported from some of them that "al-marz", in the dialect of the people of al-Yamamah, means pinching with the fingertips.

When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade praying over the hypocrites and standing at their graves to ask forgiveness for them, this act became among the greatest acts of devotion for the believers, so it was prescribed. In performing it there is a great reward, as has been established in the Sahih collections and others from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever attends a funeral until it is prayed over, he has one qirat (of reward), and whoever attends it until it is buried, he has two qirats." It was said: "What are the two qirats?" He said: "The smaller of them is like Mount Uhud." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih no. (1325) and Muslim in his Sahih no. (945).]

As for standing at the grave of a believer after he has died, Abu Dawud said: Ibrahim ibn Musa al-Razi narrated to us, Hisham informed us, from ʿAbdullah ibn Bahir, from Hani' — who is Abu Saʿid al-Barbari, client of ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan — from ʿUthman, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ finished burying a man, he would stand over him and say: "Ask forgiveness for your brother, and ask Allah to make him firm, for he is now being questioned."

Abu Dawud alone narrated it, may Allah have mercy on him. [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3221).]
The commentary on a parallel to this noble verse has already been given [see the commentary on verse 55 of this surah]. And to Allah belongs all praise.

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah, the Exalted, says, rebuking and censuring those who stayed behind from jihad, who shrank from it although they had the ability to do it and the means and capacity for it: "They asked your permission, [O Muhammad], to remain behind, and said, 'Leave us to be with those who sit back.'" They were content for themselves with shame and with sitting in the city with the women, who are the "khawalif" (those left behind), after the army had gone out. When the fighting comes, they are the most cowardly of people; and when there is safety, they are the most talkative of people. Allah, the Exalted, said about them in another verse: ﴿And when fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like one fainting before death. But when fear departs, they lash you with sharp tongues﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 19], meaning: their tongues become loud with sharp, forceful speech during peace, while in war they are the most cowardly of things. As the poet said:

Among peace-time donkeys, there is coarseness and harshness,
But in war, they resemble the women in their menstrual state.[[The verse is in Ibn Hisham's al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (1/656), attributed to Hind bint 'Utbah. "Al-a'yar" is the plural of "ir," meaning donkey; "al-'awarik" means those who are menstruating.]]

Allah, the Exalted, also said in another verse: ﴿And those who believe say, "Why has a surah not been sent down?" But when a clear surah is sent down and fighting is mentioned in it, you see those in whose hearts is disease looking at you with the look of one fainting from death. So woe to them. Obedience and good speech [would have been better]. And when the matter is resolved, if they had been true to Allah, it would have been better for them. So would you, if you were to take charge, do corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship?﴾ [Muhammad: 20–22]

* *

His saying: ﴿And Allah has sealed over their hearts﴾ means: because of their shrinking from jihad and from going out with the Messenger in the way of Allah. ﴿So they do not understand﴾ means: they do not comprehend what is good for them so that they would do it, nor what is harmful to them so that they would avoid it.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 9, verse 88–89:

When Allah (Exalted is He) mentioned the blame of the hypocrites, He explained the praise of the believers and what awaits them in their Hereafter. So He said: ﴿But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their wealth and their lives﴾, up to the end of the two verses, describing their state and their final outcome.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And those will have the good things﴾, meaning: in the Abode of the Hereafter, in the Gardens of Firdaws and the high ranks.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And those will have the good things﴾, meaning: in the Abode of the Hereafter, in the Gardens of Firdaws and the high ranks.

Then Allah, exalted is He, clarified the condition of those with valid excuses for abandoning jihad, those who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) offering their apologies to him, and explaining to him the weakness and inability to go out in which they found themselves. They were among the Bedouin Arabs living around Madinah.

Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to read, "wa-ja'a al-mu'dhirun" (وَجَاءَ المُعْذَرُون) with the light pronunciation (taskhif, i.e., without the doubled letter), and he would say: "They are the people of valid excuse (ahl al-'udhr)."

Similarly, Ibn 'Uyaynah reported from Humayd, from Mujahid, the same.

Ibn Ishaq said: "It has reached me that they were a group from the Banu Ghifar, among them Khufaf ibn Ima' ibn Rahada."

This view is the most apparent meaning of the verse, because after this He said: ﴿And those who lied to Allah and His Messenger sat (at home)﴾, meaning they did not come to offer excuses.

Ibn Jurayj reported from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And the excuse-makers among the Bedouins came﴾, that he said: "They were a group from the Banu Ghifar. They came and made excuses, but Allah did not accept their excuses." Likewise said al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq. However, the first view is more apparent, and Allah knows best, because of what we mentioned earlier of His saying after it: ﴿And those who lied to Allah and His Messenger sat (at home)﴾, meaning, other Bedouins sat back from coming to make excuses. Then He threatened them with a painful punishment, saying: ﴿Those among them who disbelieved will be struck by a painful punishment﴾.

Then Allah, exalted is He, explained the excuses for which there is no blame on one who stays behind from fighting. He mentioned among them what is inherent in a person and never leaves him, which is weakness in the physical constitution that prevents him from enduring the hardship of jihad, such as blindness, lameness and the like. For this reason He began with it. Then He mentioned what is incidental, caused by an illness that affects his body and keeps him from going out in the way of Allah, or by his poverty (in T and A: "faqr") that prevents him from equipping himself for war. There is no blame on these people if they stay behind, provided they give sincere counsel while they remain at home, do not spread fear among the people, and do not discourage them, and they are doing good in this state. For this reason He said: ﴿There is no blame upon the good-doers, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay, from Abu Thumama, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Disciples (al-Hawariyyun) said: "O Spirit of Allah, tell us about the one who gives sincere counsel to Allah." He said: "The one who prefers the right of Allah over the right of people. When two matters come to him, or the matter of this world and the matter of the Hereafter appear to him, he begins with the one that belongs to the Hereafter, and then he devotes himself to the one that belongs to this world."

Al-Awza'i said: The people went out for the prayer for rain (istisqa'), and Bilal ibn Sa'd stood among them, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "O assembly of those present, do you not acknowledge your wrongdoing?" They said: "O Allah, yes." He said: "O Allah, we hear You saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the good-doers﴾. O Allah, we have acknowledged our wrongdoing, so forgive us, have mercy upon us, and give us rain." He raised his hands and they raised their hands, and they were given rain.

Qatada said: This verse was revealed concerning A'idh ibn Amr al-Muzani.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Ubayd Allah al-Razi narrated to us, Ibn Jabir narrated to us, from Ibn Farwa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "I used to write for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I was writing Bara'a (Surat al-Tawba), and I had placed the pen behind my ear when we were commanded to fight. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept looking at what was being revealed to him. A blind man came and said: 'What about me, O Messenger of Allah, since I am blind?' So Allah revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick﴾, to the end of the verse." [Al-Daraqutni narrated it in al-Afrad, as cited in al-Atraf of Ibn Tahir (p. 134), and said: "It is gharib (unusual) from the hadith of Abu Farwa, Muslim ibn Salim, from him, i.e. Ibn Abi Layla, from Zayd. Muhammad ibn Jabir alone narrated it from him, and it is gharib from the hadith of Ibn Abi Layla; no one is known to have narrated it from him except Abu Farwa."]

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning this verse: The reason was that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded the people to set out campaigning with him. A group of his Companions came to him, among them Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal al-Muzani (in T, K and A: "Abd Allah ibn Ma'qil ibn Muqarrin"), and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, carry us." He said to them: "By Allah, I do not find anything to carry you on." So they turned away weeping, and it grieved them to sit out from jihad while they could not find provisions or a mount. When Allah saw their eagerness for His love and the love of His Messenger, He revealed their excuse in His Book, saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who find nothing to spend, when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger﴾, to His words: ﴿Then they do not know.﴾

Mujahid said concerning His words: ﴿nor upon those who came to you that you might carry them, [and] you said, "I cannot find anything to carry you on"﴾: it was revealed concerning the sons of Muqarrin of Muzayna.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: They were seven men: from Banu Amr ibn Awf, Salim ibn Umayr (in K: "Awf"); from Banu Waqif, Hirmi (in all copies: "Harmi," corrected from Usd al-Ghaba and al-Isaba) ibn Amr; from Banu Mazin ibn al-Najjar, Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b, who was called Abu Layla; from Banu al-Mu'alla, [Salman ibn Sakhr]; from Banu Harithah, Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, Abu Abla, who is the one who gave up his honour in charity, and Allah accepted it from him [this addition is from T, K and al-Tabari; in H: "Fadl Allah"]; from Banu Salima, Amr ibn Anama (in K: "Anaza") and Abd Allah ibn Amr al-Muzani.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said in the course of recounting the expedition of Tabuk: Then some men among the Muslims came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They were the weepers, seven men from the Ansar and others, from Banu Amr ibn Awf (in A: "Awf"): Salim ibn Umayr, and Ulba ibn Zayd, brother of Banu Harithah, and Abu Layla Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b, brother of Banu Mazin ibn al-Najjar, and Amr ibn al-Hammam ibn al-Jamuh, brother of Banu Salima, and Abd Allah ibn al-Mughaffal al-Muzani. Some people say it was Abd Allah ibn Amr al-Muzani; and Harami ibn Abd Allah, brother of Banu Waqif; and Irbad (in all copies: "Iyad," corrected from Ibn Hisham, as noted in the margin of the Shu'ayb edition) ibn Sariya al-Fazari. They asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to provide them with mounts, and they were in need. He said: "I do not find anything to carry you on." So they turned away, their eyes overflowing with tears from grief that they could not find anything to spend. [Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya (2/518).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Umar ibn al-Awdi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There are people you left behind in Madina; you did not spend any expenditure, nor cross any valley, nor gain any gain from an enemy, except that they have shared the reward with you." Then he recited: ﴿nor upon those who came to you that you might carry them, [and] you said, "I cannot find anything to carry you on"﴾, to the end of the verse.

The origin of this hadith is in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of [blank space in all copies, about one word], that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, in Madina there are people; you did not cross a valley, nor travel a journey [...] (a word added from A and Muslim) except that they were with you." They said: "And they are in Madina?" He said: "Yes, the excuse has held them back." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2839, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him; Sahih Muslim, no. 1911, from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You have left behind in Madina men (in T and A: "peoples") who, whenever you crossed a valley or travelled a road, shared the reward with you; the illness held them back."

Muslim and Ibn Majah narrated it through several chains, from al-A'mash, with the same wording.

Then He mentioned what is incidental, caused by an illness that affects his body and keeps him from going out in the way of Allah, or by his poverty (in T and A: "faqr") that prevents him from equipping himself for war. There is no blame on these people if they stay behind, provided they give sincere counsel while they remain at home, do not spread fear among the people, and do not discourage them, and they are doing good in this state. For this reason He said: ﴿There is no blame upon the good-doers, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay, from Abu Thumama, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Disciples (al-Hawariyyun) said: "O Spirit of Allah, tell us about the one who gives sincere counsel to Allah." He said: "The one who prefers the right of Allah over the right of people. When two matters come to him, or the matter of this world and the matter of the Hereafter appear to him, he begins with the one that belongs to the Hereafter, and then he devotes himself to the one that belongs to this world."

Al-Awza'i said: The people went out for the prayer for rain (istisqa'), and Bilal ibn Sa'd stood among them, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "O assembly of those present, do you not acknowledge your wrongdoing?" They said: "O Allah, yes." He said: "O Allah, we hear You saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the good-doers﴾. O Allah, we have acknowledged our wrongdoing, so forgive us, have mercy upon us, and give us rain." He raised his hands and they raised their hands, and they were given rain.

Qatada said: This verse was revealed concerning A'idh ibn Amr al-Muzani.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Ubayd Allah al-Razi narrated to us, Ibn Jabir narrated to us, from Ibn Farwa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "I used to write for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I was writing Bara'a (Surat al-Tawba), and I had placed the pen behind my ear when we were commanded to fight. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept looking at what was being revealed to him. A blind man came and said: 'What about me, O Messenger of Allah, since I am blind?' So Allah revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick﴾, to the end of the verse." [Al-Daraqutni narrated it in al-Afrad, as cited in al-Atraf of Ibn Tahir (p. 134), and said: "It is gharib (unusual) from the hadith of Abu Farwa, Muslim ibn Salim, from him, i.e. Ibn Abi Layla, from Zayd. Muhammad ibn Jabir alone narrated it from him, and it is gharib from the hadith of Ibn Abi Layla; no one is known to have narrated it from him except Abu Farwa."]

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning this verse: The reason was that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded the people to set out campaigning with him. A group of his Companions came to him, among them Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal al-Muzani (in T, K and A: "Abd Allah ibn Ma'qil ibn Muqarrin"), and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, carry us." He said to them: "By Allah, I do not find anything to carry you on." So they turned away weeping, and it grieved them to sit out from jihad while they could not find provisions or a mount. When Allah saw their eagerness for His love and the love of His Messenger, He revealed their excuse in His Book, saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who find nothing to spend, when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger﴾, to His words: ﴿Then they do not know.﴾

Mujahid said concerning His words: ﴿nor upon those who came to you that you might carry them, [and] you said, "I cannot find anything to carry you on"﴾: it was revealed concerning the sons of Muqarrin of Muzayna.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: They were seven men: from Banu Amr ibn Awf, Salim ibn Umayr (in K: "Awf"); from Banu Waqif, Hirmi (in all copies: "Harmi," corrected from Usd al-Ghaba and al-Isaba) ibn Amr; from Banu Mazin ibn al-Najjar, Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b, who was called Abu Layla; from Banu al-Mu'alla, [Salman ibn Sakhr]; from Banu Harithah, Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, Abu Abla, who is the one who gave up his honour in charity, and Allah accepted it from him [this addition is from T, K and al-Tabari; in H: "Fadl Allah"]; from Banu Salima, Amr ibn Anama (in K: "Anaza") and Abd Allah ibn Amr al-Muzani.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said in the course of recounting the expedition of Tabuk: Then some men among the Muslims came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They were the weepers, seven men from the Ansar and others, from Banu Amr ibn Awf (in A: "Awf"): Salim ibn Umayr, and Ulba ibn Zayd, brother of Banu Harithah, and Abu Layla Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b, brother of Banu Mazin ibn al-Najjar, and Amr ibn al-Hammam ibn al-Jamuh, brother of Banu Salima, and Abd Allah ibn al-Mughaffal al-Muzani. Some people say it was Abd Allah ibn Amr al-Muzani; and Harami ibn Abd Allah, brother of Banu Waqif; and Irbad (in all copies: "Iyad," corrected from Ibn Hisham, as noted in the margin of the Shu'ayb edition) ibn Sariya al-Fazari. They asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to provide them with mounts, and they were in need. He said: "I do not find anything to carry you on." So they turned away, their eyes overflowing with tears from grief that they could not find anything to spend. [Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya (2/518).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Umar ibn al-Awdi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There are people you left behind in Madina; you did not spend any expenditure, nor cross any valley, nor gain any gain from an enemy, except that they have shared the reward with you." Then he recited: ﴿nor upon those who came to you that you might carry them, [and] you said, "I cannot find anything to carry you on"﴾, to the end of the verse.

The origin of this hadith is in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of [blank space in all copies, about one word], that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, in Madina there are people; you did not cross a valley, nor travel a journey [...] (a word added from A and Muslim) except that they were with you." They said: "And they are in Madina?" He said: "Yes, the excuse has held them back." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2839, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him; Sahih Muslim, no. 1911, from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You have left behind in Madina men (in T and A: "peoples") who, whenever you crossed a valley or travelled a road, shared the reward with you; the illness held them back."

Muslim and Ibn Majah narrated it through several chains, from al-A'mash, with the same wording.

Then Allah, exalted is He, turned the reproach toward those who ask permission to stay behind while they are wealthy, and He rebuked them for being content to be with the women who stay behind in the tents (al-khawalif fi al-rihal), ﴿and Allah has sealed upon their hearts, so they do not know.﴾

Allah, the Exalted, informed about the hypocrites that when they return to Madinah, they will offer excuses to you. ﴿Say: "Do not offer excuses; we will never believe you"﴾, meaning: we will never accept you as truthful. ﴿Allah has already informed us of your news﴾, meaning: Allah has already made known to us your circumstances. ﴿And Allah will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger﴾, meaning: He will make your deeds manifest to people in this world. ﴿Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾ [[In A: "ستردون" which is an error.]], meaning: He will inform you of your deeds, both good and bad, and will recompense you for them.

Then He informed about them that they would swear oaths while making excuses, so that you would turn away from them and not reproach them. ﴿So turn away from them﴾, out of contempt for them. ﴿Indeed, they are impure﴾, meaning: they are corrupt, and their inner selves and beliefs are unclean. ﴿And their refuge is Hell﴾ in their Hereafter, ﴿as recompense for what they used to earn﴾, meaning: of sins and transgressions.

He also informed that even if they seek your pleasure by their oaths to you, ﴿indeed, Allah is not pleased with the defiant people﴾, meaning: those who go out of obedience to Him and to His Messenger. Indeed, fisq (defiance) is going out, and from it the mouse was named "fuwaysiqah" because it comes out of its hole to cause corruption. And it is said: "fasaqat al-rutabah" when the date emerges from its sheath [[In T: "كمامها".]].
