Ibn Kathir said: Allah, the Exalted, informs that among the Bedouins (al-A'rab) there are disbelievers, hypocrites and believers, and that their disbelief and hypocrisy are greater and more severe than those of others, and more deserving, meaning more likely, that they not know the limits of what Allah has sent down to His Messenger. As al-A'mash related from Ibrahim, who said: A Bedouin sat with Zayd ibn Sawhan while he was narrating to his companions, and his hand had been struck on the day of Nahawand. The Bedouin said: "By Allah, your speech delights me, but your hand troubles me." Zayd said: "What about my hand troubles you? It is the left one." The Bedouin said: "By Allah, I do not know: do they cut off the right or the left?" Then Zayd ibn Sawhan [in K: "Sawkhan"] said: "Allah has spoken the truth: ﴿The Bedouins are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy, and more likely not to know the limits of what Allah has sent down to His Messenger﴾."

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Musa, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever dwells in the desert becomes coarse, whoever follows game becomes heedless, and whoever visits the ruler is tested."

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also narrated it through various chains, from Sufyan al-Thawri, with the same wording.[[Al-Musnad (1/357), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2859), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2256), and Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/195).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib; we only know it from the hadith of al-Thawri."

Since harshness and coarseness are found among the people of the deserts, Allah did not send a Messenger from among them; rather, the prophethood was from the people of the towns, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns﴾ [Yusuf: 109]. When that Bedouin presented that gift to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he returned to him several times its value until he was satisfied, and he said: "I had intended not to accept a gift except from a Qurashi, or a Thaqafi, or an Ansari, or a Dawsi."[[Narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan (6/279) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] This is because these people lived in the cities: Makkah, al-Ta'if, al-Madinah and Yemen, so they were more refined in character than the Bedouins, because of the coarseness inherent in the Bedouins' natures.

The hadith of the [Bedouin] concerning kissing children: Muslim said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, both saying: Abu Usamah and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aishah, who said: Some Bedouins came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Do you kiss your children?" They said: "Yes." They said: "But by Allah, we do not kiss them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What can I do if Allah has removed mercy from your hearts?" Ibn Numayr said: "from your heart is mercy."[[Sahih Muslim no. (2317).]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾, meaning: All-Knowing of who deserves to be taught faith and knowledge, and All-Wise in what He has apportioned among His servants of knowledge and ignorance, faith and disbelief, and hypocrisy. He is not questioned about what He does, due to His knowledge and wisdom.

Allah, the Exalted, also informs that among them is one who ﴿takes what he spends﴾, meaning in the way of Allah, ﴿as a loss﴾, meaning a penalty and a deprivation, ﴿and awaits misfortunes for you﴾, meaning he waits for calamities and afflictions to befall you. ﴿Upon them is the evil turn of fortune﴾, meaning it is reflected back upon them, and the evil revolves upon them. ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾, meaning He hears the supplications of His servants and knows who deserves victory and who deserves abandonment.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And among the Bedouins is one who believes in Allah and the Last Day, and takes what he spends as means of nearness to Allah and for the prayers of the Messenger﴾. This is the praiseworthy category of the Bedouins, those who take what they spend in the way of Allah as an act of nearness through which they draw close to Allah, seeking by it the Messenger's supplication for them. ﴿Unquestionably, it is a means of nearness for them﴾, meaning that this reward is indeed attained by them. ﴿Allah will admit them into His mercy. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Ibn Kathir said: He, exalted is He, informs us of His pleasure with the foremost (al-Sabiqun) among the Muhajirun (Emigrants) and the Ansar (Helpers), and with those who followed them in excellence. They are pleased with Him for what He has prepared for them of Gardens of bliss and enduring delight.

Ash-Sha'bi said: "The foremost, the first, among the Muhajirun and the Ansar are those who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan (Bay'at al-Ridwan) in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah."

Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Muhammad ibn Sirin, al-Hasan, and Qatadah said: "They are those who prayed towards both qiblahs (al-qiblatayn) with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) passed by a man who was reciting: ﴿And the foremost, the first, of the Muhajirun and the Ansar﴾. Umar took him by the hand and said, "Who taught you this?" He said, "Ubayy ibn Ka'b." Umar said, "Do not leave me until I take you to him." When they came to him, Umar said, "Did you teach him this verse in this way?" He said, "Yes." Umar said, "And did you hear it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said, "Yes." Umar said, "I used to think that we had attained a rank that no one after us would reach." Ubayy said, "The confirmation of this verse is in the beginning of Surah al-Jumu'ah: ﴿And others from among them who have not yet joined them. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ (Al-Jumu'ah: 3). And in Surah al-Hashr: ﴿And those who came after them say, 'Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith﴾ (Al-Hashr: 10). And in Surah al-Anfal: ﴿And those who believed after [them] and emigrated and fought alongside you – they are of you﴾ (Al-Anfal: 75), up to the end of the verse." Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated it. [Tafsir al-Tabari (14/438).]

He (Ibn Jarir) said: It is reported from al-Hasan al-Basri that he used to recite it with the "al-Ansar" in the nominative case (raf'), as a conjunction (ma'tuf) upon ﴿and the foremost, the first﴾.

So Allah, the Mighty, has informed us that He is pleased with the foremost, first ones among the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and those who followed them in excellence. Woe, then, to whoever hates them, reviles them, or hates or reviles some of them. This is especially true of the master of the Companions after the Messenger (ﷺ), the best and most excellent of them, namely the Siddiq al-Akbar (the greatest truthful one) and the greatest Caliph, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah (may Allah be pleased with him). The forsaken sect of the Rafidah (an extremist Shi'i group) show enmity to the most excellent of the Companions, hate them, and revile them – we seek refuge in Allah from that. This indicates that their minds are inverted and their hearts are overturned. How can they have faith in the Qur'an when they revile those with whom Allah is pleased? As for the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah), they seek Allah's pleasure for those with whom He is pleased, revile those whom Allah and His Messenger have reviled, show loyalty to those who are loyal to Allah, and show enmity to those who oppose Allah. They are followers, not innovators; they follow the example and do not initiate innovation. For this reason they are the Party of Allah, the successful, and His believing servants.

Allah informs His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, that among the Arab tribes around Madinah there are hypocrites (munafiqun), and among the people of Madinah too there are hypocrites: ﴿They have persisted in hypocrisy﴾. That is, they became accustomed to it and continued in it. From this comes the saying: a devil who is marid (obstinate, rebellious), and it is said: so-and-so rebelled (tamarrada) against Allah, meaning he became insolent and tyrannical.

* *

His saying: ﴿You do not know them; We know them﴾ does not contradict His saying: ﴿And if We willed, We would have shown them to you, and you would have known them by their marks; and you will surely know them by the tone of their speech﴾ [Muhammad: 30]. This is because it is a matter of recognizing them through characteristics by which they are known, not that he knew all of the hypocrites and doubters among those with him individually and by name. He did know that some of those who mixed with him from the people of Madinah were hypocrites, even though he saw them morning and evening. The evidence for this, with a sound chain, is what Imam Ahmad related in his Musnad, where he said:

Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Nu'man ibn Salim, from a man, from Jubayr ibn Mut'im, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, they claim that there is no reward for us in Makkah." He said: "Your rewards will surely reach you, even if you were in the hole of a fox." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ inclined his head towards me and said: "Indeed, among my companions there are hypocrites." [[al-Musnad (4/83).]]

Its meaning: some hypocrites and rumour-mongers may utter words that have no basis, and such a statement as the one Jubayr ibn Mut'im heard came from people of this sort. It has already been mentioned in the commentary on His saying: ﴿And they planned what they could not attain﴾ [al-Tawbah: 74] that he, peace be upon him, [[In A: "sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam".]] informed Hudhayfah of the identities of fourteen or fifteen hypocrites. This is a specification which does not imply that he knew all of their names and identities. And Allah knows best.

Al-Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir related in the biography of "Abu 'Umar al-Bayruti," through the route of Hisham ibn 'Ammar: Sadaqah ibn Khalid narrated to us, Ibn Jabir narrated to us, the Shaykh of Beirut, who was known as Abu 'Umar, narrated to me, I think, from Abu al-Darda': that a man called "Harmalah" came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Faith is here" — and he pointed with his hand to his tongue — "and hypocrisy is here" — and he pointed with his hand to his heart — "and he does not mention Allah except a little." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Allah, make for him a tongue that remembers You, and a heart that gives thanks, grant him my love and the love of those who love me, and turn his affair towards good." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I had companions among the hypocrites and I was a leader among them; shall I not bring them to you?" He said: "Whoever comes to us, we will ask forgiveness for him; but whoever persists in his religion, then Allah is more entitled to him, and do not tear open the veil of anyone." [[See: Mukhtasar Tarikh Dimashq by Ibn Manzur (29/76).]]

He said: Likewise, Abu Ahmad al-Hakim related it from Abu Bakr al-Baghandi, from Hisham ibn 'Ammar, with it.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah concerning this verse, that he said: "What is the matter with people who burden themselves with knowing the people's affairs? So-and-so is in Paradise, and so-and-so is in Hell. When you ask one of them about himself, he says, 'I do not know!' By my life, you know your own share better than you know the conditions of people! You have taken on something that the prophets before you did not take on. The Prophet of Allah Nuh said: ﴿He said: And what knowledge have I of what they used to do?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 112]. The Prophet of Allah Shu'ayb said: ﴿What remains with Allah is better for you, if you are believers. And I am not a guardian over you﴾ [Hud: 86]. And Allah said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿You do not know them; We know them﴾." [[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/253).]]

Al-Suddi said, from Abu Malik, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this verse: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood to deliver a sermon on Friday and said: "Go out, O so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite; and go out, O so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite." So he expelled from the mosque some people among them, and exposed them. 'Umar came while they were being removed from the mosque, and he hid from them out of shame, because he had not attended the Friday prayer, and he thought the people had dispersed. They too hid from 'Umar, thinking that he had learned of their matter. Then 'Umar came and entered the mosque, and found that the people had not prayed. A man among the Muslims said to him: "Rejoice, O 'Umar, for Allah has today exposed the hypocrites." Ibn 'Abbas said: "This is the first punishment, when he expelled them from the mosque, and the second punishment is the punishment of the grave." [[Related by al-Tabari in his tafsir (14/441).]]

Likewise al-Thawri said, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, something similar to this.

Mujahid said concerning His saying: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾: it means killing and captivity; and he said, in another narration: hunger and the punishment of the grave. ﴿Then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾.

Ibn Juraij said: the punishment of this world and the punishment of the grave; then they will be returned to the punishment of the Fire.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: a punishment in this world and a punishment in the grave.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: As for the punishment in this world, it is wealth and children, and he recited the saying of Allah: ﴿So let not their wealth and their children impress you; Allah only intends to punish them through them in this world﴾ [al-Tawbah: 85]. So these calamities are a punishment for them, while for the believers they are a reward; and there is a punishment in the Hereafter, in the Fire: ﴿Then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾. He said: that is the Fire.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾: he said, as it has reached me, it is what they are in of the affair of Islam, and what enters upon them of rage at that without reckoning; then their punishment in the graves when they go to them; then the great punishment to which they will be returned, the punishment of the Hereafter and abiding in it.

Sa'id related from Qatadah concerning His saying: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾: the punishment of this world and the punishment of the grave; ﴿Then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾.

It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ confided to Hudhayfah the names of twelve men among the hypocrites, and said: "Six of them, the Dubaylah will suffice them: a flame from the Fire of Hell that takes hold of the shoulder of one of them until it reaches his chest; and six who will die a natural death." It has also been mentioned to us that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, whenever a man died who was thought to be among them, would look at Hudhayfah; if he prayed over him, 'Umar would too, otherwise he would leave him. It has also been mentioned to us that 'Umar said to Hudhayfah: "I adjure you by Allah, am I among them?" He said: "No, and I will not vouch for anyone after you." [[Related by al-Tabari in his tafsir (14/443). The Dubaylah: a large boil or abscess that appears in the interior, which usually kills its owner.]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 9, verse 102:

When Allah (Exalted is He) explained the condition of the hypocrites who stayed behind from the military expeditions out of aversion to them, denial and doubt, He began to explain the condition of the sinners who lagged behind from jihad out of laziness and inclination toward ease, despite their faith and their affirmation of the truth. So He said: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins﴾, meaning: they confessed to them and admitted them between themselves and their Lord, and they had other righteous deeds, mixing these with those. These, then, are under the pardon and forgiveness of Allah.

Although this verse was revealed concerning specific people, it is general in its application to all sinners, the sincere ones who are stained (by their sins).

Mujahid said: It was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah when he said to the Banu Qurayzah: "It is the slaughter," and he pointed with his hand to his throat.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿And others﴾ was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah and a group of his companions who stayed behind from the expedition of Tabuk. Some of them said: Abu Lubabah and five with him; it was said: and seven with him; and it was said: and nine with him. When the Prophet ﷺ returned from his expedition, they tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque and swore that none would release them except the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins﴾, the Prophet ﷺ released them and pardoned them.

Al-Bukhari said: Mu'ammal ibn Hisham narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, 'Awf narrated to us, Abu Raja' narrated to us, Samurah ibn Jundub narrated to us, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: "Two visitors came to me tonight and took me up, and we reached a city built of gold bricks and silver bricks. Men met us, half of whose creation was like the best you have ever seen, and half like the ugliest you have ever seen. The two said to them: Go and plunge into that river. So they plunged into it, then returned to us, the ugliness having left them, and they had become in the best form. The two said to me: This is the Garden of Eden, and this is your abode. As for the people who were half good and half ugly, they had mixed a righteous deed with another evil one, and Allah pardoned them."

He narrated it in abridged form here, concerning the interpretation of this verse. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4674]

Allah the Exalted commanded His Messenger ﷺ to take from their wealth a charity (ṣadaqah) by which He purifies them and causes them to grow. This is general, even though some of them referred the pronoun in "their wealth" to those who acknowledged their sins and mixed a righteous deed with another, evil one. For this reason, some of the zakat (obligatory almsgiving) withholders among the Arab tribes believed that paying zakat to the imam (leader) was not required, and that this was specific to the Messenger of Allah [[In K: "to the Prophet".]] ﷺ. They used as evidence His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow, and pray for them, for your prayer is a comfort for them﴾. But this interpretation and corrupt understanding was refuted by al-Ṣiddīq Abū Bakr and the rest of the Companions. They fought them until they paid zakat to the caliph (khalīfah), just as they used to pay it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Al-Ṣiddīq said: "By Allah, if they withheld from me a cord (ʿiqāl) which they used to pay to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would fight them for withholding it." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, nos. (7284, 7285), with the wording: "If they withheld from me a cord ('iqāl)." He said: "Ibn Bukayr and Abdullah narrated from al-Layth: 'a female goat ('anāq), and this is more sound'."]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And pray for them﴾, meaning: supplicate for them and ask forgiveness for them, as Muslim narrated in his Sahih from ʿAbd Allah ibn Abī Awfā, who said: "When the charity of a people was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he would pray for them. My father brought his charity to him, and he said: 'O Allah, send Your blessings upon the family of Abī Awfā.'" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1078), and al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (1497).]] In another hadith, a woman said: "O Messenger of Allah, pray for me and for my husband." He said: "May Allah bless you and your husband." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. (1533), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (10256), from the hadith of Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Inna ṣalātak﴾ [Indeed your prayer]: some read "ṣalawātika" in the plural, and others read ﴿inna ṣalātaka﴾ in the singular.

﴿Sakan lahum﴾ [a comfort for them]: Ibn ʿAbbās said: "A mercy for them." Qatadah said: "A tranquility (waqār)."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah is Hearing﴾, meaning: of your supplication, ﴿Knowing﴾, meaning: of who deserves that from you and who is worthy of it.

Imam Aḥmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Abū al-ʿUmays narrated to us, from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUtbah, from a son of Ḥudhayfah, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ, whenever he prayed for a man, it would reach him, his child, and his grandchild. [[Al-Musnad (5/385).]]

Then he narrated it from Abū Nuʿaym, from Misʿar, from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUtbah, from a son of Ḥudhayfah. Misʿar said: "He mentioned it once from Ḥudhayfah." [The narration says]: "Indeed the prayer of the Prophet ﷺ reaches the man, his child, and his grandchild." [[Al-Musnad (5/400).]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Did they not know that Allah is He who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities?﴾ This is an incitement to repentance and to charity, each of which erases sins, purifies them, and eliminates them.

He, the Exalted, informed that whoever repents to Him, He accepts his repentance, and whoever gives a charity from lawful earnings, Allah, the Exalted, accepts it with His right hand and makes it grow for its giver, until a date becomes like Uhud. This is as the hadith reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as al-Thawri and Waki' both said, both from ʿAbbad ibn Manṣūr, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, that he heard Abū Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah accepts charity and takes it with His right hand, and makes it grow for one of you, just as one of you raises his foal, until a morsel becomes like Uhud." The confirmation of this is in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿[Did they not know that Allah] is He who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities﴾ [[Addition from K.]] and [His saying] [[Addition from K.]] ﴿Allah deprives usury of blessing and makes charities grow﴾ [al-Baqarah: 276]. [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/461). Note: an error occurred in the verse here and in al-Tabari's, and what we have recorded is the correct form.]]

Al-Thawri and al-Aʿmash both said, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Sāʾib, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Abī Qatādah, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Indeed charity falls into the hand of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, before it falls into the hand of the beggar." Then he recited this verse: ﴿Did they not know that Allah is He who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities﴾ [[In T: "taʿlamū" (did they not know).]].

Ibn ʿAsākir narrated in his Tarikh, in the biography of ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Shāʿir al-Sakasaki al-Dimashqi, whose origin was from Homs, and who was one of the jurists, who narrated from Muʿawiyah and others, and from whom Hawshab ibn Sayf al-Sakasaki al-Ḥimṣi related: He said: "The people fought in the time of Muʿawiyah, may Allah be pleased with him, and over them was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khālid ibn al-Walīd. A man among the Muslims embezzled one hundred Roman dinars. When the army returned, he regretted it and came to the commander, but he refused to accept it from him, and said: 'The people have dispersed, and I will not accept it from you until you bring it to Allah on the Day of Resurrection.' The man began to ask the Companions, and they would say to him the same thing. When he arrived in Damascus, he went to Muʿawiyah to have it accepted from him, but he refused. He left his presence weeping and saying 'Inna lillah,' and he passed by ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Shāʿir al-Sakasaki, who said to him: 'What makes you weep?' So he told him his matter. He said: 'Will you obey me?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Go to Muʿawiyah and say to him: Accept from me one-fifth (khums) of it, so give him twenty dinars, and examine the remaining eighty and give them in charity on behalf of that army, for Allah accepts repentance from His servants, and He knows their names and their places.' The man did so, and Muʿawiyah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'That I had issued a fatwa with it would be more beloved to me than everything I possess. May the man be rewarded well.'" [[Tarikh Dimashq (9/401), manuscript edition.]]

This is general, even though some of them referred the pronoun in "their wealth" to those who acknowledged their sins and mixed a righteous deed with another, evil one. For this reason, some of the zakat (obligatory almsgiving) withholders among the Arab tribes believed that paying zakat to the imam (leader) was not required, and that this was specific to the Messenger of Allah [[In K: "to the Prophet".]] ﷺ. They used as evidence His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow, and pray for them, for your prayer is a comfort for them﴾. But this interpretation and corrupt understanding was refuted by al-Ṣiddīq Abū Bakr and the rest of the Companions. They fought them until they paid zakat to the caliph (khalīfah), just as they used to pay it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Al-Ṣiddīq said: "By Allah, if they withheld from me a cord (ʿiqāl) which they used to pay to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would fight them for withholding it." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, nos. (7284, 7285), with the wording: "If they withheld from me a cord ('iqāl)." He said: "Ibn Bukayr and Abdullah narrated from al-Layth: 'a female goat ('anāq), and this is more sound'."]]

Imam Aḥmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Abū al-ʿUmays narrated to us, from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUtbah, from a son of Ḥudhayfah, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ, whenever he prayed for a man, it would reach him, his child, and his grandchild. [[Al-Musnad (5/385).]]
