[[Tarikh Dimashq (9/401), manuscript edition.]]

Mujahid said: This is a warning from Allah, exalted is He, to those who oppose His commands, that their deeds will be presented to Him, blessed and exalted is He, and to the Messenger, and to the believers. This is certain to happen on the Day of Resurrection, as He said: ﴿On that Day you will be exposed; not a secret of yours will be concealed﴾ [al-Haqqah: 18], [[In manuscript T: "you will be exposed, not a secret will be concealed"]] and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿On the Day when the secrets will be examined﴾ [al-Tariq: 9], and He said: ﴿And what is within the breasts will be made known﴾ [al-'Adiyat: 10]. It may also become apparent to people in this world, as Imam Ahmad said:

Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "If one of you works inside a hard, solid rock that has no door and no window, Allah will bring out his deed for the people, whatever it may be." [[Al-Musnad (3/28); Darraj from Abu al-Haytham is weak.]]

It has also been reported that the deeds of the living are presented to the dead among their relatives and kinsfolk in the barzakh (the intermediate realm), as Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: al-Salt ibn Dinar narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Your deeds are presented to your relatives and kinsfolk in their graves. If it is good, they rejoice in it; and if it is other than that, they say: 'O Allah, inspire them to act in obedience to You.'" [[Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. 1794.]]

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Sufyan, from one who heard Anas say: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Your deeds are presented to your relatives and kinsfolk among the dead. If it is good, they rejoice in it; and if it is other than that, they say: 'O Allah, do not let them die until You guide them as You guided us.'" [[Al-Musnad (3/164); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (2/228): "In it is a man who was not named."]]

Al-Bukhari said: 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "If the good deed of a person pleases you, then say: ﴿Act, for Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger and the believers﴾" [[Sahih al-Bukhari (13/503, Fath).]]

A similar hadith has also been reported. Imam Ahmad said:

Yazid narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no harm for you in being impressed by anyone until you see how his life will end. For the worker may labor for a period of his life, or a span of his time, at a righteous deed, which, had he died upon it, would have admitted him to Paradise; then he changes and does an evil deed. And a servant may labor for a period of his time at an evil deed, which, had he died upon it, would have admitted him to the Fire; then he changes and does a righteous deed. When Allah wills good for a servant, He makes him work before his death." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how does He make him work?" He said: "He enables him to do a righteous deed and then takes his soul upon it." [[Al-Musnad (3/120); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/211): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]] Ahmad alone narrated it through this chain.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and others said: They are the three who were left behind, meaning, left behind from repentance. They are Murarah ibn al-Rabi', Ka'b ibn Malik and Hilal ibn Umayyah. They stayed behind from the expedition to Tabuk along with those who stayed behind, out of laziness and a desire for comfort, shelter, good fruit and shade, not out of doubt or hypocrisy. Some of them tied themselves to the pillars, as Abu Lubabah and his companions did, while others did not do so, and these were the three mentioned. The repentance of those others was revealed before theirs, and the repentance of these three was deferred until the following verse was revealed, which is His saying: ﴿Allah has certainly turned in forgiveness to the Prophet and the Muhajirun and the Ansar﴾ [al-Tawbah: 117], and ﴿And [He turned in forgiveness] to the three who were left behind, until when the earth was constricted for them despite its vastness and their souls were constricted for them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 118], as will be explained in the hadith of Ka'b ibn Malik.

* *

His saying: ﴿Either He will punish them or He will turn to them in forgiveness﴾ means: they are under the will of Allah. If He wills, He will do this to them, and if He wills, He will do that to them. But His mercy overcomes His anger. And He is ﴿All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾, meaning: All-Knowing of who deserves punishment and who deserves pardon, All-Wise in His actions and His words. There is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him.

The Reason for the Revelation of These Noble Verses: There was in Medina, before the arrival of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ there, a man of the Khazraj called Abu 'Amir al-Rahib (the Monk), who had become a Christian in the Jahiliyyah and had studied the knowledge of the People of the Book. He had worship in the Jahiliyyah, and he had great nobility among the Khazraj. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ migrated to Medina, the Muslims gathered around him, the word of Islam became supreme, and Allah granted them victory on the day of Badr, this accursed Abu 'Amir choked on his saliva, openly declared enmity, and openly showed it. He fled to the disbelievers of Mecca from the polytheists of Quraysh and incited them against the war with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They gathered with those among the Arab tribes who agreed with them and came in the year of Uhud. What happened to the Muslims happened, Allah tested them, and the final outcome was for the God-fearing.

This wicked man had dug pits between the two lines, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell into one of them. He was injured that day: he was wounded in his face, his lower right incisor was broken, and his head was cut open, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

Abu 'Amir advanced at the beginning of the combat toward his people from the Ansar, addressed them, and tried to win them over to support him and agree with him. When they recognized his speech, they said: "May Allah not grant you comfort, O wicked one, O enemy of Allah!" and they attacked him and cursed him. He returned saying: "By Allah, my people have been struck by evil after me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had called him to Allah before his flight, recited the Qur'an to him, but he refused to embrace Islam and rebelled, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against him that he would die far away and expelled, and this supplication befell him.

When the people had finished with Uhud and he saw the Messenger's affair rising and becoming prominent, he went to Heraclius, the king of the Romans, seeking his help against the Prophet ﷺ. Heraclius promised him and gave him hope, and he stayed with him. He wrote to a group of his people among the Ansar, those of hypocrisy and doubt, promising and encouraging them that he would come with an army to fight the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, defeat him, and turn him back from what he was upon. He ordered them to build for him a stronghold where those who came from him with his letters could arrive and which would serve as a station for him when he came to them afterward. They began to build a mosque adjoining the Mosque of Quba, and they built it, made it firm, and finished it before the Prophet ﷺ set out for Tabuk. They came and asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to come to them and pray in their mosque, so that they could use his prayer there as evidence for its approval and establishment. They mentioned that they had built it only for the weak among them and those with excuses on cold, rainy nights. Allah protected him from praying in it, and he said: "We are on a journey, but when we return, if Allah wills, we will [visit you]."

When he, peace be upon him, returned from Tabuk to Medina, and only a day or part of a day remained between him and it, the revelation came down concerning the Mosque of Harm, and the disbelief its builders had intended and the division they had caused among the congregation of the believers in their mosque, the Mosque of Quba, which was founded from the first day upon piety. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent to that mosque men who demolished it, before his arrival at Medina, as 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm [and disbelief and division among the believers]﴾, and they were people of the Ansar who built a mosque. Abu 'Amir had said to them: "Build a mosque and prepare whatever strength and weapons you can, for I am going to Caesar, the king of the Romans, to bring an army of Romans and expel Muhammad and his companions." When they finished their mosque, they came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "We have finished building our mosque, and we would love for you to pray in it and invoke blessing for us." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Do not stand in it ever. A mosque founded upon piety from the first day is more worthy of you to stand in it﴾ up to ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾.

The same was related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Qatadah, and other than one of the scholars.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said, from al-Zuhri, Yazid ibn Ruman, 'Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah and others, they said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came back (meaning from Tabuk) until he alighted at Dhu Awan, a place an hour's journey from Medina during the day. The people of the Mosque of Harm had come to him while he was preparing for Tabuk and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have built a mosque for the sick and those in need, on rainy nights and cold nights, and we would love for you to come to us and pray for us in it." He said: "I am on the verge of a journey and occupied with affairs, or as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said; but if we return, if Allah the Exalted wills, we will come to you and pray for you in it." When he alighted at Dhu Awan, news of the mosque reached him, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called Malik ibn al-Dukhshum, brother of Banu Salim ibn 'Awf, and Ma'n ibn 'Adi, or his brother 'Amir ibn 'Adi, brother of Balajlan, and said: "Go to this mosque whose people are wrongdoers, demolish it and burn it." So they went out quickly until they came to Banu Salim ibn 'Awf, who were the kin of Malik ibn al-Dukhshum. Malik said to Ma'n: "Wait for me until I bring you fire from my family." He entered his household, took a palm frond, lit fire in it, then they both went out running until they entered the mosque with its people in it, burned and demolished it, and they dispersed from it. Concerning them there was revealed in the Qur'an what was revealed: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief﴾ to the end of the story. The builders of it were twelve men: Khudhām ibn Khalid, from Banu 'Ubayd ibn Zayd, one of the grandfathers of Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, and from his house the Mosque of Discord was taken out; Tha'labah ibn Hatib from Banu 'Ubayd, and he belongs to Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd; Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, from [Banu] Dubay'ah ibn Zayd; Abu Habibah ibn al-Al'dhar, from Banu Dubay'ah ibn Zayd; 'Abbad ibn Hunayf, brother of Sahl ibn Hunayf, from Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf; Jariyah ibn 'Amir and his two sons: Mujammi' ibn Jariyah and Zayd ibn Jariyah; Nabtal [ibn] al-Harith, and they are from Banu Dubay'ah; Bahzaj, who is from Banu Dubay'ah; Bijad ibn 'Uthman, who is from Banu Dubay'ah; [and Wadi'ah ibn Thabit, who belongs to Banu Umayyah], the kin of Abu Lubabah ibn 'Abd al-Mundhir. [Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (2/530), and al-Tabari related it in his tafsir (14/468). See the discussion of this narration and its refutation in the book of al-Fadil 'Adhab al-Hamash, "Tha'labah ibn Hatib, the Falsely Accused" (p. 138).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they will surely swear﴾, that is, those who built it: ﴿"We intended nothing but good"﴾, that is, we intended by its construction nothing but goodness and kindness to the people. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah testifies that they are liars﴾, that is, in what they intended and in what they purposed. They built it only to harm the Mosque of Quba, out of disbelief in Allah, to divide the believers, and as a waiting station for whoever wars against Allah and His Messenger, and that was Abu 'Amir the wicked, who was called "the Monk", may Allah curse him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Do not stand in it ever﴾, it is a prohibition from Allah to His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and the Ummah follows him in that, against standing in it, that is, praying in it, ever.

Then He urged him to pray in the Mosque of Quba, which was founded from the first day of its building upon piety, which is obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger, and a unification of the word of the believers, and a stronghold and refuge for Islam and its people. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿A mosque founded upon piety from the first day is more worthy of you to stand in it﴾, and the context is only concerning the Mosque of Quba. Therefore there came in the authentic hadith that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Prayer in the Mosque of Quba is like an 'umrah." [Related by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (324), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. (1411), by way of Abu Usamah 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Abu al-Abrad, mawla of Banu al-Khatmah, from Usayd ibn Zuhayr al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him, and with the same. al-Tirmidhi said, as in Tuhfat al-Ashraf (1/275): "A hasan sahih hadith; we know of nothing authentic from Usayd ibn Zuhayr other than this hadith, and we know it only from the hadith of Abu Usamah."] And in the Sahih: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to visit the Mosque of Quba, riding and walking. [Sahih Muslim, no. (1399), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.] And in the hadith: that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ built and founded it at the first of his arrival and his dwelling with Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, it was Jibril who designated for him the direction of the qiblah. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (44); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3100); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (357).] And Allah knows best.

Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Yunus ibn al-Harith, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Maymunah, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "This verse was revealed concerning the people of Quba: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾." He said: "They used to cleanse themselves with water, so the verse was revealed concerning them."

al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah related it, from the hadith of Yunus ibn al-Harith, and he is weak. al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib from this route."

al-Tabarani said: al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Ma'mari narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Humayd al-Razi narrated to us, Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent to 'Uwaym ibn Sa'idah and said: "What is this purification with which Allah has praised you?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, no man or woman has come out from the toilet without washing his private part, or he said: his rear," and the Prophet ﷺ said: "That is it." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/67), in which Muhammad ibn Humayd is weak, and Ibn Ishaq is a mudallis who related with 'an'anah.]

Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abu Uways narrated to us, Shurahbil narrated to us, from 'Uwaym ibn Sa'idah al-Ansari: that the Prophet ﷺ came to them at the Mosque of Quba and said: "Indeed Allah the Exalted has praised you concerning purification in the story of your mosque. What is this purification with which you purify yourselves?" They said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we know nothing except that we had Jewish neighbors who used to wash their rears after defecation, so we washed as they washed."

Ibn Khuzaymah related it in his Sahih. [Al-Musnad (3/422) and Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah, no. (83). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/212): "In it is Shurahbil ibn Sa'd, whom Malik, Ibn Ma'in and Abu Zur'ah weakened, and Ibn Hibban declared trustworthy."]

Hushaym said, from 'Abd al-Hamid al-Madani, from Ibrahim ibn Isma'il al-Ansari: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to 'Uwaym ibn Sa'idah: "What is this with which Allah has praised you: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves﴾?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we wash the rear with water." [Related by al-Tabari in his tafsir (14/487).]

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Umara al-Asadi narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Shurahbil ibn Sa'd, who said: I heard Khuzayma ibn Thabit say: This verse was revealed: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves﴾. He said: They used to wash their rear ends (adbar) after relieving themselves (al-ghaʾit, the low ground used for defecation). [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/487).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Malik narrated to us, meaning Ibn Mighwal, I heard Sayyar Abu al-Hakam, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived, meaning at Quba, he said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has praised you concerning purification (tuhur) with good words. Will you not tell me?" He meant His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves﴾. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we find it written against us in the Torah: istinja' with water." [[Al-Musnad (6/6).]] [In manuscript A: "laqad" instead of "lamma".]

Several of the early scholars (al-salaf) explicitly stated that it is the Mosque of Quba. 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr. It was also said by 'Atiyya al-'Awfi, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Sha'bi, and al-Hasan al-Basri. Al-Baghawi transmitted it from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Qatada.

It has been reported in an authentic hadith that the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which is in the center of Madina, is the mosque founded upon piety. This is authentic, and there is no contradiction between the verse and this, because if the Mosque of Quba was founded upon piety from the first day, then the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is more deserving of this by priority and greater right. For this reason Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said in his Musnad:

Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir al-Aslami narrated to us, from 'Imran ibn Abi Anas, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b: that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The mosque founded upon piety is this mosque of mine." Ahmad alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (5/116).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Rabi'a ibn 'Uthman al-Taymi narrated to us, from 'Imran ibn Abi Anas, from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, who said: Two men differed during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the mosque founded upon piety. One of them said: It is the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The other said: It is the Mosque of Quba.

They came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him, and he said: "It is this mosque of mine." [[Al-Musnad (5/331). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7/34): "Its narrators are the narrators of the authentic (sahih)."]] Ahmad alone narrated it too.

Another hadith: Ahmad said: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from 'Imran ibn Abi Anas, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Two men disputed about the mosque founded upon piety. One of them said: It is the Mosque of Quba. The other said: It is the Mosque of the Prophet ﷺ. The Prophet ﷺ said: "It is this mosque of mine." [[Al-Musnad (3/89).]] Ahmad alone narrated it.

Another route: Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn 'Isa narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, 'Imran ibn Abi Anas narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Sa'id, from his father, that he said: Two men disputed about the mosque founded upon piety from the first day. One man said: It is the Mosque of Quba. The other said: It is the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It is my mosque."

Similarly, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it from Qutayba, from al-Layth. [[Al-Musnad (3/7); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3099); al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11228).]] al-Tirmidhi declared it authentic, and Muslim narrated it as will come.

Another route: Ahmad said: Yahya narrated to us, from Unays ibn Abi Yahya, who narrated to me, my father, who said: I heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: Two men differed: a man from the Banu Khudra and a man from the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, about the mosque founded upon piety. The Khudri said: It is the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The 'Amri said: It is the Mosque of Quba. They came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him about that. He said: "It is this mosque," meaning the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "In that there is much good [khayr kathir]," meaning the Mosque of Quba. [[Bracketed words are from manuscripts T, K, A and al-Musnad. In A: "khayr kabir". Al-Musnad (3/23).]]

Another route: Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Humayd al-Kharrat al-Madani narrated to us: I asked Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'id, and I said: How did you hear your father speak about the mosque founded upon piety? He said: My father said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I entered upon him in a room belonging to one of his wives. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, where is the mosque founded upon piety?" He took a handful of pebbles and struck the ground with them, then said: "It is your mosque this one." Then he said: [I said to him: "Like this?"] Did you hear your father mention it? [[Bracketed words are from manuscripts T, K, A and al-Tabari. In A: "which mosque" (ayy masjid). Tafsir al-Tabari (14/477); Sahih Muslim, no. (1398).]]

Muslim narrated it alone, from Muhammad ibn Hatim, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, with this chain. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1398).]] It was also narrated from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba and others, from Hatim ibn Isma'il, from Humayd al-Kharrat, with this chain. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1398).]]

Many of the early (salaf) and later (khalaf) scholars held that it is the Mosque of the Prophet ﷺ. This is narrated from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, his son 'Abd Allah, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib. Ibn Jarir also chose this view.

* *

His saying: ﴿Surely a mosque founded upon piety from the first day is more worthy that you stand in it. In it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves﴾ is evidence for the recommendation (istihbab) of praying in ancient mosques founded from the first day of their construction upon the worship of Allah alone, with no partner; and for the recommendation of praying with the company of the righteous and the diligent worshippers who are careful to perform the wudu' (ablution) thoroughly and who keep themselves clear of filth.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, I heard Shabib Abu Rawh narrate from a man of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led them in the dawn prayer and recited in it [al-Rum] (Surah of the Romans), and he made a mistake. When he finished he said: "Indeed the Qur'an was confused for us. Indeed some people among you pray with us but do not perform the wudu' well. Whoever attends the prayer with us, let him perform the wudu' well." [[In manuscripts T and A: "fiha" instead of "bihim". Al-Musnad (3/471, 472).]]

Then he narrated it through two other routes, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Shabib Abu Rawh of Dhu al-Kala', that he prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, and he mentioned it. [[Al-Musnad (3/471, 472).]] This shows that completing the purification makes standing in worship easier, and helps in completing it and perfecting it and carrying out its prescribed acts.

Abu al-'Aliya said regarding His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah loves those who purify themselves﴾: Purification with water is indeed good, but they are the ones who purify themselves from sins.

Al-A'mash said: [it is] repentance from sin, and purification from shirk.

It has been reported in the hadith transmitted through several routes, in the Sunan and elsewhere, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the people of Quba: "Allah has praised you concerning purification. What do you do?" They said: We perform istinja' with water.

The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: 'Abd Allah ibn Shabib narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: I found it in my father's book, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed concerning the people of Quba: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves﴾. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked them, and they said: "We follow the stones with water."

Then he said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz alone narrated it from al-Zuhri, and no one narrated from him except his son. [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (247). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (1/212): "In its chain is Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Umar al-Zuhri, whom al-Bukhari and al-Nasa'i declared weak, and he is the one who pointed to [the narration of] the mantle of Malik."]]

I say: I only mentioned it in this wording because it is well known among the jurists (fuqaha'), while many of the later scholars of hadith did not recognize it, or all of them did not, and Allah knows best.

The Reason for the Revelation of These Noble Verses: There was in Medina, before the arrival of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ there, a man of the Khazraj called Abu 'Amir al-Rahib (the Monk), who had become a Christian in the Jahiliyyah and had studied the knowledge of the People of the Book. He had worship in the Jahiliyyah, and he had great nobility among the Khazraj. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ migrated to Medina, the Muslims gathered around him, the word of Islam became supreme, and Allah granted them victory on the day of Badr, this accursed Abu 'Amir choked on his saliva, openly declared enmity, and openly showed it. He fled to the disbelievers of Mecca from the polytheists of Quraysh and incited them against the war with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They gathered with those among the Arab tribes who agreed with them and came in the year of Uhud. What happened to the Muslims happened, Allah tested them, and the final outcome was for the God-fearing.

This wicked man had dug pits between the two lines, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell into one of them. He was injured that day: he was wounded in his face, his lower right incisor was broken, and his head was cut open, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

Abu 'Amir advanced at the beginning of the combat toward his people from the Ansar, addressed them, and tried to win them over to support him and agree with him. When they recognized his speech, they said: "May Allah not grant you comfort, O wicked one, O enemy of Allah!" and they attacked him and cursed him. He returned saying: "By Allah, my people have been struck by evil after me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had called him to Allah before his flight, recited the Qur'an to him, but he refused to embrace Islam and rebelled, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against him that he would die far away and expelled, and this supplication befell him.

When the people had finished with Uhud and he saw the Messenger's affair rising and becoming prominent, he went to Heraclius, the king of the Romans, seeking his help against the Prophet ﷺ. Heraclius promised him and gave him hope, and he stayed with him. He wrote to a group of his people among the Ansar, those of hypocrisy and doubt, promising and encouraging them that he would come with an army to fight the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, defeat him, and turn him back from what he was upon. He ordered them to build for him a stronghold where those who came from him with his letters could arrive and which would serve as a station for him when he came to them afterward. They began to build a mosque adjoining the Mosque of Quba, and they built it, made it firm, and finished it before the Prophet ﷺ set out for Tabuk. They came and asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to come to them and pray in their mosque, so that they could use his prayer there as evidence for its approval and establishment. They mentioned that they had built it only for the weak among them and those with excuses on cold, rainy nights. Allah protected him from praying in it, and he said: "We are on a journey, but when we return, if Allah wills, we will [visit you]."

When he, peace be upon him, returned from Tabuk to Medina, and only a day or part of a day remained between him and it, the revelation came down concerning the Mosque of Harm, and the disbelief its builders had intended and the division they had caused among the congregation of the believers in their mosque, the Mosque of Quba, which was founded from the first day upon piety. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent to that mosque men who demolished it, before his arrival at Medina, as 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm [and disbelief and division among the believers]﴾, and they were people of the Ansar who built a mosque. Abu 'Amir had said to them: "Build a mosque and prepare whatever strength and weapons you can, for I am going to Caesar, the king of the Romans, to bring an army of Romans and expel Muhammad and his companions." When they finished their mosque, they came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "We have finished building our mosque, and we would love for you to pray in it and invoke blessing for us." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Do not stand in it ever. A mosque founded upon piety from the first day is more worthy of you to stand in it﴾ up to ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾.

The same was related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Qatadah, and other than one of the scholars.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said, from al-Zuhri, Yazid ibn Ruman, 'Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah and others, they said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came back (meaning from Tabuk) until he alighted at Dhu Awan, a place an hour's journey from Medina during the day. The people of the Mosque of Harm had come to him while he was preparing for Tabuk and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have built a mosque for the sick and those in need, on rainy nights and cold nights, and we would love for you to come to us and pray for us in it." He said: "I am on the verge of a journey and occupied with affairs, or as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said; but if we return, if Allah the Exalted wills, we will come to you and pray for you in it." When he alighted at Dhu Awan, news of the mosque reached him, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called Malik ibn al-Dukhshum, brother of Banu Salim ibn 'Awf, and Ma'n ibn 'Adi, or his brother 'Amir ibn 'Adi, brother of Balajlan, and said: "Go to this mosque whose people are wrongdoers, demolish it and burn it." So they went out quickly until they came to Banu Salim ibn 'Awf, who were the kin of Malik ibn al-Dukhshum. Malik said to Ma'n: "Wait for me until I bring you fire from my family." He entered his household, took a palm frond, lit fire in it, then they both went out running until they entered the mosque with its people in it, burned and demolished it, and they dispersed from it. Concerning them there was revealed in the Qur'an what was revealed: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief﴾ to the end of the story. The builders of it were twelve men: Khudhām ibn Khalid, from Banu 'Ubayd ibn Zayd, one of the grandfathers of Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, and from his house the Mosque of Discord was taken out; Tha'labah ibn Hatib from Banu 'Ubayd, and he belongs to Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd; Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, from [Banu] Dubay'ah ibn Zayd; Abu Habibah ibn al-Al'dhar, from Banu Dubay'ah ibn Zayd; 'Abbad ibn Hunayf, brother of Sahl ibn Hunayf, from Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf; Jariyah ibn 'Amir and his two sons: Mujammi' ibn Jariyah and Zayd ibn Jariyah; Nabtal [ibn] al-Harith, and they are from Banu Dubay'ah; Bahzaj, who is from Banu Dubay'ah; Bijad ibn 'Uthman, who is from Banu Dubay'ah; [and Wadi'ah ibn Thabit, who belongs to Banu Umayyah], the kin of Abu Lubabah ibn 'Abd al-Mundhir. [Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (2/530), and al-Tabari related it in his tafsir (14/468). See the discussion of this narration and its refutation in the book of al-Fadil 'Adhab al-Hamash, "Tha'labah ibn Hatib, the Falsely Accused" (p. 138).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they will surely swear﴾, that is, those who built it: ﴿"We intended nothing but good"﴾, that is, we intended by its construction nothing but goodness and kindness to the people. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah testifies that they are liars﴾, that is, in what they intended and in what they purposed. They built it only to harm the Mosque of Quba, out of disbelief in Allah, to divide the believers, and as a waiting station for whoever wars against Allah and His Messenger, and that was Abu 'Amir the wicked, who was called "the Monk", may Allah curse him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Do not stand in it ever﴾, it is a prohibition from Allah to His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and the Ummah follows him in that, against standing in it, that is, praying in it, ever.

Then He urged him to pray in the Mosque of Quba, which was founded from the first day of its building upon piety, which is obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger, and a unification of the word of the believers, and a stronghold and refuge for Islam and its people. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿A mosque founded upon piety from the first day is more worthy of you to stand in it﴾, and the context is only concerning the Mosque of Quba. Therefore there came in the authentic hadith that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Prayer in the Mosque of Quba is like an 'umrah." [Related by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (324), and Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. (1411), by way of Abu Usamah 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Abu al-Abrad, mawla of Banu al-Khatmah, from Usayd ibn Zuhayr al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him, and with the same. al-Tirmidhi said, as in Tuhfat al-Ashraf (1/275): "A hasan sahih hadith; we know of nothing authentic from Usayd ibn Zuhayr other than this hadith, and we know it only from the hadith of Abu Usamah."] And in the Sahih: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to visit the Mosque of Quba, riding and walking. [Sahih Muslim, no. (1399), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.] And in the hadith: that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ built and founded it at the first of his arrival and his dwelling with Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, it was Jibril who designated for him the direction of the qiblah. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (44); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3100); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (357).] And Allah knows best.

Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Yunus ibn al-Harith, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Maymunah, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "This verse was revealed concerning the people of Quba: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾." He said: "They used to cleanse themselves with water, so the verse was revealed concerning them."

al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah related it, from the hadith of Yunus ibn al-Harith, and he is weak. al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib from this route."

al-Tabarani said: al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Ma'mari narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Humayd al-Razi narrated to us, Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent to 'Uwaym ibn Sa'idah and said: "What is this purification with which Allah has praised you?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, no man or woman has come out from the toilet without washing his private part, or he said: his rear," and the Prophet ﷺ said: "That is it." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/67), in which Muhammad ibn Humayd is weak, and Ibn Ishaq is a mudallis who related with 'an'anah.]

Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abu Uways narrated to us, Shurahbil narrated to us, from 'Uwaym ibn Sa'idah al-Ansari: that the Prophet ﷺ came to them at the Mosque of Quba and said: "Indeed Allah the Exalted has praised you concerning purification in the story of your mosque. What is this purification with which you purify yourselves?" They said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we know nothing except that we had Jewish neighbors who used to wash their rears after defecation, so we washed as they washed."

Ibn Khuzaymah related it in his Sahih. [Al-Musnad (3/422) and Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah, no. (83). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/212): "In it is Shurahbil ibn Sa'd, whom Malik, Ibn Ma'in and Abu Zur'ah weakened, and Ibn Hibban declared trustworthy."]

Hushaym said, from 'Abd al-Hamid al-Madani, from Ibrahim ibn Isma'il al-Ansari: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to 'Uwaym ibn Sa'idah: "What is this with which Allah has praised you: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves﴾?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we wash the rear with water." [Related by al-Tabari in his tafsir (14/487).]

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Umara al-Asadi narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Shurahbil ibn Sa'd, who said: I heard Khuzayma ibn Thabit say: This verse was revealed: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves﴾. He said: They used to wash their rear ends (adbar) after relieving themselves (al-ghaʾit, the low ground used for defecation). [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (14/487).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Malik narrated to us, meaning Ibn Mighwal, I heard Sayyar Abu al-Hakam, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived, meaning at Quba, he said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has praised you concerning purification (tuhur) with good words. Will you not tell me?" He meant His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves﴾. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we find it written against us in the Torah: istinja' with water." [[Al-Musnad (6/6).]] [In manuscript A: "laqad" instead of "lamma".]

Several of the early scholars (al-salaf) explicitly stated that it is the Mosque of Quba. 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr. It was also said by 'Atiyya al-'Awfi, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Sha'bi, and al-Hasan al-Basri. Al-Baghawi transmitted it from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Qatada.

It has been reported in an authentic hadith that the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which is in the center of Madina, is the mosque founded upon piety. This is authentic, and there is no contradiction between the verse and this, because if the Mosque of Quba was founded upon piety from the first day, then the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is more deserving of this by priority and greater right. For this reason Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said in his Musnad:

Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir al-Aslami narrated to us, from 'Imran ibn Abi Anas, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b: that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The mosque founded upon piety is this mosque of mine." Ahmad alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (5/116).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Rabi'a ibn 'Uthman al-Taymi narrated to us, from 'Imran ibn Abi Anas, from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, who said: Two men differed during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the mosque founded upon piety. One of them said: It is the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The other said: It is the Mosque of Quba.

They came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him, and he said: "It is this mosque of mine." [[Al-Musnad (5/331). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7/34): "Its narrators are the narrators of the authentic (sahih)."]] Ahmad alone narrated it too.

Another hadith: Ahmad said: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from 'Imran ibn Abi Anas, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Two men disputed about the mosque founded upon piety. One of them said: It is the Mosque of Quba. The other said: It is the Mosque of the Prophet ﷺ. The Prophet ﷺ said: "It is this mosque of mine." [[Al-Musnad (3/89).]] Ahmad alone narrated it.

Another route: Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn 'Isa narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, 'Imran ibn Abi Anas narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Sa'id, from his father, that he said: Two men disputed about the mosque founded upon piety from the first day. One man said: It is the Mosque of Quba. The other said: It is the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It is my mosque."

Similarly, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it from Qutayba, from al-Layth. [[Al-Musnad (3/7); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3099); al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11228).]] al-Tirmidhi declared it authentic, and Muslim narrated it as will come.

Another route: Ahmad said: Yahya narrated to us, from Unays ibn Abi Yahya, who narrated to me, my father, who said: I heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: Two men differed: a man from the Banu Khudra and a man from the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, about the mosque founded upon piety. The Khudri said: It is the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The 'Amri said: It is the Mosque of Quba. They came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him about that. He said: "It is this mosque," meaning the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "In that there is much good [khayr kathir]," meaning the Mosque of Quba. [[Bracketed words are from manuscripts T, K, A and al-Musnad. In A: "khayr kabir". Al-Musnad (3/23).]]

Another route: Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Humayd al-Kharrat al-Madani narrated to us: I asked Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'id, and I said: How did you hear your father speak about the mosque founded upon piety? He said: My father said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I entered upon him in a room belonging to one of his wives. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, where is the mosque founded upon piety?" He took a handful of pebbles and struck the ground with them, then said: "It is your mosque this one." Then he said: [I said to him: "Like this?"] Did you hear your father mention it? [[Bracketed words are from manuscripts T, K, A and al-Tabari. In A: "which mosque" (ayy masjid). Tafsir al-Tabari (14/477); Sahih Muslim, no. (1398).]]

Muslim narrated it alone, from Muhammad ibn Hatim, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, with this chain. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1398).]] It was also narrated from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba and others, from Hatim ibn Isma'il, from Humayd al-Kharrat, with this chain. [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1398).]]

Many of the early (salaf) and later (khalaf) scholars held that it is the Mosque of the Prophet ﷺ. This is narrated from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, his son 'Abd Allah, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib. Ibn Jarir also chose this view.

* *

His saying: ﴿Surely a mosque founded upon piety from the first day is more worthy that you stand in it. In it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves﴾ is evidence for the recommendation (istihbab) of praying in ancient mosques founded from the first day of their construction upon the worship of Allah alone, with no partner; and for the recommendation of praying with the company of the righteous and the diligent worshippers who are careful to perform the wudu' (ablution) thoroughly and who keep themselves clear of filth.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, I heard Shabib Abu Rawh narrate from a man of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led them in the dawn prayer and recited in it [al-Rum] (Surah of the Romans), and he made a mistake. When he finished he said: "Indeed the Qur'an was confused for us. Indeed some people among you pray with us but do not perform the wudu' well. Whoever attends the prayer with us, let him perform the wudu' well." [[In manuscripts T and A: "fiha" instead of "bihim". Al-Musnad (3/471, 472).]]

Then he narrated it through two other routes, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Shabib Abu Rawh of Dhu al-Kala', that he prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, and he mentioned it. [[Al-Musnad (3/471, 472).]] This shows that completing the purification makes standing in worship easier, and helps in completing it and perfecting it and carrying out its prescribed acts.

Abu al-'Aliya said regarding His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah loves those who purify themselves﴾: Purification with water is indeed good, but they are the ones who purify themselves from sins.

Al-A'mash said: [it is] repentance from sin, and purification from shirk.

It has been reported in the hadith transmitted through several routes, in the Sunan and elsewhere, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the people of Quba: "Allah has praised you concerning purification. What do you do?" They said: We perform istinja' with water.

The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: 'Abd Allah ibn Shabib narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: I found it in my father's book, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed concerning the people of Quba: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and Allah loves those who purify themselves﴾. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked them, and they said: "We follow the stones with water."

Then he said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz alone narrated it from al-Zuhri, and no one narrated from him except his son. [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (247). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (1/212): "In its chain is Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Umar al-Zuhri, whom al-Bukhari and al-Nasa'i declared weak, and he is the one who pointed to [the narration of] the mantle of Malik."]]

I say: I only mentioned it in this wording because it is well known among the jurists (fuqaha'), while many of the later scholars of hadith did not recognize it, or all of them did not, and Allah knows best.

Allah the Exalted says: Those who lay the foundation of their building upon piety from Allah and His good pleasure are not equal to one who lays the foundation of his building upon the brink of a crumbling bank that collapses with him into the fire of Hell. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people. That is, the brink of a pit. Its example is: "into the fire of Hell. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people." That is, He does not set right the work of the corrupters.

Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah said: I saw the mosque that was built for harm, smoke coming out of it during the time of the Prophet ﷺ.

Ibn Jurayj said: It was mentioned to us that some men dug and found smoke coming out of it. Qatadah also said the same.

Khalaf ibn Yasin al-Kufi said: I saw the mosque of the hypocrites that Allah the Exalted mentioned in the Qur'an, and in it there was a hole from which smoke came out, and today it is a rubbish dump. Ibn Jarir narrated it, may Allah have mercy on him.

* *

His saying: "Their building which they have built will not cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts" means: a doubt and hypocrisy, because of their undertaking this shameful act, which bred hypocrisy in their hearts, just as the worshippers of the calf were made to drink in their hearts the love of it.

* *

His saying: "Unless their hearts are cut to pieces" means: by their death. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Suddi, Habib ibn Abi Thabit, al-Dahhak, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and many other scholars of the early generations.

"And Allah is All-Knowing" means: of the deeds of His creation, "All-Wise" in recompensing them for them, whether good or evil.

Allah the Exalted says: Those who lay the foundation of their building upon piety from Allah and His good pleasure are not equal to one who lays the foundation of his building upon the brink of a crumbling bank that collapses with him into the fire of Hell. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people. That is, the brink of a pit. Its example is: "into the fire of Hell. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people." That is, He does not set right the work of the corrupters.

Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah said: I saw the mosque that was built for harm, smoke coming out of it during the time of the Prophet ﷺ.

Ibn Jurayj said: It was mentioned to us that some men dug and found smoke coming out of it. Qatadah also said the same.

Khalaf ibn Yasin al-Kufi said: I saw the mosque of the hypocrites that Allah the Exalted mentioned in the Qur'an, and in it there was a hole from which smoke came out, and today it is a rubbish dump. Ibn Jarir narrated it, may Allah have mercy on him.

* *

His saying: "Their building which they have built will not cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts" means: a doubt and hypocrisy, because of their undertaking this shameful act, which bred hypocrisy in their hearts, just as the worshippers of the calf were made to drink in their hearts the love of it.

* *

His saying: "Unless their hearts are cut to pieces" means: by their death. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Suddi, Habib ibn Abi Thabit, al-Dahhak, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and many other scholars of the early generations.

"And Allah is All-Knowing" means: of the deeds of His creation, "All-Wise" in recompensing them for them, whether good or evil.

Ibn Kathir says: God informs that He has exchanged with His believing servants their selves and their wealth, since they expended them in His way, for Paradise. This is from His grace, His generosity and His kindness, for He accepted in exchange for what He owns, by what He bestowed upon His obedient servants. For this reason al-Hasan al-Basri and Qatadah said: "By God, He made a bargain with them and set a high price for them."

Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah said: "There is no Muslim but that he has a pledge (ba'ah) to God, Mighty and Majestic, around his neck, which he either fulfils or dies upon." Then he recited this verse.

For this reason it is said: "Whoever carries (arms) in the way of God has made a pledge with God," meaning he accepted this contract and fulfilled it.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and others said: 'Abdullah ibn Rawahah, may Allah be pleased with him, said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, on the night of 'Aqabah: "Stipulate for your Lord and for yourself whatever you wish!" He said: "I stipulate for my Lord that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him, and I stipulate for myself that you protect me as you protect your own selves and your wealth." They said: "What will we have if we do that?" He said: "Paradise." They said: "The sale is profitable; we will not cancel it, nor will we ask to cancel it." Then the verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties﴾ to the end of the verse.

* *

His saying: ﴿They fight in the way of Allah, so they kill and are killed﴾ means: whether they kill or are killed, or both happen to them, Paradise has become due to them. For this reason it is reported in the two Sahihs: "Allah has guaranteed for whoever goes out in His way, moved only by jihad in My way and belief in My messengers, that He will either cause him to die and enter him into Paradise, or return him to the dwelling from which he went out, with whatever reward or spoils he has gained." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3123, and Sahih Muslim, no. 1876]

* *

His saying: ﴿A promise binding upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Quran﴾ is an affirmation of this promise, and an information that He has prescribed it upon Himself, the Noble, and sent it down to His messengers in their great books: the Torah revealed to Musa (Moses), the Gospel revealed to 'Isa (Jesus), and the Quran revealed to Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all.

* *

His saying: ﴿And who is more faithful to his covenant than Allah?﴾ [meaning: there is no one more faithful to what He has covenanted than Allah] for He does not break the promise. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And who is more truthful in statement than Allah?﴾ [An-Nisa: 87] ﴿And who is more truthful in speech than Allah?﴾ [An-Nisa: 122]. For this reason He said: ﴿So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. And that is the great attainment.﴾ That is: let whoever upholds the requirement of this contract and fulfils this covenant rejoice in the great triumph and lasting bliss.

This is the description of the believers, whom Allah has purchased their selves and their wealth from, by these beautiful attributes and noble qualities: ﴿those who repent﴾ from all sins, those who abstain from immoralities, ﴿those who worship﴾, i.e., those who stand in the worship (ʿibadah) of their Lord, maintaining it. It consists of statements and actions. Among the most distinguished statements is praise [[In A: "al-hamdu lillah" (All praise is for Allah).]]; therefore He said: ﴿those who praise﴾. Among the best actions is fasting (sawm), which is abstaining from the pleasures of food, drink, and intercourse, and this is what is meant by "tourism" (siyahah) here. Therefore He said: ﴿those who travel (sa'ihun)﴾, as He described the wives of the Prophet [[In T, A: "the Messenger".]] (ﷺ) with it in His saying: ﴿fasting women﴾ [al-Tahrim: 5], i.e., fasting. Likewise, bowing and prostration, which are an expression for prayer (salah): therefore He said: ﴿those who bow and those who prostrate﴾. Along with that, they benefit the creation of Allah and guide them to obedience to Allah by enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, together with knowledge of what should be done and what must be avoided, which is guarding the limits of Allah in what He has made lawful and what He has made unlawful, in knowledge and in action. Thus they stood in the worship of the Truth and in advising the creation. Therefore He said: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾, because faith encompasses all of this, and complete happiness belongs to whoever is characterized by it.

[Explanation that the meaning of tourism (siyahah) is fasting] [[Addition from T, K, A.]]:

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from ʿAsim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, who said: ﴿those who travel﴾ are those who fast. Likewise it was narrated from Saʿid ibn Jubayr and al-ʿAwfi, from Ibn ʿAbbas.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn ʿAbbas: Every mention of tourism (siyahah) in the Qur'an refers to those who fast. Likewise said al-Dahhak, may Allah have mercy on him.

Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Yazid narrated to us, from al-Walid ibn ʿAbd Allah, from ʿA'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The tourism (siyahah) of this Ummah is fasting. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/505).]]

Likewise said Mujahid, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, ʿAta', Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah, and others: that what is meant by ﴿those who travel﴾ is those who fast.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿those who travel﴾ are those who fast the month of Ramadan.

Abu ʿAmr al-ʿAbdi said: ﴿those who travel﴾ are those among the believers who persist in fasting.

A similar statement has come in a raised (marfuʿ) hadith. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Bazi' narrated to me, Hakim ibn Hizam narrated to us, Sulayman narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Those who travel are those who fast." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/503).]]

[Then he narrated it from Bundar, from Ibn Mahdi, from Isra'il, from Sulayman al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, that he said: ﴿those who travel﴾ are those who fast.] [[Addition from T, K, A.]]

This stopped version (mawquf) is more authentic.

He also said: Yunus narrated to me, from Ibn Wahb, from ʿUmar ibn al-Harith, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about those who travel, and he said: "They are those who fast." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (14/502).]]

This is a good mursal narration.

So these are the most authentic and well-known opinions. There is also what indicates that tourism is jihad, which Abu Dawud narrated in his Sunan from the hadith of Abu Umamah that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to travel (siyahah)." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The tourism of my Ummah is jihad in the way of Allah." [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2486).]]

Ibn al-Mubarak said, from Ibn Lahi'ah: ʿUmarah ibn Ghaziyyah informed me that tourism was mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has replaced it for us with jihad in the way of Allah and glorifying Allah (takbir) on every high point." [[This is mu'dal; ʿUmarah ibn Ghaziyyah did not meet any of the Companions.]]

It is narrated from ʿIkrimah that he said: They are the seekers of knowledge. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: They are the emigrants (muhajirun). Ibn Abi Hatim narrated both.

The meaning of tourism is not what some who worship by mere wandering through the earth may understand, isolating themselves on the peaks of mountains, in caves, and in deserts. This is not prescribed except in times of trials and upheavals in religion, as established in Sahih al-Bukhari from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Soon the best wealth of a man will be sheep that he takes to the mountain peaks and the places of rainfall, fleeing with his religion from trials." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (19).]]

Al-ʿAwfi and ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and those who guard the limits of Allah﴾, he said: those who stand in obedience to Allah. Likewise said al-Hasan al-Basri, and there is a narration from him: ﴿and those who guard the limits of Allah﴾, he said: the obligations of Allah. In another narration: those who stand upon the command of Allah.

قَالَ الْإِمَامُ أَحْمَدُ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، حَدَّثَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنِ ابْنِ الْمُسَيَّبِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: لَمَّا حَضَرَتْ أَبَا طَالِبٍ الْوَفَاةُ [[في أ: "الفائدة".]] دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ وَعِنْدَهُ أَبُو جَهْلٍ، وَعَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أَبِي أُمَيَّةَ، فَقَالَ: "أَيْ عَمِّ، قُلْ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ. كَلِمَةٌ أُحَاجُّ لَكَ بِهَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ، عَزَّ وَجَلَّ". فَقَالَ أَبُو جَهْلٍ وَعَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أَبِي أُمَيَّةَ: يَا أَبَا طَالِبٍ، أَتَرْغَبُ عَنْ مِلَّةِ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ؟ [قَالَ: فَلَمْ يَزَالَا يُكَلِّمَانِهِ، حَتَّى قَالَ آخِرَ شَيْءٍ كَلَّمَهُمْ بِهِ: عَلَى [[في ت، ك، أ: "فقال: أنا على ملة".]] مِلَّةِ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ]. [[زيادة من ت، ك، أ، والمسند.]] فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: "لَأَسْتَغْفِرَنَّ لَكَ مَا لَمْ أُنْهَ عَنْكَ". فَنَزَلَتْ: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ وَلَوْ كَانُوا أُولِي قُرْبَى مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُمْ أَصْحَابُ الْجَحِيمِ﴾. قَالَ: وَنَزَلَتْ فِيهِ: ﴿إِنَّكَ لَا تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ﴾ [الْقَصَصِ: ٥٦]. أَخْرَجَاهُ. [[المسند (٥/٥٣٣) وصحيح البخاري برقم (٤٦٧٥) وصحيح مسلم برقم (٢٤).]]

وَقَالَ الْإِمَامُ أَحْمَدُ: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ آدَمَ، أَخْبَرَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ أَبِي الْخَلِيلِ، عَنْ عَلِيٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَجُلًا يَسْتَغْفِرُ لِأَبَوَيْهِ وَهُمَا مُشْرِكَانِ، فَقُلْتُ: أَيَسْتَغْفِرُ الرَّجُلُ لِأَبَوَيْهِ وَهُمَا مُشْرِكَانِ؟ فَقَالَ: أَوَلَمْ يَسْتَغْفِرْ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ؟ فَذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لِلنَّبِيِّ ﷺ، فَنَزَلَتْ: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ أَنَّهُ عَدُوٌّ لِلَّهِ﴾. قَالَ: "لَمَّا مَاتَ"، فَلَا أَدْرِي قَالَهُ سُفْيَانُ أَوْ قَالَهُ إِسْرَائِيلُ، أَوْ هُوَ [[في ت، أ: "وهو".]] فِي الْحَدِيثِ "لَمَّا مَاتَ". [[المسند (١/٩٩).]]

قُلْتُ: هَذَا ثَابِتٌ عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: لَمَّا مَاتَ.

وَقَالَ الْإِمَامُ أَحْمَدُ: حَدَّثَنَا الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُوسَى، حَدَّثَنَا زُهَيْرٌ، حَدَّثَنَا زُبَيْدُ بْنُ الْحَارِثِ الْيَامِيُّ [[في أ: "السامي".]] عَنْ مُحَارِبِ بْنِ دِثَارٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ بُرَيْدَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: كُنَّا مَعَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ، فَنَزَلَ بِنَا وَنَحْنُ مَعَهُ قَرِيبٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ رَاكِبٍ، فَصَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ، ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْنَا بِوَجْهِهِ وَعَيْنَاهُ تَذْرِفَانِ، فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ وَفَدَاهُ بِالْأَبِ وَالْأُمِّ، وَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، مَا لَكَ؟ قَالَ: "إِنِّي سَأَلْتُ رَبِّي، عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، فِي الِاسْتِغْفَارِ لِأُمِّي، فَلَمْ يَأْذَنْ لِي، فَدَمِعَتْ عَيْنَايَ رَحْمَةً لَهَا مِنَ النَّارِ، وَإِنِّي كُنْتُ نَهَيْتُكُمْ عَنْ ثَلَاثٍ: نَهَيْتُكُمْ عَنْ زِيَارَةِ الْقُبُورِ فَزُورُوهَا، لِتُذَكِّرَكُمْ زِيَارَتُهَا خَيْرًا، وَنَهَيْتُكُمْ عَنْ لُحُومِ الْأَضَاحِيِّ بَعْدَ ثَلَاثٍ، فَكُلُوا وَأَمْسِكُوا مَا شِئْتُمْ، وَنَهَيْتُكُمْ عَنِ الْأَشْرِبَةِ فِي الْأَوْعِيَةِ، فَاشْرَبُوا فِي أَيِّ وِعَاءٍ [[في ت، ك، أ: "أي وعاء شئتم".]] وَلَا تَشْرَبُوا مُسْكِرًا". [[المسند (٥/٣٥٥).]]

وَرَوَى ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ، مِنْ حَدِيثِ عَلْقَمَةَ بْنِ مَرْثَدٍ، عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ بُرَيْدَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ؛ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ لَمَّا قَدِمَ مَكَّةَ أَتَى رَسْمَ قَبْرٍ، فَجَلَسَ إِلَيْهِ، فَجَعَلَ يُخَاطِبُ، ثُمَّ قَامَ مُسْتَعْبِرًا. فَقُلْنَا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّا رَابَنَا مَا صَنَعْتَ. قَالَ: "إِنِّي اسْتَأْذَنْتُ رَبِّي فِي زِيَارَةِ قَبْرِ أُمِّي، فَأَذِنَ لِي، وَاسْتَأْذَنْتُهُ فِي الِاسْتِغْفَارِ لَهَا فَلَمْ يَأْذَنْ لِي". فَمَا رُئِيَ بَاكِيًا أَكْثَرَ مِنْهُ يَوْمَئِذٍ. [[تفسير الطبري (١٤/٥١٢) ورواه البيهقي في دلائل النبوة (١/١٨٩) من طريق سفيان عن علقمة بن مرثد به نحوه.]]

وَقَالَ ابْنُ أَبِي حَاتِمٍ فِي تَفْسِيرِهِ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، حَدَّثَنَا خَالِدُ بْنُ خِدَاشٍ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ وَهْبٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ هَانِئٍ، عَنْ مَسْرُوقٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ قَالَ: خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ يَوْمًا إِلَى الْمَقَابِرِ، فَاتَّبَعْنَاهُ، فَجَاءَ حَتَّى جَلَسَ إِلَى قَبْرٍ مِنْهَا، فَنَاجَاهُ طَوِيلًا ثُمَّ بَكَى فَبَكَيْنَا لِبُكَائِهِ ثُمَّ قَامَ فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ، فَدَعَاهُ ثُمَّ دَعَانَا، فَقَالَ: "مَا أَبْكَاكُمْ؟" فَقُلْنَا: بَكَيْنَا لِبُكَائِكَ. قَالَ: "إِنَّ الْقَبْرَ الَّذِي جَلَسْتُ عِنْدَهُ قَبْرُ آمِنَةَ، وَإِنِّي اسْتَأْذَنْتُ رَبِّي فِي زِيَارَتِهَا فَأَذِنَ لِي" [[ورواه الحاكم في المستدرك (٢/٣٣٦) ومن طريقه البيهقي في دلائل النبوة (١/١٨٩) من طريق بحر بن نصر عن ابن وهب به نحوه.]] ثُمَّ أَوْرَدَهُ مِنْ وَجْهٍ آخَرَ، ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ مِنْ حَدِيثِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ قَرِيبًا مِنْهُ، وَفِيهِ: "وَإِنِّي اسْتَأْذَنْتُ رَبِّي فِي الدُّعَاءِ لَهَا فَلَمْ يَأْذَنْ لِي، وَأَنْزَلَ عَلَيَّ: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ وَلَوْ كَانُوا أُولِي قُرْبَى﴾ فَأَخَذَنِي مَا يَأْخُذُ الْوَلَدَ لِلْوَالِدَةِ، وَكُنْتُ نَهَيْتُكُمْ عَنْ زِيَارَةِ الْقُبُورِ فَزُورُوهَا، فَإِنَّهَا تُذَكِّرُ الْآخِرَةَ". [[وأصل الحديث رواه مسلم في صحيحه برقم (٩٧٦) عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: زَارَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَبْرَ أُمِّهِ فَبَكَى وَأَبْكَى مَنْ حَوْلَهُ. فَقَالَ: "اسْتَأْذَنْتُ رَبِّي فِي أَنْ أَسْتَغْفِرَ لَهَا فَلَمْ يُؤْذَنْ لِي، وَاسْتَأْذَنْتُهُ فِي أَنْ أَزُورَ قَبْرَهَا فَأَذِنَ لِي، فَزُورُوا الْقُبُورَ فَإِنَّهَا تُذَكِّرُ الْمَوْتَ".]]

حَدِيثٌ آخَرُ فِي مَعْنَاهُ: قَالَ الطَّبَرَانِيُّ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ الْمَرْوَزِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الدَّرْدَاءِ عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ [[في ت: "أبو الدرداء عن عبد العزيز".]] بْنُ مُنِيبٍ، حَدَّثَنَا إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ كَيْسَانَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ؛ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَمَّا أَقْبَلَ مِنْ غَزْوَةِ تَبُوكَ وَاعْتَمَرَ، فَلَمَّا هَبَطَ مِنْ ثَنِيَّةِ عُسْفَانَ أَمَرَ أَصْحَابَهُ: أَنِ اسْتَنِدُوا إِلَى الْعَقَبَةِ حَتَّى أَرْجِعَ إِلَيْكُمْ، فَذَهَبَ فَنَزَلَ عَلَى قَبْرِ أُمِّهِ، فَنَاجَى رَبَّهُ طَوِيلًا ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ بَكَى فَاشْتَدَّ بُكَاؤُهُ، وَبَكَى هَؤُلَاءِ لِبُكَائِهِ، وَقَالُوا: مَا بَكَى نَبِيُّ اللَّهِ بِهَذَا الْمَكَانِ إِلَّا وَقَدْ أُحْدِثَ فِي أُمَّتِهِ شَيْءٌ لَا تُطِيقُهُ. فَلَمَّا بَكَى هَؤُلَاءِ قَامَ فَرَجَعَ إِلَيْهِمْ، فَقَالَ: "مَا يُبْكِيكُمْ؟". قَالُوا: يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ، بَكَيْنَا لِبُكَائِكَ، فَقُلْنَا: لَعَلَّهُ أُحْدِثَ فِي أُمَّتِكَ شَيْءٌ لَا تُطِيقُهُ، قَالَ: "لَا وَقَدْ كَانَ بَعْضُهُ، وَلَكِنْ نَزَلْتُ عَلَى قَبْرِ أُمِّي فَدَعَوْتُ اللَّهَ أَنْ يَأْذَنَ لِي فِي شَفَاعَتِهَا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، فَأَبَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَأْذَنَ لِي، فَرَحِمْتُهَا وَهِيَ أُمِّي، فَبَكَيْتُ، ثُمَّ جَاءَنِي جِبْرِيلُ فَقَالَ: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اسْتِغْفَارُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ إِلَّا عَنْ مَوْعِدَةٍ وَعَدَهَا إِيَّاهُ فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ أَنَّهُ عَدُوٌّ لِلَّهِ تَبَرَّأَ مِنْهُ﴾ فَتَبَرَّأْ أَنْتَ مِنْ أُمِّكَ، كَمَا تَبَرَّأَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ مِنْ أَبِيهِ، فَرَحِمْتُهَا وَهِيَ أُمِّي، وَدَعَوْتُ رَبِّي أَنْ يَرْفَعَ عَنْ أُمَّتِي أَرْبَعًا، فَرَفَعَ عَنْهُمُ اثْنَتَيْنِ، وَأَبَى أَنْ يَرْفَعَ عَنْهُمُ اثْنَتَيْنِ: دَعَوْتُ رَبِّي أَنْ يَرْفَعَ عَنْهُمُ الرَّجْمَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْغَرَقَ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ، وَأَلَّا يُلْبِسَهُمْ شِيَعًا، وَأَلَّا يُذِيقَ بَعْضَهُمْ بَأْسَ بَعْضٍ، فَرَفَعَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمُ الرَّجْمَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ، وَالْغَرَقَ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ، وَأَبَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَرْفَعَ عَنْهُمُ الْقَتْلَ وَالْهَرْجَ". وَإِنَّمَا عَدَلَ إِلَى قَبْرِ أُمِّهِ لِأَنَّهَا كَانَتْ مَدْفُونَةً تَحْتَ كَدَاءٍ [[في ت، أ: "كذا وكذا"، وفي ك: "كذا وكذا".]] وَكَانَتْ عُسْفَانُ لَهُمْ. [[المعجم الكبير (١١/٣٧٤).]]

وَهَذَا حَدِيثٌ غَرِيبٌ وَسِيَاقٌ عَجِيبٌ، وَأَغْرَبُ مِنْهُ وَأَشَدُّ نَكَارَةً مَا رَوَاهُ الْخَطِيبُ الْبَغْدَادِيُّ فِي كِتَابِ "السَّابِقِ وَاللَّاحِقِ" بِسَنَدٍ مَجْهُولٍ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ فِي حَدِيثٍ فِيهِ قِصَّةُ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَحْيَا أُمَّهُ فَآمَنَتْ ثُمَّ عَادَتْ. [[ساقه القرطبي في: التذكرة في أحوال الموتى وأمور الآخرة (ص ١٦) وقال: خرّجه أبو بكر أحمد بن علي الخطيب في كتاب السابق واللاحق، وأبو حفص عمر بن شاهين في الناسخ والمنسوخ، ولا يصح الحديث، لمخالفته ما في صحيح مسلم برقم (٩٧٦) من حديث أبي هريرة قال: زار النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قبر أمه فبكى وأبكى من حوله. فقال: "استأذنت ربي في أن أستغفر لها فلم يأذن لي، واستأذنته في أن أزور قبرها فأذن لي، فزوروا القبور فإنها تذكر الموت"، ولضعف إسناده.]] وَكَذَلِكَ مَا رَوَاهُ السُّهَيْلِيُّ فِي "الرَّوْضِ" بِسَنَدٍ فِيهِ جَمَاعَةٌ مَجْهُولُونَ: أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَحْيَا لَهُ أَبَاهُ وَأُمَّهُ [[في ت: "وآمنة".]] فَآمَنَا بِهِ. [[الروض الأنف (١/١١٣).]]

وَقَدْ قَالَ الْحَافِظُ ابْنُ دِحْيَةَ: [هَذَا الْحَدِيثُ مَوْضُوعٌ يَرُدُّهُ الْقُرْآنُ وَالْإِجْمَاعُ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَلَا الَّذِينَ يَمُوتُونَ وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ﴾ [النِّسَاءِ: ١٨]. وَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْقُرْطُبِيُّ: إِنَّ مُقْتَضَى هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ. . . وَرَدَّ عَلَى ابْنِ دِحْيَةَ] [[زيادة من ت، ك، أ.]] فِي هَذَا الِاسْتِدْلَالِ بِمَا حَاصِلُهُ: أَنَّ هَذِهِ حَيَاةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ، كَمَا رَجَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ بَعْدَ غَيْبُوبَتِهَا فَصَلَّى عَلِيٌّ الْعَصْرَ. قَالَ الطَّحَاوِيُّ: وَهُوَ [حَدِيثٌ] [[زيادة من ت، ك، أ.]] ثَابِتٌ، يَعْنِي: حَدِيثَ الشَّمْسِ.

قَالَ الْقُرْطُبِيُّ: فَلَيْسَ إِحْيَاؤُهُمَا يَمْتَنِعُ عَقْلًا وَلَا شَرْعًا، قَالَ: وَقَدْ سَمِعْتُ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَحْيَا عَمَّهُ أَبَا طَالِبٍ، فَآمَنَ بِهِ. [[التذكرة (ص ١٧). وَمَا ذَكَرَهُ الْقُرْطُبِيُّ لَا يَصِحُّ؛ أَمَّا إِحْيَاؤُهُمَا وَإِيمَانُهُمَا فَلَا يَمْتَنِعُ عَقْلًا، وَأَمَّا شَرْعًا فَقَدْ جَاءَ فِي صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَنَسٍ؛ أَنَّ رَجُلًا قَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَيْنَ أَبِي؟ قَالَ: "فِي النَّارِ"، فَلَمَّا قَفَّى دَعَاهُ وَقَالَ: "إِنَّ أَبِي وَأَبَاكَ فِي النَّارِ". وَمَنَعَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مِنَ الِاسْتِغْفَارِ لِأُمِّهِ، وَهَذَا الْمَنْعُ مُتَأَخِّرٌ، بِخِلَافِ مَنْ قَالَ بِأَنَّ مَا جَاءَ فِي أَنَّهُمَا - أَيْ أَبَوَيْهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - فِي النَّارِ مَنْسُوخٌ بِحَدِيثِ عَائِشَةَ الَّذِي رَوَاهُ الْخَطِيبُ، فَإِنَّ دَعْوَى النَّسْخِ غَيْرُ قَائِمَةٍ وَلَا تُعْتَمَدُ عَلَى أَصْلٍ. وَأَمَّا قَوْلُ الْقُرْطُبِيِّ بِأَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَحْيَا عَمَّهُ أَبَا طَالِبٍ. . . إِلَخ، فَهَذَا أَبْعَدُ عَنِ الصِّحَّةِ؛ فَإِنَّ فِي الصَّحِيحِ مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ؛ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ شَفَعَ لَهُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ فَهُوَ فِي النَّارِ يُجْعَلُ ضَحْضَاحٌ مِنْ نَارٍ تَحْتَ قَدَمَيْهِ يَغْلِي مِنْهَا دِمَاغُهُ، وَفِي صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ مَرْفُوعًا: "أَهْوَنُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ عَذَابًا أَبُو طَالِبٍ". فَمَنْ يَكُونُ فِي النَّارِ كَيْفَ يُقَالُ: إِنَّهُ آمَنَ فِي قَبْرِهِ؟!]] قُلْتُ: وَهَذَا كُلُّهُ مُتَوَقِّفٌ عَلَى صِحَّةِ الْحَدِيثِ، فَإِذَا صَحَّ فَلَا مَانِعَ مِنْهُ [[وَقَدْ رَأَيْتَ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ لَا يَصِحُّ. وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.]] وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.

وَقَالَ الْعَوْفِيُّ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ فِي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ الْآيَةَ، فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرَ لِأُمِّهِ، فَنَهَاهُ اللَّهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ [[في ت، أ: "عنه".]] فَقَالَ: "فَإِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ خَلِيلَ اللَّهِ اسْتَغْفَرَ لِأَبِيهِ"، فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اسْتِغْفَارُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ إِلَّا عَنْ مَوْعِدَةٍ وَعَدَهَا إِيَّاهُ﴾ [[في ت: "إياها".]] الْآيَةَ.

وَقَالَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي طَلْحَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، فِي هَذِهِ الْآيَةِ: كَانُوا يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لَهُمْ، حَتَّى نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الْآيَةُ، فَلَمَّا [نَزَلَتْ [[في أ: "أنزلت".]] أَمْسَكُوا عَنِ الِاسْتِغْفَارِ لِأَمْوَاتِهِمْ، وَلَمْ يَنْهَهُمْ أَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْأَحْيَاءِ حَتَّى يَمُوتُوا]. [[زيادة من ت، ك، أ.]] ثُمَّ أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اسْتِغْفَارُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ﴾ الْآيَةَ.

وَقَالَ قَتَادَةُ فِي هَذِهِ الْآيَةِ: ذُكِرَ لَنَا أَنَّ رِجَالًا مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ قَالُوا: يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ، إِنَّ مِنْ آبَائِنَا مَنْ كَانَ يُحْسِنُ الْجِوَارَ، وَيَصِلُ الْأَرْحَامَ، وَيَفُكُّ الْعَانِيَ، وَيُوفِي بِالذِّمَمِ؛ أَفَلَا نَسْتَغْفِرُ لَهُمْ؟ قَالَ: فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: "بَلَى، وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لَأَسْتَغْفِرُ لِأَبِي كَمَا اسْتَغْفَرَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ". فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ حَتَّى بَلَغَ: ﴿الْجَحِيمِ﴾. ثُمَّ عَذَرَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ، فَقَالَ: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اسْتِغْفَارُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ إِلَّا عَنْ مَوْعِدَةٍ وَعَدَهَا إِيَّاهُ فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ أَنَّهُ عَدُوٌّ لِلَّهِ تَبَرَّأَ مِنْهُ﴾. قَالَ: وَذُكِرَ لَنَا أَنَّ نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ قَالَ: "أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ كَلِمَاتٌ، فَدَخَلْنَ فِي أُذُنِي وَوَقَرْنَ فِي قَلْبِي: أُمِرْتُ أَلَّا أَسْتَغْفِرَ لِمَنْ مَاتَ مُشْرِكًا، وَمَنْ أَعْطَى فَضْلَ مَالِهِ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَهُ، وَمَنْ أَمْسَكَ فَهُوَ شَرٌّ لَهُ، وَلَا يَلُومُ اللَّهُ عَلَى كَفَافٍ".

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 9, verses 113–114 (part 2 of 2)

Al-Thawri narrated from al-Shaybani, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A Jewish man died, and he had a Muslim son who did not go out with him (to the funeral). This was mentioned to Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "It was incumbent upon him to walk with him and bury him, and to pray that he be guided to righteousness for as long as he was alive. When he died, he should have left him to his own affair." Then he recited: ﴿The prayer for forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him.﴾ He did not supplicate for him.

[I say:] This is supported by what Abu Dawud and others narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "When Abu Talib died, I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, your uncle, the misguided old man, has died.' He said: 'Go and bury him, and do not do anything until you come to me.'" And he mentioned the rest of the hadith.[1]

It is narrated that when the funeral of his uncle Abu Talib passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Kinship has been joined to you, O uncle."[2]

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: "I would not abandon the funeral prayer for anyone from the people of the qiblah (those who face the Ka'bah in prayer), even if she were a pregnant Abyssinian woman from fornication, because I have not heard that Allah forbade the prayer except for the polytheists. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists...﴾"

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn WakI', from his father, from 'Isma ibn Zamil, from his father, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: "May Allah have mercy on a man who asks forgiveness for Abu Hurayrah and his mother." I said: "And for his father?" He said: "No. My father died a polytheist."[3]

* *

His saying: ﴿But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Ibrahim continued to ask forgiveness for his father until he died. When it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him." In another narration: "When he died, it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah."

Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah and others said the same, may Allah have mercy on them.

'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: On the Day of Resurrection, Ibrahim will disassociate himself from him when he meets his father, and on his father's face will be dust and darkness. He will say: "O Ibrahim, I used to disobey you, but today I will not disobey you." Ibrahim will say: "My Lord, did You not promise me that You would not disgrace me on the Day they are raised? What disgrace is greater than my father being far from mercy?" It will be said: "Look behind you," and he will look and see a smeared *dhīkh*, meaning he has been transformed into a hyena (*ḍib'ān*). Then he will be dragged by its legs and thrown into the Fire.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was *awwāh*, forbearing.﴾ Sufyan al-Thawri and others narrated from 'Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that he said: "The *awwāh* is the one who supplicates much (*al-da''ā'*)." This is also narrated through other chains from Ibn Mas'ud.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna narrated to me: al-Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us: 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram narrated to us: Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Had, who said: "While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting, a man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the *awwāh*?' He said: 'The one who humbles himself in supplication (*al-mutaḍarri'*).' He said: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was *awwāh*, forbearing.﴾"[4]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Ibn al-Mubarak, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, with the same chain, and he said: "*Al-mutaḍarri'* is the one who supplicates (*al-da''ā'*)."

Al-Thawri narrated from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim al-Batin, from Abu al-'Ubaydayn, that he asked Ibn Mas'ud about the *awwāh*, and he said: "It is the merciful (*al-raḥīm*)."

Mujahid, Abu Maysarah 'Amr ibn Shurahbil, al-Hasan al-Basri and Qatadah said the same: that it is the merciful, i.e., toward the servants of Allah.

Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Khalid, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The *awwāh* is the one who is certain (*al-mūqin*) in the language of Abyssinia." Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas similarly, that it is the one who is certain. Mujahid and al-Dahhak said the same. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah and Mujahid narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "The *awwāh* is the believer." 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah added from him: "The believer who repents often (*al-tawwāb*)." Al-'Awfi narrated from him: "It is the believer in the language of Abyssinia." Ibn Jurayj likewise said: "It is the believer in the language of Abyssinia."

Ahmad said: Musa narrated to us: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from al-Harith ibn Yazid, from 'Ali ibn Rabah, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to a man called "Dhu al-Bijadayn": "Indeed, he is an *awwāh*." That was because he was a man who remembered Allah often, and who recited the Qur'an and raised his voice in supplication.[5]

Ibn Jarir also narrated it.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Sha'bi said: The *awwāh* is the one who glorifies Allah (*al-musabbiḥ*). Ibn Wahb narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, from Abu al-Zahiriyyah, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "None remains consistent in the voluntary Duha prayer except an *awwāh*."[6] Shufayy ibn Mani' narrated from Ayyub: "The *awwāh* is the one who, when he remembers his sins, asks forgiveness for them."

From Mujahid: "The *awwāh* is the one who is vigilant and fearful, who commits a sin in secret and then repents of it in secret."

Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated all of this.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn WakI' narrated to us: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from al-Hakam, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim ibn Yannaq: "A man used to remember Allah often and glorify Him, and this was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'Indeed, he is an *awwāh*.'"[7]

He also said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Ibn Yaman narrated to us: al-Minhal ibn Khalifah narrated to us, from Hajjaj ibn Artah, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) buried a dead man and said: "May Allah have mercy on you, for indeed you were an *awwāhan*!" meaning: one who recites the Qur'an much.[8]

Shu'bah narrated from Abu Yunus al-Bahili, who said: "I heard a man in Makkah, whose origin was Roman and who was a storyteller, narrating from Abu Dharr, who said: 'A man used to circumambulate the Sacred House and say in his supplication: "*Awwih, awwih*" (an expression of grief). This was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Indeed, he is an *awwāh*." Abu Dharr said: "I went out one night, and there was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) burying that man at night, with a lamp with him."'"

This is a *gharīb* hadith (one transmitted through a single chain, so its transmission is singular), narrated by Ibn Jarir, who also transmitted it in a *mashsha* (a dubious manner).[9]

It is narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar that he said: "*Inna Ibrahima la-awwāh*": he used to say, whenever he mentioned the Fire, "*Awwih* from the Fire!"

Ibn Jurayj said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was *awwāh*﴾: he was a jurist (*faqīh*)."

The Imam al-'Alam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: The most preferable of the opinions is the view of the one who said that it is the one who supplicates much (*al-da''ā'*), and this fits the context. When Allah the Exalted mentioned that Ibrahim only asked forgiveness for his father because of a promise he had made to him, and that Ibrahim was one who supplicated much and was forbearing toward those who wronged him and caused him harm, he asked forgiveness for his father despite his father's severe harm to him, in His saying: ﴿Do you reject my gods, O Ibrahim? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so leave me for a long time. He said: Peace be upon you. I will ask my Lord to forgive you; indeed He is ever gracious to me.﴾ [Maryam: 46–47]. So he was forbearing toward him despite his harm, and he prayed for him and asked forgiveness for him. For this reason, the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was *awwāh*, forbearing.﴾[10]
