قَالَ الْإِمَامُ أَحْمَدُ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، حَدَّثَنَا مَعْمَرٌ، عَنِ الزُّهْرِيِّ، عَنِ ابْنِ الْمُسَيَّبِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: لَمَّا حَضَرَتْ أَبَا طَالِبٍ الْوَفَاةُ [[في أ: "الفائدة".]] دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ وَعِنْدَهُ أَبُو جَهْلٍ، وَعَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أَبِي أُمَيَّةَ، فَقَالَ: "أَيْ عَمِّ، قُلْ: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ. كَلِمَةٌ أُحَاجُّ لَكَ بِهَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ، عَزَّ وَجَلَّ". فَقَالَ أَبُو جَهْلٍ وَعَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أَبِي أُمَيَّةَ: يَا أَبَا طَالِبٍ، أَتَرْغَبُ عَنْ مِلَّةِ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ؟ [قَالَ: فَلَمْ يَزَالَا يُكَلِّمَانِهِ، حَتَّى قَالَ آخِرَ شَيْءٍ كَلَّمَهُمْ بِهِ: عَلَى [[في ت، ك، أ: "فقال: أنا على ملة".]] مِلَّةِ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ]. [[زيادة من ت، ك، أ، والمسند.]] فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: "لَأَسْتَغْفِرَنَّ لَكَ مَا لَمْ أُنْهَ عَنْكَ". فَنَزَلَتْ: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ وَلَوْ كَانُوا أُولِي قُرْبَى مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُمْ أَصْحَابُ الْجَحِيمِ﴾. قَالَ: وَنَزَلَتْ فِيهِ: ﴿إِنَّكَ لَا تَهْدِي مَنْ أَحْبَبْتَ﴾ [الْقَصَصِ: ٥٦]. أَخْرَجَاهُ. [[المسند (٥/٥٣٣) وصحيح البخاري برقم (٤٦٧٥) وصحيح مسلم برقم (٢٤).]]

وَقَالَ الْإِمَامُ أَحْمَدُ: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ آدَمَ، أَخْبَرَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ أَبِي الْخَلِيلِ، عَنْ عَلِيٍّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَجُلًا يَسْتَغْفِرُ لِأَبَوَيْهِ وَهُمَا مُشْرِكَانِ، فَقُلْتُ: أَيَسْتَغْفِرُ الرَّجُلُ لِأَبَوَيْهِ وَهُمَا مُشْرِكَانِ؟ فَقَالَ: أَوَلَمْ يَسْتَغْفِرْ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ؟ فَذَكَرْتُ ذَلِكَ لِلنَّبِيِّ ﷺ، فَنَزَلَتْ: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ أَنَّهُ عَدُوٌّ لِلَّهِ﴾. قَالَ: "لَمَّا مَاتَ"، فَلَا أَدْرِي قَالَهُ سُفْيَانُ أَوْ قَالَهُ إِسْرَائِيلُ، أَوْ هُوَ [[في ت، أ: "وهو".]] فِي الْحَدِيثِ "لَمَّا مَاتَ". [[المسند (١/٩٩).]]

قُلْتُ: هَذَا ثَابِتٌ عَنْ مُجَاهِدٍ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: لَمَّا مَاتَ.

وَقَالَ الْإِمَامُ أَحْمَدُ: حَدَّثَنَا الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُوسَى، حَدَّثَنَا زُهَيْرٌ، حَدَّثَنَا زُبَيْدُ بْنُ الْحَارِثِ الْيَامِيُّ [[في أ: "السامي".]] عَنْ مُحَارِبِ بْنِ دِثَارٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ بُرَيْدَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: كُنَّا مَعَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ، فَنَزَلَ بِنَا وَنَحْنُ مَعَهُ قَرِيبٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ رَاكِبٍ، فَصَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ، ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْنَا بِوَجْهِهِ وَعَيْنَاهُ تَذْرِفَانِ، فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ وَفَدَاهُ بِالْأَبِ وَالْأُمِّ، وَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، مَا لَكَ؟ قَالَ: "إِنِّي سَأَلْتُ رَبِّي، عَزَّ وَجَلَّ، فِي الِاسْتِغْفَارِ لِأُمِّي، فَلَمْ يَأْذَنْ لِي، فَدَمِعَتْ عَيْنَايَ رَحْمَةً لَهَا مِنَ النَّارِ، وَإِنِّي كُنْتُ نَهَيْتُكُمْ عَنْ ثَلَاثٍ: نَهَيْتُكُمْ عَنْ زِيَارَةِ الْقُبُورِ فَزُورُوهَا، لِتُذَكِّرَكُمْ زِيَارَتُهَا خَيْرًا، وَنَهَيْتُكُمْ عَنْ لُحُومِ الْأَضَاحِيِّ بَعْدَ ثَلَاثٍ، فَكُلُوا وَأَمْسِكُوا مَا شِئْتُمْ، وَنَهَيْتُكُمْ عَنِ الْأَشْرِبَةِ فِي الْأَوْعِيَةِ، فَاشْرَبُوا فِي أَيِّ وِعَاءٍ [[في ت، ك، أ: "أي وعاء شئتم".]] وَلَا تَشْرَبُوا مُسْكِرًا". [[المسند (٥/٣٥٥).]]

وَرَوَى ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ، مِنْ حَدِيثِ عَلْقَمَةَ بْنِ مَرْثَدٍ، عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ بُرَيْدَةَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ؛ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ لَمَّا قَدِمَ مَكَّةَ أَتَى رَسْمَ قَبْرٍ، فَجَلَسَ إِلَيْهِ، فَجَعَلَ يُخَاطِبُ، ثُمَّ قَامَ مُسْتَعْبِرًا. فَقُلْنَا: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إِنَّا رَابَنَا مَا صَنَعْتَ. قَالَ: "إِنِّي اسْتَأْذَنْتُ رَبِّي فِي زِيَارَةِ قَبْرِ أُمِّي، فَأَذِنَ لِي، وَاسْتَأْذَنْتُهُ فِي الِاسْتِغْفَارِ لَهَا فَلَمْ يَأْذَنْ لِي". فَمَا رُئِيَ بَاكِيًا أَكْثَرَ مِنْهُ يَوْمَئِذٍ. [[تفسير الطبري (١٤/٥١٢) ورواه البيهقي في دلائل النبوة (١/١٨٩) من طريق سفيان عن علقمة بن مرثد به نحوه.]]

وَقَالَ ابْنُ أَبِي حَاتِمٍ فِي تَفْسِيرِهِ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، حَدَّثَنَا خَالِدُ بْنُ خِدَاشٍ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ وَهْبٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ هَانِئٍ، عَنْ مَسْرُوقٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ قَالَ: خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ يَوْمًا إِلَى الْمَقَابِرِ، فَاتَّبَعْنَاهُ، فَجَاءَ حَتَّى جَلَسَ إِلَى قَبْرٍ مِنْهَا، فَنَاجَاهُ طَوِيلًا ثُمَّ بَكَى فَبَكَيْنَا لِبُكَائِهِ ثُمَّ قَامَ فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ، فَدَعَاهُ ثُمَّ دَعَانَا، فَقَالَ: "مَا أَبْكَاكُمْ؟" فَقُلْنَا: بَكَيْنَا لِبُكَائِكَ. قَالَ: "إِنَّ الْقَبْرَ الَّذِي جَلَسْتُ عِنْدَهُ قَبْرُ آمِنَةَ، وَإِنِّي اسْتَأْذَنْتُ رَبِّي فِي زِيَارَتِهَا فَأَذِنَ لِي" [[ورواه الحاكم في المستدرك (٢/٣٣٦) ومن طريقه البيهقي في دلائل النبوة (١/١٨٩) من طريق بحر بن نصر عن ابن وهب به نحوه.]] ثُمَّ أَوْرَدَهُ مِنْ وَجْهٍ آخَرَ، ثُمَّ ذَكَرَ مِنْ حَدِيثِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ قَرِيبًا مِنْهُ، وَفِيهِ: "وَإِنِّي اسْتَأْذَنْتُ رَبِّي فِي الدُّعَاءِ لَهَا فَلَمْ يَأْذَنْ لِي، وَأَنْزَلَ عَلَيَّ: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ وَلَوْ كَانُوا أُولِي قُرْبَى﴾ فَأَخَذَنِي مَا يَأْخُذُ الْوَلَدَ لِلْوَالِدَةِ، وَكُنْتُ نَهَيْتُكُمْ عَنْ زِيَارَةِ الْقُبُورِ فَزُورُوهَا، فَإِنَّهَا تُذَكِّرُ الْآخِرَةَ". [[وأصل الحديث رواه مسلم في صحيحه برقم (٩٧٦) عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ: زَارَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَبْرَ أُمِّهِ فَبَكَى وَأَبْكَى مَنْ حَوْلَهُ. فَقَالَ: "اسْتَأْذَنْتُ رَبِّي فِي أَنْ أَسْتَغْفِرَ لَهَا فَلَمْ يُؤْذَنْ لِي، وَاسْتَأْذَنْتُهُ فِي أَنْ أَزُورَ قَبْرَهَا فَأَذِنَ لِي، فَزُورُوا الْقُبُورَ فَإِنَّهَا تُذَكِّرُ الْمَوْتَ".]]

حَدِيثٌ آخَرُ فِي مَعْنَاهُ: قَالَ الطَّبَرَانِيُّ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ الْمَرْوَزِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الدَّرْدَاءِ عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ [[في ت: "أبو الدرداء عن عبد العزيز".]] بْنُ مُنِيبٍ، حَدَّثَنَا إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ كَيْسَانَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ؛ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَمَّا أَقْبَلَ مِنْ غَزْوَةِ تَبُوكَ وَاعْتَمَرَ، فَلَمَّا هَبَطَ مِنْ ثَنِيَّةِ عُسْفَانَ أَمَرَ أَصْحَابَهُ: أَنِ اسْتَنِدُوا إِلَى الْعَقَبَةِ حَتَّى أَرْجِعَ إِلَيْكُمْ، فَذَهَبَ فَنَزَلَ عَلَى قَبْرِ أُمِّهِ، فَنَاجَى رَبَّهُ طَوِيلًا ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ بَكَى فَاشْتَدَّ بُكَاؤُهُ، وَبَكَى هَؤُلَاءِ لِبُكَائِهِ، وَقَالُوا: مَا بَكَى نَبِيُّ اللَّهِ بِهَذَا الْمَكَانِ إِلَّا وَقَدْ أُحْدِثَ فِي أُمَّتِهِ شَيْءٌ لَا تُطِيقُهُ. فَلَمَّا بَكَى هَؤُلَاءِ قَامَ فَرَجَعَ إِلَيْهِمْ، فَقَالَ: "مَا يُبْكِيكُمْ؟". قَالُوا: يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ، بَكَيْنَا لِبُكَائِكَ، فَقُلْنَا: لَعَلَّهُ أُحْدِثَ فِي أُمَّتِكَ شَيْءٌ لَا تُطِيقُهُ، قَالَ: "لَا وَقَدْ كَانَ بَعْضُهُ، وَلَكِنْ نَزَلْتُ عَلَى قَبْرِ أُمِّي فَدَعَوْتُ اللَّهَ أَنْ يَأْذَنَ لِي فِي شَفَاعَتِهَا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، فَأَبَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَأْذَنَ لِي، فَرَحِمْتُهَا وَهِيَ أُمِّي، فَبَكَيْتُ، ثُمَّ جَاءَنِي جِبْرِيلُ فَقَالَ: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اسْتِغْفَارُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ إِلَّا عَنْ مَوْعِدَةٍ وَعَدَهَا إِيَّاهُ فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ أَنَّهُ عَدُوٌّ لِلَّهِ تَبَرَّأَ مِنْهُ﴾ فَتَبَرَّأْ أَنْتَ مِنْ أُمِّكَ، كَمَا تَبَرَّأَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ مِنْ أَبِيهِ، فَرَحِمْتُهَا وَهِيَ أُمِّي، وَدَعَوْتُ رَبِّي أَنْ يَرْفَعَ عَنْ أُمَّتِي أَرْبَعًا، فَرَفَعَ عَنْهُمُ اثْنَتَيْنِ، وَأَبَى أَنْ يَرْفَعَ عَنْهُمُ اثْنَتَيْنِ: دَعَوْتُ رَبِّي أَنْ يَرْفَعَ عَنْهُمُ الرَّجْمَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْغَرَقَ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ، وَأَلَّا يُلْبِسَهُمْ شِيَعًا، وَأَلَّا يُذِيقَ بَعْضَهُمْ بَأْسَ بَعْضٍ، فَرَفَعَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمُ الرَّجْمَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ، وَالْغَرَقَ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ، وَأَبَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَرْفَعَ عَنْهُمُ الْقَتْلَ وَالْهَرْجَ". وَإِنَّمَا عَدَلَ إِلَى قَبْرِ أُمِّهِ لِأَنَّهَا كَانَتْ مَدْفُونَةً تَحْتَ كَدَاءٍ [[في ت، أ: "كذا وكذا"، وفي ك: "كذا وكذا".]] وَكَانَتْ عُسْفَانُ لَهُمْ. [[المعجم الكبير (١١/٣٧٤).]]

وَهَذَا حَدِيثٌ غَرِيبٌ وَسِيَاقٌ عَجِيبٌ، وَأَغْرَبُ مِنْهُ وَأَشَدُّ نَكَارَةً مَا رَوَاهُ الْخَطِيبُ الْبَغْدَادِيُّ فِي كِتَابِ "السَّابِقِ وَاللَّاحِقِ" بِسَنَدٍ مَجْهُولٍ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ فِي حَدِيثٍ فِيهِ قِصَّةُ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَحْيَا أُمَّهُ فَآمَنَتْ ثُمَّ عَادَتْ. [[ساقه القرطبي في: التذكرة في أحوال الموتى وأمور الآخرة (ص ١٦) وقال: خرّجه أبو بكر أحمد بن علي الخطيب في كتاب السابق واللاحق، وأبو حفص عمر بن شاهين في الناسخ والمنسوخ، ولا يصح الحديث، لمخالفته ما في صحيح مسلم برقم (٩٧٦) من حديث أبي هريرة قال: زار النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قبر أمه فبكى وأبكى من حوله. فقال: "استأذنت ربي في أن أستغفر لها فلم يأذن لي، واستأذنته في أن أزور قبرها فأذن لي، فزوروا القبور فإنها تذكر الموت"، ولضعف إسناده.]] وَكَذَلِكَ مَا رَوَاهُ السُّهَيْلِيُّ فِي "الرَّوْضِ" بِسَنَدٍ فِيهِ جَمَاعَةٌ مَجْهُولُونَ: أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَحْيَا لَهُ أَبَاهُ وَأُمَّهُ [[في ت: "وآمنة".]] فَآمَنَا بِهِ. [[الروض الأنف (١/١١٣).]]

وَقَدْ قَالَ الْحَافِظُ ابْنُ دِحْيَةَ: [هَذَا الْحَدِيثُ مَوْضُوعٌ يَرُدُّهُ الْقُرْآنُ وَالْإِجْمَاعُ، قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَلَا الَّذِينَ يَمُوتُونَ وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ﴾ [النِّسَاءِ: ١٨]. وَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْقُرْطُبِيُّ: إِنَّ مُقْتَضَى هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ. . . وَرَدَّ عَلَى ابْنِ دِحْيَةَ] [[زيادة من ت، ك، أ.]] فِي هَذَا الِاسْتِدْلَالِ بِمَا حَاصِلُهُ: أَنَّ هَذِهِ حَيَاةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ، كَمَا رَجَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ بَعْدَ غَيْبُوبَتِهَا فَصَلَّى عَلِيٌّ الْعَصْرَ. قَالَ الطَّحَاوِيُّ: وَهُوَ [حَدِيثٌ] [[زيادة من ت، ك، أ.]] ثَابِتٌ، يَعْنِي: حَدِيثَ الشَّمْسِ.

قَالَ الْقُرْطُبِيُّ: فَلَيْسَ إِحْيَاؤُهُمَا يَمْتَنِعُ عَقْلًا وَلَا شَرْعًا، قَالَ: وَقَدْ سَمِعْتُ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَحْيَا عَمَّهُ أَبَا طَالِبٍ، فَآمَنَ بِهِ. [[التذكرة (ص ١٧). وَمَا ذَكَرَهُ الْقُرْطُبِيُّ لَا يَصِحُّ؛ أَمَّا إِحْيَاؤُهُمَا وَإِيمَانُهُمَا فَلَا يَمْتَنِعُ عَقْلًا، وَأَمَّا شَرْعًا فَقَدْ جَاءَ فِي صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَنَسٍ؛ أَنَّ رَجُلًا قَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، أَيْنَ أَبِي؟ قَالَ: "فِي النَّارِ"، فَلَمَّا قَفَّى دَعَاهُ وَقَالَ: "إِنَّ أَبِي وَأَبَاكَ فِي النَّارِ". وَمَنَعَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مِنَ الِاسْتِغْفَارِ لِأُمِّهِ، وَهَذَا الْمَنْعُ مُتَأَخِّرٌ، بِخِلَافِ مَنْ قَالَ بِأَنَّ مَا جَاءَ فِي أَنَّهُمَا - أَيْ أَبَوَيْهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ - فِي النَّارِ مَنْسُوخٌ بِحَدِيثِ عَائِشَةَ الَّذِي رَوَاهُ الْخَطِيبُ، فَإِنَّ دَعْوَى النَّسْخِ غَيْرُ قَائِمَةٍ وَلَا تُعْتَمَدُ عَلَى أَصْلٍ. وَأَمَّا قَوْلُ الْقُرْطُبِيِّ بِأَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَحْيَا عَمَّهُ أَبَا طَالِبٍ. . . إِلَخ، فَهَذَا أَبْعَدُ عَنِ الصِّحَّةِ؛ فَإِنَّ فِي الصَّحِيحِ مِنْ حَدِيثِ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ؛ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ شَفَعَ لَهُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ فَهُوَ فِي النَّارِ يُجْعَلُ ضَحْضَاحٌ مِنْ نَارٍ تَحْتَ قَدَمَيْهِ يَغْلِي مِنْهَا دِمَاغُهُ، وَفِي صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ مَرْفُوعًا: "أَهْوَنُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ عَذَابًا أَبُو طَالِبٍ". فَمَنْ يَكُونُ فِي النَّارِ كَيْفَ يُقَالُ: إِنَّهُ آمَنَ فِي قَبْرِهِ؟!]] قُلْتُ: وَهَذَا كُلُّهُ مُتَوَقِّفٌ عَلَى صِحَّةِ الْحَدِيثِ، فَإِذَا صَحَّ فَلَا مَانِعَ مِنْهُ [[وَقَدْ رَأَيْتَ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ لَا يَصِحُّ. وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.]] وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.

وَقَالَ الْعَوْفِيُّ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ فِي قَوْلِهِ: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ الْآيَةَ، فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرَ لِأُمِّهِ، فَنَهَاهُ اللَّهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ [[في ت، أ: "عنه".]] فَقَالَ: "فَإِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ خَلِيلَ اللَّهِ اسْتَغْفَرَ لِأَبِيهِ"، فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اسْتِغْفَارُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ إِلَّا عَنْ مَوْعِدَةٍ وَعَدَهَا إِيَّاهُ﴾ [[في ت: "إياها".]] الْآيَةَ.

وَقَالَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي طَلْحَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، فِي هَذِهِ الْآيَةِ: كَانُوا يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لَهُمْ، حَتَّى نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الْآيَةُ، فَلَمَّا [نَزَلَتْ [[في أ: "أنزلت".]] أَمْسَكُوا عَنِ الِاسْتِغْفَارِ لِأَمْوَاتِهِمْ، وَلَمْ يَنْهَهُمْ أَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْأَحْيَاءِ حَتَّى يَمُوتُوا]. [[زيادة من ت، ك، أ.]] ثُمَّ أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اسْتِغْفَارُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ﴾ الْآيَةَ.

وَقَالَ قَتَادَةُ فِي هَذِهِ الْآيَةِ: ذُكِرَ لَنَا أَنَّ رِجَالًا مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ قَالُوا: يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ، إِنَّ مِنْ آبَائِنَا مَنْ كَانَ يُحْسِنُ الْجِوَارَ، وَيَصِلُ الْأَرْحَامَ، وَيَفُكُّ الْعَانِيَ، وَيُوفِي بِالذِّمَمِ؛ أَفَلَا نَسْتَغْفِرُ لَهُمْ؟ قَالَ: فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: "بَلَى، وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لَأَسْتَغْفِرُ لِأَبِي كَمَا اسْتَغْفَرَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ". فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ حَتَّى بَلَغَ: ﴿الْجَحِيمِ﴾. ثُمَّ عَذَرَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ، فَقَالَ: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اسْتِغْفَارُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ إِلَّا عَنْ مَوْعِدَةٍ وَعَدَهَا إِيَّاهُ فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ أَنَّهُ عَدُوٌّ لِلَّهِ تَبَرَّأَ مِنْهُ﴾. قَالَ: وَذُكِرَ لَنَا أَنَّ نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ قَالَ: "أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ كَلِمَاتٌ، فَدَخَلْنَ فِي أُذُنِي وَوَقَرْنَ فِي قَلْبِي: أُمِرْتُ أَلَّا أَسْتَغْفِرَ لِمَنْ مَاتَ مُشْرِكًا، وَمَنْ أَعْطَى فَضْلَ مَالِهِ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَهُ، وَمَنْ أَمْسَكَ فَهُوَ شَرٌّ لَهُ، وَلَا يَلُومُ اللَّهُ عَلَى كَفَافٍ".

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 9, verses 113–114 (part 2 of 2)

Al-Thawri narrated from al-Shaybani, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A Jewish man died, and he had a Muslim son who did not go out with him (to the funeral). This was mentioned to Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "It was incumbent upon him to walk with him and bury him, and to pray that he be guided to righteousness for as long as he was alive. When he died, he should have left him to his own affair." Then he recited: ﴿The prayer for forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him.﴾ He did not supplicate for him.

[I say:] This is supported by what Abu Dawud and others narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "When Abu Talib died, I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, your uncle, the misguided old man, has died.' He said: 'Go and bury him, and do not do anything until you come to me.'" And he mentioned the rest of the hadith.[1]

It is narrated that when the funeral of his uncle Abu Talib passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Kinship has been joined to you, O uncle."[2]

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: "I would not abandon the funeral prayer for anyone from the people of the qiblah (those who face the Ka'bah in prayer), even if she were a pregnant Abyssinian woman from fornication, because I have not heard that Allah forbade the prayer except for the polytheists. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists...﴾"

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn WakI', from his father, from 'Isma ibn Zamil, from his father, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: "May Allah have mercy on a man who asks forgiveness for Abu Hurayrah and his mother." I said: "And for his father?" He said: "No. My father died a polytheist."[3]

* *

His saying: ﴿But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Ibrahim continued to ask forgiveness for his father until he died. When it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him." In another narration: "When he died, it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah."

Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah and others said the same, may Allah have mercy on them.

'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: On the Day of Resurrection, Ibrahim will disassociate himself from him when he meets his father, and on his father's face will be dust and darkness. He will say: "O Ibrahim, I used to disobey you, but today I will not disobey you." Ibrahim will say: "My Lord, did You not promise me that You would not disgrace me on the Day they are raised? What disgrace is greater than my father being far from mercy?" It will be said: "Look behind you," and he will look and see a smeared *dhīkh*, meaning he has been transformed into a hyena (*ḍib'ān*). Then he will be dragged by its legs and thrown into the Fire.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was *awwāh*, forbearing.﴾ Sufyan al-Thawri and others narrated from 'Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that he said: "The *awwāh* is the one who supplicates much (*al-da''ā'*)." This is also narrated through other chains from Ibn Mas'ud.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Muthanna narrated to me: al-Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us: 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram narrated to us: Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Had, who said: "While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting, a man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the *awwāh*?' He said: 'The one who humbles himself in supplication (*al-mutaḍarri'*).' He said: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was *awwāh*, forbearing.﴾"[4]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Ibn al-Mubarak, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, with the same chain, and he said: "*Al-mutaḍarri'* is the one who supplicates (*al-da''ā'*)."

Al-Thawri narrated from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim al-Batin, from Abu al-'Ubaydayn, that he asked Ibn Mas'ud about the *awwāh*, and he said: "It is the merciful (*al-raḥīm*)."

Mujahid, Abu Maysarah 'Amr ibn Shurahbil, al-Hasan al-Basri and Qatadah said the same: that it is the merciful, i.e., toward the servants of Allah.

Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Khalid, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The *awwāh* is the one who is certain (*al-mūqin*) in the language of Abyssinia." Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas similarly, that it is the one who is certain. Mujahid and al-Dahhak said the same. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah and Mujahid narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "The *awwāh* is the believer." 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah added from him: "The believer who repents often (*al-tawwāb*)." Al-'Awfi narrated from him: "It is the believer in the language of Abyssinia." Ibn Jurayj likewise said: "It is the believer in the language of Abyssinia."

Ahmad said: Musa narrated to us: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from al-Harith ibn Yazid, from 'Ali ibn Rabah, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to a man called "Dhu al-Bijadayn": "Indeed, he is an *awwāh*." That was because he was a man who remembered Allah often, and who recited the Qur'an and raised his voice in supplication.[5]

Ibn Jarir also narrated it.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Sha'bi said: The *awwāh* is the one who glorifies Allah (*al-musabbiḥ*). Ibn Wahb narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, from Abu al-Zahiriyyah, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "None remains consistent in the voluntary Duha prayer except an *awwāh*."[6] Shufayy ibn Mani' narrated from Ayyub: "The *awwāh* is the one who, when he remembers his sins, asks forgiveness for them."

From Mujahid: "The *awwāh* is the one who is vigilant and fearful, who commits a sin in secret and then repents of it in secret."

Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated all of this.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn WakI' narrated to us: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from al-Hakam, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim ibn Yannaq: "A man used to remember Allah often and glorify Him, and this was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'Indeed, he is an *awwāh*.'"[7]

He also said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Ibn Yaman narrated to us: al-Minhal ibn Khalifah narrated to us, from Hajjaj ibn Artah, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) buried a dead man and said: "May Allah have mercy on you, for indeed you were an *awwāhan*!" meaning: one who recites the Qur'an much.[8]

Shu'bah narrated from Abu Yunus al-Bahili, who said: "I heard a man in Makkah, whose origin was Roman and who was a storyteller, narrating from Abu Dharr, who said: 'A man used to circumambulate the Sacred House and say in his supplication: "*Awwih, awwih*" (an expression of grief). This was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Indeed, he is an *awwāh*." Abu Dharr said: "I went out one night, and there was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) burying that man at night, with a lamp with him."'"

This is a *gharīb* hadith (one transmitted through a single chain, so its transmission is singular), narrated by Ibn Jarir, who also transmitted it in a *mashsha* (a dubious manner).[9]

It is narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar that he said: "*Inna Ibrahima la-awwāh*": he used to say, whenever he mentioned the Fire, "*Awwih* from the Fire!"

Ibn Jurayj said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was *awwāh*﴾: he was a jurist (*faqīh*)."

The Imam al-'Alam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: The most preferable of the opinions is the view of the one who said that it is the one who supplicates much (*al-da''ā'*), and this fits the context. When Allah the Exalted mentioned that Ibrahim only asked forgiveness for his father because of a promise he had made to him, and that Ibrahim was one who supplicated much and was forbearing toward those who wronged him and caused him harm, he asked forgiveness for his father despite his father's severe harm to him, in His saying: ﴿Do you reject my gods, O Ibrahim? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so leave me for a long time. He said: Peace be upon you. I will ask my Lord to forgive you; indeed He is ever gracious to me.﴾ [Maryam: 46–47]. So he was forbearing toward him despite his harm, and he prayed for him and asked forgiveness for him. For this reason, the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was *awwāh*, forbearing.﴾[10]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 9, verses 118–119:

Imam Ahmad said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Ibn Akhi al-Zuhri Muhammad ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from his paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik informed me that Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, who was the guide of Ka'b from among his sons when Ka'b went blind, said: I heard Ka'b ibn Malik relate his account of when he stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the expedition to Tabuk. Ka'b ibn Malik said: "I never stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in any expedition he undertook except the expedition to Tabuk, except that I had stayed behind from the expedition of Badr, and no one who stayed behind from it was blamed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out only seeking the caravan of Quraysh, until Allah brought them together with their enemy without a prior appointment. I was present with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of 'Aqabah, when we pledged together to Islam, and I would not want to exchange it for the presence at Badr, although Badr is more mentioned among the people and more famous." He said: "The account of my staying behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the expedition to Tabuk is that I had never been stronger or better off than when I stayed behind from him on that expedition. By Allah, I had never before gathered two riding beasts, but I gathered two for that expedition. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rarely wanted an expedition he undertook without concealing it by mentioning another destination, until that expedition, which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) undertook in intense heat, facing a long journey and a desert wasteland, and facing a great enemy. So he made the matter clear to the Muslims that they might prepare for their enemy, and he informed them of the direction he intended. The Muslims with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were numerous, and no register (diwan, a record book) gathered them." Ka'b said: "Few men wished to stay behind without thinking that it would remain hidden from him, as long as no revelation from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had come down concerning it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) undertook that expedition when the fruits had ripened and the shade was pleasant, and I was inclined toward it." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prepared for it, and the believers with him prepared too. I began going out in the morning to prepare with them, but I would return without having accomplished anything of my provisions, and I would say to myself: 'I am able to do that whenever I want.' This kept on with me until the people were seized with earnestness, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out in the morning while the Muslims were with him, and I had not accomplished anything of my provisions. I said: 'I will prepare the provisions a day or two after him, then I will catch up with him.' I went out after they had departed to prepare, but I returned without accomplishing anything of my provisions. Then I went out again and returned without accomplishing anything. This kept on with me until they hurried on and the expedition had passed me by. I resolved to set out and catch up with them, and I wish I had done so, but that was not decreed for me. So when I went out among the people after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had left, I walked among them, and it grieved me that I saw none but a man accused of hypocrisy, or a man whom Allah had excused. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not mention me until he reached Tabuk, and while he was sitting among the people at Tabuk he said: 'What did Ka'b ibn Malik do?' A man from Banu Salamah said: 'O Messenger of Allah, his two cloaks and his admiration of his own sides have held him back.' Mu'adh ibn Jabal said to him: 'What an evil thing you have said! By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we know nothing of him but good!' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent. Ka'b ibn Malik said: "When it reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had turned back from Tabuk on his return, my distress overwhelmed me. I began to think of falsehood and to say: 'By what can I escape his displeasure tomorrow?' I sought help in that from every man of judgment among my family. When it was said that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had come near, arriving, falsehood departed from me, and I knew that I would never be saved from it by anything at all. So I resolved to be truthful. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in the morning, and whenever he returned from a journey he would begin with the mosque and pray two rak'ahs in it, then sit down for the people. When he did that, those who had stayed behind came to him and began to make excuses to him and swear oaths to him—they were eighty-some men—and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted their outward profession, asked forgiveness for them, and left their inner states to Allah, Exalted. Then I came, and when I greeted him he smiled a smile of one who is angry, then said to me: 'Come here.' I came walking until I sat before him. He said to me: 'What kept you back? Had you not bought your mount?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if I were sitting before anyone other than you among the people of this world, I would think I could escape his displeasure with an excuse. I have indeed been given eloquence in argument, but by Allah, I know that if I tell you today a false story to win your approval, Allah will soon make you angry with me. And if I tell you the truth, about which you will be displeased with me, I hope for the best outcome from Allah, Mighty and Majestic in that. By Allah, I had no excuse. By Allah, I was never stronger or better off than when I stayed behind from you.'" He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'As for this man, he has spoken the truth. Stand up until Allah decides concerning you.'" So I stood up, and some men from Banu Salamah hastened after me and followed me. They said to me: "By Allah, we did not know you to have committed any sin before this. You were unable to make an excuse to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) like the excuses the others who stayed behind made, for the Messenger of Allah's seeking forgiveness for you would have sufficed you for your sin." He said: "By Allah, they did not cease rebuking me until I wanted to go back and call myself a liar." He said: "Then I said to them: 'Has anyone else met with what I have met?' They said: 'Yes, two men met with it along with you, and they said what you said, and they were told what you were told.' I said: 'Who are they?' They said: 'Murarah ibn al-Rabi' al-Amiri and Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqifi.' They mentioned to me two righteous men who had witnessed Badr, in whom there is a pattern for me." He said: "So I went on when they mentioned them to me. He (the narrator) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had forbidden the Muslims to speak to us, the three of us, from among those who stayed behind. So the people avoided us and changed toward us, until the earth became strange to me, not the earth I had known. We remained in that state for fifty nights. As for my two companions, they grew humble and stayed in their houses weeping, but as for me, I was the youngest and strongest of the people, so I used to attend the prayer with the Muslims and walk through the markets, but no one spoke to me. I would come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was in his gathering after the prayer and greet him, and I would say to myself: 'Did he move his lips to return my greeting or not?' Then I would pray near him and steal glances at him. When I turned to my prayer he would look at me, and when I turned toward him he would turn away. When this grew long for me, because of the shunning by the Muslims, I walked until I climbed over the wall of Abu Qatadah, who was my cousin and the dearest of people to me. I greeted him, but by Allah, he did not return my greeting. I said to him: 'O Abu Qatadah, I adjure you by Allah: do you know that I love Allah and His Messenger?' He was silent. I repeated it, and he was silent. I repeated it again, and he said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' Then my eyes overflowed, and I turned away until I climbed back over the wall. While I was walking in the market of Madinah, behold, a Nabataean (a Syrian farmer) from among the Nabat of Syria, who had come bringing food to sell in Madinah, was saying: 'Who will direct me to Ka'b ibn Malik?' So the people began pointing to me, until he came and handed me a letter from the king of Ghassan. I was a writer, so I read it, and in it was: 'To proceed: we have heard that your companion has treated you harshly, but Allah has not made you a place of humiliation or neglect, so join us and we will console you.' I said when I had read it: 'This too is one of the trials.' So I took the letter to the oven and set it alight, until forty nights of the fifty had passed. Then behold, a messenger of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to me and said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commands you to keep away from your wife.' I said: 'Shall I divorce her, or what should I do?' He said: 'No, just keep away from her and do not approach her.' He said: 'He sent the same message to my two companions.' So I said to my wife: 'Go to your family and stay with them until Allah decides this matter.' Then the wife of Hilal ibn Umayyah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, Hilal is a frail old man with no servant. Do you dislike it if I serve him?' He said: 'No, but let him not come near you.' She said: 'By Allah, he has no inclination toward anything, and by Allah, he has not ceased weeping since this matter of yours began until this day.' He said: "Some of my family said to me: 'If only you would ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permission regarding your wife, for he has permitted the wife of Hilal ibn Umayyah to serve him.' I said: 'By Allah, I will not ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permission regarding her, and I do not know what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would say if I asked him, while I am a young man.'" He said: "We remained after that for ten nights, so the fifty nights were completed for us from the time he forbade people to speak to us. Then I prayed the dawn prayer on the fiftieth morning on the roof of one of our houses. While I was sitting in the state Allah, Exalted, has described concerning us—my soul had become constricted for me and the earth had become confining for me despite its vastness—I heard a crier who had climbed onto Mount Sal' shouting at the top of his voice: 'O Ka'b ibn Malik, rejoice!' He said: 'I fell down prostrating, and I knew that relief had come. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had announced Allah's acceptance of our repentance when he prayed the dawn prayer. The people went off to give us good news, and messengers went off to my two companions with good news, and a rider galloped toward me, and a man from the tribe of Aslam ran and climbed the mountain, and the voice was faster than the horse.'" [Footnote: he is recorded as having said: "...and he will be written before Allah as a liar."]

Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in their Sahihs. [Source note: al-Musnad (1/384), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6094), and Sahih Muslim no. (2607).]

Shu'bah said, from Amr ibn Murrah, who heard Abu Ubaydah narrate from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Lying is not fitting in any form, whether seriously or jokingly. Recite if you wish: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and be among the truthful.﴾" [In another reading he recited it thus.] Then he said: "Do you find for anyone a concession in it?"

And from Abd Allah ibn Umar: ﴿Fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾, meaning with Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Companions.

Al-Dahhak said: "With Abu Bakr and Umar and their companions."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "If you want to be with the truthful, then you must adopt asceticism in this world and restrain yourself from harming the people of the religion."

Ka'b said: "Few men wished to stay behind without thinking that it would remain hidden from him, as long as no revelation from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had come down concerning it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) undertook that expedition when the fruits had ripened and the shade was pleasant, and I was inclined toward it." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prepared for it, and the believers with him prepared too. I began going out in the morning to prepare with them, but I would return without having accomplished anything of my provisions, and I would say to myself: 'I am able to do that whenever I want.' This kept on with me until the people were seized with earnestness, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out in the morning while the Muslims were with him, and I had not accomplished anything of my provisions. I said: 'I will prepare the provisions a day or two after him, then I will catch up with him.' I went out after they had departed to prepare, but I returned without accomplishing anything of my provisions. Then I went out again and returned without accomplishing anything. This kept on with me until they hurried on and the expedition had passed me by. I resolved to set out and catch up with them, and I wish I had done so, but that was not decreed for me. So when I went out among the people after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had left, I walked among them, and it grieved me that I saw none but a man accused of hypocrisy, or a man whom Allah had excused. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not mention me until he reached Tabuk, and while he was sitting among the people at Tabuk he said: 'What did Ka'b ibn Malik do?' A man from Banu Salamah said: 'O Messenger of Allah, his two cloaks and his admiration of his own sides have held him back.' Mu'adh ibn Jabal said to him: 'What an evil thing you have said! By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we know nothing of him but good!' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent. Ka'b ibn Malik said: "When it reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had turned back from Tabuk on his return, my distress overwhelmed me. I began to think of falsehood and to say: 'By what can I escape his displeasure tomorrow?' I sought help in that from every man of judgment among my family. When it was said that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had come near, arriving, falsehood departed from me, and I knew that I would never be saved from it by anything at all. So I resolved to be truthful. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in the morning, and whenever he returned from a journey he would begin with the mosque and pray two rak'ahs in it, then sit down for the people. When he did that, those who had stayed behind came to him and began to make excuses to him and swear oaths to him—they were eighty-some men—and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted their outward profession, asked forgiveness for them, and left their inner states to Allah, Exalted. Then I came, and when I greeted him he smiled a smile of one who is angry, then said to me: 'Come here.' I came walking until I sat before him. He said to me: 'What kept you back? Had you not bought your mount?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if I were sitting before anyone other than you among the people of this world, I would think I could escape his displeasure with an excuse. I have indeed been given eloquence in argument, but by Allah, I know that if I tell you today a false story to win your approval, Allah will soon make you angry with me. And if I tell you the truth, about which you will be displeased with me, I hope for the best outcome from Allah, Mighty and Majestic in that. By Allah, I had no excuse. By Allah, I was never stronger or better off than when I stayed behind from you.'" He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'As for this man, he has spoken the truth. Stand up until Allah decides concerning you.'" So I stood up, and some men from Banu Salamah hastened after me and followed me. They said to me: "By Allah, we did not know you to have committed any sin before this. You were unable to make an excuse to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) like the excuses the others who stayed behind made, for the Messenger of Allah's seeking forgiveness for you would have sufficed you for your sin." He said: "By Allah, they did not cease rebuking me until I wanted to go back and call myself a liar." He said: "Then I said to them: 'Has anyone else met with what I have met?' They said: 'Yes, two men met with it along with you, and they said what you said, and they were told what you were told.' I said: 'Who are they?' They said: 'Murarah ibn al-Rabi' al-Amiri and Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqifi.' They mentioned to me two righteous men who had witnessed Badr, in whom there is a pattern for me." He said: "So I went on when they mentioned them to me. He (the narrator) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had forbidden the Muslims to speak to us, the three of us, from among those who stayed behind. So the people avoided us and changed toward us, until the earth became strange to me, not the earth I had known. We remained in that state for fifty nights. As for my two companions, they grew humble and stayed in their houses weeping, but as for me, I was the youngest and strongest of the people, so I used to attend the prayer with the Muslims and walk through the markets, but no one spoke to me. I would come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was in his gathering after the prayer and greet him, and I would say to myself: 'Did he move his lips to return my greeting or not?' Then I would pray near him and steal glances at him. When I turned to my prayer he would look at me, and when I turned toward him he would turn away. When this grew long for me, because of the shunning by the Muslims, I walked until I climbed over the wall of Abu Qatadah, who was my cousin and the dearest of people to me. I greeted him, but by Allah, he did not return my greeting. I said to him: 'O Abu Qatadah, I adjure you by Allah: do you know that I love Allah and His Messenger?' He was silent. I repeated it, and he was silent. I repeated it again, and he said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' Then my eyes overflowed, and I turned away until I climbed back over the wall. While I was walking in the market of Madinah, behold, a Nabataean (a Syrian farmer) from among the Nabat of Syria, who had come bringing food to sell in Madinah, was saying: 'Who will direct me to Ka'b ibn Malik?' So the people began pointing to me, until he came and handed me a letter from the king of Ghassan. I was a writer, so I read it, and in it was: 'To proceed: we have heard that your companion has treated you harshly, but Allah has not made you a place of humiliation or neglect, so join us and we will console you.' I said when I had read it: 'This too is one of the trials.' So I took the letter to the oven and set it alight, until forty nights of the fifty had passed. Then behold, a messenger of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to me and said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commands you to keep away from your wife.' I said: 'Shall I divorce her, or what should I do?' He said: 'No, just keep away from her and do not approach her.' He said: 'He sent the same message to my two companions.' So I said to my wife: 'Go to your family and stay with them until Allah decides this matter.' Then the wife of Hilal ibn Umayyah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, Hilal is a frail old man with no servant. Do you dislike it if I serve him?' He said: 'No, but let him not come near you.' She said: 'By Allah, he has no inclination toward anything, and by Allah, he has not ceased weeping since this matter of yours began until this day.' He said: "Some of my family said to me: 'If only you would ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permission regarding your wife, for he has permitted the wife of Hilal ibn Umayyah to serve him.' I said: 'By Allah, I will not ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permission regarding her, and I do not know what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would say if I asked him, while I am a young man.'" He said: "We remained after that for ten nights, so the fifty nights were completed for us from the time he forbade people to speak to us. Then I prayed the dawn prayer on the fiftieth morning on the roof of one of our houses. While I was sitting in the state Allah, Exalted, has described concerning us—my soul had become constricted for me and the earth had become confining for me despite its vastness—I heard a crier who had climbed onto Mount Sal' shouting at the top of his voice: 'O Ka'b ibn Malik, rejoice!' He said: 'I fell down prostrating, and I knew that relief had come. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had announced Allah's acceptance of our repentance when he prayed the dawn prayer. The people went off to give us good news, and messengers went off to my two companions with good news, and a rider galloped toward me, and a man from the tribe of Aslam ran and climbed the mountain, and the voice was faster than the horse.'" [Footnote: he is recorded as having said: "...and he will be written before Allah as a liar."]

Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in their Sahihs. [Source note: al-Musnad (1/384), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6094), and Sahih Muslim no. (2607).]

Shu'bah said, from Amr ibn Murrah, who heard Abu Ubaydah narrate from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Lying is not fitting in any form, whether seriously or jokingly. Recite if you wish: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and be among the truthful.﴾" [In another reading he recited it thus.] Then he said: "Do you find for anyone a concession in it?"

And from Abd Allah ibn Umar: ﴿Fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾, meaning with Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Companions.

Al-Dahhak said: "With Abu Bakr and Umar and their companions."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "If you want to be with the truthful, then you must adopt asceticism in this world and restrain yourself from harming the people of the religion."

Almighty Allah rebukes those who stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during the expedition of Tabuk, from among the people of Madinah and the Arab tribes around it, and their preference for their own selves over sharing in his hardship in what befell them of toil. They diminished their own reward, because ﴿no thirst afflicts them﴾, that is: thirst; ﴿nor fatigue﴾, that is: weariness; ﴿nor hunger﴾, that is: famine. [[In T, A: "because he"]] ﴿Nor do they tread any path that enrages the disbelievers﴾, meaning: they do not descend to a place that terrifies their enemy. ﴿Nor do they inflict on the enemy any harm [or] gain any victory over him﴾, except that Allah records for them, through these deeds which are not within their power and which arise from their actions, righteous deeds and great reward. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost﴾, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We do not allow the reward of one who does good deeds to be lost﴾ [Al-Kahf: 30].

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 9, verse 121:

He, exalted is He, says: "Nor do these warriors spend any expense in the way of Allah, ﴿small or great﴾," meaning: little or much. "Nor do they cross a valley," meaning: in their march toward the enemy, "except that it is written for them," and He did not say here "by it" because these are actions proceeding from them; and for this He said: ﴿that Allah may reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾.

Amir al-Mu'minin Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, obtained from this noble verse a great share and a mighty portion, for he spent in this expedition magnificent expenses and abundant wealth, as 'Abd Allah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said:

Abu Musa al-'Anazi related to us, 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith related to us, Sakan ibn al-Mughirah related to me, al-Walid ibn Abi Hashim related to me, from Farqad Abi Talhah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Khabbab al-Sulami, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave a sermon and urged (people) to equip the army of hardship (Jaysh al-'Usrah). Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "On me are one hundred camels with their saddle-cloths and their pack-saddles." He said: Then he (the Prophet) urged again, and Uthman said: "On me are another hundred with their saddle-cloths and their pack-saddles." He said: Then he (the Prophet) descended one step from the pulpit and urged again, and Uthman ibn Affan said: "On me are another hundred with their saddle-cloths and their pack-saddles." He said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) moving his hand like this," shaking it. And 'Abd al-Samad extended his hand in the manner of one who is amazed: "Nothing will harm Uthman what he does after this." [[Zawa'id al-Musnad (4/75). Al-Tirmidhi related it in his Sunan under no. (3700) through the route of Sakan ibn al-Mughirah with it, and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith from this route; we do not know it except from the hadith of Sakan ibn al-Mughirah."]]

'Abd Allah also said: Harun ibn Ma'ruf related to us, Dhamrah related to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Shawdhab related to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim, from Kathir, the freedman of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah, who said: Uthman came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with one thousand dinars in his garment when the Prophet (ﷺ) was equipping the army of hardship. He said: He poured them into the lap of the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) began turning them over with his hand and saying: "Nothing will harm Ibn Affan what he does after today," repeating it several times. [[Zawa'id al-Musnad (5/63). Al-Tirmidhi related it in his Sunan under no. (3701) through the route of al-Hasan ibn Waqi' from Dhamrah ibn Rabi'ah with it, and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from this route."]]

Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿Nor do they cross a valley except that it is written for them﴾ to the end of the verse, said: No people increased in distance from their families in the way of Allah except that they increased in nearness to Allah.

This is an explanation from Allah, the Exalted, regarding what He intended by the call to go forth in the Battle of Tabuk, when the tribes were summoned to march with the Messenger. Some of the early scholars (al-salaf) held that it was obligatory for every Muslim to go forth whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ [al-Tawbah: 41], and He said: ﴿It was not fitting for the people of Madinah and those of the Bedouins around them to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah: 120]. They said: this was abrogated (naskh) by this verse.

It may be said: this is an explanation of what Allah, the Exalted, intended by the going forth of all the living, or a group from every tribe if they do not all go out, so that those who went out with the Messenger might gain understanding (yatafaqqahu) of what was revealed to him, and so that they might warn their people when they returned to them about the matter of the enemy. Thus both matters are combined for them in this: the going forth to assist, and after it, (the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, being present), the group that goes forth from the tribe is either for gaining understanding or for jihad, since it is a communal obligation (fard kifayah) upon the living.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding: ﴿The believers should not go forth all together﴾. He said: the believers should not all go forth together and leave the Prophet ﷺ alone. ﴿Why should not a group from every section of them go forth﴾: meaning a company ('usbah), meaning the raiding detachments (al-sarayā), and they should not set out except with his permission. When the detachments returned, and a revelation had come down after they had left, those who stayed behind learned it from the Prophet ﷺ, and they said: Allah has sent down a Qur'an to your Prophet, and we have learned it. So the detachments would remain and learn what Allah had revealed to their Prophet after them, and he would send out other detachments. This is His saying: ﴿so that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾, meaning: so that they may learn what Allah revealed to their Prophet, and so that they may teach the detachments when they return to them, ﴿so that they may be cautious﴾.

Mujahid said: this verse was revealed concerning some of the companions of Muhammad ﷺ who went out into the desert regions, and they obtained some kindness from the people and abundance of produce from which they benefited, and they called those whom they met to guidance. The people said to them: we see you have only left your companions and come to us. They felt some discomfort because of this, and they all came from the desert until they entered upon the Prophet ﷺ. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Why should not a group from every section of them go forth﴾, seeking good (yabtaghūna al-khayr), ﴿so that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾, and so that they may hear what is among the people and what Allah has revealed after them, ﴿and so that they may warn their people﴾, meaning all the people, ﴿when they return to them, so that they may be cautious﴾.

Qatadah said regarding this verse: this applies when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sends the armies. Allah commanded them not to leave his Prophet ﷺ alone, and a group remains with the Messenger of Allah to gain understanding in the religion, while another group sets out to call their people and warn them of the punishments of Allah upon those who passed before them.

Al-Dahhak said: when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to fight in person, it was not lawful for any of the Muslims to remain behind from him, except those with valid excuses. And when he stayed (in Madinah), and the detachments went out, it was not lawful for them to set out except with his permission. So when a man went out with a detachment and then a Qur'an was revealed after him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would recite it to his companions who remained with him. When the detachment returned, those who had stayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say to them: Allah has sent down a Qur'an to His Prophet after you. Then they would recite it to them and instruct them in the religion. This is His saying: ﴿The believers should not go forth all together﴾, meaning, when the Messenger of Allah remains (in Madinah): it is not proper for the Muslims to all go forth while the Prophet of Allah ﷺ is seated. Rather, when the Prophet of Allah stays behind, the detachments go out, and the greater part of the people remain with him.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿The believers should not go forth all together﴾, that it is not about jihad. Rather, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against Mudar with years of drought, their lands became barren, and a tribe from among them would come, all of them, until they arrived in Madinah in hardship, professing Islam while they were liars. They then pressed upon the companions of the Prophet ﷺ and burdened them. So Allah revealed, informing His Messenger that they were not believers, and the Messenger of Allah sent them back to their clans and warned their people not to do what they had done. This is His saying: ﴿and so that they may warn their people when they return to them, so that they may be cautious﴾.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding this verse: from every Arab clan a band would set out and come to the Prophet ﷺ, asking him about what they wanted of the matters of their religion, and gaining understanding in their religion. They would say to the Prophet of Allah: what do you command us to do? And inform us what we should say to our clans when we return and go to them. He said: the Prophet of Allah would command them to obey Allah and obey His Messenger, and he would send them to their people with (instructions regarding) prayer and zakah. When they came to their people they would call out: whoever has embraced Islam is one of us. And they would warn them, to the extent that a man would separate from his father and mother. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would inform them and warn their people, and when they returned to them, they would call them to Islam, warn them of the Fire, and give them glad tidings of Paradise.

Ikrimah said: when this verse was revealed, ﴿If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾ [al-Tawbah: 39], and ﴿It was not fitting for the people of Madinah and those of the Bedouins around them to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah: 120], the hypocrites said: the people of the desert who remained behind from Muhammad and did not go forth with him have perished. Some of the companions of the Prophet ﷺ had gone out to the desert to their people, to instruct them in the religion. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿The believers should not go forth all together. Why should not a group from every section of them go forth﴾, to the end of the verse, and there was revealed: ﴿And those who dispute concerning Allah after He has been responded to﴾ [al-Shura: 16].

Al-Hasan al-Basri said regarding: ﴿Why should not a group from every section of them go forth, so that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾: so that those who went out may gain understanding through what Allah causes them of victory over the polytheists, and support, and so that they may warn their people when they return to them.

God commanded the believers to fight the disbelievers, first the nearest, then the next nearest, according to their proximity to the territory of Islam (*hawzat al-Islam*). Therefore the Messenger of God (ﷺ) began by fighting the polytheists in the Arabian Peninsula (*Jazirat al-'Arab*). When he had finished with them, and God had granted him the conquest of Makkah, Madinah, al-Ta'if, Yemen, al-Yamamah, Hajar, Khaybar, Hadramawt, and other regions of the Arabian Peninsula, and people from all the tribes of the Arabs entered the religion of God in multitudes, he turned to fighting the People of the Book (*Ahl al-Kitab*). He prepared to invade the Romans, who were the nearest people to the Arabian Peninsula and the most deserving of being called to Islam because they were People of the Book. He reached Tabuk and then returned because of the hardship of the people, the drought of the land, and the straitened circumstances. That was in the ninth year of his Hijrah, peace be upon him. [[In T, K, and A: "al-nas" (the people).]] [[In A: "peace and blessings of God be upon him".]]

Then in the tenth year he occupied himself with his Hajj, the Farewell Pilgrimage (*Hajjat al-Wada'*). Then death overtook him, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him, eighty-one days after the Hajj, and God chose him for what He had with Him.

After him, his vizier, his companion, and his successor Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, took up the affair. The religion had inclined to a deviation that nearly caused it to stumble, but God strengthened it through him. He consolidated the foundations and firmly established the pillars. He brought back the runaway from the religion while he was humbled. He returned the people of apostasy (*ahl al-riddah*) to Islam, and took the zakat from those among the rabble who had withheld it. He made the truth clear to those who were ignorant of it, and he fulfilled what he had been charged with conveying from the Messenger. Then he began to equip the Islamic armies against the Romans, the worshippers of crosses, [[In A: "al-asnam" (the idols).]] and against the Persians, the worshippers of fire. God opened the lands through the blessing of his mission, humbled the pride of Chosroes and Caesar and of those among the servants who obeyed them, and spent their treasures in the way of God, just as the Messenger of God had informed.

The completion of the matter came at the hands of his appointed successor (*wasiyyuhu*) after him, and his designated heir, al-Faruq al-Awwab, the martyr of the prayer niche, Abu Hafs 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. Through him God humbled the noses of the disbelieving heretics, suppressed the tyrants and hypocrites, and gained control of the realms east and west. Treasuries of wealth were brought to him from all the regions, near and far, and he distributed them in the lawful manner and in the approved way.

Then, when he died a martyr after having lived praiseworthy, the Companions, from among the Muhajirun and the Ansar, agreed upon the caliphate of the Commander of the Believers [Abu 'Amr] [[Addition from T, K, A.]] 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, the martyr of the house. So Islam was clothed by his majesty in a complete robe of leadership. The conclusive proof of God was extended over the necks of the servants in all the regions, Islam appeared in the eastern and western parts of the earth, the word of God became supreme, and His religion prevailed. The Hanifite community (*al-ummah al-hanifiyyah*) attained from the enemies of God the ultimate of their aims. Whenever they conquered one nation, they moved on to the next, and then to the tyrannical and wicked peoples who followed them, in obedience to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, fight those disbelievers who are near to you﴾, and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and let them find in you harshness﴾ [i.e., and let the disbelievers find in you harshness against them in your fighting against them], for the complete believer is the one who is gentle toward his believing brother and stern toward his disbelieving enemy, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿So God will bring a people He loves and who love Him, humble toward the believers, mighty over the disbelievers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 54], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves﴾ [al-Fath: 29], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh with them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 73; al-Tahrim: 9]. And in the hadith: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I am the laughing one, the fighter", meaning: he is cheerful in the face of his friend, and a fighter against the head of his enemy.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And know that God is with the righteous﴾, meaning: fight the disbelievers, put your trust in God, and know that God is with you if you fear Him and obey Him.

And so it is with the matter: when the three generations, who are the best of this Ummah, were in the utmost uprightness and in carrying out obedience to God, the Exalted, they continued to prevail over their enemy, conquests were abundant, and the enemies remained in decline and loss. Then, when temptations, desires, and disputes arose among the kings, the enemies coveted the outlying regions of the lands and advanced toward them. They met no resistance, because the kings were occupied with one another. Then they advanced into the territory of Islam, taking many cities from the borders, and they did not cease until they seized much of the lands of Islam. Yet to God, glorified is He, belongs the command, before and after. Whenever a king from the kings of Islam arose, obeyed the commands of God, and put his trust in God, God opened the lands to him, and he recovered from the enemies in proportion to his devotion, and in accordance with what he possessed of God's guardianship (*wilayat Allah*). And God is the One asked and the One hoped in, that He enable the Muslims over the foreheads of His disbelieving enemies, and exalt His word in all the regions. Indeed He is Generous and Noble.

Allah the Exalted says: "And whenever a surah is sent down, among them [the hypocrites] are some who say, 'Which of you has had its faith increased by this?'" That is, some of them say to others, "Which of you has had his faith increased by this surah?" Allah the Exalted then says: "As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice."

This verse is among the strongest proofs that faith increases and decreases, which is the position of the majority of the earlier (salaf) and later (khalaf) leading scholars. Indeed, more than one scholar has related a consensus (ijma') on this. The matter has been discussed at length at the beginning of "Sharh al-Bukhari" (may Allah have mercy on him). "And as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it has added defilement to their defilement." That is, it has added doubt to their doubt and suspicion to their suspicion, as Allah the Exalted says: "And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss" [al-Isra' 17:82], and He says: "Say: It is, for those who believe, a guidance and a healing. But as for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them. Those are being called from a distant place" [Fussilat 41:44]. It is part of their wretchedness that what guides hearts becomes a cause of their misguidance and ruin, just as when a person of bad temperament is nourished with what nourishes others, it only increases him in corruption and deficiency.

Allah the Exalted says: "And whenever a surah is sent down, among them [the hypocrites] are some who say, 'Which of you has had its faith increased by this?'" It is part of their wretchedness that what guides hearts becomes a cause of their misguidance and ruin, just as when a person of bad temperament is nourished with what nourishes others, it only increases him in corruption and deficiency.

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah the Exalted says: "Do these hypocrites not see" ﴿that they are tested﴾, meaning: they are put to the test, ﴿every year once or twice, yet they do not repent, nor do they take heed﴾, meaning: they do not repent of their past sins, nor do they take heed regarding what lies ahead of their circumstances.

Mujahid said: they are tested with drought and hunger.

Qatadah said: with campaigning once or twice a year.

Sharik narrated from Jabir (he is al-Ju'fi), from Abu al-Duha, from Hudhayfah, regarding "Do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year?" He said: "We used to hear one or two lies every year, by which a large group of people would go astray." Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

And in a hadith from Anas: "The matter does not increase except in severity, and people do not increase except in stinginess, and there is no year except that the one after it is worse than it," I heard it from your Prophet (ﷺ).

[[This hadith is a composite of two hadiths from Anas. The first: narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. (4039), and by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (4/441), through Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Jundi, from Aban ibn Salih, from al-Hasan, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), marfu': "The matter does not increase except in severity, nor the world except in turning away, nor people except in stinginess, and the Hour will not come except upon the worst of people, and the Mahdi is none other than Isa ibn Maryam." It contains weakness and irregularity; the author, the Hafiz Ibn Kathir, pointed this out in al-Nihayah fi al-Fitan wa al-Malahim (1/32). As for the second: it is narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (7068), through Sufyan, from al-Zubayr ibn Adi, who said: "We came to Anas ibn Malik and complained to him about what we suffered at the hands of al-Hajjaj, and he said: 'Be patient, for there will not come upon you a time except that the one after it is worse than it, until you meet your Lord.' I heard it from your Prophet (ﷺ)."]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whenever a surah is revealed, some of them look at others, [saying], "Does anyone see you?" Then they turn away. Allah has turned their hearts away, because they are a people who do not comprehend﴾ — this is also a report about the hypocrites: that when a surah was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ﴿some of them looked at others﴾, meaning they glanced around, ﴿"Does anyone see you?" Then they turned away﴾, meaning they turned away from the truth and withdrew from it. This is their condition in religion: they do not stand firm before the truth, nor do they accept it or uphold it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder? As if they were startled donkeys fleeing from a lion﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 49–51], and He said: ﴿So what is wrong with those who disbelieve, rushing toward you from the right and from the left in groups?﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 36–37], meaning: what is wrong with these people that they scatter away from you to the right and to the left, fleeing from the truth and going off toward falsehood.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then they turned away; Allah turned their hearts﴾, it is like His saying: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff: 5]. ﴿Because they are a people who do not comprehend﴾, meaning: they do not understand Allah's address from Him, nor do they aim to understand it or desire it; rather they are in heedlessness of it and aversion to it, and for this reason they came to the state they came to.

(4039), and by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (4/441), through Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Jundi, from Aban ibn Salih, from al-Hasan, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), marfu': "The matter does not increase except in severity, nor the world except in turning away, nor people except in stinginess, and the Hour will not come except upon the worst of people, and the Mahdi is none other than Isa ibn Maryam." I heard it from your Prophet (ﷺ)."]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whenever a surah is revealed, some of them look at others, [saying], "Does anyone see you?" Then they turn away. * *

As for His saying: ﴿Then they turned away; Allah turned their hearts﴾, it is like His saying: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff: 5]. ﴿Because they are a people who do not comprehend﴾, meaning: they do not understand Allah's address from Him, nor do they aim to understand it or desire it; rather they are in heedlessness of it and aversion to it, and for this reason they came to the state they came to.

The Most High says, bestowing a favour upon the believers by sending them a Messenger from among themselves, meaning from their own kind and in their own language, as Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said: ﴿Our Lord, and raise up among them a Messenger from themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 129]. He also said: ﴿Indeed, Allah conferred favour upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran: 164]. And He said: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from yourselves﴾, meaning from among you and in your language, as Ja'far ibn Abi Talib said to al-Najashi, and al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah said to the messenger of Kisra: "Indeed, Allah has sent among us a Messenger from ourselves. We know his lineage, his description, his entrance and his exit, his truthfulness and his trustworthiness," and he mentioned the hadith.

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, concerning His saying ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from yourselves﴾: "Nothing of the births of the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance) befell him." And he (ﷺ) said: "I came forth from a marriage and did not come forth from illegitimate union (sifah)."

This has also been transmitted by another route, as al-Hafiz Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ramahurmuzi said in his book "al-Fasil bayn al-Rawi wal-Wa'i" (The Separator between the Narrator and the Retainer): Abu Ahmad Yusuf ibn Harun ibn Ziyad narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: "I testify concerning my father that he narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I came forth from a marriage and did not come forth from illegitimate union, from Adam until my father and mother bore me; nothing of the illegitimate unions of the Jahiliyyah touched me.'" [[In manuscripts T and A: "لم يصبني" ("did not befall me"); in manuscript K: "لم يمسسني" ("did not touch me").]] [[al-Fasil bayn al-Rawi wal-Wa'i (p. 136).
