* *

His saying ﴿It grieves him that you suffer﴾ means: that which causes his nation hardship and difficulty grieves him. For this reason it came in the hadith related through several routes from him that he said: "I was sent with the upright, tolerant monotheism (al-hanifiyyah al-samhah)." [[Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (5/266) from Abu Umamah, and (6/233) from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] And in the Sahih: "Indeed, this religion is ease." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 39, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] Its entire law is easy, tolerant, and complete, facilitated for whomever Allah the Most High makes it easy for.

﴿Concerned over you﴾ means: concerned for your guidance and for the arrival of benefit, both worldly and otherworldly, to you.

Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hadrami narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri' narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Fitr, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Abu Dharr, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) left us, and there was no bird flapping its wings in the air except that he reminded us of knowledge concerning it." He said: And he (ﷺ) said: "Nothing remains that brings one near to Paradise and distances one from the Fire except that it has been made clear to you." [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/155). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/265): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih except Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri', who is trustworthy."]]

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Fatan narrated to us, al-Sa'udi narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'd, from 'Abdah al-Nahdi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah does not forbid a prohibition except that He knows that someone among you will peer at it. Beware! I am holding you back by your waistbands from falling into the Fire, like the falling of moths or flies." [[al-Musnad (1/390).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was visited by two angels, in what the sleeper sees. One of them sat at his feet and the other at his head. The one at his feet said to the one at his head: "Strike a parable for this one and his nation." He said: "The parable of him and his nation is like the parable of a people travelling who reached the edge of a desert, having with them no provision with which to cross the desert, nor anything with which to return. While they were in this state, there came to them a man in a striped Yemeni garment, who said: 'Do you see, if I bring you to lush pastures and sparkling watering-holes, will you follow me?' They said: 'Yes.' So he led them off, and brought them to lush pastures and sparkling watering-holes; they ate, drank and grew fat. Then he said to them: 'Did I not find you in that condition, and did you not promise me that if I brought you to lush pastures and sparkling watering-holes you would follow me?' They said: 'Indeed.' He said: 'Truly, before you are pastures greener than these, and watering-holes more refreshing than these, so follow me.' A group said: 'He has spoken the truth; by Allah, we will certainly follow him.' And another group said: 'We are content with this, and we will remain upon it.'" [[al-Musnad (1/267). 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an is weak.]]

Al-Bazzar said: Salamah ibn Shabib and Ahmad ibn Mansur narrated to us, both saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that a Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) seeking his help in a matter. 'Ikrimah said: I think he said "concerning blood money." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave him something, then said: "Have I done well by you?" The Bedouin said: "No, nor have you done beautifully." Some of the Muslims became angry and wanted to rise against him, but the Messenger of Allah gestured to them: "Hold back." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and reached his house, he called the Bedouin into the house and said to him: "You came to us and asked us, so we gave you, and you said what you said." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) added something to what he had given him, and said: "Have I done well by you?" The Bedouin said: "Yes; may Allah reward you with good from your family and tribe." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You came to us asking us, so we gave you, and you said what you said, and my companions have something in their hearts against you because of that. So when you go out, say before them what you said before me, until it leaves their chests." He said: "Yes." When the Bedouin came, [the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)] said: "Indeed, your companion came to us asking us, so we gave him, and he said what he said; and we called him and gave him, and he claims that he is content. Is that so, O Bedouin?" The Bedouin said: "Yes; may Allah reward you with good from your family and tribe." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, my parable and the parable of this Bedouin is like the parable of a man who had a she-camel which bolted from him, so people pursued her but only increased her flight. The owner of the she-camel said to them: 'Leave me between myself and my she-camel, for I am gentler with her and more knowing of her.' So he approached her, took for her some of the dust of the earth, called her until she came and responded, and fastened her saddle on her. And indeed, if I had obeyed you when he said what he said, he would have entered the Fire." Then al-Bazzar said: "We do not know this to be narrated except through this route." [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2476 (Kashf al-Astar). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (9/15): "In it is Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Aban, who is abandoned (matruk)."]]

I say: It is weak because of the condition of Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Aban, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying ﴿toward the believers, Kind and Merciful﴾ is as He said: ﴿And lower your wing to those who follow you of the believers. And if they disobey you, say: "Indeed, I am free from what you do." And rely upon the Exalted in Might, the Merciful﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 215–217].

Thus He commanded him.

As for this noble verse, which is His saying ﴿But if they turn away﴾, meaning: if they turn away from what you have brought them of the great, pure, complete and comprehensive law, ﴿say: "Sufficient for me is Allah; there is no deity except Him. Upon Him I have relied."﴾ As He said: ﴿Lord of the East and the West; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as Disposer of affairs﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 9].

﴿And He is the Lord of the Great Throne﴾ means: He is the Owner and Creator of everything, for He is the Lord of the Great Throne, which is the ceiling of creation. All creatures, from the heavens and the earths and what is in them and between them, are subdued beneath the Throne by the power of Allah the Most High. His knowledge encompasses everything, His decree takes effect in everything, and He is Guardian over everything.

'Abd Allah ibn Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me, Bishr ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "The last verse of the Qur'an to be revealed was this verse: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from yourselves﴾ to the end of the surah." [[Zawa'id al-Musnad (5/117). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/36): "In it is 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, who is trustworthy but has poor memory, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy." I say: the imams have agreed on the weakness of 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an.]]

'Abd Allah ibn al-Imam Ahmad also said: Rawh ibn 'Abd al-Mu'min narrated to us, 'Umar ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him: that they collected the Qur'an into codices (masahif) during the caliphate of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. Men were writing, and Ubayy ibn Ka'b was dictating to them. When they reached this verse in the surah of Bara'ah (al-Tawbah): ﴿Then they turned away; Allah has turned their hearts away, because they are a people who do not understand﴾ [al-Tawbah: 127], they thought that this was the last of the Qur'an to be revealed. Ubayy ibn Ka'b said to them: "Indeed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to me two verses after it: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from yourselves, it grieves him that you suffer, concerned over you, toward the believers Kind and Merciful﴾" to: ﴿And He is the Lord of the Great Throne﴾. He said: "This is the last of what has been revealed of the Qur'an." He said: Thus it was concluded with what it was opened with, by Allah, there is no deity except Him, and that is His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25]. [[Zawa'id al-Musnad (5/134). Also gharib (strange).]]

Imam Ahmad said: 'Ali ibn Bahr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yahya ibn 'Abbad, from his father 'Abbad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: al-Harith ibn Khazamah came with these two verses from the end of Bara'ah: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from yourselves﴾ to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and said: "Who is with you in this?" He said: "I do not know. By Allah, I testify that I heard them from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I understood them and memorised them." 'Umar said: "And I testify that I heard them from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." Then he said: "If they were three verses, I would have made them a separate surah. So look for a surah of the Qur'an and place them in it." So they placed them at the end of Bara'ah. [[al-Musnad (1/199).]]

It has already been mentioned that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was the one who advised Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with them both, to collect the Qur'an, so he commanded Zayd ibn Thabit, who collected it. 'Umar used to attend them while they were writing that. In the Sahih it is reported that Zayd said: "I found the last verses of the surah Bara'ah with Khuzaymah ibn Thabit, or Abu Khuzaymah." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4679.]] And we have mentioned that a group of the Companions remembered that from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as Khuzaymah ibn Thabit did when he began to recite them, and Allah knows best.

And Abu Dawud related it from Yazid ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Razzaq ibn Umar (and he said: "he was among the trustworthy Muslims, among the devout worshippers"), from Mudrik ibn Sa'd (Yazid said: "a trustworthy shaykh"), from Yunus ibn Maysara, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', who said: "Whoever says, when he enters the morning and when he enters the evening: 'Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but Him. In Him I have placed my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne,' seven times, Allah will suffice him for whatever concerns him."[[In K: "what troubles him."]][[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 5081.]]

It was also related by Ibn 'Asakir in the biography of this Abd al-Razzaq ibn Umar, through the narration of Abu Zur'a al-Dimashqi, from him, from Abu Sa'd Mudrik ibn Abi Sa'd al-Fazari, from Yunus ibn Maysara ibn Halays, from Umm al-Darda', who said: I heard Abu al-Darda' say: "No servant says: 'Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but Him. In Him I have placed my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne,' seven times, whether he says it truthfully or falsely, but that Allah will suffice him for whatever he is concerned about."[[Tarikh Dimashq (10/291, manuscript edition).]]

This addition is strange. Then he related it in the biography of Abd al-Razzaq Abu Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Razzaq, from his grandfather Abd al-Razzaq ibn Umar, with its chain, and he raised it (to the Prophet), and mentioned the like of it with the addition.[[Tarikh Dimashq (10/312, manuscript edition).]] This is munkar (rejected), and Allah knows best.

The end of Surah Bara'ah, and all praise is due to Allah alone.[[Written in K: "On the fourteenth of Rabi' al-Awwal, in the year eighty, in the seventh year of the Prophet's migration (hijra). Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Mighty."]]

The Most High says, bestowing a favour upon the believers by sending them a Messenger from among themselves, meaning from their own kind and in their own language, as Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said: ﴿Our Lord, and raise up among them a Messenger from themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 129]. He also said: ﴿Indeed, Allah conferred favour upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran: 164]. They said: 'Yes.' So he led them off, and brought them to lush pastures and sparkling watering-holes; they ate, drank and grew fat. Then he said to them: 'Did I not find you in that condition, and did you not promise me that if I brought you to lush pastures and sparkling watering-holes you would follow me?' They said: 'Indeed.' He said: 'Truly, before you are pastures greener than these, and watering-holes more refreshing than these, so follow me.' A group said: 'He has spoken the truth; by Allah, we will certainly follow him.' And another group said: 'We are content with this, and we will remain upon it.'" [[al-Musnad (1/267). 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an is weak.]]

Al-Bazzar said: Salamah ibn Shabib and Ahmad ibn Mansur narrated to us, both saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that a Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) seeking his help in a matter. 'Ikrimah said: I think he said "concerning blood money." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave him something, then said: "Have I done well by you?" The Bedouin said: "No, nor have you done beautifully." Some of the Muslims became angry and wanted to rise against him, but the Messenger of Allah gestured to them: "Hold back." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and reached his house, he called the Bedouin into the house and said to him: "You came to us and asked us, so we gave you, and you said what you said." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) added something to what he had given him, and said: "Have I done well by you?" The Bedouin said: "Yes; may Allah reward you with good from your family and tribe." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You came to us asking us, so we gave you, and you said what you said, and my companions have something in their hearts against you because of that. So when you go out, say before them what you said before me, until it leaves their chests." He said: "Yes." When the Bedouin came, [the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)] said: "Indeed, your companion came to us asking us, so we gave him, and he said what he said; and we called him and gave him, and he claims that he is content. Is that so, O Bedouin?" The Bedouin said: "Yes; may Allah reward you with good from your family and tribe." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, my parable and the parable of this Bedouin is like the parable of a man who had a she-camel which bolted from him, so people pursued her but only increased her flight. The owner of the she-camel said to them: 'Leave me between myself and my she-camel, for I am gentler with her and more knowing of her.' So he approached her, took for her some of the dust of the earth, called her until she came and responded, and fastened her saddle on her. And indeed, if I had obeyed you when he said what he said, he would have entered the Fire." Then al-Bazzar said: "We do not know this to be narrated except through this route." [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2476 (Kashf al-Astar). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (9/15): "In it is Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Aban, who is abandoned (matruk)."]]

I say: It is weak because of the condition of Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Aban, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying ﴿toward the believers, Kind and Merciful﴾ is as He said: ﴿And lower your wing to those who follow you of the believers. And if they disobey you, say: "Indeed, I am free from what you do." And rely upon the Exalted in Might, the Merciful﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 215–217].

Thus He commanded him.

As for this noble verse, which is His saying ﴿But if they turn away﴾, meaning: if they turn away from what you have brought them of the great, pure, complete and comprehensive law, ﴿say: "Sufficient for me is Allah; there is no deity except Him. Upon Him I have relied."﴾ As He said: ﴿Lord of the East and the West; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as Disposer of affairs﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 9].

﴿And He is the Lord of the Great Throne﴾ means: He is the Owner and Creator of everything, for He is the Lord of the Great Throne, which is the ceiling of creation. All creatures, from the heavens and the earths and what is in them and between them, are subdued beneath the Throne by the power of Allah the Most High. His knowledge encompasses everything, His decree takes effect in everything, and He is Guardian over everything.

'Abd Allah ibn Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me, Bishr ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "The last verse of the Qur'an to be revealed was this verse: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from yourselves﴾ to the end of the surah." [[Zawa'id al-Musnad (5/117). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/36): "In it is 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, who is trustworthy but has poor memory, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy." I say: the imams have agreed on the weakness of 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an.]]

'Abd Allah ibn al-Imam Ahmad also said: Rawh ibn 'Abd al-Mu'min narrated to us, 'Umar ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him: that they collected the Qur'an into codices (masahif) during the caliphate of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. Men were writing, and Ubayy ibn Ka'b was dictating to them. When they reached this verse in the surah of Bara'ah (al-Tawbah): ﴿Then they turned away; Allah has turned their hearts away, because they are a people who do not understand﴾ [al-Tawbah: 127], they thought that this was the last of the Qur'an to be revealed. Ubayy ibn Ka'b said to them: "Indeed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to me two verses after it: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from yourselves, it grieves him that you suffer, concerned over you, toward the believers Kind and Merciful﴾" to: ﴿And He is the Lord of the Great Throne﴾. He said: "This is the last of what has been revealed of the Qur'an." He said: Thus it was concluded with what it was opened with, by Allah, there is no deity except Him, and that is His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25]. [[Zawa'id al-Musnad (5/134). Also gharib (strange).]]

Imam Ahmad said: 'Ali ibn Bahr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yahya ibn 'Abbad, from his father 'Abbad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: al-Harith ibn Khazamah came with these two verses from the end of Bara'ah: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from yourselves﴾ to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and said: "Who is with you in this?" He said: "I do not know. By Allah, I testify that I heard them from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I understood them and memorised them." 'Umar said: "And I testify that I heard them from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." Then he said: "If they were three verses, I would have made them a separate surah. So look for a surah of the Qur'an and place them in it." So they placed them at the end of Bara'ah. [[al-Musnad (1/199).]]

It has already been mentioned that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was the one who advised Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with them both, to collect the Qur'an, so he commanded Zayd ibn Thabit, who collected it. 'Umar used to attend them while they were writing that. In the Sahih it is reported that Zayd said: "I found the last verses of the surah Bara'ah with Khuzaymah ibn Thabit, or Abu Khuzaymah." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4679.]] And we have mentioned that a group of the Companions remembered that from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as Khuzaymah ibn Thabit did when he began to recite them, and Allah knows best.

And Abu Dawud related it from Yazid ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Razzaq ibn Umar (and he said: "he was among the trustworthy Muslims, among the devout worshippers"), from Mudrik ibn Sa'd (Yazid said: "a trustworthy shaykh"), from Yunus ibn Maysara, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', who said: "Whoever says, when he enters the morning and when he enters the evening: 'Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but Him. In Him I have placed my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne,' seven times, Allah will suffice him for whatever concerns him."[[In K: "what troubles him."]][[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 5081.]]

It was also related by Ibn 'Asakir in the biography of this Abd al-Razzaq ibn Umar, through the narration of Abu Zur'a al-Dimashqi, from him, from Abu Sa'd Mudrik ibn Abi Sa'd al-Fazari, from Yunus ibn Maysara ibn Halays, from Umm al-Darda', who said: I heard Abu al-Darda' say: "No servant says: 'Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but Him. In Him I have placed my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne,' seven times, whether he says it truthfully or falsely, but that Allah will suffice him for whatever he is concerned about."[[Tarikh Dimashq (10/291, manuscript edition).]]

This addition is strange. Then he related it in the biography of Abd al-Razzaq Abu Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Razzaq, from his grandfather Abd al-Razzaq ibn Umar, with its chain, and he raised it (to the Prophet), and mentioned the like of it with the addition.[[Tarikh Dimashq (10/312, manuscript edition).]] This is munkar (rejected), and Allah knows best.

The end of Surah Bara'ah, and all praise is due to Allah alone.[[Written in K: "On the fourteenth of Rabi' al-Awwal, in the year eighty, in the seventh year of the Prophet's migration (hijra). Sufficient for us is Allah, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Mighty."]]
